For an owner who lives in the home: property tax, the county fee where it applies, insurance, the HOA or condo fee and upkeep.
In Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach the middle condo costs more to own each year than the middle house. But it costs less to buy: in Myrtle Beach, less than half as much. Weigh the smaller loan against the larger fee.

## What are the steps to buy a house in South Carolina?
Eight steps, from choosing an agent to the deed recorded in Conway. The biggest difference from many states: every South Carolina home closing must be supervised by a South Carolina attorney.

-

### 1 Step 1: Sign a buyer agreement with your agent
In South Carolina, no firm represents you as your agent until you both sign a written agreement that says so. We sign it with you before your first tour.
It states what your agent is paid. That fee is negotiable, and a seller may still offer to pay it.

-

### 2 Step 2: Choose a home and make an offer
Before you offer, we find the home's flood zone and get an insurance quote for the address, if you buy with Chapter3. You can sign the offer by e-signature from anywhere; South Carolina law counts it the same as ink.

-

### 3 Step 3: Inspect the home and read the papers
In South Carolina, inspecting the home is the buyer's job. We line up the inspection.
The seller of most resale houses must give you the state's disclosure form before you sign. For a condo, we get the HOA papers and the rental rules.

-

### 4 Step 4: The loan and the appraisal
Within three business days of your application, your lender must send a Loan Estimate, a form that lists the loan's terms and costs.
You get a free copy of the appraisal as soon as it is done.

-

### 5 Step 5: The closing attorney
A South Carolina attorney supervises the title search, the loan papers, the closing and the recording of the deed. With a home loan for personal or family use, the lender must ask which attorney you want and follow your choice.
We work with several closing attorneys and can recommend them once we are working with you. At least three business days before closing, your lender sends the Closing Disclosure: the loan's final terms and costs.

-

### 6 Step 6: Closing, here or from home
You can sign at the attorney's office. From another state, you can sign the deed papers and the mortgage before a notary where you live, with two witnesses.

-

### 7 Step 7: The deed is recorded in Conway
The deed and mortgage are recorded at the Horry County Register of Deeds in Conway. The seller pays the state's deed fee. To look up a recorded deed, use our Horry County property lookup .
What the buyer pays at closing is listed fee by fee on its own page.

-

### 8 Step 8: Apply for the 4 percent tax rate
A home you live in and apply for is taxed on 4 percent of its value; a second home or a rental on 6 percent. The 4 percent rate is not automatic: you apply to the county after you buy.
On a house the county values at $350,000 outside the cities, the current tax is about $1,290 a year at 4 percent and about $4,220 at 6 percent. A sale resets the county's value, so the seller's tax bill is not yours.

Buying from another state?
Tell us where you live and what you want. We line up the inspection, the insurance quote and a closing attorney.

## Can I buy a home in Myrtle Beach from out of state?
Yes, and many buyers do:

- 3 in 10 homes sold went to a buyer with a tax bill in another state or country

- Over half of condos sold went to such a buyer

North Carolina sends the most out-of-state buyers by far, then New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Virginia. In the same building or subdivision, buyers with an out-of-state tax bill paid the same middle price as South Carolina buyers.
More people keep coming. In the latest Census count, the Myrtle Beach metro grew faster than every U.S. metro but one. About 39 more people a day moved into Horry County from the rest of the country than moved out.

## What can go wrong when buying in Myrtle Beach?
Six things here surprise buyers from other states. Each has a fix, and we handle most of them before you offer. The ten costliest buyer mistakes are ranked on their own page.

-

### Flood zone
About 1 in 4 condos and 1 in 15 houses resold in Horry County in the past year sat in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. There, most mortgages require flood insurance. For a house you live in there, a federal flood policy cost a middle of about $1,070 a year.
We find the zone before you offer, and look for past flooding too.

-

### Insurance
The middle owner of a one-family house here pays about $2,000 a year for home insurance , about 40 percent more than in the rest of South Carolina. A condo owner pays about $800 for their own policy.
We get a quote for the address before you offer, if you buy with us.

-

### The second-home tax rate
If you never apply for the 4 percent rate, your home is taxed at 6 percent, as a second home is: about three times the tax (step 8).
We work out the tax at both rates on any address you send.

-

### A low appraisal
In our experience, low appraisals are rare here.
When one comes in low, we send comparable sales with a request to look at the value again. Once, the value changed and the borrower brought less to closing.

-

### Nightly rentals
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, a rental under 90 days is legal only where the zoning allows it. About 3 in 4 condos are in such zones; about 96 in 100 houses are not. In North Myrtle Beach a short-term rental needs a business license, and for now there is no special zoning or permit process beyond it.
We read the zoning and the HOA papers before you offer.

-

### Condos run like hotels
Fannie Mae, which backs many ordinary home loans, will not back one in a building run like a hotel. Signs include a front desk, daily cleaning, or a rule that owners join the rental program. Buyers there need a different loan or cash.
We read the building's rules before you offer, so you know which loans can work there.

Common questions

## Buying in Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach a buyer's market?
For condos, yes: across Horry County, the condos for sale would take about 7.5 months to sell. For houses under $700,000, not yet.

### Will home prices in Myrtle Beach go down?
We do not forecast prices. Horry County house prices were about flat in the latest year, after four years of gains.

### Do you need a lawyer to buy a house in South Carolina?
Yes. Every South Carolina home closing must be supervised by a South Carolina attorney. Step 5 says how you choose one.

### What is a CL-100?
The termite letter, the Official South Carolina Wood Infestation Report. Only a licensed pest control applicator may issue it for a sale or a loan. It reports visible insect damage, active infestations, and moisture and decay under the house.

### Can I rent my Myrtle Beach condo by the night?
Often, if it is inside the City of Myrtle Beach, where most condos sit in zones that allow it. The condo's own rules can still ban it.

### How much are property taxes in Myrtle Beach?
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, on a house the county values at $350,000, about $1,410 a year if you live in it and apply. As a second home, about $5,350.

# The Myrtle Beach buyer mistakes that cost the most.

- Your home taxed at 6 percent 3 times the 4 percent bill

- Houses for sale in the flood zone 8 in 10 listings do not say so

- One flood outside the zone $26,400 paid

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
The costliest mistake is paying the second-home 6 percent tax on a home you live in: about $2,930 a year on a $350,000 house. Nine more follow, by cost.

The short answer
Of people who bought a house in Horry County in 2024 and have its tax bill mailed to that house, about 1 in 7 are still taxed at 6 percent. That is the rate for second homes and rentals. It is the costliest mistake here, and it comes back every year until they apply for the 4 percent rate for the home they live in.
The seller's low tax bill, flood insurance and wind cover come next.

## Are you paying the 6 percent tax on a home you live in?
Yes, until you apply. A home you live in is taxed on 4 percent of its value once you apply and qualify, and it does not pay the part of the tax that runs the schools. Until then, the county bills it at 6 percent, the rate for second homes and rentals.
Property tax a year on a house the county values at $350,000, outside the city limits How the house is taxed, rate tax a year

Your home, after you apply · 4 percent rate about $1,290
The same house at 6 percent about $4,220

Horry County's 2026 tax rates. The county's stormwater fee and small special districts are left out.
Newer owners are the most likely to still pay it.
1 in 5 bought in 2025
1 in 7 bought in 2024
1 in 17 bought in 2018 or 2019, not sold since

The share, rounded, of houses owned by a person who gets the tax bill at that same house, still taxed at 6 percent. The newest buyers can still apply for this year.

### Why do people moving here miss it?
The county does not apply it for you. It asks for South Carolina papers that a new arrival does not have yet:

- a South Carolina driver's license or ID at the home's address, for each owner who lives there and a spouse;

- South Carolina registration for every vehicle you own, at that address;

- your state and federal tax returns, or the Social Security 1099;

- if you own another home, its tax bill showing no exemption, or a letter that the exemption was removed.

You also certify that no one in the home claims the 4 percent rate on another home. That means you, a spouse or a child under 18 you support. None of you can claim to be a legal resident of another state.

- You apply once
Unless the ownership or who lives there changes.

- Move in partway through a year
You get the 4 percent rate for that whole year.

- Aim for the end of May
Apply by then, and the bill the county mails later that year comes at 4 percent. If you miss May, you can still apply for that year until its bill is due, usually January 15 of the next year.

## Why is my tax bill so much higher than the seller's?
The seller's bill shows what the seller pays, not what you will pay. A home owned for many years is often taxed on a value far below the county's own value of it. A sale resets that value, and the new value is first taxed the year after the sale.
Example: the seller has lived in a house since about 2010. The county taxes it on much less than its full value. You buy the house as a second home. Your bill is on the full value, at the second-home rate. You pay about five times the seller's bill.
Example: tax a year on one house the county values at $350,000 Whose bill, why tax a year

The seller's bill · their home for many years about $800
Your bill, as your home · after you apply about $1,290
Your bill, as a second home · 6 percent rate about $4,220

Outside the city limits, at the county's 2026 rates. The seller's figure taxes about 63 percent of the value, the average share for homes whose last deed was in 2005 to 2014.
We can work out your bill at your price and your tax rate, not from the seller's bill. Our property tax guide explains how a sale resets the value. To see what the county bills a house now, use our property lookup for any Horry County address .

## Do I need flood insurance if the house is not in a flood zone?
Federal law does not require flood insurance outside FEMA's high-risk zone. But since 2015, 3 in 10 paid flood claims in Horry County were on buildings outside that zone, and those repairs cost more.

## Does a homeowners policy cover wind near the beach?
Not always. In Horry County east of U.S. 17 or Bypass 17, whichever is farther west, and in named coastal areas of other counties, South Carolina lets an insurer leave wind and hail out of a homeowners policy. In Myrtle Beach, that line is the Bypass. Outside those areas, an insurer needs the state insurance director's approval to do it.
If wind is left out, you need a separate wind policy. The state's backup insurer for wind sells one to owners in this coastal area who cannot get it from another insurer. Our coastal insurance guide explains the three policies a house here can need.
Before you offer, we can tell you which side of the line a house is on, and get a homeowners quote that shows whether wind is in it.

## How do I know a condo building has saved enough for repairs?
Only from the building's own budget and records. South Carolina does not require a condo to keep repair savings, called reserves, or to study what its repairs will need.
More than half of the condos for sale on the Grand Strand are in buildings 30 years old or older.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Oceanfront towers in Myrtle Beach. Roofs, balconies and pools like these are what a condo's repair savings pay for.

Example An 80-unit building has saved 26 percent of what it should hold by now for its repairs. Association Reserves , a firm that studies condo savings, calls anything under 30 percent weak, with a high chance of a special bill to the owners.
In our example, the bill five years out is about $4,750 a unit, split evenly. It leaves out inflation and interest.

Freddie Mac buys home loans from lenders. For loan applications from January 4, 2027, it needs a building's budget to put at least 15 percent of its dues into savings. A buyer whose loan follows Freddie Mac's rules needs a building that meets it.
Our pages on condo reserves , special assessments and condos in a lawsuit explain each one.

## Can I rent my Myrtle Beach house by the week?
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, only where the zoning allows rentals under 90 days. Most of the city's residential neighborhoods are not zoned for them.

- Zoning districts starting with R
No rentals under 90 days.

- The RMV district
The one R district where rentals under 90 days are allowed.

- 24 houses
In the whole city, only 24 houses in the traditional residential zones keep an older right to rent for under 90 days.

A violation is a misdemeanor, with a fine of up to $500, 30 days in jail, or both, each time. Where the zoning allows a short-term rental, the city requires a business license for it.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Houses and condo towers side by side in Myrtle Beach. Each lot has its own zoning district, and the district decides whether it can be rented for under 90 days.

The city is rewriting its zoning code . The rules also differ in each other town and in the county outside the cities; our short-term rental rules page has each one. Before you make an offer, we can look up the zoning of any address in the city.

## Should I skip the inspection to win the house?
No. Under South Carolina law, inspecting the house is the buyer's job, and the agents have no duty to inspect it.
The seller's disclosure form is not an inspection. On most resales of a house with one to four units, the seller must give you the state's form before you sign, unless the contract says otherwise. It tells you only what the seller knows.
The law exempts some sales from the form, such as a new home no one has lived in, a foreclosure, an estate sale and an auction.
Septic tanks are rare at the beach and more common inland. About 1 in 16 houses for sale on the Grand Strand list one, and 79 list well water.

## Will the HOA let me keep my boat, golf cart or rental?
Only if its recorded rules allow it. About 7 in 10 houses for sale on our MLS, which covers the Grand Strand and inland Horry County, have an HOA fee, so most houses here come with a homeowners association (HOA) and its rules.
In South Carolina, those rules bind you only if they are on file with the county. The HOA's papers are recorded at the county's Register of Deeds. A rule the board adds or changes must be recorded by January 10 of the next year to stay in force. Our guide to searching Horry County land records by name shows how to find them.
The biggest mistake we see from buyers moving from New York is not checking that a community's rules fit how they live: its rules on boats, golf carts, rentals and pools. The same check matters for any buyer with a boat, a cart or a rental plan. For one community's rules, read the HOA rules in The Farm at Carolina Forest .
Many communities here ban renting the house out at all. When we search for you, we leave those out, and we read the HOA papers for any rule that would block your rental plan. If you would rather have no HOA, see our page on homes with no HOA .

Find out if a community's rules fit how you live
Send us the community or the address. We can read its HOA papers for the boat, the golf cart, the pool and renting before you offer.
Have us read the HOA rules

## Does the agent I called work for me?
Not until you both sign. In South Carolina, no brokerage firm represents you until you and the firm agree to it in writing.

- Before you both sign
You are the firm's customer. Under the law, the firm can help the sale along without representing you or the seller.

- After you both sign an agreement
The firm is your agent, on the terms the agreement states, including its pay.

Paying an agent does not by itself make the agent yours.
Since 2024, agents who use the MLS , the shared list of homes for sale, must sign a written agreement with you before you tour a home. It must state the agent's pay as an amount or a rate, and bar the agent from taking more from any source. It must also say that fees are fully negotiable and not fixed by law.
An agent on your side also tells you when a house is not a good buy. One buyer spent over a year sending his agent Zillow links. Each time, he was told it was a good buy in an up and coming neighborhood. He came to us after that.
Before we show you a home, we put in writing what we will do for you and what we are paid.

Common questions

## Buyer mistakes FAQ

### How do I apply for the 4 percent rate in Horry County?
Online, on the county's Online Services page, under Legal Residence Application. If the county asks for a missing paper, you can send it by mail, fax or email, or bring it to the Assessor's Office. The office's phone number is 843-915-5040.

### How far back can I get a refund of the 6 percent tax on my home?
If you qualified for the 4 percent rate and paid at 6 percent, you can claim the extra tax back from the county assessor. Under state law, you have two years from the day you paid that bill, and a county council may allow refunds of the county's own share for more past years.

### Does a condo's HOA fee show whether it has saved enough for repairs?
No. In our count of condos for sale here, the middle HOA fee is about $640 a month, and about $690 in buildings built in 1986 or earlier. Older buildings do not charge much more, so the fee alone does not show what a building has saved for its age.

### Can I change jobs while buying a house in Myrtle Beach?
Wait until after closing if you can. On a loan that follows Fannie Mae's rules, the lender checks again that you still have your job no more than 10 business days before closing, or 15 in some cases. A loan officer at our preferred lender can tell you what your loan will need.

## First-Time Home Buyer in Myrtle Beach: Cash and $10,000 Help

# Your first home in Myrtle Beach may take less cash than you think.

- Often no down payment on VA and USDA loans

- Seller-paid closing costs on FHA and VA

- $10,000 from SC Housing under its income limit

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Your cash to buy in Myrtle Beach is the down payment plus the closing costs, and a first-time buyer can often bring less of each.

The short answer
Your down payment depends on your loan. Your lender gives you the figure when it pre-approves you, after checking your credit and income. Part of your cash is earnest money, the deposit you give with your offer. In an ordinary sale it is credited to you at closing.
A VA loan often needs no down payment. A USDA loan can cover the full price inside USDA's area, mostly around Conway, Loris, Aynor and Longs, for low- and moderate-income buyers. On an FHA loan, a credit score of 580 or more gets FHA's smallest down payment, and the seller can pay your closing costs. SC Housing adds $10,000 for buyers under its income limit.

## How much cash do you need to buy a first home in Myrtle Beach?
The closing costs are the fees to make the loan and close the sale. Seven things can lower what you bring.

- FHA's smallest down payment, at a 580 score Every buyer with a credit score of 580 or more can get FHA's smallest down payment. From 500 to 579 you put more down, and below 500 FHA does not insure the loan. Your lender gives you the dollar figure for your price.

- No down payment on a VA loan A loan backed by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) often needs no down payment, as long as the price is not above the appraised value. That is the value an appraiser gives the home for the loan. Our VA loan guide covers who can use one.

- No down payment on a USDA loan A USDA loan, backed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, can cover the full price, with no down payment, when the appraiser values the home at the price or more. It is for low- and moderate-income buyers in USDA's area. On our map, about 6 in 10 houses listed at or under $450,000 in Horry County are inside that area. Nearly all have a Conway, Loris, Aynor or Longs address.

- The seller pays your closing costs On an FHA loan, insured by the Federal Housing Administration, the seller, a builder or the agents can pay up to 6 percent of the price in all toward your closing costs. On a $270,000 house, the middle one listed now at or under $300,000, that is up to $16,200. It can cover only your actual closing costs, and the seller has to agree to it in your offer.

- $10,000 from SC Housing SC Housing, the South Carolina State Housing Finance and Development Authority, gives an eligible buyer $10,000 toward the down payment and closing costs. Our guide to SC down payment assistance has who qualifies, when it is repaid and the steps.

- A gift toward the purchase On an FHA loan, the money can be a gift from family, an employer or labor union, a charity or a government homebuyer program. The lender needs a gift letter signed by the giver.

- Up to $10,000 from an IRA You can take up to $10,000 out of an IRA, an individual retirement account, for a first home without the 10 percent early-withdrawal penalty. You, and your spouse if you are married, must not have owned a main home in the last two years. The money must be spent within 120 days.

Our closing cost calculator adds up each closing cost for your price.

## Should your first home in Myrtle Beach be a condo or a house?
A house, if your budget reaches about $250,000 and you can live inland. Below that, most homes that sell are condos, and a condo can be a good first home once we have checked the building.

- A condo
A condo is the lowest price into a home of your own here. The loan is the hard part: the building has to be approved for it. HUD, the federal housing department, lists only 9 condo communities in all of Horry County that are approved for FHA loans.
About 1 in 6 condos that sold under $300,000 were in a high-risk flood zone, where the lender will require flood insurance. About half went to owners who get their tax bill in another state.

- A house
A house costs more, and the loan is simpler: there is no building to approve. The middle house listed at or under $300,000 has about twice the floor space of the middle condo, and a yard.
Only about 3 in 100 houses and townhouses that sold under $300,000 were in a high-risk flood zone. About 1 in 7 went to owners whose tax bill goes to another state.

In our experience, condo buildings with a rental program usually do not meet the rules most conventional loans follow, because so many owners are investors. An FHA loan in a building that is not on HUD's list needs an approval for that one unit.
A condo also has a monthly fee to its homeowners association (HOA), and the chance of a special assessment, a one-time bill for repairs. Our guide to special assessments explains them. Many houses have an HOA too; our guide to homes with no HOA lists places without one.

### What we check before you make an offer

- The building's loan approval. For a condo, we find out whether the building is approved for your loan before you offer.

- The HOA papers. We read the rules, the budget, the money saved for repairs and the financial statements, so a fee rise or a one-time repair bill is no surprise.

- The flood zone. We look up every home you offer on, so you know whether the lender will require flood insurance.

- The insurance quote. If you buy with us, we get you one before you make an offer on a house.

### Flood and wind
A lender must require flood insurance when the building is in a high-risk flood zone. A policy bought while the mortgage is made starts with no wait; otherwise there is a 30‑day wait. Before you close in that zone, check what flood insurance costs here .

## Do you qualify as a first-time home buyer in South Carolina?
These are the lines that decide whether the help above fits you.

- Have you owned a home before? SC Housing's main program in Horry County does not ask whether you owned a home in the past. It asks only that you own no other property, or a share of one, on the day the loan closes. Bare land is allowed. The IRA rule above is different: no main home in the last two years.

- Your credit score SC Housing needs at least a 640 credit score. FHA needs 500, and 580 for its smallest down payment.

- Your income, for SC Housing In Horry County, SC Housing's household income limit is about $115,000 a year for one or two people and about $134,000 for three or more. The home's price can be up to $450,000.

- Living in it On an FHA loan, one buyer moves in within 60 days of closing and plans to stay at least a year.

Is there a federal first-time buyer tax credit? Not yet. The SC Housing programs are the help you can use now.

## What are the steps to buy your first home in South Carolina?

- Get pre-approved by a lender. The lender checks your credit and income and gives you a price to shop under. When an SC Housing program fits, a Chapter3 agent connects you with an SC Housing approved lender.

- Choose a home. We send homes in your budget and run the checks above on each one you like.

- Make the offer. You can ask the seller to pay your closing costs in the offer. If a real estate broker holds your earnest money, it stays in the broker's trust account until the sale closes. In an ordinary sale it is credited to you at closing.

- Inspect the house. A home inspector looks over the house for you.

- The appraisal. The lender's appraiser gives the home a value. Low appraisals are rare here. When one comes in low, our agents gather recent sales of similar homes and ask for the value to be looked at again.

- Close with an attorney. Every South Carolina home closing must be supervised by a South Carolina attorney.

- Move in, then file for the 4 percent rate. Apply to the county assessor by January 15 after the year you move in.

Our guide to buying a home in Myrtle Beach covers the purchase in more detail, and our common buyer mistakes page lists what goes wrong. Moving from another state? Our relocation guide covers the move.

Common questions

## First-time home buyer questions

### Is there a first-time home buyer tax credit in South Carolina?
SC Housing no longer offers its tax credit certificate. The tax break an owner gets here is the 4 percent rate on the home you live in, which needs an application to the county assessor.

### Is there a homestead exemption for first-time buyers in Horry County?
Not for being a first-time buyer. In South Carolina the homestead exemption is for owners 65 or older who have lived in the state a year, or who are disabled or blind. It exempts the first $50,000 of the home's value.

### Is there help if I earn more than SC Housing's limit?
Palmetto Home Advantage, another SC Housing program, has an income limit of $140,000 in every county, counted on the buyers' own income, not the whole household. It is open to first-time and repeat buyers. Its help is forgiven after 10 years, and repaid in full on a sale, refinance or move before then.

### What is the FHA loan limit in Horry County?
FHA's 2026 loan limit for a one-unit home in Horry County is about $541,000. That is well above HUD's own estimate of the area's middle sale price, $340,000.

## SC Down Payment Assistance Programs in Horry County | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/programs/
Summary: SC Housing's $10,000 down payment help in Horry County: the income and price limits, who qualifies, when it is repaid, which homes count, and how to apply.

Home / Buyers / SC Down Payment Help
Buying a home

# Down payment help in Horry County: you do not have to be a first-time buyer.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
SC Housing gives an eligible buyer $10,000. Most houses for sale in Conway, Loris, Aynor and Longs are under its price limit. Across the beach towns, about a third are.

The short answer
The $10,000 is a second mortgage from SC Housing, the state's housing agency. A second mortgage is a second loan on the home. It pays toward the down payment and closing costs. After you have lived in the home 15 years, SC Housing forgives it, and you owe nothing on the $10,000. If you sell, refinance or move out sooner, you repay all of it, from the sale or the new loan.
To qualify, a household of one or two can earn up to $114,960, or $134,120 for three or more. The home can cost up to $450,000, you need a credit score of 640, and you must own no other property when the loan closes.

Homes that fit SC Housing's limits, sent to you

## Do you qualify for SC Housing's down payment help in Horry County?
You qualify for SC Housing's Homebuyer Program if you pass the seven tests below.

- Household income Up to $114,960 for 1 or 2 people, $134,120 for 3 or more The income of everyone on the loan or the deed counts together.

- Home price Up to $450,000 The lot can be 5 acres at most.

- What you own now No other property when the loan closes Owning bare land is allowed.

- Credit and debts A credit score of 640 or more If the FHA, VA, USDA or conventional loan's own rules ask for a higher score, the higher score applies. All your monthly debt payments together can be at most 45 percent of your income.

- Citizenship A U.S. citizen or a permanent resident A permanent resident needs a green card. A visa of any kind does not qualify.

- Who is on the loan Only buyers who will live in the home The Homebuyer Program allows no cosigner. A gift toward the purchase can come from a relative, a domestic partner or a fiancé.

- The homebuyer course One buyer takes it before loan approval Online or in a classroom, within 12 months of closing, even if you have owned a home before. The lender arranges it.

### Do you earn too much?
Probably not. SC Housing's limit for one or two people is about 1.7 times the median, or middle, household income in Horry County.
SC Housing's income limits beside what households here earn Income, what it is yearly income

SC Housing limit, 3 or more people · Homebuyer Program $134,120
SC Housing limit, 1 or 2 people · Homebuyer Program $114,960
Middle household income, Horry County · all household sizes about $68,500

The median (middle) household income is the U.S. Census Bureau's latest one-year figure for Horry County, for households of every size.
About four in five renter households in the county earn under $100,000, below the limit for any household size.

### How much of your own money do you still need?
With a VA or USDA loan, the $10,000 can cover most or all of the cash you bring to closing. Those loans need no down payment, so all of it goes to closing costs and prepaid items. Prepaid items are the first property taxes, homeowners insurance and loan interest paid at closing.
With an FHA or conventional loan, you also need a down payment, and the $10,000 goes toward both.
The $10,000 comes only with SC Housing's own first mortgage, which can be any of these four loans:

- FHA: insured by the Federal Housing Administration, part of HUD.

- VA: backed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, for veterans and service members.

- USDA: backed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, for homes inside its area on our map below.

- Conventional: a loan no government agency backs.

Our closing cost guide adds up the costs at closing for a home at your price. Before you make an offer, we get the lender's figure for that home, so you know your number first.

## Do you have to pay back SC Housing's $10,000?
Only if you sell, refinance or stop living in the home before 15 years are up. It does not shrink a little each year: until year 15, you owe all of it.
What you owe on SC Housing's $10,000, year by year You owe the full $10,000 in every one of years 1 to 15
$0
Move in Year 10 After year 15
Sell, refinance or move out in year 10 The full $10,000 is repaid from the sale or the new loan.
Still living there after year 15 SC Housing forgives all of it. You repay nothing.

### Is there a tax if you sell early?
Only if three things are all true: you sell within nine years, you sell at a gain, and your income has risen above the levels in the recapture notice from your lender. Then you may owe a federal recapture tax, an increase in your federal income tax for the year you sell. SC Housing pays it back if you ask in writing by June 30 of the next year; the refund is reported to the IRS as income.

## Which homes count in Horry County, and where are they under $450,000?
Houses, townhomes, condos in an approved building, and modular homes count, up to $450,000. A modular home is built in sections in a factory and set on a foundation, not on a steel frame.
Conway has more houses for sale at or under $450,000 than any other town, Myrtle Beach included.

### Condos: under the price limit, but the building must be approved

- 89% of condos for sale in the same towns are listed at or under $450,000.

- 9 condo projects in all of Horry County are approved for FHA loans. HUD, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, keeps the list.

Several of those nine are approved only for some phases or buildings. An FHA loan on a condo in any other building needs a separate approval for that one unit.
In Chapter3's experience, a building with a rental program usually fails the rules for a conventional loan, because so many owners are investors. Our guide to condos most lenders will not lend on explains why. We check the building's approval before you make an offer on a condo.

### Manufactured homes
A manufactured home, once called a mobile home, is built on a permanent steel frame to HUD's code. The Homebuyer Program does not take it. Palmetto Home Advantage takes doublewide or larger manufactured homes on a permanent foundation, usually with a credit score of at least 660. A doublewide is built in two sections; a single-wide does not qualify.

## Can you buy with no money down in Horry County?
Yes, with a USDA or VA loan. SC Housing offers both with no down payment. A USDA loan needs a home inside USDA's area, and that area leaves out the coast.
The part left out is the coastal strip from Little River through Myrtle Beach to Murrells Inlet, and inland past Carolina Forest and Socastee. It is less than a fifth of the county's land.

## Which SC Housing program fits you in Horry County?
Four SC Housing programs are open to Horry County buyers now. A fifth, Palmetto Heroes, is closed until its next round. The voucher program works only where the local housing authority takes part. Find the line that matches you.

- You own no other property, your household is under the income limit, and the home costs $450,000 or less. The Homebuyer Program The $10,000 on this page

- You earn more, the home costs more than $450,000, you already own a home, or you want a manufactured home. Palmetto Home Advantage Up to 4 percent of the loan, forgiven after 10 years

- You are a teacher, nurse, police officer, firefighter, EMT, veteran, or in the military or National Guard. Palmetto Heroes $10,000, closed for 2026

- You, or anyone in your household, has a permanent disability shown by Social Security disability income (SSI or SSDI) or long-term disability income. Families with Disabilities The same 15-year forgivable help, homes up to $450,000

- You have had a Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) for at least a year in the county where you buy. Voucher homeownership Where the local housing authority takes part

### Palmetto Home Advantage
Palmetto Home Advantage counts only the borrowers' own income, not the whole household: up to $140,000, for any household size. SC Housing has no price limit for it, but the FHA, VA, USDA or conventional loan still has its own. A repeat buyer may hold at most two financed homes, the new one included. If you sell, refinance or move out within the 10 years, you repay all of the help.

### Palmetto Heroes and Families with Disabilities
Palmetto Heroes' 2026 round filled in about four weeks, after 272 loans. SC Housing has not published a date for the next round. A buyer needs a signed sales contract to get the help, so we start the home search before it opens.
Families with Disabilities is open in every county, has no first-time buyer rule, and uses FHA, VA or USDA loans.

## Is there down payment help from Horry County or Myrtle Beach?
Not from the county or the cities directly. Horry County runs HUD's HOME program for Horry, Georgetown and Williamsburg counties, and that money goes to developers and nonprofits, not to buyers. Two other routes help buyers themselves.

- Habitat for Humanity of Horry County Builds and sells homes For households earning 35 to 80 percent of the county's median income: for three people in 2026, about $23,000 to $62,000 a year. You must have lived in Horry County for the last 12 months. Buyers put in at least 180 hours of work. You start with a short interest form on its homeownership page, and Habitat pairs you with a volunteer Financial Mentor.

- Federal Home Loan Bank of Atlanta Grants through member banks Earning under 80 percent of the area's median income: up to $17,500 for a first-time buyer, and up to $20,000 for police, teachers, firefighters, health care workers and veterans. Earning 80 to 120 percent: up to $15,000, from its Workforce Housing Plus+ grants.

The bank grants go through banks that applied for them, and we find out which nearby banks still have money.

### Can you use a bank grant and SC Housing's $10,000 together?
Yes, if the grant's own rules allow it. SC Housing's checklist for the lender has a line for a grant from anyone else, and the lender puts the grant's approval letter in the file.

## How do you apply for SC Housing's down payment help?
You apply through an SC Housing approved lender, in the five steps below. The lender handles the application and the reservation.

### Is the $10,000 open now?
Yes. SC Housing's program page offers the $10,000. The only program it lists as closed is Palmetto Heroes.
The money is limited, and SC Housing pays it out while money lasts. Once the lender reserves your loan and the $10,000, SC Housing holds them for 60 days on an existing home or 120 days on a new one, and the lender can ask for more time.

### The five steps

- Pick an SC Housing approved lender. SC Housing's Find a Lender list for Horry County has about 90 loan officers at about 40 companies. The lender takes your application and checks that you qualify.

- Take the homebuyer course. The lender arranges it. One buyer finishes it, online or in a classroom, before the loan is approved.

- Find a home under the limit with us. We search houses, townhomes and condos at or under $450,000 in the towns you pick.

- Reserve the money. Once you qualify and decide to go ahead, the lender reserves your loan and the $10,000.

- Close. The $10,000 goes toward your down payment, closing costs and prepaid items at closing. It cannot pay a real estate commission or an appraisal gap, which is the difference when a home appraises for less than its price.

Our preferred lender is not on SC Housing's lender list for Horry County, so when one of these programs fits you, we introduce you to an approved lender.

### If you still own a home somewhere else
Example: Dana rents in Myrtle Beach and still owns a house in Ohio.
She wants SC Housing's down payment help for a house in Conway.
Her Chapter3 agent finds the problem before she makes an offer. SC Housing will not close the Conway loan while she owns the Ohio house.
The agent writes the Conway closing date into the contract for a day after the Ohio sale closes.
What this means for you: set the closing on your new home for after the sale of the old one.

Our first-time home buyer guide explains the rest of the first-time buyer steps . If you are deciding where to look, our guide to the most affordable places to live around Myrtle Beach describes each one.

Common questions

## SC Housing questions

### Do I have to be a first-time buyer in Horry County?
No. Horry County is one of SC Housing's "targeted" counties, where the first-time buyer rule does not apply. A buyer who has owned a home before can use the $10,000 once that home is sold.

### Can I use SC Housing's help on a new home from a builder?
Yes, if the price is $450,000 or less. SC Housing has a form for the builder who sells the home. Its lender list for Horry County includes DHI Mortgage, Lennar Mortgage and NVR Mortgage Finance, the mortgage companies of the builders D.R. Horton, Lennar and NVR.

### Can the seller pay part of my closing costs with SC Housing's help?
Yes, within the limits of your FHA, VA, USDA or conventional loan. SC Housing's guide adds no limit of its own on help from the seller.

### Who decides the interest rate on an SC Housing loan?
SC Housing decides the rate on its own first mortgage. It is a fixed rate, posted every day for its approved lenders, and your lender locks it for you when it reserves the loan. SC Housing makes the loan with or without the $10,000, so we have the lender quote it both ways before you choose.

### Can I get SC Housing's Made It Home! help or its tax credit in Horry County?
No. SC Housing's Made It Home! help is only for new homes in five other cities, and its Mortgage Credit Certificate, a federal tax credit for buyers, has ended.

# Relocating to Myrtle Beach? You can buy before you move. How to buy from home, and every moving guide by question.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
When relocating to Myrtle Beach from another state, you can sign, inspect and close on a home from where you live now.

The short answer
If you are relocating to Myrtle Beach, you can buy a home before you move. The offer can be signed electronically, and a South Carolina attorney may close by mail, so you do not have to be at the closing.
In the latest IRS count, about 15,000 households moved into Horry County in one year, and about 9,100 moved out. In Myrtle Beach, a January day averages a high of about 56 degrees. An owner who lives in the home here typically pays about $944 a year in property tax. Our guide to why so many people move here gives the four reasons, with numbers.

## Can I buy a house in Myrtle Beach before I move?
We do most of the work here while you stay where you are. These are the seven steps, in order.

- Pick the towns first. Tell us how you want to live, and we narrow the search to the towns that fit. Start with our 13 towns near Myrtle Beach, compared .

- See the houses. We tour the homes you like for you, and we tell you what the listing photos do not show. If you want to see a house yourself, we plan the showings around your trip.

- Know the insurance before you offer. When you buy with us, we get an insurance quote for the address before you make an offer.

- Offer from home. Under South Carolina law , an electronic signature on a contract has the same effect as one in ink. You can sign the offer from anywhere.

- Inspect. A home inspection is the buyer's job in South Carolina. We line up the inspection.

- Choose the closing attorney. Every South Carolina home closing must be supervised by a South Carolina attorney . We work with several closing attorneys and can recommend them once we are working with you.

- Sign the closing papers at home. In a closing by mail , the papers are sent to you to sign and return. The attorney must be reachable by phone or email to explain them. You sign the deed or mortgage before a notary where you live, with two witnesses, and it is filed here . A lender may set its own signing rules.

You will not be the only buyer doing this from afar. About 3 in 10 homes sold in Horry County in the latest year went to a buyer whose tax bill goes to another state or country. For condos it was more than half.
The market and the steps to buy a house in South Carolina are in our buying guide. Still own a home where you live now? Sell first or buy first shows the three ways to time the two sales.

## Questions about relocating

### Can I sign my closing papers on a video call?
Not with a South Carolina notary. South Carolina law has no remote (video) notarization. Ask your closing attorney how you will sign.

### Who picks the closing attorney?
You do, when you buy with a home loan for personal or family use. The lender must ask which attorney you want for the closing and follow your choice.

### Which state do most out-of-state buyers come from?
North Carolina, by far. Our count of Horry County deeds over one year found 916 buyers with a tax bill in North Carolina. New York was next, with 438.

### Can I move to Myrtle Beach before I have a job here?
Yes. Most of our buyers who move here find work within a month or two. That is our clients' experience, not a promise.

# Cost of living in Myrtle Beach: your money buys a lot more house.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026

The short answer

## Your money buys a lot more house here
The typical home in the Myrtle Beach area sells for about $342,000. In the New York area it is about $737,000. Boston is about $742,000, Washington about $580,000 and Philadelphia about $392,000. Sell in any of those and you can often buy here outright, or buy a much bigger house for the same payment.
Day to day costs move less than the house does. Food, power and everyday items run close to the national average. Rent is the one that drops, at about 17 percent below average.
Not every move saves you money on a house. Cleveland averages about $254,000 and Pittsburgh about $232,000, so both are cheaper than here. If you are coming from the Midwest, put your city in the calculator before you assume the coast is a bargain.

Real bills

## What our customers pay each month
These are real bills from a customer in a 1,400 square foot two-story house in 2026, not an area average. Power averages about $119.89 and water about $51.42. Your bill moves with the size of the house and how cold you keep it.
Internet costs about $40 to $75 a month. Most addresses can choose between a local fiber co-op and cable, so it is worth getting both prices.

### Peak Hours: how your power bill works
Both utilities that serve Horry County, Santee Cooper and Horry Electric Cooperative, charge a residential account two ways. You pay for the power you use, and you pay again for your highest single hour of use that month. On their published 2026 schedules that second charge runs $8 to $12 for each kilowatt in that one hour.
The company calls that window Peak Hours. It runs 3pm to 6pm from April to October, and 6am to 9am from November to March. Run the dryer, the oven and the pool pump together at 5pm in July and you pay for it all month. Spread them out and the same power costs less.
Opening an account needs a credit check and may need a deposit. Water and sewer outside the city needs one day of notice, so call before you move in. Who serves your street is on our moving checklist .

Rates, brackets and retirement rules come from each state's own department of revenue and statutes for 2026, and the Myrtle Beach property tax uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for an owner-occupied home outside the city limits, with the 4 percent residential ratio, the school operating exemption and the 65 and older homestead exemption. Left out on both sides: federal tax, car taxes, insurance, and any credit that depends on your own return. Where a state rule is too detailed to model we leave it out, and almost every one of those left out would RAISE the bill in the state you are leaving, not lower it: Connecticut's tax recapture, New York's supplemental tax, and the exemption phase-outs in Maryland and Ohio. Three would LOWER it, and we name them: Pennsylvania's tax forgiveness and the Massachusetts senior circuit breaker are low-income credits we do not apply, and Florida caps how fast a homesteaded home's assessed value can rise, so a long-held Florida home's real bill is below our estimate. If one of those is you, your bill in the state you are leaving is lower than we show. Insurance is a separate cost to check on this coast, usually higher here than in the states up north; coming from coastal Florida it is priced address by address, in both directions. Taxes

## Taxes are lower here
Taxes drop for almost everyone who moves here. The drop is bigger than the price difference on food or power.
We compare the taxes side by side, state by state, for New York , New Jersey , Pennsylvania , Ohio , Maryland , Virginia , North Carolina , Massachusetts , Connecticut and Florida .
This is general information, not tax advice. Rates and deductions change, and your own situation decides the answer. Confirm anything you plan around with a tax professional or the Horry County Auditor.

### Income tax
For the 2026 tax year, South Carolina charges 1.99 percent on your first $30,000 of taxable income and 5.21 percent above that. No city or county adds its own income tax. Social Security is not taxed. Military retirement pay is not taxed at any age. Other retirement income gets a deduction of up to $3,000 before you turn 65 and up to $10,000 after. At 65 there is also a deduction of up to $15,000 against any income, but it is reduced by whatever retirement deduction you already took, so the two do not stack. A couple where both are 65 can claim up to $30,000.

### Property tax
These are assessment ratios, not tax rates. Only 4 percent of a main home's value is assessed, and a main home is also exempt from the school operating tax. For a second home or a rental, 6 percent is assessed and the school tax applies. On a $350,000 house in the unincorporated county that is roughly $1,300 a year as a main home against roughly $4,200 as a second home. You have to apply for the lower rate yourself. Our property tax page has the form and a calculator.

### Car tax, which is new for most people
South Carolina taxes your car every year. New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ohio do not. North Carolina, Virginia and Massachusetts already do, so check yours. The tax reaches past cars: the county bills boats and campers every year too. A $30,000 car costs about $360 a year outside the city and about $460 inside Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 road fee. You also pay $250 once per car when you first register it here.

### Sales tax and gas
Sales tax is 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside Myrtle Beach. Food you cook at home is not taxed at all here. Gas is cheaper too. In August 2026 South Carolina averaged about 40 cents a gallon below the national average, about 45 cents below Ohio and about 45 cents below New York. One of our team, who moved here from Ohio, calls cheaper gas the best everyday change since the move.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach cost of living FAQ

### Is the cost of living cheaper in Myrtle Beach?
Yes. The biggest difference is the house. A typical home here sells for about $342,000, against about $737,000 in the New York area and about $742,000 in Boston. Day to day costs are closer to average, and rent is about 17 percent below the national average.

### What salary do I need to live in Myrtle Beach?
It depends on where you live now, which is what the calculator on this page is for. On the price index behind the calculator, someone earning $70,000 in Los Angeles would need about $43,000 here for the same buying power. Not every move saves money. Someone coming from Montgomery, Alabama would need about the same, and from a few smaller southern metros slightly more.

### Is Myrtle Beach cheaper than Charlotte or Raleigh?
On the house, yes. A typical home here is about $342,000. Charlotte is about $389,000 and Raleigh about $437,000. Property tax on a main home is also lower here because South Carolina taxes an owner-occupied home on 4 percent of its value.

### What costs more in Myrtle Beach than people expect?
Two things. South Carolina taxes your car every year, which most northern states do not, and that runs a few hundred dollars per vehicle. A second home or rental is taxed at about three times the rate of a main home.

### Where does the calculator get its data?
Home values and rents come from Zillow. Everything else comes from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis, which measures what things cost in 387 metro areas and every state. Both are averages for a whole metro area, not a quote for one house.

### Does the calculator include South Carolina taxes?
The cost of living calculator does not. The tax calculator further down this page does. Put in what you earn, how you earn it and what your house is worth. It shows the state income tax and the property tax you pay now next to what you would pay here. Car taxes are covered separately, because South Carolina charges one every year and most northern states do not.

# Living in Myrtle Beach year-round: the honest pros and cons.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Living in Myrtle Beach, from people who live here: the two costs that are new, the weather season by season, and a beach town after the visitors go home.

The short answer

## Is Myrtle Beach a good place to live?
It depends what you want from a place. A home costs less here, the winters are mild, and you are near the water. You give up walkability, higher pay, and some big city services. Our page on why so many people are moving to Myrtle Beach has the growth numbers.
“Life down here is different. It is relaxing and a little fast paced at the same time. Yes, it is cheaper, but depending on where you are coming from, some things will feel like a real upgrade and some things may make you reconsider. We want to sell you a home, but this is a small town. We want to run into you at the grocery store and hear that you are happy here, not that you regret the move, so tell us what you want, and we will tell you honestly whether it is here.”
What Tim Nash, our Broker-in-Charge, tells every relocation client in the first ten minutes.

The pros and the cons, split into two lists so you can scan them.

### Pros of living in Myrtle Beach
+ A typical home costs about $342,000, well under most of the Northeast
+ Mild winters. January highs average the mid 50s
+ Sixty miles of beach, and the ocean is swimmable from June into October
+ No state tax on Social Security, and none on military retirement pay
+ Property tax on a main home is low. Only 4 percent of the value is assessed, so a $350,000 house is taxed around $1,300 a year
+ Sunnier than the northern cities most people leave
+ Traffic is light compared with any large metro
+ Golf carts are a real way to get around in many neighborhoods

### Cons of living in Myrtle Beach
&minus; You cannot walk to much. This is a driving area
&minus; Pay is lower than in a northern metro
&minus; Summers are hot and humid, with about 22 days a year over 90 degrees
&minus; Hurricane season runs June to November
&minus; Insurance costs more on the oceanfront, though it drops inland
&minus; Your car is taxed every year, which is new for most movers
&minus; More mosquitoes than a dense city
&minus; Some specialist medical care means a drive to Charleston

Money

## What it costs to live in Myrtle Beach
Housing is where you gain. A typical home here costs about $342,000. The same measure is about $737,000 in the New York area, $742,000 in Boston and $580,000 in Washington. Rent is about 17 percent below the national average.
Everything else is closer to normal. Food, power and everyday items sit near the national average, so do not plan on the grocery bill falling. Pay is lower here too , which matters if you are still working.
Two costs are new. South Carolina taxes your car every year, which most northern states do not, and a second home is taxed at about three times the rate of a main home. Both are covered on our cost of living page , which compares your city with this one directly.

Weather

## What the weather is like

### Winters are mild
January averages a high near 56 and a low in the mid 30s. Snow is rare: about an inch a year on average, and most years get none. Two recent winters each produced a 5 inch storm, and the record is 14 inches from a Christmas storm in 1989. When it does snow, roads and schools close for a day or two, because there is no reason to own plows here.

### Summers are hot and humid
July averages a high near 87 and a low near 72. The area gets about 22 days a year at or above 90 degrees and almost none at 100, so the raw temperature is not extreme. The humidity is what people feel. Most newcomers say they adjust within a season or two.

### It is brighter than most places people leave
The nearest long term weather station records about 62 percent of possible sunshine and 111 clear days a year. Pittsburgh averages about 42 percent, Buffalo about 47 percent, and Cleveland about 66 clear days. People from those cities notice it in the first month. The month by month numbers, including ocean water temperatures, are on our weather page .

Storms

## Do hurricanes destroy houses in Myrtle Beach?
Hurricanes reach this coast and they do damage property. The last storm to flatten a large part of it was Hugo in 1989, more than 35 years ago. Since then the Grand Strand has taken a direct Category 1 landfall at Georgetown, a close pass from a Category 1, and a string of tropical storms. Those destroyed piers and dunes. They did not level the towns.
Water damaged the most houses, and it was inland. When Florence came ashore in North Carolina in 2018, the wind here was survivable. Days later the Waccamaw River crested at a record 21 feet and flooded around a thousand homes and businesses near Conway and Socastee, miles from the ocean. Matthew did a smaller version two years earlier.
Homes built to the current coastal wind code are engineered for higher wind loads than older stock, which is part of why insurers price them differently. That is a construction standard, not a guarantee for any particular storm or any particular house. What decides the risk is the address: the year it was built, when the roof was last replaced, its flood zone, and whether it has flooded before. A Zone X designation is not proof that it has not.
Every storm since Hugo is listed, one by one, with what each did, on our hurricane history page . We wrote up how to pull a property's real flood history on how to find out if a house flooded . Insurance is higher on the oceanfront and drops as you move inland, and the coastal insurance page explains what drives a quote.
Send us an address and we will pull its flood history before you offer.
Have us check an address Call 854.333.2135

Getting around

## It is a golf cart area, not a walking city
This is the complaint we hear most from people who moved from a real city, and it is fair. Outside a few pockets you cannot walk to a grocery store, and there is no transit network worth planning a life around. What the area has instead is golf carts. Large parts of the Grand Strand are built around them, and in many neighborhoods that is how people get to the beach, dinner and a neighbor's house.
There are rules. A cart needs a state permit, the driver needs a license and insurance, and it can only run on roads posted 35 mph or less, within four miles of the address on the permit. For any house, check the speed limits between that house and where you want to go. A 45 mph road you cannot drive along ends the trip. The rules by town are on our moving checklist .

Traffic

## Traffic is lighter than newcomers expect
Summer brings visitors, and it still does not compare with a big city commute. Rush hour typically adds five to ten minutes. Leaving between 5 and 8 in the morning gets you most places without a real stop.
Which road you take matters more than the season. US-17 Business runs through stop lights end to end. SC-31 and SC-22 are limited access and usually faster even when the mileage is longer. Locals default to the highways and visitors do not, which is most of the difference.
For scale, the busiest road in the county carries about 82,000 vehicles a day averaged across the year, and the Long Island Expressway carries about 210,000. Off peak, North Myrtle Beach is about 30 minutes from Myrtle Beach, Surfside about 15, Murrells Inlet about 25, Conway about 25 and Carolina Forest about 20. Wilmington is under two hours, Charleston and Columbia about three.

The off season

## What Myrtle Beach is like in the winter
Quieter, and less different than the reputation suggests. The water parks and some attractions close and some places trim their hours, but the town keeps running. Restaurants, shops and the boardwalk stay open, and from about October to April everything is easier to get into.
Locals use the off season. In the City of Myrtle Beach, dogs are allowed on the beach at any hour from the day after Labor Day through April 30. In summer they are limited to before 10 a.m. and after 5 p.m., and each town sets its own hours. Golf courses, restaurants and spas run off season rates, hotel rooms sell well below summer prices, and there is no line for any of it. Several of our clients say the off season is the reason they stayed: the vacation attractions spend the winter serving the people who live here.

Where you buy matters

## Know whether you are buying in a visitor area or a year-round one
The Grand Strand is two housing markets sitting next to each other. Some streets are mostly short-term rentals, close to the beach, busy in summer and quiet in January. Others are ordinary year-round neighborhoods where the same cars are in the same driveways in February.
Neither is better. They suit different plans. If you are buying an investment property, rental activity near the beach is the point, and our short-term rental rules page covers where it is allowed.
Rental activity is a matter of public record rather than opinion. Short-term rental permits are filed with the municipality, and an association's rental cap and minimum lease term are written into its covenants. Ask us for the covenants and the permit records on any address and read them yourself.
We will pull the covenants and permit records on any address you are considering.
Get the documents Call 854.333.2135

If you run a business

## You cannot charge northern prices here
Business owners who move down repeatedly find they have to cut their rates. That is not a local quirk, it is the same fact that made the housing cheap: prices and wages across this market are lower than in a northern metro, so the going rate for your work is lower too. If your plan depends on keeping your old prices, price your service against local competitors before you count on the income. Plenty of people make the trade happily, because the lower cost of living absorbs it. It is only a problem when nobody warned you.

Healthcare

## What medical care is here, and what is a drive
Better covered than most areas this size, and expanding. Grand Strand Medical Center in Myrtle Beach has 403 beds and is a verified adult Level I trauma center, so the most serious adult emergencies are treated here rather than transferred. Conway Medical Center has 222 beds, McLeod Health Seacoast in Little River 155, Tidelands Waccamaw in Murrells Inlet 124, Tidelands Georgetown 131 and McLeod Health Loris 50.
McLeod held a ribbon cutting for its new 48-bed hospital in Carolina Forest in August 2026. Two more hospitals are under construction . One is a 59-bed Grand Strand Health hospital on the US-17 Bypass, expected in late 2027. The other is a 36-bed Tidelands hospital with MUSC at the SC-31 and SC-707 interchange, expected in late 2028. Bed counts and timelines come from each health system.
What is not here is Level I pediatric trauma and organ transplant. Both are at MUSC in Charleston, about two hours south, and some specialist care follows the same pattern. For veterans, the Myrtle Beach VA clinic is outpatient only and the nearest VA medical center is also in Charleston.

Small stuff that is not small

## Bugs, and the rest of coastal life
Mosquitoes are more noticeable than in a dense city, because much of the county is low, wet and rural. Horry County runs a mosquito control program with truck and aerial spraying that starts in early May, and residents outside city limits can request treatment. Near marsh you also meet biting midges, which everyone here calls no-see-ums. They are small enough to pass through a standard screen, so a finer mesh and a fan on the porch do more than repellent. The big outdoor bugs locals call palmetto bugs live in trees and mulch, not inside houses, and one wanders indoors now and then. None of this is a reason not to move. All of it is a reason to budget for pest control and look at the screens.

Common questions

## Living in Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach a good place to live?
It depends what you want from a place. Housing costs less than most of the Northeast, winters are mild, and you are near the water. You give up walkability, higher pay and some big city services. Summers are hot and humid, and hurricane season runs June to November.

### What are the biggest downsides of living in Myrtle Beach?
You cannot walk to much, so you drive everywhere. Pay is lower than in a northern metro. Summers are humid. Your car is taxed every year, which is new for most movers. Insurance costs more on the oceanfront, though it drops as you move inland.

### Do hurricanes destroy houses in Myrtle Beach?
Hurricanes reach this coast and they do damage property. The last storm to flatten a large part of the Grand Strand was Hugo in 1989, and since then the worst losses have come from river flooding inland rather than wind on the beach. Risk is decided by the address, not the region: ask what year the house was built, when the roof was last replaced, its flood zone, and whether it has flooded before.

### How bad is summer traffic in Myrtle Beach?
Lighter than newcomers from a large metro expect. Rush hour typically adds five to ten minutes. Which road you take matters more than the season: US-17 Business runs through stop lights, while SC-31 and SC-22 are limited access and usually faster even when the mileage is longer.

### Does it snow in Myrtle Beach?
Rarely. The average is about an inch a year and most years get none. Two recent winters each produced a 5 inch storm, and the record is 14 inches from a Christmas storm in 1989. When it does snow, roads and schools close for a day or two.

### What is Myrtle Beach like in the winter?
Quieter, and less different than people expect. The water parks and some attractions close and some places trim their hours, but the town keeps running. From about October to April everything is easier to get into.

# Moving to Myrtle Beach: your first 45 days.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
The moving checklist for your first 45 days in Myrtle Beach: the DMV steps, the $250 fee per car, the property tax application due May 31, and utilities by address.

The direct answer

## The whole move, on one screen
Each step links to its details.
1 Pack the paperwork One folder: identity, Social Security number, two address proofs. Details 2 Switch your auto insurance To a South Carolina insurer, before any office visit. Details 3 County: pay each vehicle's tax The Auditor writes the bill, the Treasurer takes payment. Details 4 DMV: license and plates About $305 per car. 45 days from the move. ### The three deadlines that cost money if you miss them
First, 45 days from the day you move to get a South Carolina driver's license and to register every vehicle you own. The DMV charges about $305 per car, and the county charges its annual vehicle tax before the DMV will hand you a plate. Second, the 4 percent legal residence application for your new home, which Horry County wants by May 31; without it your first property tax bill is calculated at the 6 percent second-home rate. Third, voter registration, which closes 30 days before any election.
One of our team moved here from Ohio three years ago, missed the 45 day license window, and did not learn about the free resident beach parking until his second year. This is the checklist he wishes someone had handed him.

Before the truck leaves

## What to bring, because the DMV will ask for it
Every step below asks for the same short stack of paper. Pack it in the car, not the moving truck. If you have children, school registration has its own list, on our page on school zones and registration .
Proof of who you are a certified birth certificate or an unexpired U.S. passport.
Your Social Security number. The DMV checks it electronically; the card itself is not required, but the number is.
Two proofs of your new South Carolina address, from two different organizations, dated within nine months : a lease or closing statement, a utility bill or approved application for service, a bank statement, an insurance bill, a pay stub, or the Postal Service change-of-address confirmation. One proof gets you a standard license; two get you a REAL ID at the same price.
Your out-of-state driver's license. You surrender it.
The name of an auto insurer licensed in South Carolina. Switch your policy before the DMV visit; the county wants it too.
For each vehicle the current out-of-state registration or title, and the lienholder's name if there is a loan.
If married your spouse's license and registration will be needed for the property tax application later, even if the house is in one name.

Week one

## Insurance, then the county, then the DMV: the order matters
South Carolina charges an annual property tax on cars, paid a year in advance to the county, and the DMV will not register a vehicle until it is paid. The sequence is fixed. Get South Carolina auto insurance. Take each vehicle's registration or title and proof of your Horry County address to the county Auditor, who writes the vehicle tax notice. Pay it at the county Treasurer. Take the paid receipt to the DMV.
In Myrtle Beach the county Auditor and Treasurer are at 1201 21st Avenue North and the DMV branch is at 1200 21st Avenue North, across the street. In Little River the county office and the DMV share 107 Highway 57 North. Conway has the county offices at 1301 Second Avenue and the DMV at 4103 Highway 701 North. Offices run weekdays; the DMV opens at 8:30 and at 9:30 on Wednesdays. There is no DMV branch in Surfside, Socastee, or Carolina Forest.

### What each vehicle costs
At the DMV: a one-time $250 infrastructure maintenance fee, a $15 title fee, and $40 for a plate and registration that lasts two years. That is $305 per standard passenger vehicle. The $250 fee is South Carolina's version of vehicle sales tax, and you pay it once, on arrival, in place of tax on a car you already own. Owners 65 and older pay $36 for the plate instead of $40.
At the county: the vehicle tax, which New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ohio do not charge and which surprises almost everyone who arrives from them. It is not only cars: the county also bills boats and campers every year, so count them when you budget. Vehicles are assessed at 6 percent of value and then taxed at the local millage, and it comes due every year with the plate renewal. Horry County publishes a vehicle tax estimator on its vehicle tax page. A high-mileage discount exists, but only in the month the tax is due, so ask the Auditor about it at the counter.

### The license itself
Same visit if you brought the paperwork above. An eight-year license is $25. Expect a vision test; if your old license has been expired nine months or more, expect the knowledge and road tests too. Military members and students living here temporarily can keep their home-state license.
Buying before you move? We can time the closing around these dates.
