The one that saves the most

## File the 4 percent legal residence application by May 31
This is general information, not tax or legal advice. Deadlines and required documents change. Confirm your own situation with the Horry County Auditor or a tax professional before you rely on any of it.
Horry County taxes an owner-occupied home at a 4 percent assessment and everything else at 6 percent, and the 4 percent rate also removes the school operating tax. On the same house the difference is roughly three to one. Nobody applies for you. Our Horry County property tax rates page has the calculator and the full explanation. This section covers the deadline and the documents.
Apply online through the county's tax-payer services page. It asks for three things. A South Carolina driver's license or state ID for every owner-occupant and their spouse, showing the new address. South Carolina registration for every vehicle you own, showing the new address. Redacted copies of your most recent federal and state income tax returns, or an SSA-1099. If you still own a home in another state, you also send that county's tax bill showing no owner-occupied exemption there. That is why the license and registration come first: they are attachments to this form.
Horry County asks for the application by May 31 so the bill mailed in the fall prints at 4 percent. File later and you can still qualify for that year, but you will be dealing with a corrected bill or a refund instead of a right bill the first time.

### Homestead exemption at 65: not in year one
South Carolina exempts the first $50,000 of a legal residence's value for owners who are 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind. It requires the 4 percent status and one full year as a South Carolina legal resident as of December 31, so a retiree who moves this year applies for it next year, at the county Auditor.

Utilities

## Who provides what depends on which side of a line you are on
There is no single utility for the Grand Strand. Which company serves your house depends on the address, and neither electric provider publishes a street-level map. The fastest way to find out is to ask the seller for a recent bill or ask the closing attorney. Failing that, call and give them the address.
Provider and who it serves Deposit and fees
Santee Cooper
State-owned. The City of Myrtle Beach and the other coastal municipalities. A deposit set from the two highest consecutive bills at that address, with a floor of $100, refunded after 13 months of on-time payments. A prepaid option costs $70 up front and skips the deposit and credit check.
Horry Electric Cooperative
Member-owned. Most of the unincorporated county, including Carolina Forest, Socastee, Longs, and the rural areas. $35 in one-time fees: a $5 membership, a $10 application and a $20 connection. A deposit only if the credit check calls for one.
Grand Strand Water & Sewer Authority
Water and sewer for most of the coast outside the city limits. A $40 new service fee. Deposits run $40 to $90 for owners and $60 to $140 for tenants, depending on whether you need water, sewer, or both.
City of Myrtle Beach
Water, sewer, sanitation, and stormwater inside the city, on one monthly statement. A deposit set by meter size.
North Myrtle Beach
Water and sewer inside the city. A meter deposit, $180 for the common three-quarter-inch meter, plus a $50 service charge.
Conway
City of Conway. Water and sewer inside the city, and in some areas outside it. Inside the city, a $100 deposit and a $50 service charge. Outside the city, a $150 deposit for water and sewer or $75 for water only, plus the $50 charge. The city sets up service only after the closing.
Georgetown County Water and Sewer District
Pawleys Island and Litchfield, on the Georgetown side. A transfer fee to put the account in your name: $161 for water and sewer if you own, $261 if you rent.

### Electricity
Two providers cover almost all of Horry County. Santee Cooper and Horry Electric Cooperative both run a credit check and may want a deposit. Both want proof you own or rent the place, so have the settlement statement or lease handy.
Know about the demand charge before your first bill arrives. On their published 2026 residential schedules, both Santee Cooper and Horry Electric Cooperative bill a demand charge as well as the power you use. That means part of your bill is set by your single highest hour of use rather than your monthly total. The peak window is 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. from April through October and 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. from November through March. Running several heavy appliances at once inside that window sets a charge that applies to the whole month, so it is worth spreading the load. Our cost of living page has the rates.

### Water and sewer
Grand Strand Water & Sewer Authority asks for 24 hours notice before it turns anything on. Apply on a Friday and you are waiting until Monday, so make this call before the truck arrives, not after. Inside city limits you deal with the city.

### Gas, internet, and the rest
Natural gas is not everywhere. Dominion Energy is the gas utility, but the mains reach only some neighborhoods, so availability is checked address by address. Plenty of homes here are all electric or run propane, which matters if you were planning on a gas range.
For internet, HTC is a member-owned fiber cooperative covering much of the county, with published starting prices around $50 for 500 Mbps and about $75 for a gig. Spectrum is the incumbent cable provider and advertises lower first-year promotional rates that step up afterward. Brightspeed has fiber in parts of the city. Budget roughly $40 to $75 a month depending on the speed you need and whether you are still inside a first-year promotion.

The one nobody warns you about

## Outside the city limits, no truck comes for your trash
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, trash is easy: about $34 a month on the same utility statement as water and sewer. That buys a garbage cart, a recycling cart, and two cubic yards of bulk and yard waste a week, all collected the same day. Carts go out no earlier than 6 p.m. the night before and come in by 11 p.m. on collection day, and that is a code the city enforces. Yard waste has to be in paper bags, not plastic.
In unincorporated Horry County there is no curbside collection at all. The county solid waste authority says so plainly, and nothing starts automatically when you close. You have three options: haul your own to one of the 25 recycling and convenience centers, hire a private hauler, or rely on a neighborhood association contract that covers it. The centers are open to unincorporated residents only and cap you at four cubic yards a day. Ask which of those three applies to the specific address before you close. People move here from cities and discover this on the second weekend.
One more line item: sales tax runs 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach and 8 percent everywhere else in Horry County. Unprepared groceries are taxed at zero either way.

Free beach parking

## The resident parking decal, and who qualifies
The City of Myrtle Beach gives residents a free parking decal that covers every city-owned paid space: the on-street meters and pay stations, the street-end beach accesses, the decal-only areas in The Avenues, and events at the convention center. It does not cover the Pavilion garage or any private lot. What you can do on the sand once you park, town by town, is on our beach rules page . Given that beach access parking runs $3 an hour or $15 for the day in season, it is worth doing in your first month. One of our team lived here more than a year before he learned the decal existed.
Fewer people qualify than assume they do. It is not for all Horry County residents. It is for vehicles that live inside the city limits and on which city vehicle property tax has been paid. The city treats that tax as your parking payment. If you live in Carolina Forest or Socastee or Surfside, you do not qualify, no matter how close you are.
Apply in person the first time, at the parking office in the Pavilion Parking Garage, 914 North Kings Highway, at the Ninth Avenue North entrance; the number is 843-626-7275 and hours are worth a call first. Renewals can be done online. Bring, for each vehicle, your South Carolina registration, your driver's license, and the current Horry County vehicle tax receipt, and note that the address on the license has to match the address on the tax receipt. Golf cart owners bring the state permit number too. The decal runs two years and replacements cost $20.
The other towns work differently and the details do not transfer. North Myrtle Beach has no physical decal at all; enforcement reads your license plate, registration renews every year, and its paid season runs March through October, 9 to 5. Myrtle Beach's paid season is shorter, March through September, but runs 9 a.m. to midnight. North Myrtle Beach does sell a limited number of annual passes to Horry County residents who live outside its limits, but the allocation is small and sells out early in the year, so it is not something to count on.

Getting around

## Golf cart rules, because this is a golf cart town
Many neighborhoods here run on golf carts, and the rules changed in 2025. To drive one on a public road you need four things. A $5 state permit from the DMV, good for five years or until you move. Proof of ownership and liability insurance. A driver who is at least 16 with a valid license. The registration and insurance in the cart. Statewide, a permitted cart may run in daylight, on roads posted 35 mph or less, within four miles of the address on the permit. In a gated community the four miles are measured from the gate. It may cross a faster road at an intersection. Every passenger under 12 must be belted.
Towns can add rules, and three of them have.

- North Myrtle Beach. Sunrise to sunset, on 35 mph roads. Carts may cross Ocean Boulevard, 27th Avenue South, Highway 17 and Sea Mountain Highway, but not drive along them. The fine is $100 and up to 30 days.

- Surfside Beach. Carts with permanently mounted headlights and taillights may run at night. Carts without lights run from 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset.

- City of Myrtle Beach. Daylight hours. No carts on sidewalks or multi-use paths. Ocean Boulevard is closed to carts over Memorial Day weekend.

Outside city limits the state rules apply.
Before you buy in a neighborhood because it is “golf cart friendly,” check the posted speed limits on the roads between the house and wherever you plan to drive. A 45 mph road you cannot cross at an intersection ends the trip.

Once the license is done

## Register to vote, then look up your evacuation and flood zones
Voter registration closes 30 days before an election. You can register online at scvotes.gov once you have a South Carolina license or DMV ID. That is why it comes after the DMV step. The DMV license and golf cart forms also offer to pass your address to the election commission. Horry County's elections office is at 1515 Fourth Avenue in Conway. There is no residency waiting period and no party registration.
While you are on the county sites, look up two things for your new address: your hurricane evacuation zone on the state's Know Your Zone map, and the flood zone on FEMA's map service center. Both matter for insurance and both are on our coastal insurance page , along with what a wind and flood policy costs here. Our hurricane page covers every storm since 1989 and which areas flooded.

Common questions

## Moving to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### How long do I have to get a South Carolina driver's license after moving?
45 days. Third-party DMV sites still say 90, which is out of date. You go to a branch in person with proof of identity, your Social Security number, proof of your South Carolina address, and your old license, which you turn in. An eight-year license is $25 and there is a vision test.

### How much does it cost to register a car in South Carolina as a new resident?
About $305 per vehicle at the DMV: a one-time $250 infrastructure maintenance fee, a $15 title fee, and $40 for the plate and registration, which is good for two years. On top of that you pay the county's annual vehicle property tax before the DMV will issue the plate, and that amount depends on the vehicle's value.

### Why does the DMV send me to the county first?
Because South Carolina charges an annual property tax on vehicles, paid a year in advance, and the DMV will not register a car until it is paid. The county Auditor writes the tax notice, the Treasurer takes the payment, and the DMV needs the paid receipt. In Myrtle Beach the county office and the DMV branch face each other on 21st Avenue North, so it is one trip.

### What is the 4 percent legal residence application and when is it due?
It is the form that gets your primary home taxed at the owner-occupied rate instead of the second-home rate, which is roughly three times higher on the same house. Horry County asks for it by May 31 so your fall bill prints correctly. It requires a South Carolina driver's license and South Carolina vehicle registration for everyone on the deed, so do those first.

### Can I drive a golf cart on the road in Myrtle Beach?
Yes, with a $5 state permit that lasts five years, on roads posted 35 mph or less, within four miles of the address on the permit, in daylight unless the city has a night ordinance. Drivers must be 16 with a license and insurance, and children under 12 must be belted. North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach have their own rules on top of that.

### When can I register to vote in South Carolina?
As soon as you live here, and at least 30 days before any election you want to vote in. Online registration needs a South Carolina driver's license or DMV ID, so it comes after the license step. There is no waiting period and no party registration.

## Myrtle Beach Schools: Zones, Choice, and Registration

Zones, choice programs, and registration

# Schools, for buyers moving to the Grand Strand.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated September 7, 2026
How Horry County school attendance zones are set and changed, the choice and charter options, the application-based academies, and when you qualify for in-state tuition, for buyers moving here.
Ask about a specific address Call 854.333.2135

The direct answer

## How school zones work here
Horry County Schools serves all of Horry County: Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Conway, Carolina Forest, Socastee, Surfside Beach, Little River, Aynor, Loris, and the Horry side of Murrells Inlet. Georgetown County School District serves Pawleys Island, Litchfield, and the Georgetown side of Murrells Inlet. Every address is assigned one elementary, one middle, and one high school.
Horry County publishes an address lookup tool. Georgetown County does not, so you call the district. Both change zones when schools open or fill, so confirm the assignment for the exact address before you write an offer that depends on it.

How we handle this

## Why we do not rate schools
Fair housing law prohibits steering, which means directing a buyer toward or away from an area based on a protected characteristic. Courts have treated an agent's opinions about schools as evidence of that, because phrases like “good schools” and “poor schools” can be used as code for who lives somewhere. That is why we do not rank schools, repeat ratings, or tell you which zone to want.
That is not a dodge. South Carolina publishes a report card for every public school, both districts publish their own data, and the people who can confirm a zone will answer the phone. Everything below is where that information lives and what to ask for. You reach your own conclusion, which is the only one that matters anyway.

Step one

## Check the exact address, not the neighborhood

### Horry County
The district runs an Attendance Zone Lookup that takes a street address and returns the assigned schools. The district's own instruction is to use it if you are new to the area and unsure, and to call the technology helpdesk at 843-488-6825 if questions remain. The tool is address-based, so a house under construction may not return a result until the lot has a posted address.
The district is organized into nine attendance areas: Aynor, Carolina Forest, Conway, Green Sea Floyds, Loris, Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Socastee, and St. James. It publishes a feeder chart showing which elementary schools lead to which middle and high schools, on its Our Schools page.

### Georgetown County
There is no public address lookup. Call the district office at 843-436-7000, or the school serving the area, and ask for the zoned school for that street address. Ask for it by email so you have it in writing. The district groups its schools into four areas, and the one covering Pawleys Island, Litchfield, and the Waccamaw Neck is the Waccamaw group.
One practical note for both districts: buses. Horry County does not transport students across attendance boundaries, and Georgetown County provides bus service to students living more than a mile and a half from their zoned school. If a child is close to a boundary, ask the district's transportation office what that means for your street before you commit.
This comes up in real transactions. One family moved here because their oldest child was starting at Coastal Carolina, and their younger child still needed a school. They knew which zone they wanted, and the houses they liked sat near its edge, some inside it and some not. We checked each address against the district lookup, told them which was which, and gave no opinion on any school. They picked with the full picture, and the younger child enrolled where the family intended. That is the service: not an opinion, a confirmed address.
Looking at a specific house? We will pull the zone with you and get it confirmed.
Ask about an address Call 854.333.2135

What to check

## Zones change, and this area is building schools
Horry County is one of the faster-growing counties in the country and the district builds to keep up. When two elementary schools opened in Carolina Forest, the board redrew the lines for three existing elementary schools and published the list of affected subdivisions by name. That process took roughly four months from first draft to final vote, and the new lines took effect the following August. Another replacement school is in the district's capital plan.
Two things follow. First, the school names in a home's advertisement are not a district record. Agents and websites copy them forward for years without checking. Second, a zone you confirm in March can change for the school year after next. If a specific school assignment is the reason you are buying a particular house, confirm it with the district in writing, and understand you are confirming today's line.

### Capacity affects transfers, not enrollment
Each year Horry County publishes a list of schools at or above 95 percent of designed capacity, which the district calls Category 1 or Red Zone. A student zoned for one of those schools always enrolls there. The designation closes that school to elective transfers from outside its zone, with no exceptions for siblings or hardship. If your plan depends on transferring in, check the current list first. The list is republished every spring on the district's student transfer page.

The official data

## Read the state's report card yourself
South Carolina publishes an annual report card for every public school and district at screportcards.com . Each school's page carries an overall rating on a five-step scale, along with the underlying measures, and the site lets you compare schools and download the raw data files. It is a state publication, its methodology is public, and it is the source both districts point to.

1 Type the school's name in the Search for Your School box, or choose View Report Cards and browse by district.

2 The school's page shows the overall rating on the state's five-step scale, with the measures behind it: academics, student progress, graduation rate, college and career readiness, teacher qualifications, and the school climate surveys.

3 Use Compare Schools to put schools side by side, or open a district to see every school in Horry or Georgetown at once.

4 Report cards refresh each fall, so check the school year printed on the page before you rely on it.

We deliberately do not reprint any school's rating here, including the state's. Repeating a rating in our voice adopts it, and that is the line between giving you information and steering you. Look the schools up, decide what matters to you, and ask the district about anything the report card does not answer.
If you are not sure what to look at, the useful move is to decide first what you need. The district can answer directly on class sizes, a specific special education service, a language, a music or arts program, a sport, distance from the house, bus eligibility, and start times. None of those are on a rating scale. Both districts list every school with contact numbers: Horry County and Georgetown County .

Beyond the zoned school

## Choice programs, transfers, and application windows

### Horry County optional secondary programs
The district runs a set of application-based programs alongside the ten base high schools. They include the Academy for Arts, Science and Technology, the Academy for Technology and Academics, Scholars Academy, Early College High School, and a Middle College at St. James. There is also International Baccalaureate at three high schools, dual-credit programs with Horry-Georgetown Technical College, and technical scholars tracks in fields such as nursing, welding, and cybersecurity. Each publishes its own program guide and admission rubric.
Two mechanics matter to a family moving in. The application runs through the district's student portal in a short window in early May, so a mid-year arrival may be looking at the following year. A student accepted into one of these programs is not classed as a transfer, which means transportation is provided; an ordinary elective transfer gets none. Program details and the application link are on the district's high school programs page.

### Transfers
Horry County accepts in-district transfer applications through June for the following year, approves them one year at a time, provides no transportation, and refuses transfers into schools at or above capacity. Students living in South Carolina but outside Horry County can apply to attend, with tuition set annually from the average per-pupil tax revenue. The figure for the most recent published year was $6,713, handled through the office of student affairs at 843-488-6770.
Georgetown County is different in kind, not degree. Its attendance zones were set under a 1970 federal court order and a later consent decree with the Department of Justice, and the district describes them as inflexible. Transfers are limited to the narrow categories written into district policy, and the application window closes in the spring. Ask the district rather than assuming.

### Georgetown County magnet programs
The district operates five magnet programs from kindergarten through twelfth grade, all in the Carvers Bay area in the western part of the county rather than on the Waccamaw Neck. Any student living in the district may apply, there is no cost, transportation is provided on request, and seats are assigned by a random computerized process among timely applications. The window has typically run in April; confirm the current year with the district.

Other options

## Charter, private, virtual, and home school
Charter schools are tuition-free public schools that operate outside a district's attendance zones, with their own applications and, when demand exceeds seats, a lottery. Several operate in Horry County and more have been approved, so the current roster is worth checking directly rather than trusting a list. South Carolina authorizes charters through statewide authorizers as well as districts; the state Department of Education keeps the charter schools program page with the accredited list.
Private schools are outside both districts and set their own admission timelines, which often close earlier in the year than public registration. South Carolina also runs a scholarship program that puts state funds in an account families can spend on approved education expenses. It has income limits, a participant cap, and a per-student cap, and its rules have changed more than once, so read the current terms on the state's school choice page before counting on it.
Home schooling is legal statewide under three different oversight options, and the state runs a free online public school program for full-time and supplemental courses. Both are described on the same state pages. We have no view on which of these is right for your family; we are listing them so the choice is visible.

Enrolling

## What to bring, and the dates that bind
Horry County enrollment starts with an online pre-enrollment form for any student who was not in a district school at the end of the previous year. It asks you to upload four documents: a parent or guardian identification card, proof of residency, the student's birth certificate, and the student's immunization records. The school then emails you a code to finish the second stage. Registration for the coming year opens well before the school year starts.
Age cutoffs are firm: a child must be five years old by September 1 to enter kindergarten and six by September 1 for first grade. The four-year-old child development program has its own application, requires Horry County residence, and adds a Medicaid card or proof of income to the document list. It assigns seats by priority points and a developmental screening rather than first come first served. Applications completed after mid-July go to a waiting list.
Georgetown County requires online registration for every student and asks for two forms of residency verification for a new student, plus the birth certificate and current immunization record. Returning students need one residency document.
Immunization is worth handling early. South Carolina requires a state certificate, and an out-of-state record usually has to be converted by a South Carolina provider or the health department before a school will accept it. That conversion takes an appointment, so it is a thing to start before the truck arrives rather than the week school opens.

If you have a college student

## In-state tuition takes twelve months
South Carolina charges in-state tuition to students whose family has been domiciled in the state for at least twelve continuous months before the first day of class, and the burden of proving it sits with the student. Moving in August does not make the fall semester in-state. There are exceptions, including one for people employed full time by a South Carolina employer, and each institution applies the state regulation itself. Coastal Carolina University and Horry-Georgetown Technical College both publish their residency pages, and the state Commission on Higher Education publishes the regulation. If a child is close to college age, ask the school's residency officer how your move date lands against their deadline.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach schools FAQ

### How do I find out which school an address is zoned for in Horry County?
Use the district's Attendance Zone Lookup, which takes a street address and returns the assigned elementary, middle, and high school. If the address is new construction it may not return a result until the lot has a posted address. The district's helpdesk at 843-488-6825 answers zone questions, and the school's front office can confirm before you write an offer.

### Do school attendance zones change in Horry County?
Yes, and recently. When two elementary schools opened in Carolina Forest, the district moved the lines for three existing elementary schools and published the list of subdivisions that changed. The rezoning took about four months from first draft to board vote, and the new lines took effect the following August. Never rely on the school names in a home's advertisement, and never assume this year's zone is next year's.

### Which school district serves Pawleys Island and Murrells Inlet?
It depends on the county line. Horry County Schools serves all of Horry County, which includes Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Conway, Carolina Forest, Socastee, Surfside Beach, and the Horry side of Murrells Inlet. Georgetown County School District serves Pawleys Island, Litchfield, and the Georgetown side of Murrells Inlet.

### What documents do I need to register a child for school in Horry County?
Pre-enrollment is online and asks you to upload four things: a parent or guardian identification card, proof of residency, the student's birth certificate, and the student's immunization records. The school then sends a code to finish registration. A child must be five by September 1 for kindergarten and six by September 1 for first grade.

### Can my child attend a school we are not zoned for?
Sometimes. Horry County accepts in-district transfer applications through June, does not provide transportation for elective transfers, and denies transfers into schools at or above capacity. Its optional secondary programs are separate: students accepted there are not transfer students and do get transportation. Georgetown County's zones are set under a federal court order, so its transfers are limited to the narrow categories in district policy.

### Does Chapter3 Realty recommend schools?
No. Fair housing law treats an agent's opinions about schools as a form of steering, and we will not give you a different answer than we would give anyone else. South Carolina publishes a report card for every public school, and both districts publish their own data. This page points you to those sources and to the people who can confirm a zone.

## Moving From New York to Myrtle Beach: The Real Numbers

New York to the Grand Strand

# Moving from New York to Myrtle Beach.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
New York movers pay a 0.38 percent property tax rate and about 17 percent lower prices here, and a Long Island sale often buys a Grand Strand home outright.

The short answer

## What changes when you move
The table compares the two states for the 2026 tax year. Each line is explained below. Our pages on moving from Connecticut and moving from Massachusetts set out the same lines for New England.

New York South Carolina

Rates, brackets and retirement rules come from each state's own department of revenue and statutes for 2026, and the Myrtle Beach property tax uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for an owner-occupied home outside the city limits, with the 4 percent residential ratio, the school operating exemption and the 65 and older homestead exemption. Left out on both sides: federal tax, car taxes, insurance, and any credit that depends on your own return. Where a state rule is too detailed to model we leave it out, and almost every one of those left out would RAISE the bill in the state you are leaving, not lower it: Connecticut's tax recapture, New York's supplemental tax, and the exemption phase-outs in Maryland and Ohio. Three would LOWER it, and we name them: Pennsylvania's tax forgiveness and the Massachusetts senior circuit breaker are low-income credits we do not apply, and Florida caps how fast a homesteaded home's assessed value can rise, so a long-held Florida home's real bill is below our estimate. If one of those is you, your bill in the state you are leaving is lower than we show. Insurance is a separate cost to check on this coast, usually higher here than in the states up north; coming from coastal Florida it is priced address by address, in both directions. The coastal insurance page has the real numbers. Your accountant gives you the final answer, and we will sit down and go through it with you.

Property tax

## Property tax depends on which part of New York you leave

### Long Island, Westchester and Rockland
The drop is large. Those counties carry effective property tax rates of roughly 1.6 percent in Suffolk, 1.7 percent in Nassau, 1.8 percent in Westchester and 2.1 percent in Rockland. Horry County averages about 0.38 percent on a primary home. The federal survey stops counting at $10,000, so the published medians for those counties are floors rather than actual figures. The real median bill in all four is above $10,000. On a comparable house here you are usually looking at a bill in the low thousands.
One client of ours left a house worth about $1 million and a property tax bill over $20,000 a year. They bought a similar sized house here for about $700,000, beachfront in North Myrtle Beach with ocean views, near the restaurants they wanted and near the waterway, because they own a boat and finally wanted to use it. The county bill on the house is about $3,200. Those are one household's rounded numbers, not a promise, but they show the scale of the gap.

### Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx
The math is different in the boroughs. Effective rates are about 0.56 to 0.88 percent, because the city's assessment caps hold assessed values far below market value. That is already close to South Carolina's rates. You still gain on the purchase price. Do not expect a big drop in property tax.

### The 4 percent rate, and why you apply for it
South Carolina assesses a primary home at 4 percent of value and everything else at 6 percent. The 4 percent rate also removes the school operating tax, so the difference on the same house is roughly three to one. You have to apply for it. If you buy here before you sell in New York, or keep the New York house, this is the detail to get right. The property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

Pensions

## How South Carolina taxes a New York pension
New York does not tax New York State and local government pensions, federal pensions or military pensions. There is no dollar cap and no age test. If you retired from a New York school district, a police or fire department, a municipality or the state, New York taxes that pension at zero.
South Carolina treats it differently. Military retirement pay stays fully exempt at any age. A New York government pension is not military pay, so here it counts as ordinary retirement income. The shelter is smaller: a retirement income deduction of up to $3,000 a year before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65. There is also a separate age-65 deduction of up to $15,000 against any income, reduced by whatever retirement deduction you already claimed.
For a large public pension, that can mean paying South Carolina tax on income New York was not taxing at all. The cheaper house and the lower property tax usually outweigh it, but not always. Run the numbers before you move, not after. Social Security is untaxed in both states.
Private pensions, 401(k)s and IRAs compare better. New York's exclusion for that income is capped at $20,000 per person from age 59 and a half, and withdrawals count against that cap. We are not tax advisers, and this is the point to bring one in. We can tell you the housing side precisely.

Two costs that go up

## The car tax and the residency rule

### South Carolina taxes vehicles every year
New York charges a registration fee every two years and no property tax on cars. South Carolina charges a county property tax on every vehicle, every year, at 6 percent of the car's value, and the bill must be paid before your plate will renew. A $30,000 car is taxed roughly $360 a year outside the city limits and closer to $460 inside Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 county road fee. Arriving costs more still: a one-time $250 fee per vehicle, and you have 45 days from your move to register. A two-car household should plan on roughly $500 to $1,000 a year that did not exist in New York, and about $600 in one-time fees. The steps are on our new resident checklist , in order, because the county has to bill you before the DMV will issue a plate.

### New York can keep taxing you after you leave
This is the expensive one when it goes wrong. New York holds that your domicile does not change until you can show, in its words, with clear and convincing evidence that you abandoned it. There is a second test. Even after a genuine move, New York taxes you as a full-year resident if you keep a permanent home there for substantially all of the year and spend 184 days or more in the state.
Keep the Long Island house for the kids and spend half the year visiting, and you can end up filing and paying as a New York resident. If you plan to keep the northern property, or expect to spend much of the year back there, talk to a tax professional before you decide how the year will look. It also affects the 4 percent application here, which asks where you live.

Before you pick a neighborhood

## The mistake we see New York buyers make most
It is not a tax mistake. It is buying into a neighborhood whose rules do not fit how you plan to live. Most homes here are inside an HOA, and the covenants decide how you can use the property. They decide whether a boat or a trailer can park at the house, whether a golf cart can get you anywhere, and whether you can rent the place out. They also decide whether the pool and the social calendar you pictured exist there.
Buyers who skip the documents find out after closing. We read them with you before you offer. Start with our HOA guide and how to read HOA documents .

What the proceeds buy

## What your New York sale buys here
On the federal price index, overall prices here are about 17 percent below the New York metro area, and housing costs about 44 percent below. Utilities land about 31 percent lower, everyday goods about 13 percent lower, and other services about 7 percent lower. Our cost of living calculator uses its own estimate. It prices housing partly from home values and is adjusted to match published cost of living indexes, so it shows a bigger gap for New York, about a third lower. Typical rent is roughly $1,700 a month against about $3,600. The number most people care about is the house: about $339,000 typical here against about $725,000 there, in July 2026.
That means a Nassau or Suffolk sale often pays for a Grand Strand purchase outright. That is why so many buyers here pay cash, and why an offer backed by a strong pre-approval matters if you are financing. What you should not do is assume the whole difference is yours to keep. Insurance is higher, the car tax is new, and the first year is when people overspend. That trade is covered honestly on our pros and cons page .
The proceeds also buy differently town by town. Myrtle Beach on this page includes the towns around it: North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet and Pawleys Island. The same budget buys a different house in each one, and seeing three towns in an afternoon is a normal showing day here, not a special request. The town by town page sets out how they differ.

Common questions

## New York to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### How much cheaper is Myrtle Beach than New York?
Overall prices are about 17 percent lower than the New York metro area on the federal price index, and housing about 44 percent lower. In July 2026 the typical home was about $339,000 here against about $725,000 there. On that federal index, a household earning $95,000 in the New York metro keeps the same standard of living here on about $79,000. Our calculator, which uses its own adjusted estimate, shows a larger saving.

### Will my property taxes go down if I move from New York to South Carolina?
From Long Island, Westchester or Rockland, substantially. Those counties run effective rates of roughly 1.6 to 2.1 percent, against about 0.38 percent in Horry County on a primary home. From Brooklyn, Queens or Staten Island, much less: the boroughs average 0.56 to 0.88 percent because assessment caps hold assessed values well below market, so the gap is far smaller.

### Does South Carolina tax my pension if I move from New York?
Often, yes. New York fully exempts New York State and local government pensions, federal pensions and military pensions, with no cap. South Carolina exempts military retirement fully, but a state or municipal pension from New York becomes taxable here beyond the retirement and age-65 deductions. Social Security is untaxed in both states.

### Do I have to pay tax on my car every year in South Carolina?
Yes, and New York does not do this, so it surprises people. Vehicles are assessed at 6 percent of value at the full local rate, so a $30,000 car is taxed roughly $360 a year outside the city limits. You also pay a one-time $250 fee per vehicle when you first register it here, and you have 45 days from moving to do it.

### Can New York still tax me after I move to South Carolina?
It can, in two situations. New York says your domicile does not change until you can show with clear and convincing evidence that you abandoned it. Separately, even with a genuine domicile change, New York taxes you as a full-year resident if you keep a permanent home there for substantially all of the year and spend 184 days or more in the state. Keeping the old house and visiting family half the year is the common trap. Get advice from a tax professional before you plan your year.

### What is the biggest cost that goes up when moving from New York?
Insurance. A coastal policy here is often homeowners plus wind and hail plus flood, priced separately, with hurricane deductibles set as a percentage of the insured value. Get an insurance quote before you write an offer, because it changes the monthly number more than any other line.

What the sale buys

## What a Charlotte or Raleigh sale buys at the coast
A typical Charlotte home sells for about $389,000 and a typical Raleigh home about $437,000, against about $342,000 here. That is not the gap a New York seller sees , but it usually trades a suburban lot for a coastal one with money left over, and the property tax on it drops at the same time.
Myrtle Beach is the name people search, but the market around it is a set of towns: North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Murrells Inlet, Pawleys Island, Little River and inland Conway, each with its own prices. One of them may fit you better than the city itself, and we would love to show you the ones you have not seen on a weekend trip. What differs between them is laid out town by town .
Because the bills are this close, most North Carolina moves are about the coast itself, or a lifestyle change, not the tax math. The cost of living generally shifts less from North Carolina than from any other state we compare. The cost of living calculator shows whether your city runs more or less than Myrtle Beach and its surrounding areas, in about a minute.

Income tax

## The income tax can move either way, and the line sits near $100,000
North Carolina charges one flat rate on everything past its deduction. South Carolina charges a low rate on the first $30,000 and a higher one above it, with a deduction that shrinks as joint income climbs from $80,000 to $190,000.
We ran the two published schedules side by side for a married couple with no dependents. At $60,000 of income, South Carolina charges about $600 and North Carolina about $1,400. At $100,000 the two states land within a few dollars of each other. Above $100,000, South Carolina charges more, not less.
Dependents and credits move that line, so treat it as the shape of the comparison rather than your bill. A working couple under $100,000 saves a little, a higher earner pays a little more, and nobody should make this move for the income tax alone.

Pensions

## Check which kind of pension you hold before you move
North Carolina fully exempts some older government pensions: state, local and federal retirees who had five years of service before August 12, 1989, and military retirees with twenty years of service. If that is you, this move taxes income that has been tax free. South Carolina exempts military retirement fully at any age, but other government pensions are ordinary retirement income here, sheltered only by the deductions.
Every other retiree does better here. North Carolina taxes private pensions, 401(k)s and IRA withdrawals at the flat rate with no age break at all. South Carolina allows a retirement deduction of up to $3,000 before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65. From 65 there is also an age-65 deduction of up to $15,000, and the retirement deduction counts toward it. Social Security is untaxed in both states.

The rest of the bill

## Groceries, gas, property tax and the car

### Groceries and gas get cheaper
North Carolina puts a 2 percent local tax on groceries. Horry County puts none. Gas costs about 12.5 cents a gallon less here on the two states' published fuel taxes.

### Property tax drops, but modestly
Charlotte and Raleigh both average about 0.69 percent effective. Horry County averages about 0.38 percent on a primary home, and the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. It is a modest improvement, about $700 to $1,000 a year saved on a comparable house. You apply for the primary rate yourself; the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

### The car tax is familiar
North Carolina already taxes vehicles every year with the registration, so this one is not a surprise. The mechanics differ: here the county bills you first and the plate renews after you pay, a car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee at first registration, and you have 45 days from the move. The steps are on the new resident checklist .

### Sales tax goes up
General merchandise is taxed about 7.1 percent combined in North Carolina, against 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach.

Common questions

## North Carolina to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach cheaper than North Carolina?
Close, and it depends on the line. Houses cost less than Charlotte or Raleigh, groceries lose the 2 percent tax, gas is about 12 cents cheaper, and property tax is lower. Income tax is lower only below about $100,000 of joint income. The calculator on our cost of living page runs your exact city.

### Will my property taxes go down if I move from North Carolina to South Carolina?
Yes, on average. Charlotte and Raleigh average about 0.69 percent effective while Horry County averages about 0.38 percent on a primary home, and the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. Expect a saving of about $700 to $1,000 a year on a comparable house, not a windfall.

### Does South Carolina tax my North Carolina pension?
It depends which pension. Military retirement is exempt in both states. Some older North Carolina government pensions are fully exempt there and taxed here past the deductions, so that group should run the numbers first. Private pensions and 401(k)s usually do better here, because South Carolina has retirement deductions and North Carolina has none.

### Is the vehicle tax different in South Carolina?
The idea is the same: both states tax cars yearly with the plate. The mechanics differ here: the county bills you before the plate renews, a car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee, and you have 45 days from the move to register.

### How much do homes cost in Myrtle Beach compared with Charlotte or Raleigh?
A typical home here costs about $342,000, against about $389,000 in the Charlotte area and about $437,000 in the Raleigh area, on the same July 2026 measure.

### Why do so many people move from North Carolina to Myrtle Beach?
On the county's deed records, North Carolina sends more home buyers to Horry County than any other state. The usual reasons are the coast itself, more house for the money than the Charlotte or Raleigh metros, and retirement deductions North Carolina does not offer. The bills are close. The coast is the difference.

Income tax

## You stop paying city income tax
Ohio's state rate is one of the lowest in the country. The bill most Ohio households notice is the layer under it: city income taxes, commonly 1 to 3 percent of wages, and in some places a school district income tax on top of that.
South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere. No city rate, no district rate. For a working household this is the largest single income-tax change in the whole comparison, and it is bigger than the difference between the two state rates.

Retirees

## Retirement income: the clearest win of any state we compare
Ohio taxes pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals at its flat rate. The relief is a retirement credit that tops out at $200 a year, one per return, and ends entirely at $100,000 of income, plus a $50 credit at 65.
South Carolina works from deductions instead: up to $3,000 of retirement income before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65, per person. From 65 an age-65 deduction of up to $15,000 applies against any income, and the retirement deduction counts toward it. Social Security is untaxed in both states. For most retirees the same pension is simply taxed less here, and the property tax on the house drops at the same time.
Retiring here from Ohio? We will run your whole picture.
Have an expert run my retirement math Call 854.333.2135

The other direction

## Two things cost more here, and one of our team hit both

### South Carolina taxes your car every year
Ohio charges a flat registration of roughly $36 plus small local fees, and nothing based on the car's value. Here every vehicle is taxed yearly on its value. A $30,000 car is taxed roughly $360 outside the city limits and closer to $460 inside Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 road fee. The county bill must be paid before the plate renews. Arriving adds a one-time $250 fee per vehicle, with 45 days to register. A two-car household should plan on roughly $500 to $1,000 a year that did not exist in Ohio. The bill for boats and campers works the same way. One of our team arrived from Ohio three years ago, and this tax was the item that surprised him: his first county bill was $325 for the car, plus the one-time $250 fee and the $50 road fee. The steps, in order, are on the new resident checklist .

### Houses and sales tax
A typical home here costs about $339,000. That is against about $248,000 in the Cleveland area, about $305,000 around Cincinnati and about $326,000 around Columbus, in July 2026. The purchase itself is a step up for many Ohio buyers, even though the tax rate on it is far lower. The figure is the Myrtle Beach metro; the towns around it price differently. If you are coming from a small town, you do not have to buy in a resort city. Conway, Longs, Aynor and Little River are all within a short drive of the beach. We are glad to show them next to the beachfront so you can compare. The which town page compares all of them properly. Sales tax runs 8 percent in the county and 9 percent in the city, against about 7.3 percent combined in Ohio. Groceries are untaxed in both.

If you keep a foot in Ohio

## Ohio has a residency test with real teeth
Ohio presumes you are still a resident until you show otherwise, and its test is specific. You cannot hold an Ohio driver's license at any point in a year you claim to be gone. Ohio counts your nights in Ohio. A night counts when you are away overnight from your home outside Ohio and in Ohio for part of both days. At 213 or more in a year, the presumption that you have left no longer applies. The non-residency statement has a hard deadline: filed by October 15 of the following year, it makes your non-resident status final; missed, Ohio presumes you never left.
If the plan is a clean move, surrender the license early and the rest follows. If the plan is a winter here and a summer there, bring in a CPA before you set up the year, not after.

## What surprised one of our team after the move
One of our team moved here from Pleasant City, a village of about 400 people in Guernsey County, Ohio. Three years in, three things stand out to him. The county vehicle bill, which Ohio never sends; the numbers are further up this page. Needing sunglasses: he never owned a pair that mattered in Ohio and reaches for them daily here in summer. The work: coming from a village of 400, the range of jobs here felt like a big city's.

Common questions

## Ohio to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach cheaper than Ohio?
Mostly, not entirely. You stop paying local income tax, gas costs about 10 cents less, and property tax rates are far lower. Against that, a typical house costs more than in Cleveland, Columbus or Cincinnati, sales tax is higher, and the yearly car tax is new. The calculator on our cost of living page runs your exact city.

### Do I pay local income tax in Myrtle Beach?
No. South Carolina has no city or school district income tax anywhere. Most Ohio cities charge 1 to 3 percent of wages, so for working households this is usually the biggest single change.

### How is retirement income taxed in South Carolina compared with Ohio?
Ohio taxes pensions and retirement account withdrawals with credits that top out at $200 a year. South Carolina allows a deduction instead: up to $15,000 of income per person from age 65, with the retirement income deduction of up to $10,000 counting against that same $15,000. Social Security is untaxed in both.

### Does South Carolina tax my car every year?
Yes. Vehicles are taxed yearly on value: a $30,000 car is taxed roughly $360 to $460 plus a $50 road fee, and the bill must be paid before the plate renews. Ohio charges a flat fee of roughly $36 to $74. Add a one-time $250 fee per vehicle when you arrive, within 45 days.

### Can Ohio still tax me after I move to South Carolina?
It can if the move is not clean. Holding an Ohio driver's license at any point in the year, spending 213 or more nights in Ohio, or missing the October 15 non-residency statement each keep Ohio's claim alive. The night count does not apply in the year you move. A snowbird split between the two states should bring in a CPA first.

### What surprised one of our team most after moving from Ohio?
The county vehicle bill, which Ohio never sends: every vehicle here is taxed on its value each year. Then two he did not see coming: needing sunglasses daily in summer, and a job market far wider than Pleasant City, the village of about 400 he left.

## 1. Loris: the most land for the money
Around Loris, a big yard is normal. More than 4 in 10 house lots are an acre or more, and the usual lot is about 0.8 acre. Near the beach, lots are closer to a sixth of an acre.
Loris began in 1887 as a railroad depot, and the tracks still run through the middle of downtown. On the third Saturday in October, downtown holds the Bog-Off, with a chicken bog cooking contest, an antique car show and live performances. West of town, Cartwheel Bay Heritage Preserve has a 3.5-mile trail on old roads through longleaf pine, and wild Venus flytraps, pitcher plants and orchids grow along it. It is open dawn to dusk, with no fee.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Outside Loris: houses on wide lots along two country roads, with sheds, gardens and farm fields across the road.

More houses for sale here list parking for an RV or a boat than in any other place on this page. Most list no HOA fee. McLeod Health Loris is the nearest hospital for almost every house.
Houses around Loris sold for about $280,000, half for more and half for less. A house here also costs the least of any place on this page to keep each year. Our list of the most affordable places near Myrtle Beach goes street by street.

Send me houses in Loris

## 2. Aynor: an acre is the usual lot
Around Aynor, the usual house has about an acre of land, and more than half of house lots are an acre or more. Farm fields start at the edge of the town's grid of streets.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Aynor from above: houses on big lots along the town's grid of streets, and farm fields and woods across the highway.

State law names the third Saturday in September "Aynor Harvest Hoe-Down Festival Weekend". The Pilot Club of Aynor started the festival in 1979.

- The trade-off is distance. Aynor is the farthest of these places from the beach, and from a hospital.

Since the 1870s, candidates for county, state and national office have come to Galivants Ferry, just west of Aynor on the Little Pee Dee River, to speak at the Stump. These days they speak from the porch of the Holliday family store, and the crowd eats chicken bog and barbecue, with country and gospel music and clogging.
The river itself runs tea-colored past cypress swamps and sandbars, with a public landing on each side of the US 501 bridge, where people fish for bluegill, redbreast, bass and catfish. In October, Southern Palmetto Farms on Garner Road opens a pumpkin patch and a 6-acre corn maze, with wagon rides.
Expect about $350,000 for a house around Aynor, the middle of the past year's sales.

Send me houses in Aynor

## 3. Longs: where builders are selling
Longs is where builders are selling at the north end. About half the houses sold here in the past year were new, and about half the houses for sale now are new too.
The Waccamaw River runs past Longs through dark water and cypress, and it is the only river that starts in a Carolina bay. At Chris Anderson Landing on SC 9, a sign marks the Waccamaw River Blue Trail.
From Longs you can paddle the Waccamaw River Heritage Preserve, a state preserve along 28 miles of the river where otters and black bears live, and camp on the riverbank on preserve land. Long Bay Club in Longs is one of two Myrtle Beach area golf courses designed by Jack Nicklaus.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
A new subdivision going up beside farm fields in Longs: streets and ponds dug, some houses built or framed, and most lots still empty.

For houses for sale with a Longs address, a new house asks about the same price per square foot as one built three to ten years ago.
A Longs mailing address can be inside North Myrtle Beach. Two of the county's ten busiest new communities, Grande Dunes North and Waterside, have Longs addresses but sit inside the city. This page's Longs is the part outside the city.
Our clients from North Carolina bought land in Longs and had a new house built on it.
In Longs, about $300,000 bought a typical house in the past year. The usual HOA fee is about $100 a month.

Send me houses in Longs

## 4. Little River: old gardens on the waterway, and boat slips
Little River has a county park on the Intracoastal Waterway: Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens, more than 115 acres of forest and marsh with trails and boardwalks. A piece of the original Kings Highway, the colonial road between Boston and Charleston, is still at the front of the park. George Washington rode that road into South Carolina on April 27, 1791, and stopped to eat at the Cochran house in Little River.
Each October, Little River ShrimpFest fills the old waterfront with more than 200 vendors and two music stages; 2026 was its 20th year. Just off the coast is Waties Island, one of the last undeveloped barrier islands in South Carolina. Loggerhead turtles nest on its beach, and a few months later the hatchlings come out of the sand together and run for the water.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Two of Little River's marinas share one basin off the Intracoastal Waterway, with slips sold with their own deed.

Boats are the other draw. About 2 in 3 of the county's boat slips sold with their own deed and tax bill are here. Glen Dornoch Waterway Golf Links, in Little River, is set among live oaks, with views over the marsh and the Intracoastal Waterway.
Little River is not a town, so the county makes the rules. There is no city tax, and trash goes to a private hauler or a county drop-off center.
Half the houses here sold for more than $380,000, and half for less. Nearly every sale was a resale, not a new house.

Send me houses in Little River

## 5. Conway: a river city with its own services
Conway was laid out in 1732, as Kingston. Its older streets of houses under live oaks run down to the Waccamaw River. Locals call those oaks the city's "oldest citizens": from the city's founding, crews built roads around the trees instead of cutting them down, and the town's unofficial slogan is "The trees have the right of way."
Photo: Pubdog
An older house under a live oak, a few blocks from Main Street in Conway.

The Riverwalk is a path along the river with benches and a kayak launch. Riverfront Park beside it has a public boat landing with floating docks. Conway is a city, so it picks up trash at the curb.
Conway has held Riverfest since 1980, on the Saturday before the Fourth of July weekend. In 2026 it brought live music and vendors to Elm Street and the marina, free, and ended with fireworks over the river. Every October, Conway turns into Halloween, SC, a month of decorations and events across the city. Santee Cooper transferred nearly 800 acres, including Lake Busbee, to Conway in 2025, and the city plans new trails, an inland beach and a revitalized Riverwalk there.

- The city tax is high: about $654 a year on each $100,000 of value, against about $368 outside the towns.

- The river reached major flood stage 6 times from 2015 through 2025. The first streets to flood are low ones near Crabtree Swamp, such as Long Avenue and Sherwood Drive. About 95 in 100 homes in the city are outside both FEMA's high-risk zone and the land Florence's water reached.

At about $271,000, a typical house in Conway sold for the least of any place here.

## 6. North Myrtle Beach: most houses for sale near the sand
About 3 in 4 houses for sale in North Myrtle Beach are within a mile of the beach. Ocean Drive has Main Street, McLean Park with its lake, and the Ingram Dunes Nature Preserve, which the city calls its last maritime forest.
From June through September, the city holds free Music on Main concerts every Thursday evening at the Horseshoe on Main Street. At Fat Harold's Beach Club, a DJ plays beach music every night from 7, and couples take shag lessons on Monday nights. Three times a year, for the Society of Stranders, thousands of shag dancers fill the clubs on Main Street.
The state Senate calls North Myrtle Beach the home of the shag, South Carolina's state dance. At Cherry Grove, at the north end, about 680 houses sit on dug channels and the marsh edge. The city's boat ramp there reaches the ocean through Hog Inlet.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Houses on the dug channels at Cherry Grove, at the north end of North Myrtle Beach, from above.

From the city's boat ramp on 53rd Avenue North, you can paddle a kayak about a mile and a half through Hog Inlet, past pelicans and ospreys, to the empty beach on Waties Island. There you can walk the shore looking for shells and fossil shark teeth.
Our clients from New York bought beachfront here near the waterway, so they could finally use their boat.
On the county's tax rolls, about half the houses here are someone's main home. The rest are taxed as second homes or rentals.
Count on about $565,000 for a typical house. About half the houses for sale list no HOA fee.

Send me houses in North Myrtle Beach

## 7. Carolina Forest: the newest homes, almost no flood zone
Half the homes in Carolina Forest were built in 2007 or later, the newest of any place here. Under 1 percent of its houses are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone.
Just north of Carolina Forest, the state's Lewis Ocean Bay Heritage Preserve holds the largest group of Carolina bays in South Carolina, and it is open to the public. Wild Venus flytraps grow there and bloom in early June, and Horry is the only county in South Carolina where they still grow naturally. The preserve also has black bears, bald eagles, red-cockaded woodpeckers and pitcher plants.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Houses on streets that end in cul-de-sacs in Carolina Forest, with woods around them and land being cleared for more on the right.

It is a large planned area of neighborhoods outside the city limits, with a Myrtle Beach address. McLeod Health cut the ribbon on a new hospital here in August 2026. Off River Oaks Drive, the county's Bike and Run Park, which riders call "The Hulk", has 7 miles of mountain bike and running trails on about 70 acres.
Nearly every house for sale in the Carolina Forest ZIP code lists an HOA fee, about $125 a month in a typical listing. Almost none of the houses for sale here are listed as open to nightly rentals.
The middle sale here in the past year was about $440,000.

Send me houses in Carolina Forest

## 8. Myrtle Beach: the shortest drive to everything
From a typical house in Myrtle Beach , the beach, the airport and Coastal Grand Mall are each about 15 minutes or less by car. Pine Lakes Country Club, which opened in 1927, was the city's first golf course.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2026
The Market Common from the air: its homes, outlined, Valor Park and Grand Park beside the shops.

The Market Common is a town center with shops, restaurants and a movie theater, and apartments above the stores. Grand Park and Valor Park are next to the shops, with a lake and a path around it, sports fields and a playground. Our Market Common guide has each neighborhood's homes, prices and HOA fees.
Myrtle Beach State Park, the first state park in South Carolina to open, in 1936, keeps a mile of undeveloped beach with a forest of live oaks and magnolias behind the dunes.
On summer Wednesdays, people bring lawn chairs to Plyler Park on Ocean Boulevard for free live music from 6 to 8, then stay for fireworks at 9. After the summer season, from September to May 1, you can walk a leashed dog or ride a bike on the beach and the boardwalk at any hour.

- A city resident's parking decal costs nothing, and it covers parking at the city's meters and pay stations.

- Nearly every house in the city is outside the zones that allow rentals under 90 days.

Half the houses in the city sold for more than $535,000, and half for less.

## 9. Socastee: a historic village on the waterway
Socastee began in the late 1800s as a lumber and turpentine camp. Its old swing bridge, built in the mid-1930s, carries Dick Pond Road over the Intracoastal Waterway. The bridge, two houses, a store and a pecan grove make up a historic district on the National Register.
The bridge still turns on its pier to let tall boats pass, and the Netflix show Outer Banks booked it on four different days to film a scene. Each April, Socastee holds its Heritage Festival at the Sarvis House on Peachtree Road, next to the bridge, with a classic car show, live music on two stages and food trucks.
South of Socastee, Freewoods Farm is a 40-acre working farm museum run with mules, not tractors, and each November its cane is pressed into syrup in a mule-powered mill.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
The old Socastee swing bridge, the blue steel span, on the Intracoastal Waterway, with the newer highway bridge at the lower left.

A house here costs about what it does in Longs, but Socastee is much closer to the beach and the airport. The beach, the airport and Coastal Grand Mall are each about 15 minutes or less from a typical house.

- About 1 in 9 houses here are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone, more than twice the share in Conway or Myrtle Beach. We check the zone for each house.

That is about $300,000 for a typical house in Socastee.

Send me houses in Socastee

## 10. Surfside Beach: the sand at the end of the street
In Surfside Beach , a typical house is about 3 minutes by car from the sand, the closest of any place here. Every home in the town is less than a mile from Ocean Boulevard, the beach road.
Photo: NOAA National Geodetic Survey
The Surfside Beach pier from the air, with the beach parking lots and the streets of beach houses behind it.

The town's new concrete pier opened in 2024. Walking on it is free, and it has two restaurants, an ice cream shop and a bait shop.
On summer Monday nights, you carry a beach chair down to the sand by the pier and watch fire dancers spin flaming knives, in a free show the town puts on. On one December night, the town runs free trolleys around Surfside Beach to see the Christmas lights, with hot cocoa while you wait in Memorial Park.
The town runs a farmers market in Memorial Park every Tuesday from April to mid-December, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., with local produce, eggs and honey. From mid-September to mid-May, you can surf anywhere on the town's beach from sunup to sundown, except within 300 feet of the pier.
Fewer than half the houses here are taxed as someone's main home. Along the ocean, only about 1 in 8 homes is. On many inland streets, about 7 in 10 are.

- About 3 in 10 houses here are inside FEMA's high-risk flood zone, so we check each one.

At about $705,000, a typical house here sold for the most of any place on this page.

## 11. Garden City: between the ocean and the marsh
Garden City is a strip of beach houses between the ocean and the salt marsh. Its pier is 668 feet long, and in summer bands play every night at both ends, weather permitting. A pier pass covers fishing, with no state fishing license needed on the pier.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Beach houses at Garden City, seen from over the ocean, with the salt marsh and its creeks behind them.

From November through February, the county lets golf carts drive on its beach here, with a state permit and a licensed driver.
From a dock on the marsh, you can tie a chicken neck to a string and pull up blue crabs for dinner, and with three or fewer drop nets, fold-up traps or hand lines you need no license.
Every Fourth of July afternoon, decorated golf carts drive the "wet" parade while people along the route soak them with water guns. At the inlet end of Waccamaw Drive, people go up to the rooftop deck of Gulfstream Cafe to watch the sun set over the water. Parking is free all year at every oceanfront beach access Horry County runs in Garden City.
Houses in Garden City sold for about $406,000 at the middle, about $300,000 less than in Surfside Beach, the next place north.

Send me houses in Garden City

## 12. Murrells Inlet: the creek and the closest hospital
The Murrells Inlet on this page is the part in Georgetown County, south of the county line. Houses on the creek side of Business 17 have docks over the marsh.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Houses on the creek side of Business 17 in Murrells Inlet, with docks reaching out over the marsh edge to the creek.

The MarshWalk is a half-mile wooden boardwalk along the marsh, with restaurants and free live music. A hospital is about 6 minutes from a typical house, the closest of any place here.
The inlet's name for good cooking is older than the MarshWalk: in the 1800s, summer people came by river steamboat, and many of the steamboat cooks stayed. From the day after Thanksgiving to New Year's Eve, every restaurant along the MarshWalk is outlined in lights that play in time to Christmas music, on the hour and the half hour from 5 to 11 p.m.
Since 1983, decorated boats have paraded on July 4 from the south end of Garden City Beach up the creek in front of the MarshWalk. On the creek side stands the Hermitage, where the inlet's well-known ghost story is set. The story goes that Alice Flagg is still seen at the front door in a white dress, looking for the engagement ring her brother threw into the marsh.

- Sales tax here is 7 percent, against 8 percent in Horry County.

The middle sale here was about $610,000. A house here also costs the most of any place on this page to keep each year.

Send me houses in Murrells Inlet

## 13. Pawleys Island and Litchfield: an island town where houses rarely sell
The Town of Pawleys Island is the island itself, a town of its own since 1985. The mainland around it with a Pawleys Island address is county land, and so is Litchfield.
The town says people who come back year after year feel "their blood pressure goes down when they cross the causeway." In 2012, the island house called Liberty Lodge marked 100 years in one family. Islanders tell of the Gray Man, a figure in a long gray coat said to walk the beach before a big hurricane to warn people to leave.
A sea turtle group formed for Pawleys in 1990 walks the beach at dawn every day from May until the last nest hatches. At the town's Fourth of July parade, prizes go to floats, golf carts, decorated houses and docks.
Photo: Phoebe
The north end of Pawleys Island at low tide: houses along the dune line, and the inlet at right.

Near Litchfield, the road into Huntington Beach State Park crosses a causeway between the marsh and a freshwater lake, and more than 300 kinds of birds have been seen in the park.
The island has about 480 houses, and they rarely sell: only 10 changed hands at a market price in the past year. Every island house but one is in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. Across the whole area, about a third of houses are, the highest share on this page.
Across the island, the mainland and Litchfield, the middle sale was about $650,000, and nearly all of those sales were off the island. On the island itself, the middle sale over the last three years was about $2.45 million.

Send me houses in Pawleys Island

## What does a house cost to keep each year besides the mortgage?
For a typical house, about $6,400 to $9,700 a year, as your home and outside the flood zone. That spread is much smaller than the spread in price.
Take two places. A typical house in North Myrtle Beach sold for nearly twice what one in Longs did. Each year it costs only about $140 more to keep.

Tax, as your home $1,100 County fee $89 Insurance $2,000 HOA fee $1,200 Upkeep $3,300 Total a year $7,700

### North Myrtle Beach
Typical house: about $565,000
Tax, as your home $2,530 County fee none Insurance $2,000 HOA fee none Upkeep $3,300 Total a year $7,800

Two things keep the gap small:

- A home you live in is taxed on 4 percent of its value, not 6 percent, and most of the school tax comes off its bill.

- North Myrtle Beach has a low city tax rate, and about half its houses for sale have no HOA fee.

Two things can widen it, and both matter most near the beach:

- Insurance. The cards use about $2,000, the middle that Horry County owners pay for a house; half pay between about $1,300 and $3,000. East of US 17, or of Bypass 17 where it runs farther west, an insurer may leave wind and hail out. You can buy that cover separately.

- Flood insurance. Among Horry County owners who carry a FEMA flood policy on the house they live in, the middle policy costs about $1,070 a year in the A zones. Those are FEMA's high-risk zones where big storm waves are not expected. Outside the high-risk zones it is about $550.

Near the beach, both can apply. A typical Surfside Beach house in the high-risk flood zone, with a $3,000 insurance bill, costs about $10,400 a year to keep instead of $8,300. If you buy with us, we get you an insurance quote for the address before you make an offer.

## What changes when a house is inside city limits?
The tax rate, the trash pickup, the sales tax and the rules for rentals and golf carts. Four of the 13 places are a city or town in full. Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Conway are cities, and Surfside Beach is a town. The City of Loris, the Town of Aynor and the Town of Pawleys Island sit inside places that are mostly county land.

Trash: Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Conway pick it up at the curb, and Loris, Aynor and Surfside Beach offer service too. Renting by the night, place by place:

- Myrtle Beach: most neighborhoods of houses are not zoned for rentals under 90 days.

- North Myrtle Beach: no special zoning or permit, beyond a yearly business license and the lodging taxes.

- Surfside Beach: stays under 30 days only in the zoning districts along the ocean.

- Conway: the code allows them in three downtown districts.

- Outside the towns in Horry County: zoning puts no limit on how long a home is rented.

- Outside the towns in Georgetown County: a tourist home only in the resort residential district, as a conditional use.

Outside the towns, the county's Solid Waste Authority does not collect trash at the curb. Only county residents who live outside the towns may use its 25 drop-off centers. Under state law, a golf cart needs a $5 permit decal and liability insurance, and may use only roads posted 35 mph or less.
A subdivision's recorded rules can bar nightly rentals even where zoning allows them. Our rental rules page has each town's rule in full.

Common questions

## Questions about the towns

### Is it better to live in Myrtle Beach or North Myrtle Beach?
A typical house costs about the same in both: $535,000 in Myrtle Beach and $565,000 in North Myrtle Beach. In North Myrtle Beach it is closer to the beach, but more often in the high-risk flood zone. Myrtle Beach is much closer to the airport, and most of its neighborhoods of houses are not zoned for nightly rentals.

### Does a Myrtle Beach address mean the house is in the city?
Not always. Carolina Forest houses, and many in Socastee, have Myrtle Beach mailing addresses but are outside the city limits. They pay no city tax and get no city trash pickup. We check the city line for any address you send us.

### Where near Myrtle Beach are most houses someone's home all year?
In most of these places, about 3 in 4 houses or more are the owner's main home, taxed at the 4 percent rate. In North Myrtle Beach about half are, and in Surfside Beach fewer than half. The rest are taxed at the 6 percent rate for second homes and rentals.

### Which town near Myrtle Beach has the least crime?
Chapter3 does not rate any town on crime or describe who lives anywhere. Fair housing law bars agents from steering buyers toward or away from an area. We give you the record of the house itself: its flood zone, its tax and the rules for its address.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Jobs and the Economy
Work on the Grand Strand

# Jobs in Myrtle Beach: what the average job pays.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
The average Horry County job paid $50,053 in 2025, against $78,722 nationally. Horry County jobs grew at nearly twice the national rate from 2019 to 2025.
Talk through my move Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## What the local economy is built on
Horry County had 146,055 covered jobs across 12,762 workplaces in 2025.
One job in four is in leisure and hospitality, and that share explains the wage numbers further down. There is no dominant factory and no corporate headquarters here. The largest employer is the school district.
The growth matters as much as the mix. Employers here added jobs at nearly twice the national rate between 2019 and 2025, 9.1 percent against 5.1 percent on the federal wage files. In the Census Bureau's estimates released in March 2026, this metro ranked second in the country for percent growth in the year to July 2025, and the county has added 21.8 percent to its population since 2020. Employers have been hiring to keep up with that growth. That is why arriving buyers find open positions in more fields than in most cities.

Industry Jobs here Share of jobs Average week US average week

Trade, transport and utilities 32,162 22.0% $795 $1,241
