## Why are so many people moving to Myrtle Beach?
The City of Myrtle Beach is in Horry County, South Carolina, and the coast here is called the Grand Strand. People move here for the beach and the water, a short winter, lower house prices and low property tax.

- The beach and the water
The ocean still averages the low 70s in October. Behind the beach towns are the Intracoastal Waterway, the Waccamaw River and the Murrells Inlet marsh, each with public boat landings.

- The winter is short and mild
A January day averages a high of about 56 degrees and a low of about 37. Snow averages about an inch a year, and about two winters in three bring none.

- A house costs less than in most places movers leave
A typical home in Horry County is valued at about $320,000. Around Charlotte it is about $415,000, and on Long Island about $730,000 or more. For a side-by-side with Charleston, see our Myrtle Beach or Charleston comparison .

- The property tax is low
An owner who lives in the home here typically pays about $944 a year. On Long Island the typical bill is $10,000 or more.

The beach in Myrtle Beach in late November, seen from a high floor.

## What do people do in Myrtle Beach?
Downtown, the Boardwalk is about 1.3 miles long, beside the ocean, with a raised wooden walk and a paved path along the sand.
Photo: Tom Long, CC BY-SA 2.0
The beach downtown, by the SkyWheel on the Boardwalk.

Murrells Inlet is known for seafood. Its restaurants grew from the oyster roasts of the inlet's founding families. The MarshWalk there is a half-mile wooden boardwalk on the salt marsh, with restaurants and free live music.
From October through May, anyone with a South Carolina saltwater fishing license may gather oysters and clams on the inlet's public grounds. Parts of the grounds close at times for bacteria.
Photo: Pollinator
Fishing boats tied up in Murrells Inlet.

Inland, Conway's Riverwalk follows the Waccamaw River for about 1.5 miles, with a kayak launch and a public boat landing beside it.
Photo: Pubdog
The Riverwalk in Conway, beside the old riverfront warehouses on the Waccamaw River.

On the Intracoastal Waterway in Carolina Forest, the county's Bike and Run Park has about 7 miles of trails. Huntington Beach State Park, south of Murrells Inlet, has 3 miles of beach and a freshwater lake known for alligators.
Myrtle Beach's first golf course, Pine Lakes, opened in 1927. Anyone who lives or owns a home in Horry County can buy the Myrtle Beach Golf Passport for $72 a year. It gives member rates at the courses that take it.
The off season is quieter, not closed: in our team's experience, only the tourist attractions and water parks close in winter. One mover from Maryland noticed that farm stands and butchers fill the gap the grocery stores leave in organic food.

## Is Myrtle Beach still growing?
Yes. Horry County grew about 22 percent from the 2020 census to the latest estimate. The growth is people moving in: in the latest year, about 39 more people a day arrived from other parts of the country than left.
People living in Horry County, now and projected When people

2020 census about 351,000
Latest estimate about 427,600
2030, projected about 495,000

Census Bureau counts. The 2030 figure is South Carolina's own projection, not a count.
Among the country's metro areas, the Myrtle Beach area, which is all of Horry County, grew the second fastest from mid-2024 to mid-2025. Only Ocala, Florida grew faster.

## Is Myrtle Beach getting overcrowded?
Most of the growth is not in the beach towns. The City of Myrtle Beach itself has about 41,000 people. About three in four Horry County residents live outside any city or town.
About four in five of the people added since 2020 settled outside city limits, in places such as Carolina Forest, Socastee, Murrells Inlet and Little River.
The City of Myrtle Beach and four places outside any city where many of the new homes are. The outlines are the Census Bureau's. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.

Outside city limits is not far from the sand. With no traffic, the beach is about 10 minutes from the middle house in Murrells Inlet, 13 in Socastee, 14 in Little River and 18 in Carolina Forest.

## Where are people moving to Myrtle Beach from?
About six in seven households that move to Horry County come from another state. The South sends the most, then the Northeast.
Households that moved to Horry County in one year, by where they came from Came from, note households

Other South Carolina counties · most from Georgetown County about 2,200
The Midwest about 1,200

IRS counts of households that changed county. The South includes North Carolina, Virginia, Maryland and Florida.
The single county that sends the most is Georgetown County, South Carolina, just to the south, with about 530 households in the latest count. Outside South Carolina, the most come from Suffolk County on Long Island, then Brunswick, Mecklenburg and Wake counties in North Carolina.
Few go back north. For every household that moved from Horry County to Ocean County, New Jersey, about five came from it.
About six in ten Horry County residents were born in another state, against about one in four Americans. About 3 in 10 homes sold here in the last 12 months went to a buyer whose tax bill goes to another state or country.

In most of the out-of-state counties that send the most movers, a typical home is worth more than one here. Sell a typical Suffolk County home and buy a typical one here, and about $410,000 is left before moving costs, sale costs and any loan payoff.
From Ohio and the Pittsburgh area, the reverse is true: a typical home here costs more than one there. Pick your county to see the gap.

## Are there jobs in Myrtle Beach, and what does work pay?
Yes, and the number of jobs grew faster than in the country. Pay is lower, though: the average job here pays about 64 cents for every dollar of the national average.
Jobs and pay in Horry County and the country Where More jobs, 2019 to 2025 Average pay a year
Horry County About 9% About $50,000
United States About 5% About $79,000

Most of our buyers who need work find it within a month or two, in fields from child protective services and stores to welding. That is our clients' experience, not a promise.
Many movers bring their work with them. About half of our clients who come from the northern states arrive with a remote job.
Business owners who move here tell us they cannot charge as much for their services as they did up north. Our jobs page has more on work and pay here.

## How much are taxes and insurance in Myrtle Beach?
Property tax on a home you live in is low here, a fraction of the bill in most of the out-of-state counties movers come from.
The typical yearly property tax bill on a home its owner lives in County tax a year

Suffolk County, NY $10,000 or more
Nassau County, NY $10,000 or more
Orange County, NY $8,494
Ocean County, NJ $6,562
Wake County, NC $3,260
Mecklenburg County, NC $2,890
Brunswick County, NC $1,890
Horry County, SC $944

Census Bureau, the middle bill paid by owners who live in their homes, averaged over five years. The Census table stops at $10,000.
The bills in the chart are what owners pay today. For a house you buy, budget from its price: about $1,470 a year on a $400,000 house you live in outside the city limits. It is about $4,820 if it is a second home or a rental.

### Home insurance costs more than in the rest of the state
Owners of a house in Horry County pay about $2,000 a year for home insurance at the middle, against about $1,400 in the rest of South Carolina.
Flood insurance depends on the street. Outside FEMA's high-risk flood zone, federal rules do not require it, and a policy usually costs about $550 a year. Inside it, your lender requires one, usually about $1,070.
Few houses in Carolina Forest, Conway, Myrtle Beach or Little River are in the high-risk zone: 5 percent or fewer. In Garden City, Surfside Beach and around Pawleys Island, about 3 in 10 are. We get you an insurance quote on a house before you make an offer.

### If you are retired

- South Carolina does not tax Social Security .

- From the year you turn 65, up to $10,000 a year of retirement income is deducted for each person. A second deduction brings the total to $15,000 a person against any income. Military retirement pay is not taxed at all.

- At 65, after a year living in South Carolina, you pay no property tax on the first $50,000 of your home's value. For 2026 only, an owner who already qualified in 2025 gets $75,000.

- South Carolina has no estate tax .

If you may need care later, see our guide to senior living around Myrtle Beach .

### The tax many movers do not expect
South Carolina taxes vehicles every year. One of our team moved here from a village of about 400 in Ohio, and his first vehicle tax bill was $325.
Each car first titled in another state also pays a one-time $250 state fee when you register it here. Owners on active duty in the military, and their spouses and dependents, do not pay it.

## Are people leaving Myrtle Beach, and why?
Some are, but fewer than arrive. In the latest count, about 9,100 households left Horry County and about 15,000 arrived. The top destinations for households that leave Horry County are nearby: Georgetown County, SC, Brunswick County, NC, and Charleston County, SC.
Where the most households went when they left Horry County, in one year Went to, note households

Georgetown County, SC · next door, to the south about 490
Brunswick County, NC · next door, to the north about 220
Charleston County, SC about 220

IRS counts of households that changed county.
Those who leave reported less income: about $55,000 a household on average, against about $83,000 for those who arrived.
Making friends is harder than movers expect, because many people near the city core are tourists or a seasonal population that leaves. Our advice: buy outside the City of Myrtle Beach. Be a regular at places tourists do not go, such as gyms and clubs.
Summers are hot and humid: about 21 days a year reach 90 degrees. Hurricane season is June through November, and across the Atlantic most activity comes between mid-August and mid-October.
Our hurricane page lists the storms that have hit this coast and what each one did.

## Should you move to Myrtle Beach?
The move usually works for people who bring their money or their income with them. It is harder for people who need a local salary like the one they had up north. The rest is on our page on the honest pros and cons of living here year-round .

- If your home is worth more than a typical one here
Selling it can pay for a home here with money left over, before costs. The tool above shows the gap for your county.

- If you live on a pension, Social Security or a remote job
Lower local pay matters less to you, and the retiree tax breaks in the taxes section apply to you.

- If you need a local job
Plan on lower pay than up north, and apply for jobs on your house-hunting visit. One of our clients applied for a child protective services job on a visit and was hired a month later.

- If you want to be outside all winter
A day that stays below freezing from morning to night comes about once in three years. In our team's experience, the Boardwalk stays open all winter.

- If you want big-city night life
In summer, bands play every night at both ends of the Garden City Pier. Our clients from Virginia describe Virginia Beach as much bigger. One put it this way: nobody here parties like Miami, but people here are enjoying their money.

Common questions

## Moving to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach the fastest growing city in America?
No, but it is close. The Myrtle Beach area, which is all of Horry County, grew the second fastest of any metro area from mid-2024 to mid-2025, behind Ocala, Florida. The City of Myrtle Beach itself has about 41,000 people.

### Are people leaving Myrtle Beach?
Some are. In the latest count, about 9,100 households left Horry County and about 15,000 arrived. Most who leave go nearby, to Georgetown or Charleston County in South Carolina or Brunswick County, North Carolina.

### Where do most people moving to Myrtle Beach come from?
About six in seven come from another state, most from the South and the Northeast. The single largest source is Georgetown County, SC. Outside South Carolina, the most come from Suffolk County on Long Island.

### Is it cheaper to live in Myrtle Beach?
Homes and property tax usually cost less than in the out-of-state counties most movers come from. Home insurance costs more than in the rest of South Carolina, and local pay is lower.

### What is winter like in Myrtle Beach?
Short and mild. A January day averages a high of about 56 degrees and a low of about 37, and snow averages about an inch a year.

### Does South Carolina tax Social Security?
No, South Carolina does not tax Social Security. Military retirement pay is not taxed either.

## Myrtle Beach Beach Rules by Town: Dogs, Tents, Parking
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/beaches/
Summary: Beach rules across the Grand Strand, town by town: when dogs are allowed, umbrella and tent limits, parking, the winter golf cart season, and who sets each rule.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Beaches
The sand, practically

# Myrtle Beach beach rules by town: dogs, tents, parking.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Dog hours, tent and umbrella rules, parking and golf carts on the sand, town by town for every Grand Strand beach, before you pick a town.
Ask us about the beaches Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## Same ocean, five sets of rules
The Grand Strand's sand belongs to different governments: the cities of Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach, the towns of Surfside Beach and Pawleys Island, and Horry County for the unincorporated stretches such as most of Garden City. Each writes its own beach rules, and they differ. Where you buy decides which government's rules apply on your everyday beach.
Three rules are the same everywhere: no alcohol, no glass, no fires on the sand, anywhere. Everything else varies, and the two tables below carry the differences that change how you would use the beach: the dog clock and the shade rules. If one of these tables decides your town for you, the town by town page carries prices and the rest.

Dogs

## The dog clock, beach by beach
Every beach here allows dogs most of the year. The difference is summer. The table below states the hours dogs are allowed, in season and off, so you do not have to work it out from the ban times. Leashes are required on all of them, 7 feet or shorter.

Beach In season, dogs allowed The season Off season, dogs allowed

Myrtle Beach Before 10 a.m. and after 5 p.m. May 1 to Labor Day Any hour

North Myrtle Beach Before 10 a.m. and after 4 p.m. May 15 to Labor Day Any hour

Surfside Beach Before 10 a.m. and after 5 p.m. May 1 to Labor Day Any hour

Garden City and other county beaches Before 10 a.m. and after 5 p.m. May 1 to Labor Day Any hour

Pawleys Island Any hour, leashed 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. May 1 to September 30 Any hour, off leash under voice control

Read the last row again if the dog is family. Pawleys Island is the one beach on this coast where a July afternoon with the dog on the sand is legal, and from October to April the town allows dogs off leash under voice control with a leash in hand. Off season, Myrtle Beach opens up too: dogs any hour on the beach and the boardwalk from the day after Labor Day through April 30.
Pick up after the dog everywhere; every jurisdiction requires it and tickets get written. In North Myrtle Beach the timing differs enough to matter: the ban starts May 15 rather than May 1 and ends at 4 rather than 5, an extra hour of summer evening beach.

Shade

## What shade you can put up, and when
This is the rule visitors trip over every summer, and each government writes it differently.

Beach Peak season Rest of the year

Myrtle Beach Round umbrellas only, up to 7.5 feet, Memorial Day through Labor Day Tents up to 12 by 12 allowed

North Myrtle Beach Umbrellas only, 9 foot shade on a pole up to 7 feet 6, May 15 through Labor Day Shading devices allowed

Surfside Beach Canopies up to 10 by 10 allowed, set 10 feet behind the guard stands Same rule year round

Garden City and other county beaches Umbrellas only, up to 7 feet 6, all year; infant cabanas to 4 by 3 by 3 Same rule year round

Pawleys Island No umbrella or tent limit on the town's beach rules page. Nothing may be left on the beach overnight.

Two details save arguments. In Myrtle Beach nothing goes up before 8 a.m. and everything comes off the sand by 7 p.m.; in North Myrtle Beach and on the county beaches, anything left between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m. is removed. On Pawleys Island, anything left on the beach overnight is a risk to nesting turtles, and the town asks that nothing stay. In Surfside Beach a family canopy is legal on a July afternoon. Buyers choose a town on small facts like that.
The rest of the everywhere-rules: holes no deeper than two feet in Myrtle Beach and filled before you leave on every beach, and no fireworks. In North Myrtle Beach, swimmers stay within 50 yards of shore and no deeper than shoulder height. Myrtle Beach runs designated surfing and kayak zones at five street ends in summer between 10 and 5.

Parking and carts

## Who parks free, and the winter cart season

### Parking follows your address
Each government runs its own parking program, and the pattern is simple: residency in the right town is what makes beach parking cheap. The City of Myrtle Beach gives its residents a decal covering city paid spaces, meters and street-end accesses; Surfside Beach issues town decals; North Myrtle Beach posts its rules access by access. If you buy outside the town limits, you are a visitor in the paid zones like everyone else, which is one of the quiet differences between an address inside city limits and one outside them. How to get the decal after you close is on the new resident checklist , and the incorporated-or-not question is explained on the town by town page .

### Golf carts: on the road yes, on the sand only in winter, only in the county
Golf carts with the $5 state permit drive local streets all over the Grand Strand, and many neighborhoods are built around that. The sand is different. The cities keep carts off the beach in every season, but Horry County allows permitted carts with a licensed driver on its unincorporated beaches from November 1 through February 28. The road-permit rules are on the checklist .
On a Saturday in January, in cart season, you put the cooler and the buckets in the cart and drive down onto the sand at Garden City. The beach is empty in both directions, so you pick your spot and stop there. The kids build sandcastles. You eat lunch out of the cooler with the ocean fifty feet away and no one else around. Then you sit and watch the waves for an hour before you drive back up the beach.
Buying near the sand? We will walk the exact access with you.
Ask us about the beaches Call 854.333.2135

Our own guide

## Where we go, by mood
For the social day, the team goes downtown, to the stretch by the boardwalk. Pay about ten dollars to park for the day. You are then next to the music, the bars, the volleyball court that runs all day, and everyone staying in the hotels around you. It is the easiest place on the coast to spend a day talking to people you just met.
For the quiet day, drive to Cherry Grove, as far north as South Carolina goes. Parking is usually free at the accesses, and the walking trails at the Heritage Shores preserve on the marsh side, plus the long walk up the point, lead to stretches of sand most visitors never reach. For the slow day, Surfside Beach calls itself the Family Beach and its town beach runs at that pace: sandcastles, small crowds, short walks from the neighborhood streets behind it.
Two practical notes to finish. The chair and umbrella stands working the sand in front of the hotels are licensed beach services, and renting from them is how you set up without carrying anything. September is the locals' month: the crowds go home, the water stays warm into October, and the weather page shows it month by month.

Living with it

## What this means when you own here
Rules read differently when the beach is your daily walk instead of your vacation week. The summer dog clock stops mattering when your normal beach hour is 7 a.m. before work. The umbrella rules stop mattering in September, which is warmer in the water than June and empty of crowds; the weather page has the ocean temperatures month by month. The flags and rip current basics become second nature the way anyone's home geography does.
Decide which of these five sets of rules fits how your household uses a beach before you buy rather than after. A dog household points one way. A grandchildren-every-July household points another. Tell us which one you are and we will show you the sand along with the house.

Common questions

## Grand Strand beach rules FAQ

### Are dogs allowed on the beach in Myrtle Beach?
Yes. In the City of Myrtle Beach dogs are allowed before 10 a.m. and after 5 p.m. from May 1 through Labor Day, and at any hour the rest of the year, always on a leash of 7 feet or shorter. Each town sets its own clock: North Myrtle Beach allows dogs before 10 a.m. and after 4 p.m. starting May 15, and Pawleys Island allows dogs year round at any hour.

### Which beach near Myrtle Beach allows dogs all day in summer?
Pawleys Island. The town allows dogs on the beach year round with no daytime ban: leashed 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. from May 1 through September 30, and off leash under voice control, leash in hand, from October through April. Every other beach on the Grand Strand runs a midday summer ban.

### Are tents allowed on Myrtle Beach beaches?
Depends on the town and the season. Myrtle Beach allows only round umbrellas up to 7.5 feet from Memorial Day through Labor Day, with tents up to 12 by 12 the rest of the year. North Myrtle Beach is umbrella-only May 15 through Labor Day. Surfside Beach allows canopies up to 10 by 10. County beaches like Garden City are umbrella-only all year. Pawleys Island's beach rules list no tent or umbrella limit, but nothing may be left overnight.

### Is alcohol allowed on the beach in Myrtle Beach?
No. Alcohol and glass are prohibited on every beach on the Grand Strand, and on the county beaches the ban covers the access paths too. Fires, including barbecues, are prohibited, and holes deeper than two feet are not allowed in Myrtle Beach; fill any hole before you leave.

### Can you drive a golf cart on the beach in Myrtle Beach?
Not in the cities. On Horry County's unincorporated beaches, which include stretches of Garden City, permitted golf carts with a licensed driver are allowed on the sand from November 1 through February 28. That winter season is the exception, not the rule, and the cities do not offer one.

### Do you have to pay to park at the beach?
Depends where you live and where you park. The City of Myrtle Beach sells no visitor pass but gives its residents a decal covering city paid spaces. North Myrtle Beach posts its rules at each access. Surfside Beach uses town decals. Where you buy decides which program you are in, so pick your town deliberately.

Rates, brackets and retirement rules come from each state's own department of revenue and statutes for 2026, and the Myrtle Beach property tax uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for an owner-occupied home outside the city limits, with the 4 percent residential ratio, the school operating exemption and the 65 and older homestead exemption. Left out on both sides: federal tax, car taxes, insurance, and any credit that depends on your own return. Where a state rule is too detailed to model we leave it out, and almost every one of those left out would RAISE the bill in the state you are leaving, not lower it: Connecticut's tax recapture, New York's supplemental tax, and the exemption phase-outs in Maryland and Ohio. Three would LOWER it, and we name them: Pennsylvania's tax forgiveness and the Massachusetts senior circuit breaker are low-income credits we do not apply, and Florida caps how fast a homesteaded home's assessed value can rise, so a long-held Florida home's real bill is below our estimate. If one of those is you, your bill in the state you are leaving is lower than we show. Insurance is a separate cost to check on this coast, usually higher here than in the states up north; coming from coastal Florida it is priced address by address, in both directions. The coastal insurance page has the real numbers. Your accountant gives you the final answer, and we will sit down and go through it with you.

Property tax

## The property tax drop, done honestly
This is the number that makes people move. Bergen County averages about 1.89 percent effective. Horry County averages about 0.38 percent on a primary home, and the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. At published rates, a $400,000 owner-occupied home in the unincorporated county bills roughly $1,470 a year. Many New Jersey sellers pay five figures now.

### If you are 65 or older, do the honest version
New Jersey's senior relief exists and it does not travel. The programs many owners hold, including one that pays a large share of the bill outright and a freeze on increases, can take thousands off what you pay. Net them off your real bill before you count the saving, or the comparison flatters the move.
South Carolina's own senior break: at 65, after one year as a resident, the first $50,000 of a primary home's value comes off before tax, with no income test. You apply for the 4 percent primary rate yourself; the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.
You know this pattern from the shore: the famous name is one town on a long coast. It works the same way here. North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City and Murrells Inlet each carry their own prices and their own property tax bills, and the right town for your budget may be one over from the one you searched. Ask us to show you more than one, or start with the town comparison .
Want your real bill against a real house here?
Talk to a local expert Call 854.333.2135

Selling the New Jersey house

## There is no exit tax. There is a prepayment.
If you sell the New Jersey home after you have already become a South Carolina resident, the closing withholds an estimated income tax payment. The amount is the gain taxed at New Jersey's top rate, and never less than 2 percent of the sale price, even with no gain at all. The deed cannot be recorded without it.
The money is not lost. It is an estimated payment, reconciled on your New Jersey non-resident return, and refunded to the extent it exceeds the actual tax. Sell while you are still a New Jersey resident and the withholding generally does not apply. There is also an exemption when the entire gain on a principal residence is excludable under the federal rule.
New Jersey is one of our most common origin states, and the holdback has not stopped a move we have handled: it is either tax already owed or money that comes back. The order of the sale and the move decides which form applies, and that is a conversation for your New Jersey closing attorney, early. We will not advise on the sequencing; we will tell you it matters.

Pensions

## Some New Jersey retirees pay more income tax here, not less
New Jersey excludes up to $100,000 of retirement income for a couple at 62 and older, if total income stays at or below $150,000. That is far more generous than South Carolina's deductions. A retired couple under the cap can pay more state income tax after the move.
The cap is a cliff: one dollar of income above $150,000 and New Jersey's exclusion is gone entirely, while South Carolina's deductions remain. Social Security and military pensions are untaxed in both states. For most households the property tax difference outweighs all of it, but run the income side before you assume it helps.

The rest of the bill

## The car, the clothes, the gas and the estate

### The car tax is new
New Jersey registers cars by weight and never taxes them as property. Horry County does, every year: about $360 on a $30,000 car outside the city limits, closer to $460 inside Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 road fee, and the plate does not renew until the bill is paid. First registration adds a one-time $250 fee per vehicle, due within 45 days of the move, and the county sends the same kind of bill for a boat or camper. The order of the offices is on the new resident checklist .

### Clothing gains a tax, gas loses one
New Jersey exempts clothing; here it is taxed at 8 to 9 percent. Gas costs about 20 cents a gallon less on the two states' published fuel taxes, the largest per-gallon drop of any state we compare except Pennsylvania . Groceries are untaxed in both.

### Estate and inheritance
New Jersey has no estate tax but still taxes inheritances left to some heirs, mainly siblings, nieces, nephews and friends; spouses and children are exempt. South Carolina has neither tax. What that means for your own estate is a question for your attorney, not a page.

Common questions

## New Jersey to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### How much lower are property taxes in Myrtle Beach than New Jersey?
Bergen County averages about 1.89 percent effective; Horry County averages about 0.38 percent on a primary home, and the primary rate removes the school operating tax. At published rates a $400,000 primary home in the unincorporated county bills roughly $1,470 a year. Seniors should first net off New Jersey's relief programs, which do not travel.

### Is there a New Jersey exit tax when you sell your house?
No. It is an estimated tax withheld at closing when the seller is already a non-resident: the gain at the top rate, and never less than 2 percent of the sale price. It is reconciled on the New Jersey non-resident return and refunded to the extent it exceeds the actual tax. Raise the timing with your New Jersey closing attorney early.

### Will South Carolina tax my pension more than New Jersey does?
It can. New Jersey excludes up to $100,000 of retirement income for a couple at 62 and older when total income is $150,000 or less, which beats South Carolina's deductions. Above that cliff New Jersey gives nothing and South Carolina's deductions win. Social Security is untaxed in both.

### Do Stay NJ, the Senior Freeze or ANCHOR transfer to South Carolina?
No. They are New Jersey programs and they end with the move. South Carolina's senior break is different: at 65, after one year of residency, the first $50,000 of a primary home's value is exempt, with no income test.

### How much is the car tax in South Carolina?
It is yearly: about $360 to $460 on a $30,000 car depending on the town, plus a $50 road fee, billed by the county before the plate will renew. Each vehicle also pays a one-time $250 fee at its first South Carolina registration, within 45 days of the move.

### What gets more expensive after leaving New Jersey?
Clothing gains an 8 to 9 percent sales tax, every vehicle picks up the yearly tax, and coastal insurance is usually higher than an inland New Jersey policy. Price an insurance quote early; it is the line that moves a monthly budget most.

What drops

## Property tax, the wage tax and the most expensive gas in the region

### Property tax
A $440,000 home in Montgomery or Bucks County bills about $5,800 to $5,900 a year. The same value in unincorporated Horry County bills roughly $1,600 at the primary rate, which also removes the school operating tax. Philadelphia itself is the exception: its rate is low and its houses cheap, so a rowhouse seller sees a smaller drop. You apply for the primary rate yourself; the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

### The wage tax, if you still work
Nearly every Pennsylvania municipality taxes wages on top of the state rate, and Philadelphia's is about 3.7 percent. South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere. A working Philadelphia household keeps that entire amount. If the move needs a job on this end, say so. We have pointed arriving clients at local employers and openings that fit their background. The move only makes sense if you enjoy your life and job here in South Carolina.

### Gas
Pennsylvania's fuel tax is 57.6 cents a gallon, the highest of any state we compare. South Carolina's is 28.75 cents. That is about 29 cents a gallon, every fill, the largest drop of any move on this site.
Want your Pennsylvania bills against a real house here?
Have an expert run it both ways Call 854.333.2135

Retirees, read this first

## Retirement income tax moves against you here
Most of our Pennsylvania buyers are retirees. That is why this page leads with the one line that moves against them. Pennsylvania taxes no retirement income at all. Pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals after retirement age are simply not taxed, and neither is Social Security. That is rare, and it means a retired Pennsylvanian's state income tax bill is zero.
South Carolina taxes the same income past its deductions: up to $3,000 of retirement income before 65, and from 65 up to $15,000 per person with the retirement deduction counted inside it. A couple also gets a deduction of up to $30,000 that shrinks once income passes $80,000 and is gone at $190,000. For a typical retired couple the resulting bill is small. It is not zero, and Pennsylvania's is.
The income tax is not a reason to move. The property tax, the gas tax and the inheritance tax are, and the house math stands on its own.

The estate

## The inheritance tax, and the part that stays behind
Pennsylvania taxes inheritances from the first dollar: nothing to a spouse, 4.5 percent to children, 12 percent to siblings, 15 percent to others. South Carolina has no estate or inheritance tax at all. For a family passing a home and savings to children, that difference is measured in tens of thousands of dollars.
One part does not move with you. Pennsylvania real estate stays subject to Pennsylvania inheritance tax even after you become a South Carolina resident, so keeping the old house keeps that tax attached to it. What any of this means for your own estate is a conversation for your attorney; we are stating the two states' rules, not advising.

The rest of the bill

## The car, the clothes and the sales tax
Two smaller lines move against you. South Carolina taxes every vehicle on its value each year, roughly $360 to $460 on a $30,000 car plus a $50 road fee, where Pennsylvania charges a flat registration. Count on a one-time $250 fee per vehicle on arrival and a 45 day window to register. Clothing, which Pennsylvania never taxes, carries the full 8 to 9 percent sales tax here. Deadlines and office addresses are on the new resident checklist .
Before you shop, look at the map. Myrtle Beach in a search box covers the whole run of towns around it, and several are smaller and quieter than the city: Surfside Beach, Pawleys Island, Litchfield, Little River. Prices differ town to town, plenty of buyers who searched Myrtle Beach end up buying in one of them, and we are glad to show you several in a day. The which town page maps the differences first.

Common questions

## Pennsylvania to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Do retirees pay more income tax in South Carolina than in Pennsylvania?
Usually a little, yes. Pennsylvania taxes no retirement income at all. South Carolina taxes it past a deduction of up to $15,000 per person from 65, with the retirement deduction counted inside it. For most retired couples the bill is small, but it is new, and the honest reasons to move are property tax, gas and the inheritance tax.

### How much lower is property tax in Myrtle Beach than the Philadelphia suburbs?
A $440,000 home in Montgomery or Bucks County bills about $5,800 to $5,900 a year. The same value in unincorporated Horry County bills roughly $1,600 at the primary rate. Philadelphia itself is the exception; its rate is low and the drop is smaller.

### Does moving to South Carolina end the Pennsylvania inheritance tax?
Mostly. South Carolina has no estate or inheritance tax. But Pennsylvania real estate stays subject to Pennsylvania inheritance tax even after you move, so keeping the old house keeps that tax on it. Your attorney owns this question.

### Does the Philadelphia wage tax follow me?
No. It ends with Philadelphia residency and employment, and South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere to replace it.

### Is there a car tax in South Carolina?
Yes. South Carolina bills every vehicle yearly on its value, where Pennsylvania charges only a flat registration. Budget roughly $400 to $500 a year on a mid priced car once the $50 road fee is counted, plus a one-time $250 fee when it first gets South Carolina plates, with a 45 day deadline after the move.

### What costs less in Myrtle Beach than in Pennsylvania?
Gas by about 29 cents a gallon, property tax by roughly two thirds on a comparable suburban home, and there is no wage tax and no inheritance tax. Clothing and general sales tax cost more, and the car tax is new.

## Moving From Florida to Myrtle Beach: What You Gain

Florida to the Grand Strand

# Moving from Florida to Myrtle Beach.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Florida movers find a typical Myrtle Beach home about $36,000 below the Florida statewide price and home insurance averaging $4,472 against $6,504. The house, the town, insurance and taxes, compared.
Talk to a local expert Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## What Florida movers gain here
A typical home here cost about $342,000 in July 2026. The Florida statewide typical was about $378,000, and the large coastal metros cost more: about $478,000 around Miami and Fort Lauderdale, about $554,000 around Naples. Day-to-day prices in the Myrtle Beach area are about nine index points below the Florida average. The airport has ten airlines and more than 50 nonstop routes. Six hospitals serve the area, including the adult Level I trauma center. The local count puts golf at around 80 courses.
The reasons Florida movers give are clear: the homeowners insurance renewal, a condo special assessment, prices that rose faster than pay, and overcrowding.
Insurance is lower here on average. For the same $300,000 of coverage, a Myrtle Beach policy averages about $4,500 a year against about $6,500 across Florida, and the gap is much wider if you are coming from South Florida or the Gulf coast. The insurance section has the figure for your metro.

Halfbacks

## Halfway back: why Florida movers choose the Carolinas
A halfback is a person who moved from the Northeast or Midwest to Florida and later moved halfway back, to the Carolinas, Georgia or Tennessee. They want to keep a mild winter and the ocean, pay less to own a home, and live closer to family up north. Florida stopped being what they wanted, so they moved to a state between Florida and home.
In a national count of 2025 moves, South Carolina gained more residents 65 and older than any state, about 5,400 net. Nearly 1,900 of them came from Florida, more than from any state except North Carolina. Most people moving into the Myrtle Beach area still come from the Northeast, so a Floridian who grew up in New York or New Jersey will meet neighbors who grew up where they did.
From here, the mid-Atlantic is one day of driving instead of two. Most Northeast cities are one nonstop flight. Grandchildren can visit in either direction without a connecting flight. Winter stays warm enough to golf year-round. If you are moving for retirement, the retiring here page covers what changes in a purchase after 65.

The biggest number

## What a Florida sale buys at the coast
Your own metro matters more than the Florida statewide number. In the July 2026 price data, a typical home cost about $478,000 in the Miami and Fort Lauderdale metro, about $554,000 around Naples, and about $404,000 around Sarasota and Bradenton. A typical home around Orlando cost about $387,000 and around Tampa about $362,000, against about $342,000 here. Sell in one of the higher markets and $342,000 here buys a comparable house with money left over, or the same house with a smaller loan. Sell around Tampa or Orlando and prices are close to ours. Sell in an inland market like Ocala, where a typical home cost about $273,000, and homes here cost more. Send us your address and we will price your own metro against the Grand Strand before you plan around it.
The difference can become a smaller loan, a bigger house, or savings. Prices differ by town here, and several towns around Myrtle Beach are smaller and quieter than Myrtle Beach itself. The which town page compares them before you book a trip.

The town

## Can I live in a smaller town and keep the hospitals and the airport?
Many Florida movers want a smaller town without losing a major airport and major hospitals. This area has both. The name Myrtle Beach covers a group of separate towns, and several are much quieter than the name suggests: Surfside Beach, Pawleys Island, Litchfield, Little River, Murrells Inlet. Each has its own price range. Many buyers who start out searching for Myrtle Beach buy in one of these towns instead.
Getting back to Florida for family is one flight, and the getting around page lists the airlines and the routes. The healthcare page lists each hospital with its bed count and address. Two more hospitals are under construction, and a third held its ribbon cutting in August 2026.
On the county's unincorporated beaches you can drive a golf cart on the sand from November 1 through February 28, and the beach rules page has the dog hours and umbrella rules town by town. Summers here are hot, like Florida's. Autumn and winter are cooler than Florida's, and winter is cool enough for a jacket. The weather page has the numbers season by season, including the ocean temperature month by month.

Daily costs

## Are groceries, gas and power cheaper than in Florida?
Most daily costs are lower here. Groceries cost less than the Florida average and are untaxed in both states. The gas tax is about 11 cents a gallon lower, on top of the price difference at the pump. The typical electric bill is a few dollars a month lower. These numbers come from the same price data behind our cost of living calculator , which compares your own metro against the Grand Strand.
One cost is higher here: the general sales tax is 8 percent in unincorporated Horry County and 9 percent in the City of Myrtle Beach, against roughly 7 percent average combined in Florida.

### Income
You start paying a state income tax. A working couple on $120,000 of wages pays about $4,300 a year here that Florida never charged. Retirees pay less. Social Security stays untaxed, and at 65 and older South Carolina deducts up to $15,000 of income per person. Any retirement income deduction counts toward that $15,000. That typically leaves a couple receiving $60,000 of pension and $30,000 of Social Security owing nothing. A couple taking $100,000 or more a year from IRAs will owe income tax here, and the calculator above shows the figure. Military retirement is untaxed in both states.

### The house
The property tax is lower here: roughly $1,390 a year on a $378,000 primary home in unincorporated Horry County against about $2,900 at Florida's average rate on a new purchase. One warning for long-time owners: your current Florida bill is probably lower than that average because of the cap on assessed value. That protection ends when you sell no matter where you go next, so compare your actual bill instead of the average. The cap's benefit can move to another Florida homestead but not across the state line. At 65 and older, after a year of residency here, a homestead exemption takes the first $50,000 of value off the bill. The property tax page has the calculator and the application deadline.

### The car and the estate
The car tax is the one new bill. South Carolina taxes every vehicle yearly on its value, roughly $360 to $460 on a $30,000 car plus a $50 road fee. Each vehicle also pays a one-time $250 fee, and you have 45 days to register; the steps are on the new resident checklist . Neither state taxes estates or inheritances, so your estate plan does not need to change for tax reasons. Florida charges no tax for moving out of the state.

The calculator above runs all of it against your own numbers and says plainly when the answer is that you would pay more.

## Florida to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Why do people move from Florida to Myrtle Beach?
Four reasons repeat in the national data and reporting: the insurance renewal, condo assessments under Florida's post-Surfside inspection rules, and day-to-day costs that grew larger than the income-tax savings. Some want to be closer to family up north without giving up a mild winter. Home prices matter too, and a typical home costs less here. It is usually not taxes, and the tax section on this page says so plainly.

### What is a halfback move?
A halfback is a person who moved from the Northeast or Midwest to Florida and then moved partway back north, to the Carolinas, Georgia or Tennessee. The usual reasons are to keep a mild winter and the ocean, pay less to own a home, and live closer to family. In a national count of 2025 moves, South Carolina gained about 5,400 net residents 65 and older, more than any state; more of them came from North Carolina than anywhere else, and Florida was next at nearly 1,900.

### Is Myrtle Beach cheaper than Florida overall?
On average, yes. The price data behind our cost of living page puts the Myrtle Beach area about nine index points below the Florida statewide average. Housing is the widest gap. Groceries, gas and home insurance cost less here. One category is higher: state income tax, which Florida does not charge. For most Florida households the house and the insurance outweigh the income tax, and the calculator on this page runs your own numbers.

### Will I pay state income tax after moving from Florida to South Carolina?
Yes. Florida has none and South Carolina taxes income at 1.99 percent up to $30,000 of taxable income and 5.21 percent past it, after a deduction of up to $30,000 for a married couple that shrinks as income rises. A couple on $120,000 of wages pays about $4,300 a year. Social Security is not taxed, and the deductions at 65 leave a modest pension taxed lightly or not at all.

### Do I keep my Save Our Homes cap or homestead exemption if I leave Florida?
No. The cap's benefit can transfer to another Florida homestead, but not across the state line. Selling ends it either way: the buyer of your house is reassessed at market value. Your South Carolina house is assessed under South Carolina's rules, including the 4 percent owner-occupied rate and, at 65 and older after a year of residency, a homestead exemption on the first $50,000 of value.

### Is homeowners insurance cheaper in Myrtle Beach than in Florida?
On average, yes. Priced on the same $300,000 house, a Myrtle Beach policy averages about $4,500 a year against about $6,500 across Florida, about $15,600 in Miami, about $10,400 in Naples and about $6,300 in Tampa. Premiums are set per address, so buy through us and we get you written wind, hail and flood quotes on the exact house before you make an offer.

### Will my car cost more to own in South Carolina than in Florida?
The tax on it, yes. Florida registration is a flat fee set by the car's weight. South Carolina bills every vehicle yearly on its value, roughly $360 to $460 on a $30,000 car plus a $50 road fee. Each vehicle also pays a one-time $250 fee at its first registration here, due within 45 days of the move.

Retire here and pay no state tax on Social Security. Each 55+ community on this page is 3 to 10 minutes from a hospital.

The short answer
A retired couple on Social Security and a modest pension can owe no South Carolina income tax. Property tax here is lowest on a home you live in full time. Outside the city limits, a $400,000 house you live in is taxed about $1,290 a year at 65, with the $50,000 exemption. That exemption takes the first $50,000 of the home's value off the tax.
The four 55+ communities on this page are 4 to 15 minutes by car from the beach. Homes in them usually sell for about $300,000 in Myrtle Trace to about $665,000 for a house in Del Webb at Grande Dunes.

## Is Myrtle Beach a good place to retire?
About 128,700 people in Horry County are 65 or older, about 3 in 10 residents. In South Carolina and in the U.S. as a whole, it is about 2 in 10. Whether it suits you depends most on how you will use the home.

- If you will live here most of the year
Apply for the lower tax rate on a home you live in, called the 4 percent rate, as soon as you close. At 65, apply for the $50,000 exemption too: it takes $50,000 off the value you are taxed on.

- If it will be a second home for a few years first
A second home pays the higher rate: about $4,820 a year on a $400,000 house, until it becomes your legal home.

- If you live on Social Security and a modest pension
You may owe no South Carolina income tax. The calculator below works out yours.

- If you want to live near the beach
Each of the four 55+ communities below is 4 to 15 minutes by car from the beach.

- If you would rather not plan a hurricane evacuation
Three of the four 55+ communities are outside every hurricane evacuation zone.

To weigh Myrtle Beach against Charleston, see our Myrtle Beach vs Charleston guide .

## What is a retired week like in Myrtle Beach?
For golf, anyone who lives or owns a home in Horry County can buy the Myrtle Beach Golf Passport , $72 a year, for member rates at the courses that take it. The city's own course, Whispering Pines , charges county residents $45 a round with a cart, plus tax.
In the off season, nothing closes except the tourist attractions and the water parks. The boardwalk stays open, sometimes with shorter hours. Each 55+ community below has its own clubhouse and pool, and three of them have a lifestyle director or a club calendar.
Photo: 28bytes
The beach and the dunes in Myrtle Beach, with few people on the sand, seen from a high floor.

Family can fly straight here. The Myrtle Beach airport's route map lists nonstop flights to more than 50 cities on ten airlines, among them New York LaGuardia, Newark, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Charlotte. The airport is 20 to 35 minutes by car from the four 55+ communities. Plan on a car: most daily life here is built around driving .

Myrtle Trace, just outside Conway, has a calendar of about 70 events and club meetings a month. Its activities committee runs a coffee klatch, a dining-out group and meals for neighbors who cannot get out, and the calendar has had a Labor Day picnic and a craft fair. Owners share a clubhouse, a pool and ponds where they can fish.

Conway Medical Center is about 3 minutes away by car, downtown Conway about 10 and the beach about 15. Myrtle Trace is outside every hurricane evacuation zone, and outside the city limits, so there is no city tax.
Homes here usually sell for about $300,000, the least of the four. The HOA fee is $95 a month. Nearly 9 in 10 homes are taxed as someone's full-time home. At least one person in each home must be 55 or older, and the HOA's rules set no minimum age for anyone else. Read our Myrtle Trace guide .

## Do Myrtle Beach's 55+ communities have to evacuate for hurricanes?
Three of the four are outside every hurricane evacuation zone. Every home in Seasons at Prince Creek West is in Zone C.
South Carolina draws its evacuation zones A, B and C around storm surge, the rise of sea water in a storm. A home outside every zone is not ordered out by its zone.
The homes in all four communities are outside FEMA's high-risk flood areas, so federal law does not require flood insurance with a mortgage, though a lender may still ask for it. In Seasons, 45 lots touch a high-risk area at one edge, so we check where the house is on the lot.

## What is the weather like in Myrtle Beach all year?
January afternoons are in the mid to upper 50s: about 56 degrees in Myrtle Beach and about 58 in Conway. Each has close to 40 nights a year at or below freezing.
Summer is milder on the coast. In a normal year, Myrtle Beach has about 22 days of 90 degrees or more, and Conway, inland, about 58.

## What does a house near Myrtle Beach cost a year at 65?
Outside the city limits, a $400,000 house you live in costs about $1,380 a year in county tax and fees at 65, before insurance and any HOA fee.

A second home or a rental · the 6 percent rate $4,820

Horry County's 2026 tax rates, in the county outside the city limits. Inside a city, the city's tax is added.
The 4 percent rate is the lower tax rate on a home you live in. Until you apply for it, the county bills the house at the second-home rate. To get it, you certify that no one in your household claims to be a legal resident of another state. A house that becomes your home for any part of the year gets the lower rate for the whole year.
The $50,000 exemption at 65 is its own application. You qualify once you have lived in South Carolina for a year and turned 65 by December 31 of the year before. Until then, the same house is taxed about $1,470 a year.

## Does South Carolina tax Social Security and pensions?
South Carolina does not tax Social Security. Pensions, IRAs and 401(k) plans get a deduction for each person, larger from the year you turn 65, and military retirement pay is not taxed at all. These rules come from a new state law, Act 110 .

## Retiring to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Does a retired couple have to file a South Carolina tax return?
A married couple, both 65 or older, does not have to file a South Carolina return unless their South Carolina income is over $60,000.

### How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Horry County?
Apply at the Horry County Auditor's office, and inside a city at the city too, by July 15 for that year's bill. You must own the home and live in it as your legal home. The exemption takes the first $50,000 of the home's value off the tax.

### Do I lose the 4 percent rate if I rent the home out?
Only if you rent it out for more than 72 days in a calendar year. State law keeps the 4 percent rate on a home you live in as long as it is not rented for more than 72 days in that year.

### What makes a community 55+ under federal law?
To count as 55+ housing under federal fair housing law, a community needs at least one person 55 or older in at least 80 percent of its occupied homes. It must also publish and follow its age policy, and check ages.

## Second Homes Near Myrtle Beach: 6 Beach Places | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/second-home/
Summary: Six places on the beach for a second home near Myrtle Beach, where you may rent it by the night, what rentals take in, and the tax on a $400,000 home.

Home / Buyers / Second Home
Second homes

# Where should you buy a second home near Myrtle Beach? Six places on the beach, from Cherry Grove to Pawleys Island.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Six places on the beach, their rental rules and the yearly tax on a second home.

The short answer
For a boat at your back door, buy on the Cherry Grove canals in North Myrtle Beach. For a condo on the sand with the boardwalk outside, buy on the Myrtle Beach oceanfront. For an old beach house on an island with no hotels, buy on Pawleys Island.
North Myrtle Beach, Pawleys Island and the county outside the cities allow nightly rentals. The City of Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach allow them only in some zones. Property tax on a $400,000 second home is about $4,800 to $6,100 a year.

Map of the six places on this page, from North Myrtle Beach south to Pawleys Island. Tap a name to read about it. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.

## 1. North Myrtle Beach: a dock behind the house, the shag on Main Street
In Cherry Grove, at the north end of North Myrtle Beach, the streets from 32nd Avenue North to the end of Cherry Grove back onto canals with boat docks. The canals run out to Hog Inlet and the marsh. Cherry Grove was an island until its inlet filled in around 1950.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Cherry Grove from over the ocean: houses on the canals, many with their own docks, and the marsh behind.

A few miles south, Ocean Drive is where the shag began. In the 1940s, visitors came to dance at the beach music clubs on Main Street and Ocean Drive. Each spring and fall, the Society of Stranders brings its shag festivals back to the same streets.
North Myrtle Beach has 9 miles of beach. A nightly rental here needs only a city business license, renewed each year.
The canals fill with mud over time. Owners of lots on them in east Cherry Grove pay up to $2,400 a year toward digging them out, through a district set to last 10 years. The city has also held public meetings on new rental rules since 2024, with nothing adopted yet.
Homes in North Myrtle Beach usually sell for about $395,000.

## 2. Myrtle Beach oceanfront: condos on the boardwalk
The Myrtle Beach Boardwalk runs 1.3 miles along the ocean, from Pier 14 to 16th Avenue North. From a condo on this stretch, you walk out to the beach, the piers and the restaurants along the boardwalk.
Photo: 28bytes
The wide beach and the dunes in Myrtle Beach, seen from a high floor of an oceanfront building.

The city took its name from the wax myrtle, a shrub that grows wild here. The name won a contest in 1900, and Edgewater came second. South of the towers, Myrtle Beach State Park keeps about a mile of beach with no buildings on it. It opened in 1936 as the first park in the state system.
The city allows nightly rentals only where the zoning allows them, and most of its neighborhoods of houses are zoned against them. The fine is up to $500 for each offense.
Some oceanfront buildings run like hotels, with a registration desk and daily rentals. Those buildings are harder to finance, as the loan section explains.
One oceanfront building, the Palace Resort, has its own guide, with HOA fees by unit size .
Homes across the City of Myrtle Beach usually sell for about $325,000.

## 3. Surfside Beach: a town pier and streets of beach houses
Surfside Beach owns its fishing pier. It is concrete and 814 feet long. Walking on it is free, and a day of fishing costs $14, with the state fishing license included.
Photo: BullDawg2021
Beach houses behind the low dunes on the ocean side of Surfside Beach.

Much of the town was once The Ark Plantation. In the 1920s George J. Holiday named it Floral Beach, after his wife Flora and his daughter Floramay. It became Surfside Beach in 1952. When Hurricane Hazel came in 1954, it destroyed 18 of the 65 houses on the beach.
The town has 36 beach access points and 12 parking lots near the beach . Parking by the pier costs $4 an hour.
Stays under 30 days are allowed in only two of the town's zoning districts, called R3 and C3. The town's single-family neighborhoods do not allow them, and we tell you which district a house is in.
Homes in Surfside Beach usually sell for about $360,000.

## 4. Garden City Beach: the ocean on one side, the inlet on the other
Garden City Beach is a strip of land between the ocean and the marsh of Murrells Inlet. Houses on the marsh side have docks on the tidal creeks.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Garden City Beach from over the ocean: rows of houses between the beach and the marsh, with docks on the creeks behind.

On the Fourth of July, the Murrells Inlet boat parade starts from the point of Garden City. People watch it from the MarshWalk across the water.
Garden City is not a town. It is split between two counties, and its south end is in Georgetown County. On the Horry County side you may rent by the night, unless the house's HOA forbids it, and many houses there have no HOA . We read the HOA's rules, and check the zoning on the Georgetown County side, before you make an offer.
Homes in the 29576 ZIP code, which covers Garden City and Murrells Inlet, usually sell for about $400,000.

## 5. Murrells Inlet: seafood on the boardwalk, boats in the creek
Murrells Inlet began as a fishing village on a sheltered inlet. Its MarshWalk, a half-mile boardwalk along the water, has seafood restaurants and the docks for fishing trips.

Huntington Beach State Park, beside the inlet, has 3 miles of beach. In the park is Atalaya, the Moorish-style winter home of Archer and Anna Hyatt Huntington, now a National Historic Landmark. Brookgreen Gardens, across the highway, has one of the country's largest collections of American statues of people and animals.
Murrells Inlet is not a town either. On the Horry County side, the county has no rule on nightly stays, so only an HOA can forbid them.
The waterway along the inlet is in the highest-risk flood zone on the coast, where storms bring waves. A home there with a mortgage needs flood insurance, and we get a flood quote for any home you like.
Homes in Murrells Inlet usually sell for about $400,000.

## 6. Pawleys Island: summer houses since the 1700s
Rice planters built summer houses on Pawleys Island in the early 1700s, to get away from the rivers in summer, so it is one of the oldest beach resorts in America. Its historic district, in the middle of the island, has houses from about 1780 to 1866.
Photo: Phoebe
A wooden walkway over the dunes to the ocean on Pawleys Island.

The town incorporated in 1985 to keep out a large hotel, and it forbids commercial businesses. Apart from two historic inns, the island has no commercial buildings. The Pawleys Island rope hammock was first made here. Pawleys Creek, the tidal creek behind the island's salt marsh, is a wildlife sanctuary with no hunting.
Pawleys Island allows rentals, and the town requires no business license to rent a home out.
Parts of the island flood when heavy rain comes with a high tide, including near both causeways. The streets are narrow, with 20 feet of pavement or less.
Homes with a Pawleys Island address, on the island and the mainland side, usually sell for about $550,000.

## Can you rent it out when you are not there?
Yes, in most of these places. Each town makes its own rule, an HOA can forbid what the town allows, and your loan has its own limits.

Guests pay lodging tax on any stay under 90 days: about 13 percent in the City of Myrtle Beach, about 12 percent elsewhere in Horry County, and about 11 percent on Pawleys Island. You or your rental manager collect it from guests and send it in.
The IRS has a rule for a home you both use and rent. Use it yourself for more than 14 days a year, or more than 10 percent of the days it is rented, whichever is more, and the IRS treats it as a home. Then rent from fewer than 15 days a year is tax-free, and your rental deductions cannot be more than the rent. Our 14-day rule page has examples.

## Is it a second home or an investment property?
Decide this before you apply for a loan. Most lenders follow the rules of Fannie Mae, which buys home loans from lenders. Fannie Mae calls a home a second home only when:

- you live in it yourself for part of the year;

- it is one home, not a duplex;

- it can be lived in all year;

- no agreement gives a management company control over who stays there;

- the rent from it is not used to qualify you for the loan.

Some rent is allowed. If the lender sees rental income, the loan can still be a second-home loan, as long as the rent did not help you qualify and every other rule is met. A home you will not live in is an investment property, and lenders price that loan differently.
Fannie Mae does not buy loans in a condo building run like a hotel, with a rental pool or daily rentals, so many lenders will not finance a unit there. Other loans exist for those buildings: see loans for hotel-style condos . Our lending partner can lay out both kinds of loan for the home you choose.

## What does a second home cost to hold each year?
South Carolina taxes a second home on 6 percent of its value, and the home you live in on 4 percent. A home you live in also pays no school operating tax, the largest part of the bill. Together, the two rules make a second home's bill three to four times larger. To look up what an address is billed, use our Horry County tax records search .
A $400,000 home, 2026 If you lived in it As a second home
City of Myrtle Beach About $1,615 a year About $6,110 a year
Horry County outside the cities About $1,470 a year About $4,820 a year

In North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach, the bill on a $400,000 second home falls between these two. Every town's bill is in our property tax calculator .
Want to walk to the sand, or swim at home? Our guides to houses near the beach and homes with a pool show where they are.
Insurance is the other large cost, and the condo and beach house table below shows who insures what. A federal flood policy has a $250 yearly surcharge when the home is no one's main home. For a main home, the surcharge is $25. Renting the home out will likely raise the premium. What each policy costs here is on our coastal insurance page.
We get the insurance quotes and the HOA fee for any home you like before you make an offer, so you know the whole yearly cost.

## Should you buy a condo or a beach house?
A condo A beach house
The building The association insures it and keeps up the outside. The cost is in the monthly fee. You insure it against wind and often flood, and the roof is yours.
Your own policy Covers the inside of the unit and your things. Covers the whole house.
Big repairs An older building can send every owner a one-time bill, called a special assessment. You pay for them when they come.
The loan Harder in a building run like a hotel (see the loan ). Any second-home or investment loan.

Common questions

## Second home FAQ

### Can I get the 4 percent tax rate on a second home in South Carolina?
No. South Carolina gives the 4 percent rate only to the home your household lives in, and the owner certifies that no one in the household is a legal resident of another state. A second home is taxed on 6 percent of its value.

### Can I use a rental manager with a second-home loan?
Yes, as long as no agreement gives the manager control over who stays in the home and when. The lender also cannot count the rent toward qualifying you for a second-home loan.

### Who looks after a second home while I am away?
A local property manager can check on the home, handle repairs and, if you rent it, run the bookings. Chapter3 sells homes and does not manage them, and our property management page explains what managers here charge.

### What about hurricane season?
The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30. A beach house needs a wind policy and usually flood coverage, and a condo owner relies on the building's master policy. We check the flood zone of any home before you make an offer.

# VA loans in Myrtle Beach: which condos and homes qualify.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Your VA loan can buy most kinds of home here, but a condo must be in one of about 175 Horry County communities on the VA's list.

The short answer
You can use a VA loan on a house you will live in, if the seller agrees and the house passes the VA appraisal. The appraisal is the VA's check of the home's value and condition. About half the houses for sale on the Grand Strand are marked as taking a VA loan. A condo needs a community on the VA's list, and few oceanfront resort towers are on it.
If the VA rates you permanently and totally disabled from your service, you pay no property tax on your home. On a home the county values at $400,000, that saves about $1,470 to $2,610 a year.

## Can you use a VA loan on the home you want in Myrtle Beach?
The answer depends on the kind of home you want.

- A house you will live in Can you use VA: Yes No list to check. The seller and the VA appraisal decide.

- A townhouse Can you use VA: Yes If the community was set up as a condo, it must also be on the VA's condo list.

- A condo in a villa, golf or townhome community Can you use VA: If listed Only in a community on the VA's list. The listed communities with condos for sale are named below.

- A condo in an oceanfront resort tower Can you use VA: Rarely Only 2 of the 29 big oceanfront resort buildings we track are on the VA's list.

- A beach second home or a rental Can you use VA: No A VA loan is only for the home you live in.

- A house with 2 to 4 units Can you use VA: Yes You must live in one of the units. You can rent the others.

Towns are mailing addresses, so Myrtle Beach includes Carolina Forest and Socastee, and Conway includes country land outside the city.
Inland towns give a VA buyer the most choice. Conway also has the highest city tax, so a fully exempt veteran saves the most there. Our guides to Conway and Carolina Forest show what living there is like.
VA is most common in the middle of the market, and about 7 in 10 new houses for sale are marked VA. Our new construction guide covers buying from a builder.
A listing without the VA mark can still take a VA offer. On a house you like that is not marked, we ask the listing agent whether the seller will take VA before you make an offer.

### Flood zones
About 3 in 10 houses for sale listed as in a flood zone are marked VA. In a high-risk flood zone, a VA loan requires flood insurance for the life of the loan. Our coastal insurance guide gives what it costs.

### Taking over a seller's VA loan
A buyer can take over a seller's VA loan instead of getting a new one. This is called assuming the loan. Only 18 homes for sale on the Grand Strand are listed with a loan you can take over, of any kind, so we ask the seller's agent about the loan on each home you like.

## Can you buy a beach house or a rental with a VA loan?
Only as the home you live in. You can buy a house with 2 to 4 units, live in one and rent the others, but few sellers of these homes here mark VA: 3 of the 61 for sale. Our guide to buying a duplex or fourplex covers the rest.
A beach second home or a pure rental does not qualify. You certify that you intend to move in. If you are on active duty and cannot live there because of it, your spouse can meet the rule.

## Do disabled veterans pay property tax in South Carolina?
Not on their home, if the VA rates them permanently and totally disabled from their service. The exemption covers the home they own and live in, alone or with a spouse, with up to 5 acres, and up to two cars. A lower rating does not qualify.
Tax a fully exempt veteran saves each year, on a home the county values at $400,000 Where the home is Tax saved a year
Conway $2,610
North Myrtle Beach $1,790
Surfside Beach $1,680
City of Myrtle Beach $1,620
Murrells Inlet or Garden City Horry County side $1,570
Outside the cities Carolina Forest, Socastee, Little River $1,470

Chapter3's figures from the county's tax rates for a home you live in, worked out the same way as our property tax calculator. The county taxes its own value of the home, not the price you paid. Small special district taxes and the county's stormwater fee are left out.
A surviving spouse who has not remarried and lives in the home keeps the exemption, and can move it to a later home. Every town's tax rate is in our property tax calculator .

### How to apply, in order
The exemption is not automatic. The SC Department of Revenue grants it, not the county auditor, and the order matters.

- Get the 4 percent rate on your home. After closing, you apply to the Horry County Assessor for the 4 percent rate, the lower tax rate for the home you live in. The SC Department of Revenue will not grant the exemption until the county has.

- Get the disability certificate. It comes from the VA or from the county's veterans affairs office. A VA rating letter alone is not enough. Horry County Veterans Affairs is at 1949 Industrial Park Road in Conway, and its phone is (843) 915-5480 .

- Apply to the SC Department of Revenue. Apply online in MyDORWAY , or on Form PT-401-I. Send the recorded deed, the county's 4 percent approval and the certificate.

- Claim the whole year. A newly rated veteran can claim the exemption for the whole year the disability began, if they owned the home that year; if they bought it later, from the year they bought it. A late filer can go back up to two prior tax years if the taxes were paid on time.

### Rated below 100 percent?
At 65, after a year living in South Carolina, the first $50,000 of your home's value is not taxed. It also applies if a state or federal agency has classified you totally and permanently disabled. You apply to the county auditor by July 15.

## What does the VA appraisal check?
Two things: what the home is worth, and whether it meets the VA's minimum property requirements, which your lender confirms.

### If the appraisal comes in low
The VA loan cannot be more than the appraised value or the price, whichever is lower. The VA's own example: on a home under contract for $400,000 that appraises at $375,000, the loan is capped at $375,000. You then pay the gap in cash, the seller lowers the price, or the deal ends.
In our experience, low appraisals are rare here. When one comes in low, our agents gather comparable sales for a reconsideration of value, a request to look at the value again. Once the value changed and the buyer brought less to closing.

### Homes built before 1978
Older homes get one extra look. In a home built before 1978, the VA presumes lead paint, and any peeling or damaged paint must be fixed. Homes that old are far less common here than in the country as a whole.
Homes built before 1980, out of every 100 Where built before 1980

Horry County 14 in 100
South Carolina 32 in 100
United States 48 in 100

U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey, all homes. The Census counts homes by the decade they were built, so 1980 is the closest line to 1978.

## What does a VA buyer pay at closing?
A VA loan can need no down payment, as long as the price is not higher than the appraised value.
Unless you are exempt, you pay a one-time VA funding fee . It is a share of the loan amount. The share drops if you make a large enough down payment. With little or no down payment, it is higher if you have used a VA loan before. You can add the fee to the loan or pay it at closing. On a purchase it is the only cost you can add to the loan.

### Who pays no funding fee

- You get VA disability pay Or you are eligible for it but get retirement or active-duty pay instead.

- You are still serving and already rated Before your closing date, the VA rated you eligible for disability pay on a claim made before discharge.

- You are a surviving spouse with VA survivor pay Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC), as the surviving spouse of a veteran.

- You are on active duty with a Purple Heart You show the lender proof of it on or before the closing date.

If the VA later awards you disability pay that starts before your closing date, you can ask for the funding fee back.

### What the seller can pay
A seller can pay all of your closing costs, with no VA limit. The VA's 4 percent limit is only for other help from the seller, such as paying your funding fee or paying off a debt. It is 4 percent of the value the VA appraisal gives the home.
Who pays the commission, the lender's fee for making the loan, the appraisal fee and title insurance is up to you and the seller. We write what you ask for into your offer. Our closing cost guide lists each cost at closing in South Carolina.
Ask the seller for your closing costs
When you find the home, we write your offer and ask the seller in it to pay the closing costs you choose.

## Where is the VA clinic in Myrtle Beach?
The Myrtle Beach VA Clinic is at 1800 Airpark Drive. It offers primary care, mental health and specialty care, and replaced two older clinics in town.

The drive to the Myrtle Beach VA Clinic from the middle of each town, without traffic. Summer traffic takes longer. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.

The clinic is part of the Ralph H. Johnson VA health care system. From the clinic, the nearest VA medical center is the Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center in Charleston, about 2 hours 10 minutes away without traffic. From Loris, Little River and North Myrtle Beach, the Fayetteville VA Medical Center in North Carolina is a shorter drive.

### Military history here

Photo: Carol M. Highsmith
Jets on display at Warbird Park in Myrtle Beach.
South Carolina does not tax military retirement pay, and a surviving spouse gets the same deduction. Our guide for retirees covers the rest of the state's taxes on retirement income. Not every veteran here is retired. One of our clients is a veteran who lives here and works his New York job in alternating weeks.

## Who qualifies for a VA loan, and how much can you borrow?
You need a Certificate of Eligibility (COE), the VA's letter that says you can use the benefit. These are the service minimums for service from the Gulf War to today:

- Serving now 90 days of active duty in a row.

- A veteran 24 months in a row, or the full period you were called to active duty (at least 90 days), or less if discharged for a disability from your service.

- Guard and Reserve 90 days of qualifying active duty, or 6 qualifying years if you still serve, left honorably or retired.

- A surviving spouse If you get, or can get, certain VA survivor pay (DIC), or your spouse on active duty is missing in action or held as a prisoner of war.

### How much you can borrow
Your entitlement is the most the VA will pay your lender if you do not repay the loan. Your COE shows your basic entitlement. The rest, for a larger loan, is worked out from the loan amount and is not on the COE. With your full entitlement there is no VA loan limit : the lender decides how much you can borrow, and the appraisal must support the price.
If you still have a VA loan on another home, part of your entitlement is in use. Your remaining entitlement is worked out from the county's loan limit, which is $832,750 for a one-unit home in Horry and Georgetown counties, minus the entitlement already in use. If what is left does not cover enough of the new loan, the lender may ask for a down payment.

### Credit and down payment help
The VA requires no minimum credit score, but some lenders have their own. SC Housing's VA loans with no down payment need a score of 640. SC Housing's year-round help works with a VA loan; our guide to SC Housing's programs gives its limits.

Common questions

## VA loan questions

### Can I use a VA loan more than once?
Yes. After you sell the home and pay off the VA loan, you can ask the VA to restore your entitlement. With a VA loan still open on another home, you may have enough left for a second one.

### Can I buy a manufactured home with a VA loan?
Yes, if you will live in it. A VA loan can buy a manufactured home, or a lot for one. Few sellers here mark VA on them: about 15 in 100 manufactured homes for sale.

### Can I buy a house with a tenant in it using a VA loan?
A house with a tenant is hard to buy with a VA loan while a long lease runs, because you must be able to move in. Most lenders want you in the home within 60 days. We ask about the lease before you make an offer.

### What interest rate will I get on a VA loan?
The lender quotes your rate. We do not quote rates. We can introduce you to our preferred lender, or you can use any lender you like.
