By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
South of Myrtle Beach, people line dance at the end of the Garden City Pier, out over the ocean, and pull up blue crabs from docks on the marsh.

The short answer
Garden City, South Carolina is a beach community between Surfside Beach and Murrells Inlet. It is not a town: the county runs it, and most of its beach road is in Georgetown County, not Horry.
For a condo on the sand, look at the ocean side by the pier. For a house with a dock, look at the marsh and the Georgetown end. For a house lived in all year, out of the high-risk flood zone, look west of Business 17.

Tell us how you will use it. We send the Garden City homes that fit.
Send me Garden City homes

## Where is Garden City, SC, and which county is it in?
Garden City sits on a strip of land between the Atlantic Ocean and a salt marsh, just south of Surfside Beach. Its beach road, Waccamaw Drive, runs down the strip to Garden City Point at the inlet. Business 17 runs inland of the marsh.
The Horry and Georgetown county line crosses the beach about a third of a mile south of the Garden City Pier. Most of Waccamaw Drive is south of the line, in Georgetown County. The county decides your property tax, your rental license and the beach rules.
Most addresses use Murrells Inlet and its ZIP code, 29576. A band at the north edge uses Surfside Beach.

The dashed line is the county line. Aerial photo: USGS, public domain. Roads and the county line: U.S. Census Bureau, Horry County and OpenStreetMap contributors.
- 1 The ocean side of Waccamaw Drive : the beach and the pier

- 2 On the marsh : docks and tidal creeks

- 3 Between the marsh and Business 17 : the most kinds of homes

- 4 West of Business 17 : subdivisions lived in all year

- 5 The Georgetown end : canals, docks and the quietest beach

## Where to buy in Garden City, SC
Garden City has five parts, and each is a different way to live at the beach. The numbers match the map above.

### 1 The ocean side of Waccamaw Drive: the beach and the pier
Here you walk out of your building onto the sand. Condo buildings and a few beach houses stand between Waccamaw Drive and the ocean, from the Surfside Beach line south past the pier. The largest buildings include Royal Garden Resort, Waters Edge Resort, Surfmaster and Atalaya Towers.
The pier is the center of this side. At the far end of the Garden City Pier, rebuilt after Hurricane Hugo took the old pier in 1989, the rain shelter holds a bandstand and a dance floor bar, and people learn line dances out over the ocean.
U.S. government aerial photo
The ocean side by the pier from above: buildings and beach houses between Waccamaw Drive and the beach, and the salt marsh behind.
Its café serves breakfast. In summer, its deck bar has karaoke in the afternoons, and bands play every night at both ends of the pier, weather permitting. The arcade is there for a rainy day. A pier pass covers fishing, so no state fishing license is needed, and in summer you can fish around the clock.
Almost every home on this side is a condo. Condos here sold for about $320,000 at the middle in the past year.

Get the condos for sale on Garden City's ocean side

### 2 On the marsh: docks and tidal creeks
Behind the beach strip is salt marsh, cut by tidal creeks that reach the inlet at Garden City Point. The houses along its edges look out over the marsh, and many have a long private dock . On the beach strip they line Dogwood Drive. On the mainland side they are on streets like Creekside Drive and Rum Gully Road.
From a dock on the marsh, you can tie a chicken neck to a string and pull up blue crabs for dinner. In South Carolina you need no license to crab with three or fewer drop nets, fold-up traps or hand lines.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Beach houses along Waccamaw Drive, seen from over the ocean, with the salt marsh and its creeks behind them and docks on the far shore.
These are the most costly houses east of Business 17. The ones that sold in the past year went for about $1.24 million at the middle, about twice the other houses east of Business 17. Few come up for sale.

Get the marsh-front homes for sale in Garden City

### 3 Between the marsh and Business 17: the most kinds of homes
The rest of the land between the marsh and Business 17 is streets of houses, small condo buildings and manufactured homes. Its neighborhoods include Salters Cove, Mount Gilead, Myrtle Dunes and Woodland Terrace. It also takes in the streets north of where Waccamaw Drive ends, up to the Surfside Beach line.
Every Fourth of July afternoon, Garden City holds a "wet" golf cart parade: decorated carts drive the route while people on the side soak them with water guns. It raises money for local first responders.
U.S. government aerial photo
Streets between the marsh and Business 17 from above: houses and yards, a pond, and the salt marsh at the lower right.
This part has the widest range of prices. Away from the marsh, a house sold for about $575,000 at the middle in the past year. Condos and manufactured homes cost less. Where a home is on rented land, the lot rent is not in the price, and we find it out for each home.

Get the homes for sale in Garden City east of Business 17

### 4 West of Business 17: subdivisions lived in all year
West of Business 17 are Garden City's subdivisions, with houses on curving streets around ponds. The largest are Woodlake Village, Mallard Landing, Harbour Village and Jamestowne. Condo communities include Sweetwater at Indian Wells, South Bay Lakes, Southbridge and Tupelo Bay Golf Villas.
On the Fourth of July, decorated boats parade along the inlet in the afternoon while the crowd watches from the MarshWalk, and fireworks go up at night. In 2025 the boat parade was at 2 p.m. and the fireworks at 10 p.m. From the subdivisions west of Business 17, it is a short drive.
U.S. government aerial photo
Subdivisions west of Business 17 from above: houses on curving streets, ponds, a pool and courts, and woods.
More people live here all year: about 3 in 4 houses are taxed as the owner's main home, the most of any part. A house sold for about $340,000 at the middle in the past year and a condo for about $173,000, the lowest prices in Garden City.

Get the homes for sale in Garden City west of Business 17

### 5 The Georgetown end: canals, docks and the quietest beach
South of the county line, Waccamaw Drive runs on to Garden City Point, where the marsh meets the inlet. Houses line the beach, and behind them many sit on canals with private docks.
At the inlet end of Waccamaw Drive, Gulfstream Cafe has looked over Murrells Inlet for nearly 40 years. People go up to its rooftop deck to watch the sun set over the water, and come back for its oyster roasts in season.
U.S. government aerial photo
The Georgetown end near Garden City Point from above: houses on canals with private docks, Waccamaw Drive and the beach.
This is the quietest stretch of the beach road. Georgetown County's rules apply here. It requires no business license for a rental, and its lodging tax is lower.
Prices here are the highest in Garden City. The listings here asked about $1.45 million at the middle, more than any other part.

Get the homes for sale at Garden City's Georgetown end

## Can you Airbnb in Garden City, SC?
Yes, unless the building's own rules say no. There is no town, so no town rental ordinance applies. Horry County's list of what a nightly-rental owner must file names a business license and three tax accounts, and no rental permit. We go over the filings with you before you close.
A condo association or an HOA (homeowners association) can forbid or limit rentals in its own papers. We read the building's documents and rules before you offer. Our page on HOA rental restrictions explains how those rules work.
Guests pay lodging taxes on top of the rent: about 12 percent on the Horry side and about 11 percent on the Georgetown end. You collect that money and send it on, so it is not part of your income.

### What a Garden City Airbnb earns
AirROI, a rental data company, tracks the Airbnb listings here under the name Garden City Beach. Over the past 12 months:

- $41,200 the average listing's income in a year

- 40% of nights booked

- $371 average nightly rate

- 374 active listings

Each figure is an average across all the listings, so the nights booked times the nightly rate does not come out to the income.
Most of the money comes in summer. A listing earns about 5 times as much in an average July as in January.

## What is there to do in Garden City, SC?
A summer day here starts on the beach and ends on the pier. For dinner, the MarshWalk in Murrells Inlet is about 8 minutes away by car. The Murrells Inlet guide has its restaurants and the boat landing at its south end.
For a day out, Huntington Beach State Park is 15 to 20 minutes south. It has 3 miles of beach, a freshwater lake where you are almost sure to see alligators, and what the state calls some of the top bird-watching on the East Coast. The Pawleys Island guide has the park's history and Brookgreen Gardens across the road.
For groceries, Kroger on Business 17 is about 4 minutes from the pier by car, and the Walmart Supercenter on the Garden City Connector about 5.

### The beach rules
Horry County manages the beach from the Surfside Beach town line to the Georgetown County line. Its rules:

- Dogs Off the beach from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., May 1 through Labor Day. Otherwise on a hand-held leash.

- Shade Round umbrellas up to 7 feet 6 inches across, and small pop-up cabanas for infants. No tents or canopies, all year.

- Overnight Nothing may be left on the beach overnight.

- Alcohol None on the beach or the beach accesses.

## Is Garden City, SC busy in winter?
Summer is busy and winter is quiet, most of all on the beach road.

- On the ocean side, more than 9 in 10 homes are second homes or rentals. The county mails most of their tax bills to another state, North Carolina, New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio most often.

- At the last Census, taken in April, about 4 in 5 homes along Waccamaw Drive had no one living in them.

- The pier stays open in winter, with shorter hours for fishing and the deck bar.

- From November 1 to February 28, you may drive a golf cart onto the Horry County beach, with a state permit and a licensed driver.

Example. In the winter cart season, a golf cart with a cooler and buckets drives down onto the sand at Garden City. The beach is empty. There is time for sandcastles, lunch and an hour of watching the waves.

## Does Garden City flood?
East of Business 17, much of Garden City is in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. In that zone a lender requires flood insurance:
Part of Garden City, Horry side Homes in FEMA's high-risk flood zone
The ocean side of Waccamaw Drive Nearly all
Between the marsh and Business 17 About half
West of Business 17 None

Flood insurance costs about five times as much on the beach strip. Along Waccamaw Drive, the middle federal flood policy on a house cost about $3,260 a year. Elsewhere in Garden City's ZIP code it was about $620. To check one address, use our Horry County flood zone check .
A condo building's own flood policy on the strip cost about $17,000 a year at the middle, shared by the owners through their dues.

### What the big storms did
In September 1989, Hurricane Hugo's storm surge wiped out up to 90 percent of Garden City's homes. The pier was destroyed, and sand covered roads three blocks inland.
In 2022, Hurricane Ian's surge broke through the dunes in Garden City Beach and flooded parking lots and streets. It left up to three feet of sand on South Waccamaw Drive.

### High tides are rising
High tides that reach flood level come more often than they used to. At the nearest working tide gauge, in Myrtle Beach, they came about 8 days a year in the last ten years, against 1 or 2 days a year twenty years before.
High tides reach flood level about 8 days a year now, up from 2 Years Days a year

1995 to 2004 about 2 days
2005 to 2014 about 3 days
2015 to 2024 about 8 days
NOAA's outlook for the coming year 8 to 12 days

Days a year, the average for each ten years, at NOAA's tide gauge at Springmaid Pier in Myrtle Beach, about 7 miles north.

## What does it cost to own a home in Garden City each year?
South Carolina figures property tax on a share of a home's value: 4 percent of it for the home you live in, and 6 percent for a second home or rental. The home you live in also skips the school operating tax. As a rental, the same condo pays about 3 times the tax it pays as your main home.

- On the Georgetown end, Georgetown County decides the tax rate. The same state rule applies.

## Garden City, SC FAQ

### Is Garden City, SC in Horry County or Georgetown County?
Both. The pier is in Horry County, and most of the beach road is in Georgetown County.

### Is Garden City part of Myrtle Beach?
No. Garden City is not part of any city. Most addresses use Murrells Inlet, ZIP code 29576.

### Can you drive a golf cart on Garden City Beach?
On the Horry County beach, from November 1 to February 28, with a state permit and a licensed driver.

### Are dogs allowed on Garden City Beach?
Not from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., May 1 through Labor Day, on the Horry County beach. At other times, on a hand-held leash no longer than 7 feet.

### Is Garden City, SC safe?
We do not rate any place as safe or unsafe. On the Horry side, the Horry County Police Department, the county's main law enforcement agency, answers calls. On the Georgetown end, the Georgetown County Sheriff's Office does.

### What schools serve Garden City, SC?
Schools are assigned by address. Homes on the Horry side are in Horry County Schools, and homes on the Georgetown end are in the Georgetown County School District. We look up the assigned schools for any home you like.

Little River, SC

# Little River, SC: the boating end of the Grand Strand. About two of every three deeded boat slips in the county are here.

- Deeded slips About 220

- Beach 11 min drive

- Typical house $357,000

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
A waterway community at the North Carolina line, run by Horry County, with deeded boat slips, public ramps and people who live here all year.

The short answer
Little River is the year-round waterway community at the north end of the Grand Strand, at the North Carolina line. If the boat comes first, look at the old village, where all three marinas with deeded slips are. A deeded slip is one you buy and own, with its own deed. For golf and dry ground, look north-west toward the Waccamaw River; for the hospital and the highest-priced neighborhoods, look west.
A resold house here usually sells for about $357,000. Little River is not a town, so Horry County makes the rules and there is no city tax.

## What is it like to live in Little River, SC?
Little River sits on the Intracoastal Waterway, the boat channel behind the Grand Strand's beaches. The old village meets the water at the end of Mineola Avenue, with docks, boats and restaurants on the water, about a minute from US 17.
U.S. government aerial photo
The waterfront at the end of Mineola Avenue, and the slip basin at Mariner's Pointe, from above (NAIP aerial, 2023).
Each May, on the weekend after Mother's Day, the Blue Crab Festival fills that waterfront with seafood from local restaurants, live music and crafters. It has been held for more than 40 years, and a water taxi brings people in from the water.
The beach at Cherry Grove Pier in North Myrtle Beach, Calabash in North Carolina and McLeod Seacoast hospital are all within about 11 minutes by car, as the map shows. The airport is the long drive, about 41 minutes.

Drive times by car from the old village, without traffic. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.
A swing bridge built in 1935 still carries Sea Mountain Highway over the waterway. It turns on a center pier to let boats through, and it is one of the oldest swing bridges on SCDOT's highways. Boaters signal it to open, and at weekday rush hours it opens only on the hour and half hour.
Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens, a county park on the waterway, has about 3 miles of trails and boardwalks through forest and marsh. A piece of the colonial Kings Highway, the road from Boston to Charleston, still runs at the front of the park.
Little River is a place people live all year. When the Census last counted, about one in five of its homes was kept for seasonal use. In North Myrtle Beach, which borders it, it was nearly half.
Share of homes kept for seasonal use, 2020 Census Place Seasonal homes

North Myrtle Beach 48%
Garden City 39%
Little River 19%
All of Horry County 18%
Murrells Inlet 14%
Carolina Forest 5%
Conway 2%

Homes no one lived in on Census Day that were kept for seasonal or occasional use, such as vacation homes and many nightly rentals.

## Is Little River, SC a town?
No. Little River has no town government and no town limits, so Horry County makes its rules and collects its tax. A home here pays the county's property tax and no city tax on top.
One corner is different. A small part of the Little River ZIP code along the waterway is inside the city of North Myrtle Beach. Its homes, about 250 and mostly condos, have a Little River address and pay North Myrtle Beach's city tax. We check which side of the line a house is on.

## Living on the water in Little River: boat slips, ramps and waterfront homes
Most marinas rent their slips. At Little River's three marinas you can buy one: a deeded slip is its own piece of real estate, with its own deed and its own county tax bill. The 12 slip sales recorded here in the past year were each for a slip alone, at $10,000 to $95,000, without a condo.

- Mariner's Pointe

- Coquina Harbour

- Lightkeepers Village

- T. Craig Campbell Landing and, across the waterway, Johnny Causey Landing

- FEMA's high-risk flood zone

- The city of North Myrtle Beach

The dark line is the Little River ZIP code. Marker sizes follow the number of deeded slips. The two landings on the Waccamaw River are north-west of this map. Map data: Horry County GIS; FEMA flood map as the county carries it; U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line.

The slips come in sizes. The table gives the length of most slips at each marina, from the county's parcel map. Coquina Harbour's are about 30 to 45 feet. The county's parcel records do not give the depth of the water, so we check it at low tide for any slip you like.
Deeded boat slips and what they sold for, from county deeds Marina Most slips Sales, past year Prices Middle price
Mariner's Pointe About 30 to 35 feet 11 $10,000 to $38,000 About $16,500
Lightkeepers Village About 45 to 65 feet 1 $95,000 $95,000
Dock Holidays Marina, in North Myrtle Beach About 40 to 50 feet 10 $65,000 to $115,000 About $92,500

Coquina Harbour, with about 80 deeded slips, had no slip sales in the past year.
The county taxes a slip like a second home, on its own value for the slip. It values most Mariner's Pointe slips at $38,000 or more, above nearly every price paid there in the past year. On the county's full $38,000 value, a slip pays about $460 a year in property tax; a slip that has not sold in years may be taxed on a lower, capped value. The marina's association charges a fee on top, and its recorded papers say who may own a slip.

### Where to launch a boat
Horry County runs two public boat landings in the Little River ZIP. T. Craig Campbell Landing is on the Intracoastal Waterway at the US 17 bridge, about 7 minutes from the old village, with two ramps, a dock and a paved lot. Johnny Causey Landing faces it across the waterway, just inside North Myrtle Beach, with two more ramps and a larger lot.
On the Waccamaw River, Worthams Ferry Landing has one ramp and an unpaved lot. Chris Anderson Landing, on the river near Longs, has two ramps.

### Homes on the water
Few houses here sit on the water : fewer than 2 in every 100 have a lot on the Intracoastal Waterway, a canal off it, or the Waccamaw River. Those few cost far more. Only 5 resold in the past year, and the middle one sold for about $1.3 million.
Most homes right by the water are condos, and about half of them are in three communities: Carolina Yacht Landing, Mariner's Pointe and Lightkeepers Village. A condo by the water usually sold for about $263,000 in the past year, and one away from it for about $180,000.
A typical resold house and a Mariner's Pointe slip come to about $375,000 together. If you would rather keep the boat on a trailer at home, our guide to homes with no HOA covers where that is allowed.

### The old village and the harbors: all three marinas within a mile
This is the part to choose if the boat comes first. The waterfront at the end of Mineola Avenue, its restaurants and all three marinas with deeded slips are within about a mile of the village center. At Mariner's Pointe, the condo buildings ring the slip basin.

### North and east, toward Calabash: Heather Glen and Vereen Gardens
Heather Glen is the biggest neighborhood in Little River, with more than 1,100 houses north-east of the old village, and the busiest: more of its houses resold in the past year than in any other. Heather Lakes is east of it.

McLeod Seacoast hospital is in this part, about 6 minutes from the old village. T. Craig Campbell Landing, the county's ramp at the US 17 bridge, is at its south edge.
Carolina Yacht Landing, a condo community on the waterway west of that landing, has about half its units within about 50 feet of the water. Bay Tree, near the hospital, has condos and townhouses.
Among Little River subdivisions with at least five resales, the two highest prices are here: Sawgrass Village at Bridgewater, at about $585,000, and Waterside Village, at about $560,000. Condos at Carolina Yacht Landing resold for about $252,000.

### Far west, at SC 9: a shorter drive to Myrtle Beach
This part suits a buyer who drives south to Myrtle Beach often. SC 31, the Carolina Bays Parkway, starts at its edge. From its subdivisions, Coastal Grand Mall in Myrtle Beach is about 30 to 35 minutes by car and the airport about 35 to 40, a few minutes sooner than from the old village.
It is the part farthest from the water: the old village's waterfront is about 12 to 15 minutes back east by car, and McLeod Seacoast hospital about 9. Its three largest subdivisions, Hidden Brooke, Palm Lakes Plantation and Waterfall, are neighborhoods of houses.

## Does Little River flood?
Most of it does not. About 96 in 100 Little River homes are outside FEMA's high-risk flood zone. Homes right by the water are the exception: close to half of them are inside it.
Share of Little River homes inside FEMA's high-risk flood zone Homes In the zone

Homes within about 50 feet of the water 45%
All homes in the ZIP 3.6%
Homes away from the water 2.2%

Hurricane Hazel came ashore near Little River, at the North Carolina and South Carolina line, in October 1954 as a Category 4 hurricane. It hit at the year's highest tide, and the storm surge reached as high as 18 feet at Calabash.
Few houses for sale at our last count were in the high-risk zone. Our page on how to find out if a house flooded shows every record we use.

### Do you need flood insurance in Little River?
A lender must require flood insurance when the building is in FEMA's high-risk zone, and can ask for it anywhere.
In the Little River ZIP, a flood policy on a house outside the zone usually costs about $480 a year, and inside it about $1,250. A new policy starts 30 days after you apply and pay, unless you buy it with your home loan.

## What do homes rent for in Little River?
HUD's Small Area Fair Market Rent for a three-bedroom in the Little River ZIP is $2,100 a month, with utilities. That is above North Myrtle Beach's ZIP and Myrtle Beach's, and close to Carolina Forest's.

### A worked example
Take a typical resold house. At HUD's three-bedroom figure of $2,100 a month, a year comes to about $25,000, about 7 percent of the price. As a rental, the house pays about $4,400 a year in property tax, about 17 percent of that rent.
Insurance, upkeep, management and empty months come out of the rent too. Our rental analyzer works them out for any address.

### Short-term rentals
Little River has no city ordinance, so county rules apply. A home in Little River outside North Myrtle Beach that is rented short term needs:

- a Horry County business license;

- a county hospitality and accommodations account;

- a South Carolina sales and accommodations tax account;

- a yearly county personal property return for its furnishings, due April 30.

An HOA's rules can forbid short stays, and we read them first. See the short-term rental rules by town and what a nightly rental earns by town .

## Is the Carolina Bays Parkway being extended through Little River?
The extension is planned but not built. The Carolina Bays Parkway, SC 31, would be extended from SC 9 north-east, passing north and northwest of Little River's old village. It would cross the state line to US 17 near Shallotte, North Carolina. It would be a multi-lane freeway, partly on new ground.
South Carolina's part is in SCDOT's current program. North Carolina has not funded land buying or building for its part. The whole project is estimated at $797 million.
The two states have named a preferred route. The final choice comes after they review the comments from the public hearings.

## What are the pros and cons of living in Little River?
The good points are the water, the price and a year-round town. The hard ones are the few houses on the water, flooding at the water's edge, and the drive to the airport.

### Pros

- Deeded boat slips you can own, and public ramps on the waterway and the Waccamaw River.

- No city tax, golf in the neighborhoods, and the beach about 11 minutes away.

- A year-round community, with the waterfront, the Blue Crab Festival, the swing bridge and Vereen Gardens.

### Cons

- Few houses are on the water, and those cost far more. We pair a house with a deeded slip instead.

- Homes right at the water's edge have the most flood risk. We check the flood map and the elevation first.

- The airport is about 41 minutes away by car.

Common questions

## Little River, SC FAQ

### Is Little River, SC a city, and what county is it in?
Little River is not a city. It is an unincorporated community in Horry County, South Carolina, at the North Carolina line, and the county runs it.

### What is there to do in Little River, SC?
Most of Little River's life is on the water: the docks and restaurants on the Mineola Avenue waterfront, and public ramps on the waterway and the Waccamaw River. On land there is golf in the neighborhoods, the trails at Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens and the Blue Crab Festival each May.

### How far is Little River from Myrtle Beach?
About 36 minutes by car to Coastal Grand Mall in Myrtle Beach, without traffic. Barefoot Landing, in North Myrtle Beach, is about 18 minutes, and the airport about 41.

### Does Little River, SC flood?
Most of it does not: about 96 in 100 homes are outside FEMA's high-risk flood zone. The risk is at the water's edge, along the Intracoastal Waterway.

### What is the property tax in Little River, SC?
A home you live in pays only the county's property tax, about $1,400 a year on a typical resold house, with no city tax on top. A second home or rental is taxed at a higher rate.

### How much is a boat slip in Little River?
Deeded slips at Mariner's Pointe, most about 30 to 35 feet long, sold for $10,000 to $38,000 in the past year, each on its own deed, without a condo. Bigger slips at Dock Holidays, across the line in North Myrtle Beach, sold for $65,000 to $115,000.

### Is Little River, SC safe?
We do not rate any place as safe or unsafe. Reported crime is published by police agency, and we pull the figures for the area around any house you ask about.

### Which schools serve Little River, SC?
Horry County Schools assigns schools by address, in nine attendance areas, and none is named Little River. We look up the assigned schools for any house you like.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Murrells Inlet is the seafood village on a salt marsh south of Myrtle Beach, with the MarshWalk on the Georgetown side and golf neighborhoods on the Horry side.

The short answer
Murrells Inlet has two sides, split by the line between Horry and Georgetown counties. The Horry side has the golf neighborhoods, the new houses from builders and 7 in 10 of the homes. Its middle house price in the past year was about $450,000. The Georgetown side has the MarshWalk, the river landing and the houses on the creek. West of the US 17 bypass, its middle house price was about $570,000.
If you want a house on the creek, plan to wait: only about 7 sell in a year. Your tax bill, your schools and the paperwork to rent a house out depend on the county.

Tell us which side you want. We send the homes that fit.

## Is Murrells Inlet in Horry County or Georgetown County?
Both. Murrells Inlet is not a town, and its ZIP code, 29576, crosses the county line. Each county runs its own side. The address on the mail does not tell you the county, so we look it up for every home before you see it.
US 17 runs through Murrells Inlet as two roads: the US 17 bypass to the west, and Business 17 nearer the marsh. The map shows both, and the four parts of Murrells Inlet that the two roads and the county line make. Garden City, on the beach to the east, shares the ZIP code and has its own guide .

The dashed line is the county line. The shading covers where the homes are. Aerial photo: USGS, public domain. County line, roads and home locations: U.S. Census Bureau, Horry and Georgetown counties and OpenStreetMap contributors.

- 3 Between the bypass and Business 17 : streets in the middle of the village

- 4 The creek side : houses on the salt marsh, and the MarshWalk

## Where should you buy in Murrells Inlet?
Each of the four parts is a different way to live here. The numbers match the map above.

### 1 The Horry side: golf neighborhoods and most of the homes
Most Murrells Inlet homes are here, north of the county line and west of the US 17 bypass. The neighborhoods are laid out around golf courses and ponds: the International Club, Blackmoor, the TPC of Myrtle Beach and Indigo Creek's course are all on this side.
The largest house neighborhoods are Indigo Creek, with about 560 houses, Seasons at Prince Creek West (a 55+ community ), The Pines of St. James and Longwood Bluffs. Clients of ours sold their house in Blackmoor, a golf community with no age restriction, to buy in Seasons at Prince Creek West, an age-restricted community a few minutes away.
U.S. government aerial photo
The Horry side from above: houses on curving streets beside the ponds and fairways of the Indigo Creek golf course.
Publix and Lowes Foods are on SC 707, about 4 minutes from the middle of this side. The MarshWalk is about 9 minutes away.
Almost every house for sale here is in an HOA (homeowners association), and the middle fee was about $110 a month. Most of the houses with no HOA are on the Georgetown side. About 1 in 9 houses sold here in the past year was new from a builder. Townhouses and condos cost less, about $320,000 and $275,000.
Send me Horry-side homes in Murrells Inlet

### 2 Georgetown, west of the bypass: Wachesaw, golf and the river
South of the county line and west of the bypass, the land runs down to the Waccamaw River. Boats go in at Wacca Wache Landing, off Wachesaw Road. On the river, the tide rises and falls about half as much as in the inlet.
U.S. government aerial photo
Wacca Wache Landing on the Waccamaw River, with a marina beside it, on the Georgetown side west of the bypass.
The largest neighborhood is Wachesaw Plantation , with about 650 houses, then Linksbrook and Collins Creek. The Wachesaw Plantation Club and Wachesaw East golf courses are on this side. Prince Creek crosses the county line: Palm Bay is in Georgetown County, Seasons at Prince Creek West is in Horry, and Highwood is split between them.
The middle HOA fee on houses for sale here was about $150 a month.

### 3 Between the bypass and Business 17: streets in the middle of the village
This narrow band is on the Georgetown side, between the US 17 bypass and Business 17. It has about 800 homes on streets of houses like the ones in the photo. Tidelands Waccamaw Community Hospital and a Food Lion are just west of the bypass. The MarshWalk, the restaurants and the creek are just east of Business 17.

Between the US 17 bypass and Business 17 from above: streets of houses, with a loop street of newer houses in the middle and shops along the bypass at the left.
A house here sold for about $530,000 at the middle in the past year, and a condo or villa for about $280,000. Some streets here are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone and some are not, so we look up the zone for each house before you offer.

### 4 The creek side: houses on the salt marsh
East of Business 17, on the Georgetown side, houses line the edge of the inlet's salt marsh, many with a dock out to the creek. This is where the village began, and it is a National Register historic district. The county's named areas here include Sunnyside, the Hermitage and Vaux Hall. The MarshWalk's restaurants are on this side.
U.S. government aerial photo
Houses on the creek side of Business 17 from above, with docks reaching out over the marsh edge to the creek.
The creek side has about 370 homes. About 220 of them are houses on the edge of the marsh, and few of those come up for sale: 21 sold in the past three years. The middle one sold for about $930,000, about 1.7 times the middle house west of the bypass over the same years.
Send me creek-front homes in Murrells Inlet

## What is it like to live in Murrells Inlet?
The MarshWalk is a half-mile wooden boardwalk along the salt marsh, lined with restaurants such as Drunken Jack's, Dead Dog Saloon, Creek Ratz and The Wicked Tuna. Its live music is free to hear. Crazy Sister Marina and the county's Murrells Inlet boat landing are at its south end.
U.S. government aerial photo
The MarshWalk from above: restaurants along the boardwalk at the edge of the inlet, Business 17 behind them, and salt marsh islands in the creek.
About 85 in 100 houses outside Garden City are taxed as their owner's main home.

### Oysters in season
From October 1 into May, you can gather oysters and clams on the inlet's three public shellfish grounds with a South Carolina saltwater fishing license. They are the state grounds named Murrells Inlet and Drunken Jack Island, and a public ground at the old Lachicotte oyster factory. A resident's license costs $15 a year, and no license is needed under 16. There is a daily limit, on no more than two days in any seven, and parts of each ground are closed by the state.

### The beach, groceries and the hospital
The creek side has no ocean beach. The nearest are Huntington Beach State Park , about 9 minutes from the MarshWalk, with 3 miles of beach and a freshwater lake known for alligators, and Garden City Beach, about 9 minutes away.
On the Horry side, Publix and Lowes Foods are on SC 707 and a Walmart Neighborhood Market is on the US 17 bypass. On the Georgetown side, a Food Lion is on the bypass near the hospital. Two of our own team chose to live in Murrells Inlet. One of them drives from here to Market Common and to a gym in Carolina Forest.

## Can a creek-front house in Murrells Inlet have a dock?
Usually. South Carolina allows one dock per lot on the salt marsh, if the lot has enough marsh frontage and the creek in front of it is wide enough. Before you offer on a creek-front house, we pull the dock's permit and check the frontage and the creek's width.
Few houses for sale have a dock. Of the 465 listings with a Murrells Inlet address, Garden City included, listing agents marked a private dock on 9. Only 2 of those were on the creek side. A creek house with a dock does come up, but you may wait for one.

### How much water is at the dock?
The tide in the inlet rises and falls about 4 feet on an average day, at NOAA's prediction station at Captain Alex's Marina. About 3 low tides in 10 drop below the low-water mark on the creek's charts. At a dock with little water, a boat can sit on the mud at those tides. We look at the dock at low tide before you offer. Our waterfront homes guide covers what else to look at.

### Where can you launch a boat?
Georgetown County lists four boat landings in the Murrells Inlet ZIP code. The Murrells Inlet Landing is at the MarshWalk, Marina Colony is on Business 17 and Morse Landing is at the inlet's south end. Wacca Wache Landing is on the Waccamaw River.

## Does Murrells Inlet flood?
Few homes west of the US 17 bypass are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. Most homes on the creek side are. In that zone, a lender requires flood insurance.

On the creek side, about 1 in 9 of the houses on the marsh are in FEMA's V zone, where waves are expected in a big storm. A flood policy costs the most there.

### What flood insurance costs here
The middle federal flood policy on a house cost about $590 a year on the Georgetown side and about $580 on the Horry side. On the Georgetown side, a house in FEMA's A zone, the high-risk zone away from the waves, paid about $1,080. A house in the V zone, where FEMA expects waves, paid about $2,160.
Most of the flood policies on Georgetown-side houses are on homes outside the high-risk zone. Before you offer, we pull the flood zone and an insurance quote for the house. Our pages on coastal insurance and finding out whether a house has flooded show what we look at.

## Can you rent out a house in Murrells Inlet?
It depends on the HOA papers and the county zoning for that lot. An HOA can forbid or limit rentals in its papers, and almost every Horry-side house for sale is in one. We read the HOA papers and check the zoning before you offer.
On the Horry side, the county asks a nightly-rental owner for a business license and tax filings, and names no rental permit. Guests pay about 12 percent in lodging taxes. On the Georgetown side, the county issues no business license, and guests pay about 11 percent. The details are on our short-term rental rules page and our accommodations tax page .

AirROI, a company that tracks Airbnb listings, counts about 480 active listings in Murrells Inlet. Its count may take in Garden City Beach homes with a Murrells Inlet address. ## How did Murrells Inlet become a seafood village?
Murrells Inlet began with the homes of two rice planters. Around 1850, Sunnyside was built for Jacob Motte Alston, and the Hermitage for Dr. Allard Belin Flagg, the master of Wachesaw plantation, on the edge of the marsh. A small settlement grew up along the marsh on their old lands.
Photo: Upstateherd
Sunnyside, built about 1850, one of the two planters' houses the creek-side village grew from.
Visitors first came for oyster roasts and fried shore dinners put on by the inlet's founding families, the Morses, Nances, Vereens, Olivers, Chandlers and Lees. That grew into the restaurants that earned the nickname "Seafood Capital." Hurricane Hugo struck the creek front in 1989, and the village rebuilt.
Georgetown County plans to dredge the inlet's creeks. In a report to the state , it estimated the cost at about $30 million.

## Murrells Inlet FAQ

### What ZIP code is Murrells Inlet?
29576. It covers the Horry side, the Georgetown side and Garden City, so the ZIP code does not tell you the county.

### Is Murrells Inlet part of Myrtle Beach?
No. No part of the Murrells Inlet ZIP code is inside Myrtle Beach or any other town.

### Does Murrells Inlet have a beach?
Not on the creek side. Huntington Beach State Park and Garden City Beach are the nearest beaches.

### What schools serve Murrells Inlet?
Horry-side homes are zoned for the St. James schools of Horry County Schools. Georgetown-side homes are zoned for the Waccamaw schools of the Georgetown County School District. We look up the assigned schools for any home you like.

A 1.3-mile Boardwalk, golf, a large hospital and the airport are all inside the city. Where you buy depends on whether you will live here or rent by the night.

The short answer
Buy a house if you will live here. About 3 in 4 houses in the city are their owners' main homes, and almost none may be rented by the night. Buy an oceanfront condo if you want to rent it to visitors: about 3 in 4 condos are in zones where the city allows nightly rentals.
Houses in the city resold for about $540,000 in the middle, and their prices are steady. Condos resold for about $175,000, and their prices are falling .

## What is it like to live in Myrtle Beach?
Myrtle Beach is a city of about 40,900 people on the ocean. About 15 percent more people live here than in 2020.

- The Boardwalk. Downtown, the Boardwalk is about 1.3 miles long, beside the ocean. It has a raised wooden boardwalk, a wide section for entertainment, and a winding walk along the ocean.

- A large hospital. Grand Strand Medical Center is inside the city, about a mile from the ocean. It has a heart surgery program and a trauma center for the most serious injuries.

- The airport. Myrtle Beach International Airport is inside the city too, less than 2 miles from the ocean. It has nonstop flights to more than 50 cities.

- Golf and shops. Two golf clubs, Pine Lakes and The Dunes, are in the older neighborhoods described below . The Market Common, on the south end, has shops, restaurants, a movie theater and two parks.

### What is the off season like?
Quieter, not closed. In the off season, nothing closes except tourist attractions and water parks.
Hotels, restaurants and other leisure businesses in the county had about 30 percent more workers in July than in January last year.

## Where should you live in Myrtle Beach?
In one of three parts of the city where 7 in 10 or more of the houses are their owners' main homes: Grande Dunes, The Market Common or the older neighborhoods near the golf clubs. Or in a condo, on the oceanfront or off it. For a house near $300,000, look at the two smaller neighborhoods after part 3. To pick a neighborhood by what you want close to home, see the best neighborhoods in Myrtle Beach .

### 1 Grande Dunes: on the Waterway, with a beach club
Grande Dunes is a planned community on both sides of the Intracoastal Waterway, the inland water route behind the beach. Every homeowner gets a free household membership to the Grande Dunes Ocean Club . It has a large pool, a dining room, classes and clubs, and its own way onto the beach.
The community also has a public marina, a public golf course with holes along the water, a private members' golf course and a tennis club.
About 4 in 5 houses here are their owners' main homes. Houses, villas and townhouses resold for about $880,000 in the middle, the highest of the parts in this guide.

### 2 The Market Common: shops, a lake and parks
The Market Common is a town center with shops, restaurants and a movie theater, and apartments above the stores. It was built on land that was the Myrtle Beach Air Force Base. Our Market Common guide covers its neighborhoods, what homes there cost and the airport next door.
Grand Park and Valor Park are next to the shops. They have a lake with a 1.1-mile path around it, sports fields, picnic areas, fishing spots and Savannah's Playground, built for children of all abilities.

U.S. government aerial photo
The Market Common from the air. The homes outlined in orange are next to the shops and to the lake and ball fields of Grand Park.

About 2,500 houses are in the neighborhoods around it, among them Emmens Preserve, The Reserve, Sanctuary at Withers Preserve and Belle Harbor. About 6 in 7 are their owners' main homes, the highest share in this guide. Houses, villas and townhouses here resold for about $500,000 in the middle.
The city allows nightly rentals in the town center's zone, which includes a few hundred of these houses. It does not allow them in the other neighborhoods around it. Each neighborhood's HOA can still ban them, and we read its rules for you.

### 3 The older neighborhoods: golf and streets by the ocean
These neighborhoods are built around two golf clubs. Pine Lakes Country Club opened in 1927 as Myrtle Beach's first golf course. The Dunes Golf and Beach Club , on the ocean, hosts a PGA Tour event, the Myrtle Beach Classic.
Myrtle Heights, Oak Park, Forest Dunes and Northwood are here too. On some streets, the houses face the beach across wide lawns.

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Houses on wide lawns facing the beach, on the older streets north of downtown Myrtle Beach.

Nightly rentals are not allowed here, and about 7 in 10 houses are their owners' main homes. Houses resold for about $550,000 in the middle, with a wide range from street to street.

### Where are the houses near $300,000?
In a few smaller neighborhoods. Houses in the city resold for about $540,000 in the middle in the past year, and only about 1 in 6 sold for $350,000 or less. Of the 869 homes for sale in the city at $300,000 or less, only 8 are houses. The rest are condos and townhouses.

Bent Oak Estates, off Pridgen Road, had the most house sales at $350,000 or less. It has about 150 houses, about a mile from the beach and from the airport. About 7 in 10 are their owners' main homes.
Meridian and Summit at Meridian, west of the airport, are one planned development of 513 houses. Of the city's zoning districts with 50 or more houses, it has the highest share in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. Nightly rentals are not allowed in any of the three.
For one Myrtle Beach neighborhood in detail, see our Plantation Point guide .

### 4 A condo on the oceanfront
You can live in a condo too. Nearly every oceanfront condo building is where the city allows nightly rentals, so most of your neighbors there will be guests. Only about 1 in 18 condos there is someone's main home.
Off the oceanfront, where nightly rentals are not allowed, about 1 in 3 condos is its owner's main home. Those condos resold for about $270,000 in the middle, more than oceanfront condos, but there were only a few dozen sales. The oceanfront buildings are next.

## Can you rent a home by the night in Myrtle Beach?
Most condos, yes. Almost every house, no. Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, nightly rentals are legal only in the zones where the city allows them, and any stay shorter than 90 days counts.
Those zones include most of the oceanfront hotel and condo strip, the Broadway at the Beach area, stretches of the US 17 Bypass and US 501, and The Market Common's town center. They are the orange areas on the map .
The city bans nightly rentals in every zone for homes, except one zone set aside for visitor stays. A house outside the allowed zones cannot be switched over to nightly rentals. Breaking the rule is a misdemeanor, with a fine, jail time or both for each violation.
Which homes in the City of Myrtle Beach can rent by the night Kind of home Homes in the city Can rent by the night
Condos About 16,900 About 3 in 4
Houses About 10,300 About 4 in 100
Villas and townhouses About 850 About 3 in 5

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Houses and condo towers on the same beach in Myrtle Beach. The houses on the left are in a zone where nightly rentals are not allowed. The towers on the right are in one where they are.
The homes for sale today split the same way. Nearly every oceanfront condo for sale is in an allowed zone. Only about 1 in 5 houses and townhouses for sale in the city is.
Fewer than 30 houses in the zones for homes may still be rented by the night, because they were rented that way before the current zoning. No new ones can be added.

### If a listing says short-term rentals are allowed, can you rent it nightly?
Not always. 35 houses and townhouses for sale in the city say so in the listing. We checked each of them against our map, and 3 are not in an allowed zone. Many HOAs also ban rentals of any length. We check the zone and the HOA's rules for any home you like, and we leave out the homes where your plan is not allowed.

### What does a nightly rental need?
A city business license . Every rental in the city needs one, short or long, and its fee is based on the rent you collect.
Guests pay about 13 percent in lodging taxes on top of each stay under 90 days. When a guest books through Airbnb, Airbnb collects these taxes for the state, the county and the city. On a booking you take yourself, you collect and pay them.

## What are oceanfront condos like in Myrtle Beach?
About 460 condos in oceanfront buildings inside the city resold in the past year. They range from hotel-style studios to three-bedroom condos. For a one-bedroom on the oceanfront, plan on about $160,000, the middle asking price today.
Building by building, the fees, sale prices and units for sale are on our oceanfront condo buildings page . The Palace Resort has its own guide , with its fees by unit size.
The lowest prices are for studios of about 400 square feet at Tides, Driftwood and Oasis. Many of these buildings have a rental program for their owners.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Oceanfront condo towers south of downtown Myrtle Beach, near three of the busiest buildings in the table above. This stretch is in a zone where nightly rentals are allowed.
Most buyers here live out of state. About 3 in 4 buyers of these oceanfront condos have their tax bill mailed outside South Carolina.

### Can you get a loan on an oceanfront condo?
Yes, but in many of these buildings not the most common kind. Fannie Mae will not back a loan in a building managed like a hotel: with a front desk, daily cleaning, or a rule that owners put their unit in the rental program.
Our preferred lender can tell you which loans work in the building you like. At closing, buyers usually also pay an HOA transfer fee and a few months of HOA dues in advance.

## Does an oceanfront condo in Myrtle Beach pay for itself?
At typical figures, it covers its running costs and property tax, with about $8,100 a year left. That money must pay the HOA fee, a policy on the unit itself and any loan.
For the example below, we used the middle asking price for a one-bedroom on the oceanfront, about $160,000. We used the income of a typical one-bedroom nightly rental in the Myrtle Beach market, not this unit's own.

## Are Myrtle Beach home prices dropping?
For condos, yes. The typical condo value in Myrtle Beach is about 14 percent below its high in 2024, and it is still falling. For houses, no: the typical house value has stayed about the same since 2022.
Typical home value in Myrtle Beach, houses and condos
- Houses

- Condos

Zillow's typical value, monthly from January 2019. Houses here means single-family homes.
Condos also sell far more slowly than houses. At the past year's pace, it would take about a year and a half to sell every condo for sale now.
About 18 months to sell every condo for sale in the city, at the past year's pace
About 4 months to sell every house and townhouse for sale in the city

That gives a condo buyer room to negotiate . On the house side, there are fewer homes for sale than buyers in a year.
In the past year, condos in the city resold for about $175,000 in the middle: half sold for more, half for less. Houses resold for about $540,000.

## Is a Myrtle Beach address in the City of Myrtle Beach?
Usually not. About 3 in 4 houses and buildings with a Myrtle Beach mailing address are outside the city limits. Outside the city, the county's rental rules apply, not the city's.
Carolina Forest and Forestbrook are almost all outside the city, and Socastee is entirely outside it. Our Carolina Forest guide covers that area.
North Myrtle Beach is a separate city. A short-term rental there needs a business license, and for now there is no special zoning or permit process beyond it. Our North Myrtle Beach guide covers it.

## What do property tax and flood insurance cost in Myrtle Beach?
Inside the city, a second home or rental pays almost four times the property tax of a home you live in. You apply for the lower rate on the home you live in, and our property tax guide shows how.

A $540,000 house About $2,180 About $8,250
A $175,000 condo About $710 About $2,670

### Will you need flood insurance?
For most houses, no. Only about 1 in 23 houses in the city is in the high-risk flood zone of FEMA, the Federal Emergency Management Agency. About 1 in 4 condos is, many of them at the ocean's edge.
In the high-risk zone, your lender will require flood insurance. On a house there, it usually costs about $800 a year. Outside that zone, federal rules do not require it, and a policy usually costs about $600.
A condo's HOA insures the building itself and adds the cost to the HOA fee.

## What are the pros and cons of Myrtle Beach?
The good points are the house neighborhoods, the beach and the price of a condo. The hard ones are the condo market, the season and the flood zone at the ocean.

### Pros

- The house neighborhoods are mostly owners' main homes.

- The beach, the Boardwalk, golf, a large hospital and the airport are all inside the city.

- Condos cost far less than houses, a way to own at the beach for less.

- More people live in the city every year.

### Cons

- Condo prices are falling, and condos take far longer to sell than houses. We help you pick the building and negotiate the price.

- Rental income comes mostly in summer. We plan the year with you before you buy.

- Many oceanfront condos are in the high-risk flood zone. We check the flood zone and the building's insurance for you.

- Most houses cannot be rented by the night. We check the zone of any address you send us.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach real estate FAQ

### Can you do short-term rentals in Myrtle Beach?
Inside the city, only in the zones where the city allows them, which hold most condos and almost no houses. The city bans rentals under 90 days in every zone for homes, except one zone set aside for visitor stays.

### Is Myrtle Beach a buyer's market?
For condos, yes: there are about 18 months of condos for sale, and prices are falling. For houses, no: there are about 4 months of houses for sale.

### Is Carolina Forest in Myrtle Beach?
No. Carolina Forest has a Myrtle Beach address, but only about 1 in 75 houses and buildings in its ZIP code, 29579, is inside the city.

### What is the property tax on a second home in Myrtle Beach?
About $1,528 a year for every $100,000 of the county's value inside the city. A home you live in pays about $404.

### What is the difference between Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach?
Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach are two separate cities with different rental rules. Myrtle Beach allows nightly rentals only in some zones. North Myrtle Beach, for now, asks only for a business license, with no special zoning or permit process beyond it.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Its own city at the north end of the Grand Strand, made from four beach towns in 1968, with its own rental rules and city tax.

The short answer
North Myrtle Beach has about nine miles of beach and eight parts, each suited to a different buyer. For a boat behind the house, look in Cherry Grove. For Main Street and a maritime forest, look in Ocean Drive. For a house near the ocean for less, look in Crescent Beach or Windy Hill. For newer houses and little flood zone, look across the waterway or west of US 17.
A typical resold house sold for about $565,000 in the past year, from about $410,000 in Crescent Beach to $725,000 in Tilghman Beach. Nightly rentals need a yearly city business license, with no special rental zoning or permit.

## Which part of North Myrtle Beach should you look in?
The city has eight parts a buyer can tell apart, and each gives you something the others do not. Five run along the ocean; the other three lie inland. Under each one are the homes for sale there now.
On the ocean, from north to south

- Cherry Grove A dock behind the house, and a pier at sunrise

- Tilghman Beach Houses by the ocean, most of them the owner's main home

- Ocean Drive Main Street and its shag clubs

- Crescent Beach A house near the ocean for less, with little flood zone

- Atlantic Beach A separate town, not part of the city

- Windy Hill Beach houses at some of the lower prices by the ocean

Inland

- Little River Neck Woods and trail rides north of the Cherry Grove marsh

- West of US 17 Newer houses a few minutes' drive from the beach

- Across the waterway Four golf courses, a marina and almost no flood zone

### Cherry Grove: a dock behind the house, and a pier at sunrise
Cherry Grove is the part for a boat at the back door. Channels were dug into its marsh in the 1970s, and about 680 houses now back onto them or the marsh edge. Many have a dock behind the house , and boats reach the ocean through Hog Inlet.
U.S. government aerial photo
Cherry Grove from above, 2023 aerial: houses on the dug channels, many with a dock behind them, the marsh, the boat ramp and Heritage Shores.
From the city's boat ramp on 53rd Avenue North, you can paddle a kayak about a mile and a half through Hog Inlet, past pelicans and ospreys, to the empty beach on Waties Island. People walk the shore there looking for shells and fossil shark teeth, including megalodon teeth.
Walk 985 feet out on Cherry Grove Pier to the two-story deck at the end, where people watch the sun rise over the ocean and look for dolphins, then eat at the Driftwood restaurant on the pier. In 1964 a fisherman landed a 1,780-pound tiger shark from this pier, and the pier still lists it as a world record.
Photo: Melikamp
Cherry Grove from a height in 2012: older low beach houses beside mid-rise condos, the marsh behind them, and Cherry Grove Pier.
On the Fourth of July, the city puts on a free fireworks show over the ocean at the pier. People carry beach chairs onto the sand to watch it, after checking the tide. Heritage Shores Nature Preserve has walking paths on an island in the marsh, and the Russell Burgess Coastal Preserve has a boardwalk.
A house on the channels resold for about $715,000 at the middle (38 sales), and elsewhere in Cherry Grove about $665,000. The trade-off is flood insurance: almost every house here is in FEMA's high-risk flood zone, channel houses included. Only about 1 in 4 houses is the owner's main home.

Send me homes in Cherry Grove

### Tilghman Beach: houses by the ocean, most of them main homes
Tilghman Beach suits a buyer who wants a house by the ocean among owners who make it their main home. About 2 in 3 houses here are, the most of any beach part.
U.S. government aerial photo
Tilghman Beach from above, 2023 aerial: a row of houses along the ocean, and streets of houses around the lakes behind them.
From about May to mid-August, loggerhead turtles about three feet long come up this sand at night and lay about 120 eggs each. Volunteers from the Sea Turtle Patrol watch over and protect the nests, and 45 to 65 days later the hatchlings dig out at night and head for the moonlit water.
Tilghman Beach grew from one large tract that Charles T. Tilghman Jr. developed in 1948. Its houses sell for the most of any part. In Tilghman Estates, its largest neighborhood, the middle of 19 house resales was about $1.05 million. Seabrook Plantation resold for about $750,000, the middle of 9 sales.
Most of its homes in the flood zone are condos, not houses.

Send me homes in Tilghman Beach

### Ocean Drive: Main Street and its shag clubs
Ocean Drive is the part with Main Street, which runs back from the ocean. McLean Park, built around a small lake, is about a 5-minute walk from it.
U.S. government aerial photo
Ocean Drive from above, 2023 aerial: Main Street running back from the beach, McLean Park and its lake, and the condo towers along the ocean.
The shag is South Carolina's state dance. In the old beach towns of Ocean Drive and Crescent Beach, a pavilion and amusement park drew crowds to dance it.
Postcard, 1941, public domain
The pavilion at Ocean Drive Beach on a 1941 postcard, with "Dancing" painted on its end wall.
It is still danced on Main Street, all year:

- Every night. At Fat Harold's Beach Club, a DJ plays beach music from 7. Couples take shag lessons on Monday nights, and Tuesday night is for learning the state dance.

- January, April and September. Thousands of shag dancers fill the clubs on Main Street for the Society of Stranders: Midwinter Break, Spring Safari and Fall Migration.

- March. People set up beach chairs and golf carts along Main Street by 8:30 a.m. for a St. Patrick's Day parade of more than 100 entries, then stay for a free festival until 4.

- November. The Carolina Beach Music Awards weekend brings beach music bands to the stages of the shag clubs.

The Ingram Dunes Nature Preserve, which the city calls its last maritime forest, has dunes 30 feet tall and a half-mile trail. Houses in the Ingram Beach neighborhood resold for about $1.35 million at the middle (12 sales).
Prices here spread wide: the middle half of house resales ran from about $385,000 to $980,000. Most of its homes in the flood zone are oceanfront condos; about 1 in 10 houses is in it.

Send me homes in Ocean Drive

### Crescent Beach: a house near the ocean for less
Crescent Beach suits a buyer who wants a house near the ocean at a lower price. Its houses resold for the least of the beach parts, and only about 1 house in 100 is in the flood zone, the fewest of the beach parts.
The loggerheads nest on this beach too, and the Sea Turtle Patrol's volunteers watch over the nests until the hatchlings head for the water.
Houses on the original Crescent Beach lots resold for more. The county records those lots under two names, and their middle prices were about $665,000 and $718,000.
The 18th and Edge pocket park is its own small green space. Crescent Beach ends at Atlantic Beach, a separate town that did not join the city.
U.S. government aerial photo
Atlantic Beach, outlined, is a separate town between Crescent Beach and Windy Hill, from US 17 to the ocean (2023 aerial).

Send me homes in Crescent Beach

### Windy Hill: beach houses south of Atlantic Beach
Windy Hill suits a buyer who wants a beach house at one of the lower prices by the ocean. Local history says it got its name in 1791, when George Washington rode this stretch of beach on a windy day and his hat kept blowing off.
U.S. government aerial photo
Windy Hill from above, 2023 aerial: streets of houses under the trees, condo buildings along the ocean, and a marsh creek at the left.
Investors from Conway built it up after World War II. Houses on the original Windy Hill Beach lots resold for about $439,000 at the middle (10 sales). Most of its houses are outside the flood zone; most of its condos are in it.
Yow Park and the 41st Avenue South pocket park are its neighborhood parks.

Send me homes in Windy Hill

### Little River Neck: woods and trail rides north of the marsh
Little River Neck suits a buyer who wants a house among owners who live there. It lies north of the Cherry Grove marsh, along Little River Neck Road.
Inlet Point Plantation Stables is two miles down a one-lane dirt road through the woods. From there, an hour-long trail ride passes deer, wild turkeys and an alligator sunning by a lake, follows the Intracoastal Waterway across from Calabash, and ends at the marsh behind Waties Island.
The Open Space Institute has bought more than 600 acres on and around Waties Island and the mainland at Little River Neck. The state plans to make parts of it a new state park and parts a Heritage Trust preserve, open to the public.
Tidewater Plantation is its largest neighborhood, and about 8 in 10 of its houses are the owner's main home. Builders are still selling new houses here: 53 in the past year. The Neck also holds most of the city's manufactured homes, about 660 of 800.

Send me homes in Little River Neck

### West of US 17: newer houses a few minutes from the beach
West of US 17 suits a buyer who wants a newer house close to the beach, with little flood zone. From a typical house here, the drive to Ocean Boulevard is about 4 minutes.
U.S. government aerial photo
West of US 17 from above, 2023 aerial: new streets cleared for houses, Central Park's ball fields, and US 17.
Every Monday night in summer, Barefoot Landing, on the waterway at US 17, has a fireworks show at 10 p.m.
Builders sold 94 new houses here in the past year, and the city's 20-acre Central Park is in this part. Chestnut Greens is the largest neighborhood, and its houses resold for about $515,000 at the middle.
Sunset Harbour resold for about $760,000 (9 sales), but 68 of its homes are in the high-risk flood zone. Condos here cost the least in the city, about $175,000 at the middle.

Send me homes west of US 17

### Across the waterway: golf, newer houses and almost no flood zone
Across the Intracoastal Waterway suits a buyer who wants golf, a newer house and almost no flood zone: 2 homes of about 5,200 are in it. More of the city's new houses sold here than anywhere else.
Barefoot Resort's four golf courses were designed by Greg Norman, Davis Love III, Tom Fazio and Pete Dye. Seven holes of the Norman course run along the waterway, and the resort has a deep-water marina with a bar and grill on the water.
U.S. government aerial photo
Barefoot Landing on the Intracoastal Waterway at US 17, 2023 aerial, with the neighborhoods across the waterway on the far bank.
Barefoot Landing, the shops and restaurants on the waterway at US 17, is about 11 minutes by car from Main Street. From a typical house here, the drive to Ocean Boulevard is about 11 minutes.
Houses in Grande Dunes North resold for about $374,000 at the middle, and in Waterside for about $385,000. We pull the HOA papers and fees for any house here.

## What is North Myrtle Beach like to live in?
North Myrtle Beach has about nine miles of ocean beach, running south-west from Hog Inlet. Cherry Grove, Ocean Drive, Crescent Beach and Windy Hill voted to become one city in 1968.
From the 1970s, condo and hotel towers began replacing houses on the oceanfront. Today condos outnumber houses about 3 to 2.
About 18,800 people lived in the city at the 2020 Census, about 37 percent more than in 2010. Close to half its homes were kept for seasonal or vacation use. Our Little River guide compares that share with the towns nearby.

### How is North Myrtle Beach different from Myrtle Beach?
North Myrtle Beach is not part of Myrtle Beach. It is a separate city in Horry County, with its own city tax and its own rules for nightly rentals. The Myrtle Beach oceanfront, at the SkyWheel, is about 30 minutes south by car without traffic.
The map shows the drives from Main Street to the pier, McLeod Seacoast hospital and Barefoot Landing. The airport is about 35 minutes away and Grand Strand Medical Center about 20. Summer traffic on US 17 makes those drives longer.

Drive times by car from Main Street at Ocean Drive, without traffic. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.

## What do homes cost in North Myrtle Beach?
A typical resold house in North Myrtle Beach sold for about $565,000 in the past year; half sold between about $420,000 and $740,000. A condo sold for about $310,000, and a new house from a builder for about $440,000.
Condos sell for about the same in every part along the ocean, about $310,000 to $360,000. Houses differ by part far more. More than half the homes sold here in the past year went to a buyer whose tax bill goes to another state.

## Does North Myrtle Beach flood?
About 1 in 3 homes in North Myrtle Beach is in FEMA's high-risk flood zone, more of them condos than houses. The part you choose decides most of it.
Homes in FEMA's high-risk flood zone: most of Cherry Grove, almost none across the waterway Part Share of homes in the zone

Cherry Grove 88%
Windy Hill 54%
Ocean Drive 52%
Tilghman Beach 33%
Little River Neck 10%
Crescent Beach 10%
West of US 17 7%
Across the waterway 2 of 5,200

Every home in the county's parcel records, tested against FEMA's flood map as the county carries it.
The high-risk zone has two kinds here. The VE zone is the oceanfront, where storm waves add to the flood; the A zones are the rest of it.

### Do you need flood insurance in North Myrtle Beach?
A federally regulated lender must require flood insurance when the building is in FEMA's high-risk zone, and any lender can ask for it elsewhere. In ZIP code 29582, which covers most of the city, a federal flood policy on a house usually cost:
A federal flood policy on a house in ZIP code 29582 Where the house is A year, at the middle
Outside the flood zone About $600
In the flood zone, back from the ocean (A zone) About $1,460
In the flood zone on the oceanfront, where waves reach (VE zone) About $2,150

A new policy takes effect 30 days after you apply and pay; it can start sooner when you buy it with your home loan.
Outside the zone is not the same as never flooded. Our page on how to find out if a house flooded shows every record we use, and our coastal insurance page explains each policy.

## What does a home in North Myrtle Beach cost to own each year?
A typical house you live in costs about $8,400 a year to own, before any mortgage. A typical condo costs more, about $11,000, because of the condo fee.

As a second home or rental, the tax is three times as much. The house then costs about $13,000 a year and the condo about $14,000, if the other costs stay the same.
The tax is on the county's value of the home, and a sale resets that value toward the price you pay. You must apply for the lower rate on a home you live in; our property tax page shows how.

### Where the other figures come from
Home insurance is the middle that Horry County owners pay for a house they live in; half pay between about $1,300 and $3,000. On the beach side of US 17, an insurer may leave wind and hail out of a policy. The owner can then buy that cover separately, for example from the state's wind and hail association.
The condo fee is the middle fee of condos for sale in ZIP code 29582, about $700 a month. It may also pay the insurance on the shared building. About half the houses for sale in that ZIP code list no HOA fee.
Upkeep is the average owners spend a year in the South Atlantic states. If you buy with us, we get you an insurance quote for the address before you make an offer. Our cost to own page compares the towns nearby.

## Can you rent out a home by the night in North Myrtle Beach?
Yes, with a city business license. Every short-term rental in the city needs one, renewed each year, and must collect lodging taxes. The city has no special zoning or rental permit beyond the license.
An HOA or the deed can still bar rentals, and we read the HOA's rules and the deed before you offer. A rental owner here has five things to get right:

- The license. A city business license, renewed every year.

- The parking number. When you apply or renew, you report the parking spaces on the property's own land. That number is the most cars guests can park there. It goes in every ad and rental agreement and is posted inside. Where an HOA or the deed limits parking, the owner certifies the number matches.

- The lodging taxes. Guests pay 12 percent on a stay under 90 days, split between the state, the city and the county.

- The trash days. The city collects a rental's trash on its regular day plus Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Recycling goes out only on the regular day.

- The quiet hours. They run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m., and fireworks are banned everywhere in the city, with a $310 ticket for a first offense.

Example. On a $2,000 week, a guest pays about $240 in lodging taxes, which the owner collects and pays to the state, the city and the county.

### Is North Myrtle Beach changing its rental rules?
The city has held workshops and public sessions on possible new short-term rental rules. Its rental page lists no new rental ordinance adopted, and the license rule is the one in force. Earlier tries, a moratorium on large rental houses and a draft ordinance, failed.
Our pages on short-term rental rules by town , filing the lodging taxes and what a nightly rental earns go further.

## What are the pros and cons of living in North Myrtle Beach?
The good points are the beach, the water, the golf and the choice of parts. The hard ones are the flood zone at the north end, the condo fees, and how few houses by the ocean are main homes.

### Pros

- About nine miles of beach, Main Street at Ocean Drive, and the marsh parks and boat ramp at Cherry Grove.

- Houses on the Cherry Grove channels, with water behind the house.

- Four golf courses at Barefoot Resort, across the waterway.

- Almost no flood zone across the waterway, and about 7 in 100 homes west of US 17.

### Cons

- Cherry Grove is almost all in the high-risk flood zone, and its flood policies cost more. We check the flood zone, the elevation and the flood history before you offer.

- Most houses by the ocean are second homes or rentals, and fewer neighbors live there all year. Inland, about 3 in 4 houses are the owner's main home.

- Condo fees are high: the middle condo for sale lists about $700 a month. We read the condo's budget and rules before you offer.

- Summer traffic on US 17 slows every drive. We time the drives from any house you like.

## North Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is North Myrtle Beach part of Myrtle Beach?
No. North Myrtle Beach is its own city in Horry County, South Carolina. Four beach towns joined to form it in 1968, and it has its own city tax and rental rules. The Myrtle Beach oceanfront is about 30 minutes south by car.

### What are the sections of North Myrtle Beach?
The four old beach towns are Cherry Grove, Ocean Drive, Crescent Beach and Windy Hill. Tilghman Beach, Little River Neck, the mainland west of US 17 and the neighborhoods across the waterway make eight parts.

### Can you drive a golf cart in North Myrtle Beach?
Yes, from sunrise to sunset, on city streets posted 35 mph or less, with a state permit sticker from the DMV and a licensed driver. A cart may cross Ocean Boulevard, 27th Avenue South, US 17 and Sea Mountain Highway, but not drive along them.

### Are dogs allowed on the beach in North Myrtle Beach?
Yes, on a leash. From May 15 to Labor Day they must be off the beach from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. In that season the beach takes umbrellas only, no tents or canopies.

### What does it cost to own a home in North Myrtle Beach each year?
As your home, before any mortgage, about $8,400 for a typical house and about $11,000 for a typical condo. That covers tax, insurance, a flood policy outside the zone, the condo fee and upkeep.

### What is the property tax in North Myrtle Beach?
On a house the county values at $565,000, about $2,500 a year as your home and about $7,500 as a second home or rental.

### Is North Myrtle Beach safe?
We do not rate any place as safe or unsafe. We pull the reported crime figures for the area around any house you ask about.

### Which schools serve North Myrtle Beach?
Horry County Schools assigns schools by address. North Myrtle Beach is one of its nine attendance areas, with North Myrtle Beach High School, North Myrtle Beach Middle School and Ocean Drive Elementary. We look up the assigned schools for any house you like.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Pawleys Island is the south end of the Grand Strand: old beach houses on an island, with most homes that share its name on the mainland.

The short answer
Pawleys Island is a quiet beach town of about 480 houses on a barrier island, a narrow strip of land just off the coast. The ocean is in front, and a tidal creek and salt marsh are behind. The middle of the island is a historic district of old wooden summer houses, and beach parking is free.
Island houses rarely come up for sale: 10 sold at a market price in the past year, and over three years one sold for about $2.45 million at the middle. Most homes with a Pawleys Island address are on the mainland, where a house sold for about $580,000 to $675,000. Every island house but one is in a high-risk flood zone.

Island houses rarely list. We watch the island and call you.
