## Is Pawleys Island an island, and what are its four parts like?
Yes. Pawleys Island is a barrier island, less than 4 miles long and mostly one house wide, with salt marsh between it and the mainland. Two short causeways, the North Causeway and the South Causeway, cross the marsh.
The Town of Pawleys Island is the island itself. The mainland around it has no town government; it is run by Georgetown County. Much of it shares the island's name and its ZIP code, 29585, so a Pawleys Island address can be a house on the mainland. This page covers four parts, from the beach inland.

The shaded strip inside the dashed line is the Town of Pawleys Island: the island and the marsh behind it. The orange lines are the two causeways. Aerial: USDA NAIP via The National Map (USGS), public domain. Lines: Georgetown County GIS. Labels: Chapter3 Realty.

### Pawleys Island, the town The beach in front, the creek behind
The island is one long strip of houses between the ocean and the creek. About 220 houses face the beach. The rest look onto the marsh and the creek, or stand on the streets between. In the middle of the island are the old wooden summer houses of the historic district.
The water is close on both sides. People fish in the surf and crab from the two marsh bridges, and the island has three boat ramps. Beach parking is free: the south-end lot is the largest free beach lot in Georgetown County, and 8 other public accesses add about 141 spaces. Dogs are allowed on the beach all year, on a leash on summer days.
U.S. government aerial photo
Pawleys Island at the North Causeway from above: the salt marsh, the causeway, and the rows of houses between the marsh and the beach.
The pace is slow. The speed limit is 25 mph, and golf carts are allowed on island roads. There are no lifeguards and no fireworks. The town still calls itself by its old nickname, "arrogantly shabby".
Over three years an island house sold for about $2.45 million at the middle, more on the ocean and less on the creek side. At our last count, only 2 island houses were for sale, each asking about $3 million or more.
Send me the Pawleys Island houses for sale now

### Litchfield The beach north of the island, and more houses for sale
North of the island, Litchfield runs along the beach on the ocean side of the highway. It has about 1,200 houses, and more of them are lived in all year: about 4 in 10 are their owner's main home, twice the island's share.

- A bike path The Waccamaw Neck Bikeway runs along US 17 through Litchfield and north to Murrells Inlet.

- Huntington Beach State Park Farther north: 3 miles of beach, and Atalaya, the old winter home of Archer and Anna Hyatt Huntington.

- Brookgreen Gardens Opposite the park. The Huntingtons set it up as a nature preserve to show her sculpture and the work of other sculptors.

- A landmark Atalaya and Brookgreen Gardens together are a National Historic Landmark.

More houses sell here: 50 in the past year, at about $1.25 million at the middle. Its oceanfront houses sell for more than the island's: about $3.6 million at the middle over three years. Almost all of Litchfield's ocean side is in a high-risk flood zone too.
Get the homes for sale in Litchfield

### The mainland behind the island Shops, groceries and golf near the causeways
Between US 17 and the marsh, south of Litchfield, are about 1,200 houses, and most are their owner's main home. This is where the island shops, a few minutes by car from Town Hall.

- The Hammock Shops On the highway near the North Causeway: more than 20 shops and two restaurants, Local and BisQit.

- Groceries Two grocery stores on the highway.

- Golf Pawleys Plantation has its own course.

- A bike path The Waccamaw Neck Bikeway runs north from here.

The Pawleys Island hammock The Hammock Shops take their name from the Original Hammock Shop, which has made them since 1938. They say a riverboat captain who carried rice between Georgetown and Waverly Mills made the first one in 1889, to sleep cooler on summer nights. It was woven of cotton rope, with no thick knots where he lay. The shops still sell handmade hammocks. A house in a community with a homeowners association comes with the association's rules on rentals and changes, and we read its papers for you.
A house here sold for about $675,000 at the middle in the past year. About a third of the houses are in a high-risk flood zone.
Get the homes for sale behind Pawleys Island

### West of US 17 Most of the homes, most of the golf, the lowest prices
West of US 17 are most of the homes with a Pawleys Island address: about 4,800 houses, and most are their owner's main home. Most of the area's golf courses are here. We count nine on the map, among them Caledonia, True Blue, Heritage and Litchfield Country Club.
The grocery store nearest the island is on this side of the highway, less than 5 minutes by car from Town Hall. Only about 1 in 20 houses here is in a high-risk flood zone.
A house here sold for about $580,000 at the middle in the past year, and a condo for about $320,000.

## What is it like to live on Pawleys Island all year?
Photo: Phoebe
A walkway and a covered platform over the creek on the marsh side of Pawleys Island.
Winter on the island is quiet. On Census Day, in April, most of the island's homes were seasonal or vacation homes. The town's lodging tax shows when guests come: in 2024, almost 6 in 10 of its dollars came in from July to September, and about 2 in 100 from January to March.
Winter days are mild.

- About 57° January's normal high

- About 37° January's normal low

Those are NOAA's normals at its weather station at Brookgreen Gardens, about 6 miles north. From October through April, dogs may run on the beach off the leash, if the owner carries one and the dog comes when called. Winter is also outside hurricane season, which runs from June 1 to November 30.
That makes winter the easiest time for work on a house: rentals are fewest and the storm season is over.
Behind the island and west of the highway, about 3 in 4 houses or more are their owner's main home. On the island about 1 in 5 is.

### Where to eat
The town says island night life is dining out, long talks on screened porches, a mainland shop and a walk on the beach. On the map we count 20 restaurants from Litchfield south past the causeways, and 19 of them are within about 650 feet of US 17. Among them are the Pawleys Island Tavern, Frank's and Frank's Outback, and Local at the Hammock Shops.

## How often does a house on Pawleys Island come up for sale?
Rarely. In the past five years at least 44 of the island's 480 houses were bought at a market price, about 1 in 11. In Litchfield and west of the highway, houses were bought about twice as often.
Houses bought at a market price in the past five years Part Share of houses

Pawleys Island, the town About 1 in 11
Litchfield, ocean side of US 17 About 1 in 5
West of US 17 About 1 in 5

At least: the county keeps only the last deed on each house, so a house sold and later deeded to a trust counts as not sold. That is true in every part. Georgetown County records; a market sale is a deed of $10,000 or more.
Island houses tend to stay in families. On most of them, the last recorded transfer was not a sale. The deed shows under $1,000: the kind of deed used to pass a house to heirs or a trust, or to move it into a company.

The town says many houses in its historic district belong to the third, fourth or fifth generation of one family. About 1 in 10 island houses has not changed hands at all since before 2000. The island is also built out: in seven years, only about a dozen new buildings went up.

## Why do the old Pawleys Island houses look the way they do?
The old Pawleys Island houses were built as summer houses for rice planters' families, who came from May to November to escape the malaria of the rice fields. Enslaved people carried the households to the island each May, and enslaved workers built the older of the two causeways under a rice planter who became governor.
Cypress was the building material used most often. It was hewn on the mainland, and each timber was cut with Roman numerals so the house could be put together on the island. Most of the old houses stand on high brick foundations, which keep them above ordinary storm tides and let air move under the floor.
The middle of the island is on the National Register of Historic Places as the Pawleys Island Historic District.

### The town's historic rules
In 2026 the whole island became a local historic district. A house built in 1954 or earlier can be put on the town's list of historic houses. The owner can nominate it, and so can a member of the town council or of the town's board, so a house can be nominated without its owner asking. The council decides.
A listed house needs the board's approval for changes to its outside and to be torn down, and the board can delay a demolition for up to 180 days. The listing stays with the house when it sells. No building permit is issued while a nomination is pending. A house not on the list has none of these rules. We check whether a house you like is listed or nominated.

## What does a Pawleys Island house cost to own each year?
The biggest yearly costs are property tax and insurance. Both depend most on whether the house is your main home.

### Property tax
As a second home or rental, a house pays about 3 times the property tax it pays as the home you live in. South Carolina taxes the home you live in on 4 percent of its value and any other house on 6 percent, and the tax rate on a second home is also about twice as high.
Price Main home Second home

$2,450,000 $11,220 $34,900

The tax a year, from Georgetown County's own estimate. $580,000 is the middle sale west of US 17, and $2,450,000 the island's. A second home here includes a rental.
The estimate includes the fees on the bill. The fees are $44 a year on the island. West of the highway they are $96, for storm water and household fees together. The county taxes its own appraised value, which can differ from the price. The Town of Pawleys Island levies no property tax of its own, so an island house pays the same rates as the mainland around it.

### Flood insurance
A federal flood policy on an island house that is not its owner's main home cost more than 4 times what one on a mainland house in the same ZIP code cost. As a main home, the gap is much smaller. The town's flood work earns island owners a 25 percent discount on these policies, and the prices below already include it.

## Can you rent out a house on Pawleys Island, and what do rentals take in?
Yes. Short-term rentals are allowed on Pawleys Island. Guests pay about 11 percent in lodging taxes on stays under 90 days. The town's share is filed with the town each month.
The town's lodging tax receipts show what island rentals take in. In 2024, guests paid about $27 million to stay on the island. Spread across the roughly 380 island houses that are not an owner's main home, that is about $70,000 a house for the year, before the rental company's fee and other costs.

- About $27 million Rent guests paid on the island in a year

- About $70,000 A year, on average, per house that is not a main home

That is an average. Some houses are never rented, and some of the rent is paid on the island's condos and other rooms.
On the mainland, a homeowners association can limit rentals in its own papers, and we read them for you. The rules town by town are on our short-term rental rules page . For a yearly tenant instead, see our long-term rental guide . If you are selling a rental elsewhere to buy here, a 1031 exchange can put off the tax on the sale.

## Does Pawleys Island flood, and how often do hurricanes come?
Every island house but one is in one of FEMA's high-risk flood zones. A lender making a mortgage on any of them will require flood insurance. The island's houses are split about evenly between two zones:

- About half: water and waves Rising water and storm waves are both expected here. FEMA calls it the VE zone.

- The other half: water Water rises in a big flood, but big waves are not expected. FEMA calls it the AE zone.

The south end is the most exposed. South of the South Causeway, more than 9 in 10 houses are in the VE zone. North of the North Causeway, fewer than 1 in 10 are.
FEMA's flood height for island houses is 12 to 16 feet. It is measured from a fixed survey level, not from the ground, so it is not the depth of water at a house. The town requires the floor of a new house to sit 3 feet above that.
On ordinary days, the town's flood problem is water on the roads at the highest tides of the year, the king tides. The town has adopted a drainage plan for the whole island to deal with it.

### Hurricanes
In the past 75 years, 44 storms have passed within 50 miles of the middle of the island, and 7 of them were hurricanes at their closest point. Ian passed about 5 miles away, and Matthew and Charley came closer still.
Storms that passed within 50 miles of the island, by decade
- Hazel, 1954

- Helene, 1958

- Charley, 2004

- Matthew, 2016

- Dorian, 2019

- Isaias, 2020

- Ian, 2022

Each column is a decade, from the 1950s (’50) to the 2020s (’20). Darker: storms that were hurricanes at their closest point. NOAA National Hurricane Center storm tracks (HURDAT2), 1950 to 2025, measured from the middle of the island.
Hurricane Hazel, in 1954, washed away most of the houses built on the south end after World War II. The older houses came through it, as they had come through many storms before.

## Can you rebuild an oceanfront house on Pawleys Island?
Yes, within limits that matter most at the south end. The state draws two lines along the beach. The baseline follows the top of the front dune. The setback line runs 20 feet behind it, on the land side.
On about 100 of the island's roughly 220 oceanfront houses, part of the house stands on the ocean side of the setback line. Most of them are at the south end. On Litchfield's oceanfront it is more than half of the houses.

- Part of the house, about 200 square feet or more, is past the setback line

- The house is behind it

A stretch of the south end of the island, north of the south-end parking lot. Lines: the state's current baseline and setback line. Outlines: Georgetown County's 2024 building footprints. Aerial: USDA NAIP via The National Map (USGS), public domain. Map: Chapter3 Realty.
For a house past the setback line, state law allows:

- Repair A house damaged by a storm, but not destroyed, can be repaired.

- Rebuild A house a storm destroys can be rebuilt no larger past the setback line, no wider along the beach and no farther toward the ocean than before. It moves back from the ocean where possible, and never past the baseline.

- New house A new house built partly past the setback line can have at most 5,000 square feet of heated space.

- The town's own line The town draws its own line too, the Shore Protection Line, and it is usually stricter than the state's.

Before you offer on an oceanfront house, we get the survey and see where all three lines fall on the lot.

### What the town lets you build

- Height Up to 35 feet above the town's flood height for the lot, which is 3 feet above FEMA's.

- Size Heated floor area between 2,000 and 4,000 square feet, and no more than 40 percent of the lot.

- Paving Roofs and paved areas together no more than 40 percent of the lot. Driveways are gravel, shell or crushed stone, never paved.

- Approval A new house needs the town's Architectural Review Board. Taking down a protected tree needs a town permit.

Photo: Phoebe
The north end of Pawleys Island at low tide: houses along the dune line, and the inlet at right.

### The beach in front
The town rebuilt its beach with about 1.1 million cubic yards of new sand. The plan paid for it from three sources: the town's beach fund, which is its 3 percent lodging tax on rentals, a state grant and a bank loan.
The south tip will change. Under a settlement with the Prince George community across the inlet, a new inlet is to be cut about 800 feet south of the south-end parking lot and kept inside a set zone. The town gets a right to sand for future beach work.

## Pawleys Island FAQ

### What county is Pawleys Island in?
Georgetown County, both the island and the mainland that shares its name. Its property taxes and its public schools are Georgetown County's.

### Is Pawleys Island part of Myrtle Beach?
No. The island is its own town, and the mainland around it is run by Georgetown County. Broadway at the Beach, in Myrtle Beach, is about 26 miles north by road.

### What is the ZIP code for Pawleys Island?
29585. It covers the island and most of the mainland around it, from the beach to well west of US 17.

### How many people live on Pawleys Island?
The Census counted 130 people living in the town in 2020. Most island houses are second homes or rentals, so far more people stay in the summer.

### Is Pawleys Island expensive?
On the island, yes: over three years a house sold for about $2.45 million at the middle. On the mainland, a house sold for about $580,000 to $675,000 at the middle in the past year.

### Can you drive a golf cart on Pawleys Island?
Yes, on island roads. The cart needs a state registration and a town sticker, and the address on its registration must be within 2 miles of the town limits. The driver must be 16 or older with a license. No driving at night or in the rain.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Surfside Beach is a town of about 4,200 people with a free concrete pier, summer concerts in the park and a clear line where nightly rentals stop.

The short answer
Surfside Beach is its own town of about 4,200 people, on about 2 miles of beach south of Myrtle Beach. Every home is within about 0.8 mile of the beach road.
The town has a new concrete pier, free summer concerts and golf cart parades down Ocean Boulevard. Nightly rentals are allowed only on the blocks near the ocean. The inland streets, with bigger lots under the trees, are for living in or renting by the year.

Live there, rent it, or both? Tell us. We send the homes that fit.
Send me Surfside Beach homes

## What is it like to live in Surfside Beach?
The town calls itself the Family Beach. Its center is the pier, at the ocean end of Surfside Drive.

### The pier
The town's fishing pier is all concrete and reaches 814 feet into the ocean. It opened on the town's 60th birthday, and walking on it is free.
Photo: NOAA National Geodetic Survey
The concrete pier from the air, with the beach parking lots and the streets of beach houses behind it.
The pier has two restaurants, The Whistling Duck and Surf Diner, plus an ice cream shop and a bait shop. A day of fishing is $14. From April through October it stays open until 1 a.m.

### A year of town events
The town has its own events department, and many of its events are free. Many take place at the pier, on Ocean Boulevard or in Memorial Park.

- Spring A two-day barbecue festival with a cook-off in March. A kite festival at the pier in April. The Memorial Day golf cart parade down Ocean Boulevard.

- Summer A free concert in Memorial Park, next to the library, on Sundays from 4 to 7 p.m. The Fourth of July golf cart parade, free to join.

- Fall An end-of-summer fireworks festival at the pier in September, with free shuttles from the town's parking lots.

- All season An arts and crafts market every Thursday from March to November, at Surfside Drive and Willow Drive. The Yuletide golf cart parade in December.

### Golf carts
Most trips here need a car or a golf cart. To drive a cart on the street, South Carolina law requires a DMV permit decal, liability insurance and a licensed driver 16 or older.
Carts may use only roads posted at 35 mph or less, and never the sand. A cart driven at night must have working headlights and taillights. The town passed its own golf cart ordinance in 2025.

### The beach
The town has 36 public beach accesses and 12 beach parking lots. Five accesses have wheelchair access, and beach wheelchairs are available through the town police department.
Photo: BullDawg2021
Beach houses along the sand at Surfside Beach.
An owner who lives elsewhere gets two free parking passes per household for the town's lots. The town's lots charge by the hour from March through October. Dogs stay off the beach from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., May through Labor Day.

## Is Surfside Beach part of Myrtle Beach?
No. Surfside Beach is its own town in Horry County, incorporated in 1964, with its own council, police department and beach rules. Its mailing ZIP code is 29575.
A "Surfside Beach" address does not prove a home is in the town. Of the homes for sale with that address when we counted, about two in three were outside the town limits.
Those homes are on county land, where the town's rental rules do not apply. Horry County's zoning has no limit on how long a home there may be rented, but a subdivision's recorded rules can. We read those rules for the home you like.
How the town began. Much of its land was once the Ark Plantation. The beach was later called Roach's Beach, then Floral Beach, and took the name Surfside Beach in 1952. Hurricane Hazel in 1954 destroyed 18 of the 65 houses then at the beach.

### What do you own at Ocean Lakes?
Ocean Lakes Family Campground is next to the town's north end, about 7 minutes from the pier by car, and it is not in the town. It has about 2,600 sites leased by the year.
At Ocean Lakes you buy the house, mobile home or camper on the site, not the land. The site comes with a yearly lease from the campground, and we go through it with you before you offer.

## Where can you rent by the night in Surfside Beach?
Nightly rentals are allowed only on the blocks near the ocean, the orange band on the map. The town calls them its R3 and C3 zones, and its own zoning sheet names R3 "High Density/Weekly Rental".

South of the pier

North of the pier

North of the pier, the line follows Dogwood Drive North, and houses on that street fall on both sides. South of the pier, it follows Willow Drive South for about 0.3 mile, to about 6th Avenue South. From there it follows Lakeside Drive: houses on the ocean side of Lakeside are on the rental side, and houses on its inland side are not.
At the pier, the town's entertainment district breaks the band. Inland, the green streets reach back to the commercial strip on US 17 Business. On those streets the town allows rentals of a year or more, and none under 30 days.
The gray areas are planned developments and commercial land. Each planned development has its own approved uses, so we read the approval for the parcel.

## What does it cost to own a home in Surfside Beach each year?
Besides the mortgage and home insurance, the yearly cost here is mostly property tax and flood insurance. Both depend on where the house is and how you use it.

A buyer's tax starts from the county's value, which resets toward the price at the sale. Owners who bought years ago often pay less because of the state's 15 percent cap on reassessment.

### Why a main home pays about a third as much
South Carolina does not tax the whole value of a home. For your main home, the tax rate applies to 4 percent of the county's value, and the school operating tax is skipped.
For a second home or rental, the rate applies to 6 percent of the value, with every tax. On the same home, that makes the tax about 3 times as much. Our property tax calculator has every town's rate.

### Flood insurance near the ocean and inland
From the pier to the south end of town, most homes are on the rental side. There, a typical flood policy on a house costs about $1,250 a year. On the inland streets it is about $700.
FEMA takes 15 percent off flood insurance in the town, for the town's flood rules and programs.

## Does Surfside Beach flood?
Inland, few homes are in a high-risk flood zone: 2 percent on the smaller-lot streets and 15 percent on the largest lots. Near the ocean it is most homes, and every home on the ocean side of Ocean Boulevard. To check one address, use our flood map check .
Homes in FEMA's high-risk flood zone, inland and near the ocean Where Share of homes

Inland, smaller lots 2 percent
Inland, largest lots 15 percent
The whole town 39 percent
Near the ocean 78 percent

FEMA's high-risk flood zones on Horry County's flood map, at each home's parcel.
A federally backed or regulated mortgage on a home in a high-risk zone requires flood insurance.

### The 48 percent rule
This town rule matters most for an older, low house. It covers a building whose lowest floor is below the 100-year flood level, the flood height on FEMA's map.
If repairs or improvements cost 48 percent or more of the building's value, the whole building must be raised. It goes up to that flood level plus 3 feet.
The town uses the county assessor's building value, land excluded, unless the owner submits a licensed appraisal. Half the town's homes were built before about 1985.
Before you offer on an older house near the ocean, we pull its flood zone and the county's building value. You then know how much work the rule allows before the house must be raised.

### What the storms did
The pier was first built in 1953. Hurricanes Hazel and Hugo each destroyed it, and after Hugo it was not rebuilt until 1993. Hurricane Matthew in 2016 took more than half of its length.
Our pages on finding out whether a house has flooded and coastal insurance show what else we look at.

## Can you Airbnb a house in Surfside Beach, and what does it earn?
Yes, on the blocks near the ocean, with a town business license for each rental property. The owner also files the town's hospitality fee and local accommodations tax every month, even when nothing is due.
Guests pay about 12 percent in lodging taxes on top of the rent, to the state, the county and the town. You collect it and send it on.

### What a Surfside Beach area rental takes in
AirROI, a rental data company, counts about 550 active Airbnb listings in its Surfside Beach market, which reaches past the town limits. The average one took in about $43,000 in gross bookings over the past year, before costs.
That was up about 7 percent on the year before. Most of the money comes in summer: the average listing takes in about five times as much in July as in January.

## What are the pros and cons of living in Surfside Beach?

### Pros

- About 2 miles of beach with 36 public accesses.

- A new concrete pier, free to walk, with two restaurants.

- Free summer concerts in Memorial Park and golf cart parades on Ocean Boulevard.

- Owners who live elsewhere park free in town lots with two passes.

### Cons

- Near the ocean, only about 1 home in 8 is taxed as its owner's main home. On the inland streets with the largest lots, about 7 in 10 are.

- Flood insurance costs more near the ocean, and big work on a low house there can mean raising it. We check the zone and the building value first.

- Two in three "Surfside Beach" listings are outside the town, under county rules. We check the town limits and the subdivision's rules for every listing.

Common questions

## Surfside Beach, SC FAQ

### Is Surfside Beach part of Myrtle Beach?
No. Surfside Beach is its own town in Horry County, incorporated in 1964, with the ZIP code 29575.

### Can you Airbnb in Surfside Beach?
Only on the blocks near the ocean, in the town's R3 and C3 zoning districts. Rentals under 30 days are not allowed in the inland R1 and R2 districts.

### Can you drive a golf cart in Surfside Beach?
Yes, on town streets posted at 35 mph or less, with a state permit decal, insurance and a licensed driver 16 or older. Never on the beach.

### Are dogs allowed on Surfside Beach?
Not from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., May 1 through Labor Day. At other times, leashed dogs are welcome.

### Is parking free in Surfside Beach?
Town lots charge from March 1 to October 31, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. An owner who lives elsewhere gets two free passes per household.

### What is the property tax rate in Surfside Beach?
On a home the county values at $500,000, the town and county tax is about $2,100 a year as your main home. As a second home or rental, it is about $6,400.

### What schools serve Surfside Beach?
Horry County Schools, which assigns schools by address. We look up the assigned schools for any home you like.

### What about crime in Surfside Beach?
We do not rate places for crime. The town has its own police department, and the FBI publishes the crime each police agency reports.

# Eight real estate investment strategies on the Grand Strand, compared A local number for each, and who it fits.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Eight real estate investment strategies, from long-term and nightly rentals to BRRRR, 1031 exchanges and DSTs, each with a Grand Strand number.

The short answer
For steady income, the simplest investment strategy here is a house rented by the year, bought with a DSCR loan, which qualifies on the rent. A house listed for rent in the Myrtle Beach area asks about $2,070 a month.
Selling a rental with a big gain? A 1031 exchange or a DST puts off the tax. With cash and time for a project, a flip or BRRRR starts with a worn house.

## Which real estate investment strategy fits you?
DSCR purchases and 1031 trades are the most common we see here, and BRRRR is the rarest, because the right property is rare.

## What are the main real estate investment strategies here?
Buy a home and hold it

### Long-term rental
A long-term rental is a home leased by the year. Its rent comes in every month, in winter as in summer. It fits an investor who wants monthly income with the least to manage.
Our rent prices guide has rents by town and size, and the rental analyzer works out one address. A local manager can take the calls; our property management guide covers what to expect.
Many communities here ban renting a house at all, and we filter them out of a search. We also read the homeowners association (HOA) documents for rules that would block your rental plan.
The hard part is the tax. A rental or a second home is taxed on 6 percent of its value . The 4 percent rate is only for the home you live in, once the county approves it. The rate is lost if that home is rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year.

### Short-term rental
A short-term rental is a home rented by the night, often through Airbnb. The average Airbnb in the Myrtle Beach area took in about $26,000 from guests over a year, before costs.
Murrells Inlet's average Airbnb took in about $48,000, the most of the eight Grand Strand towns we track. Nightly rentals fit an owner who wants the most a home can earn and accepts the work, or pays a manager.
Our Airbnb income guide has the figures by town and by size.
The hard part is the rules. In the City of Myrtle Beach, a rental under 90 days is short-term, and most of the city's traditional neighborhoods are not zoned for it . Check the zoning before you buy. Our short-term rental rules guide covers each town.

Photo: USGS
Condo buildings on the beach at Garden City Beach, with the salt marsh behind them.

### Small multifamily
Small multifamily is one building with two to four homes: a duplex, triplex or fourplex. Here, many of them stand near the ocean. Nearly 3 in 4 of the county's buildings of 2 to 4 homes on one parcel are within a mile of it, in a straight line.
Horry County recorded 58 sales of buildings with 2 to 4 homes in the past year, a few buildings twice, at a middle price of about $520,000.
It fits an investor who wants several rents from one building. If you live in one unit, an FHA or VA loan can buy a building of up to four units. Our small multifamily guide has prices by town and rents by unit.
The hard part on an FHA loan: it bars renting any unit for under 30 days.

Have us run the numbers on any address.
Send us a house, a condo or a duplex you like. We work out the rent, the tax and the HOA rules on it before you offer.
Have us run an address
Pay for it

### DSCR loan
A DSCR loan is not a property. It is the loan many investors here use for a rental and for the BRRRR refinance. The lender qualifies the loan on the rent, not on your income.
A house rented by the year fits it well. Take a middle-priced 3-bedroom house in Longs or Carolina Forest, outside city limits. Its tax, insurance and HOA dues take about a third of HUD's rent figure for its ZIP, which leaves room for the loan.
Our DSCR loan guide works out the ratio on six typical homes here, from a Longs house to an oceanfront condo.
Nightly rentals are harder. Take a typical oceanfront two-bedroom condo in Myrtle Beach, booked as often as the average listing. Its dues, tax and insurance alone come to more than the income a lender counts, before any loan payment.

Add value

### BRRRR
BRRRR stands for buy, rehab, rent, refinance, repeat. You buy a worn house, fix it and rent it. A refinance then takes your cash back out for the next one.
Most good BRRRR candidates here are lower-value homes inland toward Longs or Little River, or condo units in a stable building with a distressed owner.
On one house here, about $90,000 of work took its value from about $180,000 to about $384,000 in about three months. It is now a short-term rental. Those are that investor's numbers, not a promise. Our BRRRR guide and our foreclosures guide cover where the worn houses come from.
BRRRR is rare because the worn house must also sit where rents are high, since the strategy relies on high rents. If the house appraises low at the refinance, part of your cash stays in it.

### Fix and flip
A fix and flip is a worn house you buy, repair and sell. Horry County recorded at least 344 quick resales, a home resold within 12 months of its last sale, in the past year.
When a company resold, the middle gain between the two deed prices was about $75,000, before costs. By ZIP area, houses gained most in the Conway, Carolina Forest and Little River areas.
It fits an investor with cash, a contractor and a few months. Our fix and flip guide has the gains by area.
Not every quick resale gains. Of those resales, 66 sold for less than the earlier deed price, most of them by people rather than companies.

Want the worn houses before they are fixed?
We send worn houses priced under their fixed-up value, in the areas where rent is strong, with our numbers on each.
Get the worn-house list
Trade without the tax now

### 1031 exchange
A 1031 exchange lets you sell one rental, buy another and put off the tax on the gain. Name the replacement within 45 days of the sale, and own it within 180 days or by your tax return's due date with extensions, if that comes first.
One of Tim Nash's longtime clients, an investor based in New York, owns more than 200 properties, mostly condos. When a condo stops giving him depreciation, the yearly tax deduction for a building's wear, he sells it and trades up through a 1031 exchange.
About 3 in 10 homes sold in Horry County in the past year went to buyers whose tax bill goes to another state or country. Our 1031 exchange guide has the steps and the state's rules for a seller from another state.
The hard part is the dates. Miss day 45 or day 180, and the tax comes due.

### DST
A Delaware statutory trust, or DST, sells shares in large properties that a sponsor manages. A share can be the replacement in a 1031 exchange if the trust stays inside the IRS ruling's limits and the other 1031 rules are met.
DSTs already own part of the Grand Strand. Ten trusts own 11 parcels in Horry County that the county values at about $200 million. They include two large apartment communities, one near Carolina Forest Boulevard and one in the Clear Pond area.
The usual minimum share is $100,000, and most DSTs sell only to accredited investors .
A DST fits an investor who is done being a landlord. Our DST guide has the fees, the minimums and the ways out.
The hard part is the cost and the wait. In the middle DST offering, sales commissions and finder's fees came to about 6 percent of the money raised. Plan to stay in until the trust sells the property.

Selling a rental to buy the next one?
We time your sale and the next purchase to the 45 and 180 days, and line up the property before you list.
Plan my sale and next buy

A DST share starts lowest, and a duplex to fourplex costs the most. The cash you need to start depends on the loan. Our DSCR loan guide has our affiliated lender's down payment figures for a rental.

## BRRRR or flip, long-term or nightly, 1031 or DST: how do they differ?
Each pair starts the same way and ends differently.

- BRRRR or fix and flip Both start with a worn house. A flip sells it. BRRRR keeps it, rents it and refinances. The BRRRR guide compares the two.

- Fix and flip or rent A flip pays once, when it sells. A rental pays every month, and you keep the house. The fix and flip guide has the costs.

- Long-term or nightly Our side-by-side works out the same home both ways, rented by the year and by the night.

- 1031 exchange or DST Both put off the tax. A 1031 buys a rental you manage. A DST buys a share a sponsor manages. The DST guide compares them.

## DSCR Loans in Myrtle Beach, SC: Which Rentals Pass the Ratio
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/strategies/dscr-loans/
Summary: DSCR loans in Myrtle Beach and South Carolina: the formula, what ratio passes, how much of the rent the tax and HOA dues use here, and Airbnb income rules.

Home / Strategies / DSCR Loans
Investor financing

# DSCR loans in Myrtle Beach: which rentals here pass the ratio? A house inland passes with room to spare. A nightly oceanfront condo can fail before the loan.

- 46 to 49% of the rent left for the loan on an inland house

- 75 to 80% of nightly income that lenders count

- 1.25 the ratio we aim for

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
The 6 percent rental tax and the HOA fee sit inside a DSCR loan's ratio. Houses inland often pass, while a beach condo's dues can use the rent first.

The short answer
A DSCR loan qualifies on the rent. The lender divides the rent it counts by the monthly bill: principal and interest, property tax, insurance and HOA dues. The three program sheets we read ask for a ratio of 1.00 or more.
On the Grand Strand, the middle 3-bedroom house in Longs or Carolina Forest leaves 46 to 49 percent of the rent for the loan at our 1.25 target. On the middle oceanfront two-bedroom in Myrtle Beach rented by the night, the dues, tax and insurance alone come to more than the income a lender counts.

## What is a DSCR loan, and does it work in South Carolina?
DSCR is short for debt service coverage ratio. It is the rent a home collects, divided by the monthly bill it must cover. The lender qualifies the loan on the rent, not on your income. You sign that the home is for business and that you will not live in it.
DSCR loans work on South Carolina rentals, and the formula does not change at the state line. The local numbers do. A rental here is taxed on 6 percent of its value, condo dues can be high, and towns and HOAs set their own rules on nightly rentals. Each of those sits inside the ratio.
The rent the lender counts is the appraiser's. The appraiser fills in a rent schedule with the appraisal, and with a lease in place the lender may use the lease, within limits. HUD's rents on this page are a guide; the appraiser's figure is the one that counts.

## How do you calculate DSCR on a Grand Strand rental?
Add up the monthly bill, then divide the rent by it. The bill lenders divide by holds principal and interest, the property tax, the insurance and the HOA dues.
The formula
DSCR = the monthly rent the lender counts, divided by the monthly bill: principal and interest, property tax, insurance and HOA dues.
Worked example: the middle 3-bedroom house for sale in Carolina Forest, asking about $390,000 In the ratio A month Where it comes from
Rent the lender counts $2,230 HUD's fair market rent for a 3-bedroom in the ZIP code. Your lender uses the appraiser's figure.
Property tax about $392 A rental is taxed on 6 percent of its value, at the 2026 county rate for most homes outside city limits
Insurance about $275 A landlord policy, one agency's estimate. We get a quote for the address.
HOA dues $100 The middle house's HOA fee
Principal and interest Lender's quote

The tax, insurance and HOA use about 34 percent of the rent. At a ratio of 1.25, principal and interest must fit in the 46 percent that is left.

The HOA fee counts against the rent, and a special assessment can count too; ask your lender. Flood insurance counts where a home needs it. Our rental analyzer runs the same numbers on any address.
Have us fill in the bill for an address.
Send us an address. We fill in the tax, an insurance quote and the dues, and you add your lender's quote.
Have us fill in the numbers

## What is a good DSCR for a rental, and what if it is below 1.00?
A ratio of 1.00 means the rent just covers the bill. Our target is 1.25.
What the ratio means

- 0.75 Our affiliated lender's floor BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company, starts writing DSCR loans at this ratio.

- 1.00 The rent just covers the bill The three program sheets we read ask for a ratio of 1.00 or more.

- 1.15 A nightly rental, at some programs Some ask 1.15 for a nightly rental, or 1.25 on a small loan.

- 1.25 Our target A fifth of the rent is left after the whole bill.

Below 1.00, the rent does not cover the bill, and you pay the rest each month. At 1.25, the cushion is there for an empty month or a repair.

## Which Grand Strand rentals pass a DSCR loan?
We worked out the bill on six kinds of home for sale here, at the middle asking price of each. The chart shows how much of the rent the tax, the insurance and the HOA fee use before the loan.
On a beach condo, the HOA fee and the tax use most of the rent before the loan
HOA fee Tax and insurance Cushion at 1.25 Left for the loan

- Longs house, 3 bedrooms About 49% left for the loan

- Carolina Forest house, 3 bedrooms About 46% left for the loan

- Carolina Forest condo, 2 bedrooms About 44% left for the loan

- Myrtle Beach condo in the city, 2 bedrooms About 14% left for the loan

- Garden City Beach condo, 2 bedrooms, nightly About 20% left for the loan

- Myrtle Beach oceanfront condo, 2 bedrooms, nightly More than the rent before any loan

&#9650; All the rent
Share of the monthly rent a lender counts, for the middle home for sale of each kind. Yearly leases use HUD's rent for the ZIP code. Nightly condos count 75 percent of a year of guest payments. Insurance is one agency's estimate, and flood insurance is not included.

- A city condo on a yearly lease is tight The middle 2-bedroom condo inside Myrtle Beach leaves about 14 percent. Its dues alone, about $550 a month, take 39 percent of the rent.

- An oceanfront condo rented by the night fails before the loan Take a typical oceanfront two-bedroom in Myrtle Beach, booked the nights the average listing books. That average counts listings open only part of the year. Its HOA fee is about $1,200 a month. With the tax and insurance, that is about 109 percent of the nightly income a lender counts at 75 percent. The ratio is about 0.91 with no loan at all.

Taxes stop more rental deals here than insurance does. A home that is not its owner's legal residence, such as a house rented out year-round or a second home, is taxed on 6 percent. Our property tax guide works out the bill.

### Longs: the Waccamaw River, and the most rent left for the loan
The Waccamaw River runs past Longs, and it is the only river that starts in a Carolina bay. From the landing on SC 9, you can paddle a state preserve along 28 miles of it, past bald cypress and water tupelo. Otters and black bears live there, and you may camp on the riverbank on preserve land.
Of the six homes we worked, the Longs house leaves the most of the rent for the loan, about 49 percent. The middle 3-bedroom house for sale asks about $320,000, and HUD's rent for a 3-bedroom in its ZIP code is $2,270 a month.
Much of Longs is new. About half the houses sold there in a year of county deeds were sales by builders, 280 of 607. About 2 in 5 homes in its ZIP code were built in 2010 or later. Only 3 in 100 of its houses are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. Builders here rarely offer incentives to a buyer using a DSCR loan, so plan on none.

Send me 3-bedroom rentals in Longs

### Carolina Forest: trails in the woods, and almost no houses in the flood zone
Off River Oaks Drive, the county's Bike and Run Park, which riders call "The Hulk", has 7 miles of mountain bike and running trails on about 70 acres. It sits between Carolina Forest and the Intracoastal Waterway.
Almost no houses in Carolina Forest are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone, and half its homes were built in 2007 or later. The middle 3-bedroom house for sale asks about $390,000 and leaves about 46 percent of the rent for the loan.
A condo there does almost as well. At HUD's 2-bedroom figure for the ZIP code, the middle 2-bedroom condo, about $165,000 with dues of about $425 a month, leaves about 44 percent.

## Can you use Airbnb income for a DSCR loan in Myrtle Beach?
Yes, at some lenders. Lenders count 75 to 80 percent of the nightly-rental estimate, to allow for advertising, furnishing and cleaning. A loan officer at our preferred lender says only 75 percent counts. Two of the three program sheets we read count at most 80 percent of nightly-rental income; the third asks for a 1.15 ratio instead.
The cut can make a nightly rental count for less than a yearly lease. The middle two-bedroom nightly rental in the Myrtle Beach area took in about $20,100 in a year, counting listings open only part of the year. Counted at 75 percent, that is about $1,256 a month. HUD's figure for a 2-bedroom on a yearly lease in ZIP code 29577 is $1,420.

- Some programs take it only on a refinance Two of the three sheets we read take nightly income only when you refinance. On a purchase, the home may have to qualify on the yearly-lease rent.

- The rules must allow nightly rentals The lender's appraiser must show no city, county or HOA rule against them. In the City of Myrtle Beach, a stay under 90 days is short-term, and most of the city's residential zones bar it. Our short-term rental rules guide goes town by town.

- Most condos allow them; few houses with an HOA do About 7 in 10 condos for sale in Horry County say short-term rentals are allowed. Among houses for sale with an HOA fee, about 4 in 100 say so.

### Garden City Beach: the pier, and a beach condo that still passes
Garden City Beach has a 668-foot pier. In summer, bands play every night at both ends of it, weather permitting, and you can fish from it around the clock. A pier pass covers fishing, so no state license is needed.
It is also where a condo by the sea can still pass the ratio. About two dozen condos for sale in Garden City Beach are marked for nightly rentals. The middle 2-bedroom among them has dues of about $575 a month, under half the oceanfront tower's. Counted at 75 percent, its nightly income leaves about 20 percent for the loan at 1.25.

## Can you get a DSCR loan on a condotel or non-warrantable condo here?
A non-warrantable condo is in a building that fails one of Fannie Mae's project rules, so the usual conventional loan will not work there.
Often not. About 8 in 10 condos for sale in oceanfront buildings in Horry County say the unit is in a rental program. All three DSCR program sheets we read exclude non-warrantable condos, and two of them also name condotels. Fannie Mae will not buy a loan in a building run like a hotel or with a rental pool. It is one of the two companies Congress created to buy mortgages from lenders.
Our condotel financing guide names the buildings and the loans that do work. Our non-warrantable condo guide goes tower by tower.

## How much down, what credit score and what else does a DSCR loan need?
A DSCR loan asks you for money down, a credit score, money in reserve and a plan for the first few years.

- Money down 15 to 25 percent on most purchases, and more on a condotel. Figures from our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company.

- Credit score The program sheets we read set credit score floors from 660 to 720.

- Reserves Money in the bank after closing, counted in months of the home's bill. The programs we read ask for 3 to 6 months, and one asks a first-time investor for 12.

- A fee to pay off early Many DSCR loans charge a prepayment fee if you sell or refinance in the first few years. Ask your lender before a quick resale or a BRRRR refinance .

- The price of the loan According to a loan officer at our preferred lender, with good credit and a 1.25 to 1.5 ratio, a DSCR loan is priced about like a conventional loan.

To see what the loan would cost on a home here, call us. We will work with our affiliated lender to give you solid numbers.

## Who can get a DSCR loan: an LLC, a first-time investor, a Canadian?
Each of them can get a DSCR loan at some programs, with limits.

- An LLC A DSCR loan can close in your name or in an LLC; the investor clients we work with usually close in an LLC. About 9 in 10 of them form a new LLC for each house. Our LLC guide covers the steps.

- A first-time investor One program we read takes a first-time investor with a 700 score, 12 months of reserves and a home they own and live in. Another does not take them, and a third asks them for a 1.00 ratio. All three refuse a first-time home buyer.

- A Canadian Canadians usually need a DSCR loan unless they have a Social Security number and U.S. credit, or a U.S. work card. They need a Social Security number or a U.S. taxpayer ID number from the IRS, called a TIN. Some programs take only U.S. citizens and permanent residents. Our guide for Canadian buyers has the rest.

- Someone who will use it too Plan to stay in the home more than 14 days in the coming year? Then federal rules no longer treat it as a rental its owner does not live in. The business-loan exemption may not apply. Tell your lender early.

Common questions

## DSCR loan FAQ

### What is a good DSCR for a rental property?
Our target is 1.25, which leaves a fifth of the rent after the whole monthly bill. The three program sheets we read ask for 1.00 or more.

### Can I get a DSCR loan in South Carolina without tax returns?
Yes. A DSCR loan is judged on the home's rent and its monthly bill. You sign that the home is a rental for business and that you will not live in it.

### Can I get a DSCR loan if the rent does not cover the bill?
Sometimes. Our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company, starts writing DSCR loans at a ratio of 0.75. Below 1.00, you pay the rest of the bill each month.

### Can I use Airbnb income for a DSCR loan in Myrtle Beach?
At some lenders. They count 75 to 80 percent of the nightly-rental estimate, and two of the three sheets we read take it only on a refinance. The city and the HOA must allow nightly rentals.

### Does a DSCR loan need an appraisal?
Yes. The rent the lender counts is the appraiser's market rent, written on a rent schedule with the appraisal.

### Can I get a DSCR loan in an LLC?
Yes. A DSCR loan can close in your name or in an LLC. The investor clients we work with usually close in an LLC.

### Can a first-time home buyer get a DSCR loan?
Not at the three programs we read. A first-time investor who already owns a home can qualify at some programs.

### Can Canadians get a DSCR loan?
A Canadian without a Social Security number and U.S. credit usually needs a DSCR loan, and needs a Social Security number or a U.S. taxpayer ID number (TIN). Some programs take only U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

## The BRRRR Method in Myrtle Beach: Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/strategies/brrrr/
Summary: The BRRRR method in Myrtle Beach: buy, rehab, rent, refinance, repeat. Build a Grand Strand rental portfolio using rent and DSCR numbers.

Home / Invest / Strategies / BRRRR
Strategy

# The BRRRR method in Myrtle Beach: one sum of cash, house after house.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
BRRRR reuses one sum of cash, rental after rental. In Myrtle Beach it works on a bank-owned or worn house bought below its fixed-up value, where rent is strong.

The strategy

## The BRRRR method: one sum of cash, reused house after house
BRRRR means buy, rehab, rent, refinance, repeat: one sum of cash, reused house after house. You buy a worn, outdated house cheap, fix it, rent it, then refinance to pull your cash back out. The two boxes below give you the ten-second read on whether it fits you. BRRRR is the scarcest strategy we work on the Grand Strand, because the right house is rare, and finding it is most of what Chapter3 does for a BRRRR investor.
Why people do it

- + The same cash buys house after house

- + Rent covers the new loan

- + You keep the house and the rent

What can go wrong

- ! The house appraises low and your cash stays stuck

- ! The rehab runs over budget

- ! The rent does not cover the new loan payment

The five steps

## How BRRRR works, step by step

- 1 Buy below market. Pay a price that leaves room after repairs.

- 2 Rehab it. Fix what raises the value and the rent.

- 3 Rent it. A signed lease is what the refinance lender wants to see.

- 4 Refinance: pull your cash back out. A new loan on the higher value hands most of your cash back.

- 5 Repeat with the same cash. The money you pulled out buys the next house.

The buy

## Buying below market, where the rent is strong
Aim to keep the purchase price plus rehab budget under 70 to 75 percent of the after-repair value, what the house will be worth once it is fixed up. That difference is what covers you if the work costs more than planned.
The house also has to sit where rent is strong. BRRRR pays you back through a refinance, and that loan is judged on the rent the house collects, so a cheap house on a street with weak rent does not work. Needing both in the same house is what makes these deals scarce.
On the Grand Strand, dated single-family homes in Conway, Socastee and Carolina Forest are the usual targets, and the map runs north through Longs and Little River, where prices drop again. Year-round tenant s keep the rent side steady.

Sourcing

## Where the discounted houses come from
Bank-owned listings are the usual starting point. A bank that has taken a house back sells it for less than a fixed-up house nearby, and that discount is what the strategy runs on. The buyer who can close soonest usually gets the house.
Estate sales and worn rentals coming off long tenancies make up the rest.
We hear about bank-owned and pre-listing houses early, from agents who have worked this market for decades, and our analysts screen every active listing for rent-to-price math at the same time.

Condos

## Buying a distressed condo unit
Distressed condo units in stable buildings sell at deeper discounts than houses, because the supply of condos is bigger and many investors will not buy into a building at all. The discount usually comes from the owner, not the building: one mismanaged or foreclosing unit sells cheap while the building itself still passes lender tests.
A building that fails those tests is called non-warrantable. The lenders who will still refinance you there want about 25 percent down, against the 20 percent a warrantable building can take, so another 5 percent of the value stays parked in that unit instead of funding your next purchase. Figures from our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company.
Our agents check the building before you offer. The full picture is on the condotel and non-warrantable condo financing guide .

The work

## The rehab, the lease, and how we help
Fix what raises the value and the rent, not a wish list. Our agents walk the house with you before you offer and tell you which repairs the appraiser and the tenant will pay for, and which ones you will never get back. We introduce the contractors we use here, so the bids come from people who have done this work on the Grand Strand.
Once the work is done, a signed lease is what the refinance lender wants to see. Inland areas lease fastest. Demand there comes from workers, hospitals, schools and Coastal Carolina University , not tourists. Houses approved for the housing choice voucher program lease fastest of all, and we walk owners through what the housing authority inspects and how to get a unit approved.
One local rehab for scale: a house on Woodlawn Drive took $90,317.80 of work from a local company we recommend. A new roof, replaced rotted studs, new insulation, new cabinets, counters and backsplashes, repaired floors and walls, fresh paint, and a hot tub for short-term guests. The house was worth about $180,000 before the work and appraised at $384,000 after, and BrickWood Mortgage financed the project. Start to finish, financing included, about three months, and the buyer kept it as a short-term rental. His numbers, not a promise.

The refinance

## The refinance that returns your cash
The new loan is usually a DSCR cash-out loan: the loan qualifies on the property's rent, not your tax returns. Most lenders cap the cash-out at 75 to 80 percent of the new appraised value. Many also require seasoning, meaning the lender makes you wait a few months before using the new value. See the DSCR loan guide for how the refinance works.
When an appraisal does come in low, and here that is rare, our agents pull their own comparable sales from the Coastal Carolinas MLS and file a reconsideration of value through the lender. In the past, one of those changed the number, and the borrower brought less cash to closing.

The repeat

## Doing it again with the same money
If the after-repair value holds, most of your cash is back and the tenant covers the loan. If the house appraises under the number the deal was priced on, your cash stays stuck in it. Pricing that number is the part our agents do with you before you buy, from sold homes nearby rather than from an estimate.
Tim's grandfather owned rental properties in Myrtle Beach, and Tim has his own investments today, so the numbers Chapter3 runs for you are the numbers he runs on his own investments. Run the rent and value numbers through the long-term rental analyzer before you buy. If you would rather sell the finished house than keep it, that is a fix and flip . Read that guide to see whether it suits you better.

Another way in

## The new construction version of BRRRR
The scarce ingredient is the discounted house. One way around it is to create the value instead of shopping for it. We work with a local builder whose built houses appraised for more than they cost to build, and a brand new house rents higher than a comparable older one .
The rent side gets solved during the build. We look for tenants moving to the area around the month the house will be finished, so about nine times in ten the house has a renter lined up before the work ends. The cycle is the same as BRRRR, with the discount coming from the build rather than from a distressed seller.
One house took about $260,000 of capital to build, half of it financed, and appraised at $390,000 once it was done. Those are his numbers, not a promise. This path needs a builder relationship or a real discount during construction, so it is not open to every investor. Ask us whether your numbers fit it.

Paying cash

## Benefits of buying cash
A cash offer is stronger than a financed one on these houses. Bank-owned and off-market houses are the first two places our agents look, and both usually go to the buyer who can close soonest. Cash has no appraisal to fail and no loan to fall through, which is worth more to those sellers than a slightly higher price.
Cash does not have to stay in the house either. The refinance step is the same one BRRRR already runs: buy with cash, fix it, sign a lease, then take a DSCR cash-out loan and put the money back to work.
You can still buy these houses with a loan, and off-market is where it happens, because there is no competing cash offer to lose to. Our agents talk to owners before a house is listed and find out what the seller needs. Then we build the offer around it: the closing date they want, a shorter inspection window, more earnest money, or a price that pays them for waiting on your loan. A seller who has not listed yet is usually weighing one offer instead of five, and that is the situation where financing wins.

Common questions

## Frequently asked questions

### Does the BRRRR method work in Myrtle Beach?
Yes. It works best on dated single-family homes in inland areas like Conway, Socastee, Carolina Forest, and up toward Longs and Little River. Year-round tenant demand there supports the rent side. Distressed condo units sell at deeper discounts, but HOA rules limit what you can renovate and many oceanfront buildings fail refinance lender tests, so check the building against the refinance before you buy.

### What is the 70 percent rule in BRRRR?
It is a guideline. Keep the purchase price plus rehab budget under about 70 to 75 percent of the fixed-up value. That margin is what lets you refinance later and pull most of your cash back out.

### How soon can I refinance a BRRRR property?
Many lenders require seasoning, meaning they make you wait a few months before lending on the new value. Ask the lender how long its wait is before you buy. The after-repair value is the deciding number. The refinance comes down to what the house appraises for once the work is done. Know the house, its condition, and what similar homes nearby sold for before you buy. That is what protects your cash.

### How much cash can I pull out on the refinance?
Cash-out DSCR refinances are typically capped at 75 to 80 percent of the appraised value. Whether you recover all of your cash depends on how accurate your fixed-up value estimate was.

### What is the biggest risk with BRRRR?
Guessing the fixed-up value too high. If the house appraises low, the refinance returns less cash and more of your money stays stuck. Model the value and rent before you buy.

# How do you find a fix and flip in Myrtle Beach? Local numbers from the county's deeds.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
344 quick resales (flips) in the year to September 2026. When a company resold, the middle gain was about $75,000. Houses gained most in Conway, Carolina Forest and Little River.

The short answer
Yes, a fix and flip can pay here if you buy right. In the year to September 2026, Horry County homes were resold within 12 months of their last sale at least 344 times. When a company resold the home, the middle gain between the two deed prices was about $75,000, before any costs. Conway, Carolina Forest and Little River had the biggest gains on houses.

## Do fix and flips make money in Myrtle Beach?
Most resell for more than the earlier deed price. We read every deed Horry County recorded for two years. Quick resales, a home sold again within 12 months of its last sale, were about 3 of every 100 home sales not made by a builder. The chart gives the middle gain: half gained more, half less.

The company figure is the closer guide to an investor's flip. Resales by a person hold most of the losses: about 55 of the 66 homes that sold for less than the earlier deed price. Houses also gained more than condos, a middle of about $56,000 against about $17,000.

## How do we find a house worth flipping?
Our agents use a deal finder we built to look at every home for sale on the Grand Strand in one pass. An agent checks everything it finds:

- A reason to be cheap. It pulls every house for sale that has one: a distressed sale, a foreclosure , a short sale, or an older house at the low end of the price range.

- The nearby sales. For the cheapest houses per square foot, it finds houses of about the same size that sold within a mile in the last year.

- The list. The houses furthest under the middle of their nearby sales make the list. It reads the photos and description of the top ones and lists the repairs it can see, with a cost range for each.

- The agent's call. An agent reads the sales, decides what the house will sell for once it is fixed, and works out your highest offer. That number comes from an agent who knows the streets, never from a computer.

A house far under its neighbors is not always a deal. Sometimes the size in the listing is wrong, the price is an auction's opening bid, or the house needs everything. The finder marks those, and the agent finds out which it is before you spend a dollar.
What you get on the flip list
For each house: its asking price per square foot against the middle of its nearby sales, the six nearest sales, the repairs its photos show with a cost range, and your highest offer by the 70 percent rule. Tell us your price range.
Get the flip list

## How do you work out what to offer?
Every flip starts with the after-repair value, what the house will sell for once it is fixed up. Take that number and subtract everything you spend. What is left is your profit.
Many flippers use the 70 percent rule to set their highest offer: 70 percent of the after-repair value, minus the repairs. On a house that will sell for $300,000 fixed up and needs $45,000 of work, that is $165,000. The 30 percent left over covers your costs and your profit.
Run your own deal
What it sells for fixed up $ What you pay $ Repairs $ Holding and selling costs $
Your profit $25,000
Price plus repairs, as a share of the fixed-up value 82%
Above the 70 percent most flippers aim for, so this deal leaves little room for the repairs to run over.

## What does a flip cost here besides the house and the repairs?
Four costs bill you every month you own the house: the property tax, the loan, insurance and utilities. The rest come at the two closings, and when you sell, the commission and the deed fee.
The tax is the one most investors miss. A house that is not its owner's own home is taxed on 6 percent of its value, not 4 percent, and it pays the school operating tax.
On a house the county appraises at $250,000, in one of its tax districts outside the cities, that is about $3,015 a year instead of about $919, plus an $89.40 fee on each bill. We work out the bill for the actual address, and every town's rate is in our property tax calculator .
The deed fee is $1.85 for each $500 of the price, and the law puts it on the seller: about $962 on a $260,000 sale. If you buy at the county's court-ordered foreclosure sale, you pay the fee on that deed as well.
We also get the insurance quotes for the empty house and the loan's terms, so the monthly cost of holding it is a number, not a guess.

## What permits and licenses does a flip need?
In Horry County outside the cities, you need a building permit to build, alter, repair or tear down, and for any electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing work. South Carolina licenses the people who do the work by the size of the job:
Permits and licenses for flip work in Horry County The work County permit Who may do it
Paint, wallpaper, tile, carpet, cabinets, countertops No You, or a pro registered with the state
A new roof We check first A roofer registered with the state
Electrical, plumbing, heating and air Yes A contractor licensed for the trade
Walls, structure, a full renovation Yes A licensed builder, for jobs over $5,000

Before you budget a new roof, we ask the county's code office whether it needs a permit. The county's own pages disagree.
The owner's exemption from the license does not cover a flip. It is only for a house you build or repair to live in, and a sale or rental within two years of finishing is presumed to mean it was done to sell.
Working without the license is a misdemeanor for the contractor, with a fine of $500 to $10,000, at least 30 days in jail, or both. An unlicensed contractor also cannot put a lien on the house or sue to be paid. In the City of Myrtle Beach, electrical, plumbing, gas and mechanical work each need a trade permit.

### Houses built before 1978
Many of the cheapest houses are old enough to have lead paint. In a house built before 1978, anyone paid to do work that disturbs paint must be certified in lead-safe work. The EPA says the rule applies to a flipper doing their own work too. Small patches are outside it: 6 square feet of paint or less in a room, or 20 square feet or less outside. Replacing windows is always covered.

### Houses in a flood zone
This is the rule that can end a flip. If the work costs 50 percent or more of the building's value before the work, not counting the land, the federal flood program calls it a substantial improvement. Work to fix code violations an inspector has cited, and some work on historic buildings, are left out of that count.
In unincorporated Horry County , the whole house must then meet the rules for a new building. In a high-risk flood zone marked AE on the flood map, that means a lowest floor at least 3 feet above the flood height shown on the flood map for that spot.
In the City of Myrtle Beach , work on a building in a flood zone that does not meet today's flood rules must cost less than 50 percent of the building's value.
For an older house low to the ground, the rule can mean raising it or keeping the job under the limit. We check the flood zone and the county's building value before you offer, so you know the repair budget the rule allows. Our coastal insurance page covers flood insurance on the finished house.

## How does a finished flip sell here?
Most of our buyers for a finished flip are moving from out of state, or retiring. We spend several thousand dollars a month advertising to buyers moving to the Grand Strand, so a finished flip goes in front of them the day it lists. Lighter repairs sometimes suit the rental buyers on our list before the house reaches the open market.
One investor here inherited a house and had it fully repaired over about two and a half months. An agent at Chapter3 advertised it for sale while the work was going on. It went under contract a week before the work finished, and it closed for cash the day construction ended. Repaired, the house was worth about $390,000.
Advertise before the work ends. The loan, the tax and the insurance stop the day the house sells.
Plan to list by March. The fewest homes sell here in January and February. Every other month, about 800 to 1,050 sell, and prices move little, so the season gives you more buyers, not a higher price.

## What do you owe when you sell?
When you sell a house as an investor, you give the buyer South Carolina's property condition disclosure , the same form any owner gives. There is no exemption for investors, and it goes to the buyer before both sides sign.
When you sell most homes built before 1978, you also give the buyer the EPA's lead pamphlet and a lead disclosure, and the buyer gets 10 days to have the paint tested unless the buyer waives it. If the buyer asks for a termite letter, only a licensed pest control company may issue it.
A gain on a house held one year or less is a short-term gain , taxed as ordinary income. If you flip as a business, a house held mainly for sale to customers is not a capital asset, so its gain is not a capital gain at all. A flip also cannot go into a 1031 exchange .
South Carolina's 44 percent deduction on capital gains is for property held more than a year, so a flip gets none of it. For 2026, South Carolina's top rate is 5.21 percent on income above $30,000. Talk to a tax advisor before your first sale.

## Is wholesaling allowed in South Carolina?
Not the way it used to work. South Carolina's 2024 license law defines wholesaling as holding a contract to buy a home and then marketing the house to another buyer before you own it. Marketing someone else's property for pay is a broker's work and needs a license. A real estate brokerage and its agents may not wholesale or help a wholesaler. Assigning the contract itself is not wholesaling under the law.
The agents at Chapter3 have sold on the Grand Strand for decades and often hear about discounted houses, such as estate sales and new foreclosures, before they reach the big listing websites.

## How do you pay for a flip?
Many flips use a hard money loan, a short-term loan that closes quickly and can pay for part of the repairs. Its rate is higher than a normal mortgage, so every extra month you own the house costs you money. Our preferred lender, BrickWood Mortgage , offers fix-and-flip and bridge loans, so the purchase, the loan and the repair budget are planned together.

Because of this relationship, this referral may provide Chapter3 Realty a financial or other benefit. You are never required to use BrickWood. You are free to shop any lender. See full AfBA Disclosure.
Cash is stronger. Bank-owned and off-market houses usually go to the buyer who can close soonest, and cash has no appraisal to fail. It also removes the largest holding cost, the loan interest.
You can still win with a loan off-market, where there is no cash offer to lose to. Our agents talk to owners before a house is listed and learn what the seller needs. Then we build the offer around it: the closing date, a shorter inspection, more earnest money, or a price that pays the seller for waiting on your loan.
Keep a backup plan. We run each address through our rental analyzer too, so you know what it would rent for if it does not sell. If it would rent well, you can refinance into a DSCR loan , which is approved on the rent instead of your tax returns, and keep it. That is the BRRRR strategy : buy, fix, rent, refinance, repeat. Once it is a rental, how long to hold a rental before selling shows when a sale covers its costs.

## 1031 Exchange in South Carolina: Rules, 45/180 Days, I-295
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/strategies/1031-exchange/
Summary: 1031 exchange in South Carolina: the 45 and 180 day rules, the Form I-295 box for the 5.21% hold-back, a Myrtle Beach example, a date tool and what to buy.

# 1031 exchange in South Carolina: the 45 and 180 days, and the state's hold-back Sell from another state, and one box on Form I-295 sends the state's 5.21% hold-back to your intermediary.

- 45 and 180 days to name the next property, and to own it

- 5.21% the state's hold-back rate on a 2026 sale

- Form I-295 the state form with the exchange boxes

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
South Carolina follows the federal 1031 rules. A seller who lives in another state meets one state step at closing: the 5.21 percent hold-back and Form I-295.

The short answer
A 1031 exchange works in South Carolina under the federal rules. Name the replacement within 45 days of your sale, and own it within 180 days.
If your permanent home is in another state, the buyer must hold back part of the price for state income tax, unless the sale is exempt. Tick the exchange box on Form I-295 and use a qualified intermediary, a neutral company that holds the sale money. The hold-back then goes to the intermediary, and the state is paid nothing if you finish the exchange.
