## Does a 1031 exchange work in South Carolina?
Yes. South Carolina's income tax uses the federal tax code , including section 1031, the exchange rule. A seller from any state uses the same exchange here.
In a 1031 exchange, you sell one rental or investment property, buy another, and put off the tax on the profit. The tax comes due when you later sell without exchanging. A trade counts when it meets three rules:

- What qualifies Real property held for business or investment, traded for like-kind real property held the same way. Real property in the United States is generally like-kind to other US real property, improved or not. A rental condo for a rental house counts, and so does land for a duplex. A house bought mainly to resell, a flip, does not.

- Who holds the money You may not touch the money between the sale and the purchase. If it is credited to your account or set aside so you can draw on it, you have received it. A qualified intermediary, a neutral company, can hold it under a written agreement that limits your right to it. That is one of the setups the IRS rules accept , so the money does not count as yours.

- Who cannot hold it Your real estate agent, attorney, accountant or employee of the past two years cannot be your qualified intermediary. The exception is one whose only work was on 1031 exchanges or routine title, escrow or bank services. Close relatives cannot hold it either. Chapter3 is your agent, so a separate company you choose holds the money.

The forms call the property you sell the relinquished property, and the one you buy the replacement property. Our investment strategies guide compares the exchange with the other ways investors buy here.

## How does a 1031 exchange keep South Carolina's hold-back from going to the state?
When the seller's permanent home is outside South Carolina, the buyer must hold back part of the price for South Carolina income tax, unless the sale is exempt. For a sale closed in 2026, the rate is 5.21 percent , the state's top individual rate for the year.
Form I-295 is the seller's sworn statement to the buyer. If it states your gain, the buyer holds back 5.21 percent of the gain. Without it, the buyer holds back 5.21 percent of the price less your selling costs. A seller that is a corporation is withheld at 5 percent instead. The amount is never more than the cash due to you at closing.

### Why an exchange changes the hold-back
A tax-deferred exchange is not a "sale" for this rule. The Department of Revenue counts a 1031 exchange as exempt. Its ruling still requires the hold-back when the replacement has not been named at the time of the sale. For an exchange that is not on the same day, it gives two ways to handle it.

### The exchange boxes on Form I-295
The form has three exchange boxes. Tick the one that fits your trade:

- A swap on the same day You trade one property for the other at one closing and put off the whole gain. The buyer holds back only on gain the form says will be taxed.

- An exchange where you keep some cash Part of the gain will be taxed, and you enter that gain on the form.

- An exchange through a qualified intermediary You put off the gain using an intermediary and have followed the state's steps for it, in Revenue Ruling #09-13.

### What happens when you tick the intermediary box

- You sign Form I-295 before a notary You give it to the buyer and keep a copy with your tax records. It is not sent to the state unless the state asks for it.

- Form I-290 is filled in as if the sale were taxed Form I-290 is the form that pays the hold-back to the state. It goes to your intermediary at closing, with the amount needed to pay the hold-back.

- The buyer and the intermediary sign a contract The intermediary files Form I-290 and pays the hold-back for the buyer if the exchange fails. The buyer remains liable for the payment.

- If the exchange fails, the intermediary pays It pays by the 15th of the month after the failure is clear. That is the day the exchange is given up or its time runs out, whichever comes first.

- If you finish the exchange, the state is paid nothing Form I-290 is never filed.

There is a second way. You can pay the hold-back from other money, so the whole sale goes into the exchange. The buyer sends it to the state, and you ask for it back once the exchange is complete.
Money held back beyond your tax comes back by an amended Form I-290 before your tax year ends. After that, it is a credit on your South Carolina return. Our capital gains guide has the refund steps.
Before the buyer signs, we tell the closing attorney's office and your intermediary that the sale is an exchange. The form and the dates are then in place on closing day.

## What does South Carolina hold back when you exchange a $400,000 condo?
Example. An owner who lives in another state sells a Myrtle Beach rental condo for $400,000 in 2026. They bought it for $250,000, took $60,000 of depreciation and pay 6 percent to sell.
The price less selling costs is $376,000, and the gain is $186,000.

## What are the 1031 exchange 45-day and 180-day rules?
Both deadlines count from the day your sale closes and run at the same time, in calendar days.
Your tax return can come first. The exchange must be finished by the return's due date , with extensions, if that is sooner. For a sale that closes after mid-October, day 180 falls after April 15, so an extension keeps all 180 days.
Your 1031 dates
The day your sale closes

- Day 0 Your sale closes. The money goes to your intermediary.

- Day 45 Your signed list of possible replacements is due.

- Day 180 You must own the new property.

Your tax return is due on April 15, before day 180. File an extension to keep the full 180 days.
For a person who files a tax return for the calendar year.

The IRS can postpone the 45 and 180 days after a federally declared disaster , but never past the tax return's due date with extensions. After Hurricane Helene, that relief covered every South Carolina county.

- The sale closes The money goes straight to your intermediary, and this day is day 0. We work the closing with the attorney's office so you never touch the money.

- Days 1 to 45 Shop on the numbers. Our agents check each Grand Strand property's rent, cap rate and tenant history, not the finishes.

- Day 45 Your signed list goes to your intermediary. We draft it with you and send it in time.

- Day 180 You close on the new property, and the tax stays put off. Our agents, and the lending, insurance and legal partners we work with here, work to the same date.

## How do you name replacement properties by day 45?
Write the list, sign it, and send it to your intermediary before day 45 ends . Telling your own agent, attorney or accountant does not count. Describe each property by its street address, legal description or a distinct name.
Choose one of three ways to write it:

- Up to three properties Name up to three, at any price.

- Any number, worth up to twice your sale Name more than three if their total value is no more than twice what you sold.

- Any number, if you buy nearly all of them Name as many as you like if you buy at least 95 percent of the total value you named.

Name more than the rules allow, and the IRS treats the list as if you named nothing. You can change the list before day 45 with a new signed notice to the same person. A change by phone does not count.

### How one investor trades up
One of Tim Nash's longtime clients, an investor based in New York, owns more than 200 properties, mostly condos. The IRS lets an owner deduct the cost of a residential rental building over 27.5 years, called depreciation. When a condo has used up that deduction, he sells it and trades up through a 1031 exchange.
How long to hold a rental before selling has the costs a sale must cover first. Our cost segregation guide shows how a study changes the depreciation on the new property.

## Can you 1031 exchange a vacation condo you also use?
Yes, if you rent it out enough. The IRS will not challenge the exchange of a beach condo you rent out and also use if it passes this test:

- Owned 24 months You owned the condo for at least 24 months before the exchange.

- Rented each year In each of those two years, you rented it at a fair rent for 14 days or more.

- Little personal use Personal use was no more than 14 days or 10 percent of the rented days, whichever is more. Days your family uses it, or anyone pays less than a fair rent, count as personal use.

The condo you buy passes the same test for the 24 months after you buy it. The test is not the only way in. A condo that misses it may still qualify.
A home used only as your own home does not qualify. A former main home may get the separate home-sale exclusion if you lived in it two of the last five years. The capital gains guide covers that exclusion.

## What happens if you keep some of the cash?
Cash you keep from the exchange, often called boot, is taxed , up to the amount of your gain. If the new loan is smaller than the one you paid off, the difference counts as cash you kept.
South Carolina's share comes from that part only. Your intermediary sends the state a modified Form I-290 for the money that was not put into the new property.
In the example, buy a $346,000 property and keep $30,000. The intermediary sends the state about $1,560. The state tax on that $30,000 is about $880 at the top rate, and the rest comes back when you file.
Federal tax is due on the cash too. Our capital gains calculator has the federal rates.

## How do you finance the replacement inside 180 days?
The loan for the new property must close inside the same 180 days. The lender starts during the search, so the purchase and the loan move together.
Use your own lender, or our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company. Many exchange buyers use a DSCR loan , which qualifies on the property's rent.

## How does a reverse 1031 exchange work in South Carolina?
In a reverse exchange you buy first. Another party that is not you or your agent, called an exchange accommodation titleholder, takes title to the new property first.

- The titleholder takes title It holds the new property for you until the exchange is finished.

- You sign an agreement with it You and the titleholder sign a written agreement within 5 business days after it takes title.

- You name the property you will sell Do it within 45 days after the titleholder takes title.

- You finish the exchange Sell the old property and finish within 180 days after the titleholder takes title.

A reverse exchange fits when the right property comes up before your sale is ready. For the tax put off with no property to manage, a Delaware statutory trust share is the other choice.

Common questions

## 1031 exchange FAQ

### Does a 1031 exchange have to be in the same state?
No. The rules are federal. Real property in the United States is generally like-kind to other US real property if both are held for business or investment. A rental in another state can be traded for one here.

### Can I 1031 exchange into a home I will live in?
Not one you only live in. A beach condo you rent out and also use can qualify when it passes the IRS rental test described on this page.

### Can I do a 1031 exchange with a family member, such as a parent or a child?
Yes, with a limit. It covers a spouse, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, brother or sister, and a company you control. If either of you sells the property you got within two years, the deferred gain is taxed. There are a few exceptions, such as a death.

### Does South Carolina tax the gain later?
Yes. The state follows the federal rules, so the gain you put off is taxed when you sell without exchanging. South Carolina deducts 44 percent of a net capital gain and taxes the rest.

### Is a company that sells a condo held back too?
Yes. For a corporation the rate is 5 percent. A business seller can be treated as a resident on Form I-295 if it meets four tests. It has done business in South Carolina for the last two tax years and will keep doing it. It is registered here and has filed a South Carolina return with none overdue.

### Can I exchange into a DST?
Yes. A share of a Delaware statutory trust can be the replacement if the trust stays inside the IRS ruling's limits and the other 1031 rules are met.

### Who reports a 1031 exchange to the IRS?
You do, on IRS Form 8824 with your tax return for the year of the exchange.

## J-1 Student Rentals in Myrtle Beach | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/j1-rentals/
Summary: Renting a Myrtle Beach house to J-1 summer students: who they are, which employers hire and house them, the rent per bed, the lawful bed count and the eviction rule.

Home / Invest / J-1 rentals
Seasonal rentals

# How do you rent a Myrtle Beach house to J-1 students? The program, the employers, the beds, the rules.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
J-1 students staff the Myrtle Beach summer and rent by the bed. A house holds as many as its bedroom floor area allows, at $100 to $140 a week each.

The short answer
J-1 students are college students from abroad, here on a four-month summer work visa. South Carolina hosted about 3,000 of them in 2025. Myrtle Beach was the fourth busiest destination in the country.
They rent by the bed, three or four to a room, at about $100 to $140 a week each. That is the appeal. One house, four months, several rents at once.
The limit is how many people the house may lawfully hold. The city counts bedroom floor area, 70 square feet for the first person and 50 for each one after that. A 2,500 square foot four-bedroom house holds about 10 to 13 people. A garage holds none.
We have walked through a house here with more than 60 J-1 students living in it. That is the case this page tells you not to copy, and the sections below say why.
Talk about buying a J-1 house

## What is a J-1 student, and why do they rent in Myrtle Beach?
A J-1 student is a full-time college student from another country on a Summer Work Travel visa. The program allows up to four months of seasonal work during the student's summer break, and no extension. Most students have a job before they arrive , through a sponsor organization that screens them and vets the employer.
They rent here because the jobs are here. Myrtle Beach has about 35,000 residents and about 17 million visitors a year . Hotels, restaurants and attractions need summer staff the town cannot supply. The city has hosted about 8,500 J-1 students since 2018 .
The State Department counted 104,609 Summer Work Travel students in 2025 . South Carolina had 3,003 of them, the 14th most of any state. Myrtle Beach was the fourth busiest destination in the country , after Ocean City, Orlando and Wisconsin Dells. No source gives the exact Myrtle Beach count.
The top sending countries in 2025 were Jamaica, Thailand, Mexico, Peru, Romania, Turkey, Ecuador and the Dominican Republic. Each country has its own program window . Most run May to September. Peru, Argentina, Brazil, Chile and South Africa run December to April, so some students are here in winter.

## Which employers hire the most J-1 students, and do they house them?
The employers with the most seasonal jobs. The president of Lazarus Entertainment Group said in November 2024 that 150 of the 500 summer staff at Myrtle Waves Water Park and Broadway Grand Prix are J-1 students. He said he had been pre-renting houses around the city to get enough beds. He had reserved 150 beds in the new residence hall for the next summer.
The owner of Extreme Pizza and Toasted Yolk Cafe told a reporter in February 2026 that without the students the summer would be like 2021. That was the year no one had enough staff. Sponsor job listings for the area show a pizza restaurant, a diner chain and an oceanfront resort offering housing at $100 a week. A beachwear chain offers it at $110 a week, taken from the paycheck.
The rule puts the housing duty on the sponsor, not the employer. If the employer does not provide housing, the sponsor must actively and immediately assist the student in finding it. The sponsor must also consider housing that meets local codes when it places the job. No rule requires a sponsor to inspect or approve a private landlord's house, and no rule caps the rent.
One purpose-built building exists. The International Residence Hall on Globe Drive has more than 300 beds, four to a room, with weekly rent. It opened in May 2025 , with tax incentives from the city. More buildings are planned; the reported totals differ by source. Its rent is not published.
How students find a house What the source says
Employer housing first Sponsors tell students they learn at hiring whether the employer offers housing
Their own search Sponsors list Craigslist, Apartments.com, Roommates.com, Zillow and Facebook groups
Houses that advertise to them Two North Myrtle Beach operators list rooms by the week on their own sites
A landlord who works with employers One North Myrtle Beach landlord has placed seasonal workers for employers for ten years
The city's orientation site Lists one provider, the residence hall, and warns about deposit scams

There is no sponsor portal where a landlord signs up. The visitor bureau held a J-1 forum for employers, landlords and sponsors in February 2026. Employers pre-rent, and students search. A house that an employer has rented for its staff, year after year, is the steadiest version of this rental.

## How much rent does a J-1 house collect in Myrtle Beach?
Rent is per bed, per week, with the kitchen, Wi-Fi and laundry included. One North Myrtle Beach operator lists $120 a week in spring and $130 in summer , three to a room, with a 90-day minimum lease and a $260 deposit. Another lists $130 and $140 a week , four to a room in bunk beds, with a $250 deposit. Employer housing in the sponsor listings is $100 to $110 a week.
That is about $430 to $610 a month per person.

10 $550 $22,000
10 $600 $24,000
13 $600 $31,200

The bed count in the table is the lawful count for a 2,500 square foot four-bedroom house. The season is four months because the visa allows four. Deposits of $250 a person are held through the season, and the local listings keep $50 to $100 of each for cleaning and linens at checkout.
One sponsor caps a student's rent at a third of gross pay . At 32 hours a week, the minimum in several local listings, a third of pay is a few hundred dollars a month. The rent per bed has a ceiling the students' wages put on it.
Want to rent to J-1 students?
Tell us which jobs you want to be near and what you want to spend. We find the houses that hold the beds lawfully, count them room by room, and check the license and the zoning before you offer.
Talk about buying a J-1 house

## How many people can a Myrtle Beach house lawfully hold?
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach the answer comes from bedroom floor area. The city adopts the International Property Maintenance Code . Its occupancy section says a bedroom for one person needs 70 square feet, and a bedroom for two or more needs 50 square feet for each person. Kitchens and nonhabitable spaces cannot be slept in. Every bedroom needs a path to a toilet without passing through another bedroom.
A 2,500 square foot four-bedroom house: one 14 by 16 foot bedroom holds four people. Three 12 by 12 foot bedrooms hold two each. That is ten people. If the three smaller bedrooms are 12 by 14 feet, they hold three each, and the house holds thirteen. A detached garage holds no one unless it was converted under a permit with a certificate of occupancy.
North Myrtle Beach and the unincorporated county do not list the property maintenance code among their adopted codes, as mirrored online. They enforce through the building codes, their unfit-dwelling rules and, in North Myrtle Beach, the zoning definitions. Confirm the count for the exact house with the building department before you model the rent. We do that with you.

## What happens if you put too many people in the house?
We have walked through a house here with more than 60 J-1 students living in it. Do not copy it.
The fines are per day. A code violation in the city is a civil fine of up to $200 . After seven days' notice to fix it, the fine is up to $2,000 for each day it continues. Every rental in the city needs a business license . Renting without one is a misdemeanor, with up to a $500 fine and 30 days, and each day is a separate offense.
Enforcement happens, and it starts with complaints. In July 2021 a homeowner was charged for housing three J-1 students in a garage apartment he built without permits; the students were moved. In 2025 the city described reports of more than ten students in a two-bedroom space . In 2026 the fire marshal described past citations for four or five students in one bed with an air mattress in the closet.

## Is the J-1 housing market already full?
No. The people who need the beds have said so in public, by name.
The owner of Lazarus Entertainment Group said securing beds that met his standards was hard . He described putting deposits on houses all over Myrtle Beach to get enough of them, and called it difficult and challenging. He hires about 150 J-1 students a season out of 500 seasonal staff.
The city manager said the same from the other side . When the city finds a house with too many people in it, it has to have somewhere to move those young adults to. The city needs spare beds to exist before it can enforce anything.
Then count it.

Even finished, the purpose-built building holds under half the students who work here. The rest need a house.
The gap is not only beds. It is clean beds. The mayor said in 2024 that some properties are not taken care of as they should be , and that students have been taken advantage of. A partner in the residence hall said he had heard of 19 people in one house . A house inside the lawful count, with a real bed for each person, is competing against that.

## How do you find J-1 students to rent to?
Start with the employers, not the students. The big ones rent houses before the season and put their own staff in them. The president of Lazarus Entertainment Group described putting deposits on houses all over Myrtle Beach to get enough beds, and called it difficult. A house an employer takes every year fills with no advertising at all.
Sponsors will not do it for you. The State Department lists every sponsor by name and you can call them. They no longer keep lists of landlords, and they have no staff for placing students in private houses. The rule says only that the sponsor must help the student find housing and must send information about available housing before the student leaves home. Nobody inspects or approves your house.
Where to look What it gets you
Make partnerships with local employers The steadiest version. They rent early, fill the house themselves, and come back the next year.
The visitor bureau forum It put employers, landlords and sponsors in one room in February 2026 .
Facebook groups One group covers J-1 and H-2B housing for this area . Students post asking for rooms.
The sites students are told to search Sponsors name Craigslist, Apartments.com, Roommates.com and Zillow.
The city's orientation site It lists one provider and warns about deposit scams . No sign-up for landlords, so you have to ask.

Who do you ask about that site? The police department runs it as the International Student Outreach Program , with the area chamber and the hospitality association. The program takes calls at 843-918-1806 and email at j1studentoutreach@cityofmyrtlebeach.com . The hospitality association is at 843-626-9668 . Be straight about what you are asking. Neither publishes a landlord list, so you are asking them to point students at a house, not to add you to a form.
Write the listing the way a student reads it. The weekly rent per bed. The deposit and what comes back. How far to work, in miles. A photo of the bed. Sponsors tell students to ask those exact questions , so answer them before they ask.
List the house over the winter. Employers plan the season months ahead, and the students land in May. A house first listed in March is late.

## What do J-1 students look for in a Myrtle Beach rental?

- Close to work without a car. One operator says all its houses are under two miles from the job and most students rent or buy a bike. Every Coast RTA bus carries two bikes . A house near the oceanfront employers or on a bus route fills first.

- A kitchen, Wi-Fi and laundry. Every local listing advertises all three. Linens are sometimes included.

- Weekly rent and a clear deposit. Sponsors tell students to ask the weekly cost, the deposit and what is refundable , and to check the occupancy limit in the lease.

- No scams. The city's orientation site warns students about people who take deposits and provide no room . Sponsors tell them never to wire money before arrival. A landlord who shows the house on a video call and takes the deposit on arrival removes that fear.

- Smoke detectors. Sponsors tell students to check for them. The 2013 motel closure in the city was for missing detectors and seven or eight people in rooms built for four.

## How do you screen and lease to J-1 tenants?
One lease per person, in English. Sponsors assume an English lease and tell students to read it and keep a signed copy. Put the move-in and move-out dates, the rent, the deposit and the occupancy limit in it. The student must report the address to the sponsor within ten days , so the sponsor has your address on file.
Screen every applicant the same way. National origin is a protected class , and a rule that all tenants must speak English is a practice federal housing regulators call suspect . A passport is a photo ID. Sponsors tell students a landlord can ask for photo ID, an employer letter and proof of funds from home. Every student has the sponsor's 24-hour number and can give it to you.
End the lease before the program does. The visa allows four months plus 30 days to travel, and the student must leave the country by then. A fixed term that ends on the job's end date, with the deposit returned to an address abroad, is the clean version. The landlord rules page has the deposit clock and the notices.

## What happens if you need to evict a J-1 tenant?
The same law as any tenant. The state landlord and tenant act applies to every dwelling in the state and says nothing about citizenship. The grounds are unpaid rent, a term that has ended, or a broken lease . More people in the house than the lease allows is a broken lease, and the fourteen-day notice applies.
Weekly rent with no fixed term makes a week-to-week tenancy, which either side ends on seven days' written notice. A fixed term ends on its date. Fifteen days of unexplained absence after unpaid rent is abandonment . The magistrate process, the writ and the fees are on the landlord rules page .
The student's program does not end with the housing. Losing housing is not a ground for termination . The sponsor must actively and immediately help the student find new housing , and the student reports the new address within ten days. Sponsors list eviction as a reason to call their 24-hour line. In the 2021 garage case the city moved the students the same day.
The cost of an eviction on a four-month lease is the season. A house that stays inside the lawful count, with one lease per person and the sponsor's number in the file, rarely needs one. In Chapter3's files, the problem houses are the overfilled ones, not the tenants.

## What do you do with the house the other eight months?
The season is four months because the visa allows four . A house that sits empty from October is a worse rental than a house on one yearly lease. Plan the other eight months before you buy, not after.
Some students are here in winter. Peru, Argentina, Brazil, Chile and South Africa run December to April , so their students work our winter. How many reach this area is not published.
The residence hall has said what it does. A partner in it said H-2B workers stay nine months a year , so it expects lower winter occupancy rather than an empty building. H-2B is the other seasonal visa. Those workers staff the same hotels, golf courses and restaurants, and they stay longer than a J-1 student can.
October to April What it is
H-2B workers The same seasonal jobs, a longer stay. The residence hall is built around them.
Winter monthly renters The area's winter market runs from late October to March at the lowest rents of the year. Most of it is condos, so a house is a different offer.

Run the comparison before you buy. Four months by the bed, from the table above, collects about what a yearly lease on the same house collects in twelve. You beat a yearly lease only if you fill those eight months.
Wear is the part people forget. Ten people use a house harder than three. Budget paint and cleaning every autumn. Put the turnover between tenants into the year you model.

## What can go wrong with a J-1 rental?
Neighbors notice a full house, and the city says neighbors are how it learns about overcrowding. Stay inside the lawful count and that call does not come.
The residence hall competes at the low end, with more than 300 beds in one building, and one large employer reserved 150 of them for a summer. A clean house inside the lawful count, near the jobs, competes on quality. A duplex or fourplex spreads the same model across units; the small multifamily page has the financing. Student rentals near the university are the year-round version.

Common questions

## J-1 rental FAQ

### What is a J-1 student?
A full-time college student from another country on a Summer Work Travel visa, allowed up to four months of seasonal work during the home country's summer break. The State Department counted 104,609 of them in 2025. South Carolina had 3,003, and Myrtle Beach was the fourth busiest destination in the country.

### How much do J-1 students pay for housing in Myrtle Beach?
About $100 to $140 a week per bed, three or four to a room, with the kitchen, Wi-Fi and laundry included. That is about $430 to $610 a month per person. Deposits in the local listings are $250 to $260, with $50 to $100 kept for cleaning at checkout.

### How many J-1 students can live in one house?
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, as many as the bedroom floor area allows. That is 70 square feet for one person and 50 square feet each for two or more, with no sleeping in kitchens or garages. A 2,500 square foot four-bedroom house holds about 10 to 13 people. North Myrtle Beach and the county use their building codes and unfit-dwelling rules instead, so confirm the count for the exact house.

### Which Myrtle Beach employers hire J-1 students?
The largest reported is Lazarus Entertainment Group. Its president said 150 of the 500 summer staff at Myrtle Waves and Broadway Grand Prix are J-1 students. He pre-rents houses and reserved 150 residence hall beds. Sponsor listings also show a pizza restaurant, a diner chain, an oceanfront resort and a beachwear chain offering housing at $100 to $110 a week.

### Can you evict a J-1 student?
Yes, under the same state law as any tenant, for unpaid rent, a term that has ended or a broken lease, through the magistrate court. Losing housing does not end the student's program. The sponsor must help find new housing, and the student reports the new address within ten days.

### What months do J-1 students rent in Myrtle Beach?
Most program windows run May to September, and the visa allows four months plus 30 days to travel. Students from Peru, Argentina, Brazil, Chile and South Africa have December to April windows, so some are here in winter, but no source counts them locally.

## How do you buy a duplex or fourplex in Myrtle Beach?
A duplex, triplex or fourplex is two, three or four homes in one building, bought in one purchase with one loan. You can live in one unit and rent the others, or rent them all. Buying one takes five steps:

- Pick the kind of building and the place Buildings by the ocean cost more. Buildings away from the old beach blocks cost less. We send you the buildings for sale on the Grand Strand in the place you pick.

- Add up the rent roll The rent roll is the rent from every unit added together. For one building, our agents run the number for each unit from current local leases and listings, at no cost, before you write the offer.

- Look at the whole building We go through the expenses and any association documents with you before you write an offer.

- Choose how you will pay If you will live in one unit, you can buy it with an FHA, VA or conventional loan. If you will not, you can use an investor loan such as a DSCR loan. We introduce our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company, for the numbers.

- Offer and close We write the offer with you and work with you up to closing. The seller gives you the state's disclosure form before you both sign the contract, the same form a house comes with.

## Is a duplex a good investment in Myrtle Beach?
Yes, if you will live in one unit. You can buy it with an FHA or VA home loan. On FHA, the other units' rent can count toward your income. Your own unit can be taxed at the owner's 4 percent rate.
If you will rent every unit, the whole building is taxed at 6 percent, and you borrow a smaller share of the price. Then two things count most: what each home costs, and where the building stands.

## Can you live in one unit and rent the others? FHA and VA in Horry County
Yes. Living in one unit and renting the others is called house hacking. FHA insures loans on buildings of one to four units that the buyer will live in as their main home.
At least one buyer must move in within 60 days of signing and plan to live there for at least a year.

### Loans that fit a building you live in

- FHA Rent from the other units can count toward your income. With no rent history, the lender counts 75 percent of the lower of the appraiser's market rent and the lease.

- VA A veteran can buy a home of up to 4 units with a VA loan , if the veteran will live in it. Our VA loan guide covers who qualifies.

- Conventional On Freddie Mac's standard loans, the top loan on a 2 to 4 unit building you live in matches its top loan on a one-unit home. Freddie Mac's system must accept the loan. Some of its low down payment programs allow more on a one-unit home only.

When every buyer on the loan will live there, FHA asks the same smallest down payment on a duplex or fourplex as on a one-unit home. If a co-borrower, even a family member, will not live in a 2 to 4 unit building, FHA asks for a much larger down payment.
Our first-time buyer guide has FHA's other rules.

### If you will not live there
On Freddie Mac's loans, an investor who lives elsewhere borrows a smaller share of the price. A DSCR loan is one choice: the lender qualifies the loan on the rent, not on your income.

### The tax on a building you live in
In South Carolina, the home you live in is taxed on 4 percent of its value, once you apply. The rented units on the same property are taxed on 6 percent. Our property tax guide covers the application.
About 1 in 6 of these buildings is taxed at the owner's 4 percent rate on all or part of it.

## What is the FHA self-sufficiency test for a triplex or fourplex?
For an FHA loan on a triplex or fourplex, the rents must cover the loan . FHA takes the rent from every unit, including yours, and subtracts 25 percent, or the appraiser's figure for empty months and upkeep if that is larger. The monthly loan payment, taxes and insurance must not be more than what is left.
Worked example: FHA's rent test on a fourplex

- Four 2-bedroom units at about $1,000 a month each $4,000

- Less 25 percent for empty months and upkeep &minus;$1,000

- The rent FHA counts $3,000

FHA uses the appraiser's rent estimates, so your building's figures can differ.

The lender must also see savings equal to three months of the full monthly payment, taxes and insurance, left after closing. A duplex does not take the test.

## Can you Airbnb a duplex in Myrtle Beach?
Not on an FHA loan. On an FHA loan for a 2 to 4 unit building, the buyer signs HUD's form 92561 . On it, the buyer promises not to rent any part of the building for under 30 days, or with hotel services, while the FHA loan is in place.
Each town on the Grand Strand has its own rules for nightly rentals. Our short-term rental rules guide covers them. Renting to summer workers by the season is in our J-1 rentals guide .

## Duplex and fourplex FAQ

### What is the FHA loan limit for a duplex in Horry County?
$693,050 for 2026. The limit is the largest loan FHA insures on a duplex here, not the price you pay. It is higher for a triplex or a fourplex.

### Can I use a VA loan on a duplex?
Yes. A veteran can buy a building of up to four units with a VA loan if the veteran will live in one of them.

### How much down payment does a duplex need if I live in it?
On an FHA loan, the same smallest down payment as a one-unit home, when every buyer on the loan will live there. Our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company, gives the numbers for one building.

### Is a fourplex a commercial property?
Not for an FHA home loan. FHA's home loan programs cover buildings of one to four homes that the buyer lives in.

### Does the seller of a duplex have to give a disclosure form?
Yes. The seller of a home of one to four units must give the buyer the state's disclosure form. A duplex or fourplex comes with the same form as a house.

### Can a South Carolina city cap the rent on my units?
No. South Carolina does not let a city or county limit rents on privately owned homes.

## Buying a Condo in Litigation in Myrtle Beach: When It's a Deal
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/condo-in-litigation/
Summary: Can you buy or finance a Myrtle Beach condo in litigation? What Fannie Mae and FHA allow, which suits are minor, real Grand Strand cases, and when it is a deal.

Home / Buyers / Condo in Litigation
Condo lawsuits

# Can you buy a condo in litigation in Myrtle Beach? Yes. A building that has already made its repairs can be the best deal in Myrtle Beach.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
You can still buy a Myrtle Beach condo in a building with a lawsuit, with cash or a loan made outside Fannie Mae's rules.

The short answer
Yes, you can buy a condo in a building that is in a lawsuit. Cash works, because the building rules of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA apply to the loans they buy or insure. Most of those loans cannot be used while the suit runs, unless it is a minor kind.
A building that has already made the repairs it sued over can be a real chance. FHA loans usually cannot be used there, and a conventional loan works only after the lender finds the suit minor. That leaves fewer buyers to compete for each unit. A suit over a structural problem not yet repaired can mean a large bill for every owner.

Heard the building is in a lawsuit? We find out what it is about before you offer.
Ask about a building

On this page

- Getting a loan

- What still works

- How we find out

- When it is a deal

- How long suits last

- Condo in litigation FAQ

## Can you get a mortgage on a condo in litigation?
Usually you cannot use a conventional or FHA loan, unless the suit is minor. Fannie Mae will not buy a loan on a unit in a building whose association is named in a pending lawsuit. The same goes when the developer is in a suit about the building's safety, structure, livability or use.
The exception is a suit the lender finds minor, in one of the ways Fannie Mae's guide lists. Freddie Mac's rule is close to Fannie Mae's. Arbitration or mediation that is expected to become a lawsuit counts the same as a suit.

### Which lawsuits count as minor?
If the lender finds the suit touches none of the four things named above, these suits can be minor:

- The association sues an owner for unpaid dues Or it forecloses on a unit for them. Our guide to HOA liens and foreclosure covers those suits.

- The insurer defends it and pays The association's insurer has agreed to defend the suit, and the association's insurance covers the amount.

- Small next to the savings The expected damages and legal costs are no more than 10 percent of the building's funded reserves, the money it has saved for repairs.

- Repairs already made The association is suing to recover money for repairs already made, and losing would not hurt it.

- Damage to one unit The suit is about damage to a single unit.

- No money at stake A dispute between neighbors, for example, where no one is asking for money.

A suit the association brings against the builder over defects is not minor while the repairs are still to be made.

### What does FHA allow?
FHA turns down a building in a suit about the same four things as Fannie Mae's rule, or one with a risk the association's insurance does not cover. For an FHA loan on one unit, such a suit still counts for 12 months after it ends.
Which loans work, by kind of lawsuit Kind of lawsuit Conventional loan FHA loan Cash
The association sues an owner for unpaid dues Conventional loan Yes FHA loan Yes Cash Yes
The insurer defends the suit, and insurance covers it Conventional loan Yes FHA loan Yes Cash Yes
The association sues the builder over repairs already made Conventional loan Yes, if the lender finds it minor FHA loan Usually not Cash Yes
A suit about the building's safety or structure Conventional loan No FHA loan No Cash Yes

A conventional loan here means one sold to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. A "Yes" for a loan means the lender finds the suit minor and not about the building's safety or structure. Cash has no loan for these rules to govern; the risk of a large bill stays with you.
A building can fail Fannie Mae's rules for a building for other reasons too, such as how many units are rentals.

## Which loans still work on a condo in litigation?

- Cash The building rules of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA apply to the loans they buy or insure. A cash purchase has no such loan.

- A loan kept outside Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac Some lenders keep a loan or sell it to other investors. Each writes its own building rules. One published program reviews lawsuits case by case, and will not consider one about the building's structure.

For a suit about the structure, cash may be the only way to buy. Cash does not remove the risk. A large repair bill still comes to you as an owner, and your next buyer needs a loan too, unless they pay cash.
Our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company, can tell you which loans fit the building. How those loans work is in our guide to condo loans outside Fannie Mae's rules .
Chapter3 Realty Corp has a business relationship with BrickWood Mortgage (NMLS #189497). Because of this relationship, this referral may provide Chapter3 Realty a financial or other benefit. You are never required to use BrickWood. You are free to shop any lender.

## How do you find out if a condo is in litigation?
We find out for you, before you make an offer. Our building review on every condo purchase covers any lawsuit. These papers show whether a building is in a suit, and why:

- The questionnaire lenders send It asks the association whether it is in a lawsuit, and asks for papers from its attorney. More on that form is in our guide to HOA documents .

- The attorney's letter For a suit the lender finds minor but whose cost is unknown, Freddie Mac asks for the complaint and a letter from the association's attorney. If the letter says insurance will likely not pay, the building fails Freddie Mac's rule.

- What FHA asks To approve a building with a suit, FHA wants a signed explanation. It gives the reason, the risk, when the suit may end, whether insurance can pay, and what it does to the association's money.

- The court record Horry County's court cases are listed in the state's public index, linked from the Clerk of Court's page . A suit in federal court, like Renaissance Tower's, is listed elsewhere.

The seller's state form asks about common-area problems and special assessments, not about a lawsuit, so we ask the association.
Send us the building's name.
We find out whether its association is in a lawsuit, what the suit is about, and what it could cost you, before you offer.
Ask about a building's lawsuits

## When is a condo in litigation a good deal?
A building in a suit can be a good deal when its association is suing the builder for repairs it has already made. The building has been fixed, and the owners are trying to get back money they already spent. With most FHA buyers out while the suit runs, there is less competition for each unit.
Photo: USGS
Oceanfront condo towers in Myrtle Beach, with their pools behind the dunes, seen from a plane over the ocean.

- A chance: the builder is sued, and the repairs are done Before you offer, have a lender review the suit. If it finds the suit minor, a conventional loan can work there.

- A warning: a structural problem not yet repaired A large repair bill may come to every owner as a special assessment. Our guide explains how a special assessment is set .

- A warning: owners suing their own board In the Renaissance Tower case, owners sued the board members and the management company over repairs and the savings for them.

### Can a builder still be sued over an older building?
Yes, in some cases. A defect suit must be brought within three years of when the problem was or should have been found. For a building finished after mid-2005, the limit is eight years after completion; older buildings had 13.
Neither limit protects a builder guilty of fraud, gross negligence or recklessness. A suit claiming gross negligence can come years later, as Wedgewood's did.
73 condos in buildings built in 2018 or later were for sale in the local MLS on November 10, 2026, out of 2,860 in all.

Most condos for sale here are in buildings past the usual time limit for a builder suit. A new builder suit is less likely there, but we still check the record for one before you offer.

Get the condos for sale in Myrtle Beach

## How long does condo litigation last on the Grand Strand?
In the Grand Strand condo cases we read in the court record, 7 to 14 years passed from the first filing to the last ruling. A suit just filed can run for years. A suit near its end can be worth waiting out.
Grand Strand condo lawsuits ran 7 to 14 years Condo complex and its years in court Years from filing to the last ruling

Riverwalk at Arrowhead Sued 2003, jury verdict 2009, last ruling 2017 14 years
Magnolia North Sued 2003, jury verdict 2009, last ruling 2017 14 years
Wedgewood Sued 2018, last ruling 2025 7 years
2000 2010 2020

Each bar runs from the year the association sued to the last court ruling we read. For Riverwalk and Magnolia North, the last ruling decided what the builder's insurer had to pay.

### Riverwalk at Arrowhead Country Club and Magnolia North
These two condo complexes in Myrtle Beach were built from 1997 to 2002. Both associations sued the builder in 2003. Juries found for both in 2009, and the Court of Appeals affirmed in 2011 and 2012.
At trial, the associations' experts put Magnolia North's repairs at about $9.2 million, and the defense's experts at about $2.4 million. While a suit runs, no one knows the size of the bill.
The builder had gone out of business in 2003. Whether its insurer had to pay the verdicts was decided by the state Supreme Court in 2017.

### Wedgewood
Wedgewood is a nine-building condo complex in Horry County, built from 2000 to 2001. The association sued in 2018, about 17 years after it was built. A jury found gross negligence, which lifts the time limit, and the Court of Appeals affirmed in 2025.

### Renaissance Tower
Renaissance Tower is a 21-story oceanfront condo building in Myrtle Beach. In October 2022, an engineer found it not structurally sound and ordered it evacuated. Owners sued in federal court that month.
The owners' lawsuit says some owners could not sell, and some buyers backed out of contracts. It says owners faced an assessment of more than $2 million for the steel repairs, and the association had less than $1.3 million in reserves in 2022.
51 Renaissance Tower units changed hands in the past year, after the evacuation and the owners' suit.

Units changed hands at the other three complexes too: 37 at Magnolia North, 23 at Riverwalk and 8 at Wedgewood. A building with a suit in its past still sells.

## Condo in litigation FAQ

### Can you get an FHA loan on a condo in litigation?
Not when the suit is about the building's safety, structure, livability or use, or carries a risk its insurance does not cover. For an FHA loan on one unit, such a suit still counts for 12 months after it ends.

### Does a lawsuit against an owner for unpaid dues stop a condo loan?
No. Fannie Mae and FHA do not count a suit the association brings to collect past-due dues or to foreclose on a unit.

### Does the seller have to tell you the building is in a lawsuit?
The state's disclosure form asks about common-area problems and special assessments, not about a lawsuit. We ask the association instead.

### How long does condo litigation last?
From 7 to 14 years. In three Grand Strand condo cases we read in the court record, that was the time from the association's suit to the last ruling.

### Can you sell a condo that is in litigation?
Yes. Your buyer will need cash or a loan made outside Fannie Mae's and FHA's rules, unless the suit is a minor kind. Units changed hands in the past year in every building on this page.

## How to Find Out If a House Flooded: Myrtle Beach | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/undisclosed-flooding/
Summary: Has this house flooded before? How to find a house's flood history in Myrtle Beach and Horry County, what a seller must disclose, and the county's Florence map.

Home / Buyers / Flood History
Flood history

# Did this Myrtle Beach house flood before? How to find its flood history.

- About 3 in 4 resale houses for sale: the seller's form does not ask about Florence

- 45% of paid Florence claims were insured outside FEMA's zone

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Five checks show it: FEMA's claim records, two flood maps, the county's records, repair permits and the house itself. You get all five for any house you send.

The short answer
FEMA's records of flood insurance claims on a house go only to its owner, so we ask the seller for them. We put the house on FEMA's flood map and the county's map of the flooding from Hurricane Florence. We ask the county's staff about past floods and look for permits behind repairs. At the showing, we look for clues at the house and on its street.
We run these checks before you offer. If you learn of a flood after you sign, the South Carolina REALTORS sales contract gives you a due diligence period to end it.

Have us check a house's flood history
Send us the address

## How do you find out if a house has flooded before?
Our agents check five things. Each card says what that check can miss.

- Ask the seller for the claim records From the seller The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) runs federal flood insurance. It will not give a buyer a house's flood insurance claims: federal privacy law bars it without the owner's consent.
We ask the seller for those, and for the insurance industry's claims report on the house , called CLUE.
What it misses: A flood on a house that had no flood insurance.

- Put the house on two flood maps Public maps: we pull them FEMA's flood map is a forecast of risk. After Florence, Horry County mapped how far Florence's water went .
We put the house on both maps. Our map of the two shows where they differ. To check one address on FEMA's map, use our flood zone check guide .
What it misses: Whether water got inside. The county's map shows the ground Florence's water covered, in that one storm.

- Ask the county's floodplain staff We ask the county Horry County's floodplain staff answer "Has my property ever flooded?" and keep the county's flood history, including where floods have repeated. The county also posts the signed surveys it has on file that show how high a floor is.
What it misses: A house inside a city. Each city keeps its own records, and we ask that city.

- Look for a permit behind every repair We ask the county or city Outside city limits in Horry County, any work on a building over $500 needs a permit. Inside a city, the city issues it. A flood repair done legally leaves a permit record .
What it misses: Work done with no permit. A repair with no record is a question we put to the seller.

- Read the house and the street At the showing We use the county's questions about water around a house . We look at whether water flows away from the house or stands next to the walls, whether the ditch or storm drain is clear, and whether the downspouts carry water well away.
On the street, a house raised above its older neighbors can be one that flooded and was rebuilt. Empty lots between houses can be a flood buyout.
What it misses: Proof. These are clues, and the records above confirm or rule them out.

### What if the seller will not send the records?
If the seller refuses, or does not answer, we tell you right away. You decide with what the maps, the county and the house showed: offer, offer less, or walk away.

### Can I back out if I find a flood after I sign?
Yes, inside the due diligence period on the South Carolina REALTORS sales contract. In that period the buyer can end the contract with a written notice of termination to the seller. We tell you what ending it would cost under the contract you sign, before you sign it. That is why we run these checks first.

## Does a seller have to disclose flooding in South Carolina?
Yes, on the state's disclosure form, but only for the years the seller owned the house. South Carolina law requires the form for a home with one to four units. The seller hands it over before you sign the contract, unless the contract says otherwise. Our guide to the seller disclosure form lists every question on it.
The form asks about floods, flood insurance claims, flood repairs and federal flood aid, each only for the seller's years. One question asks about any flood risk the seller knows of.
For about 3 in 4 resale houses for sale here, Florence came before the seller bought Before the seller bought The form does not ask.

### What does "No Representation" mean?
It is an answer on the form. A seller may choose it only when they do not have the knowledge to answer. The form says a seller may not choose it to avoid a question, must still disclose what they know, and is not freed from liability by it.

### Which sales need no disclosure form?
Some sales need no form at all. Among them are estate and trust sales, foreclosure sales, public auctions, the first sale of a new home no one has lived in , and a sale where both sides agree in writing to skip it. In those sales, the five checks matter more.

## Can a house flood if it is not in a flood zone?
Yes, and in Horry County it happens most in rain and river floods. Since 1978, nearly 1 in 4 paid flood insurance claims here were on buildings insured as outside FEMA's high-risk zone. That means the policy was priced for a lower-risk zone.

Each bar is the share of that storm's paid flood claims, out of 100 percent, on buildings insured as outside FEMA's high-risk zone. Storms are grouped by their main cause of flooding in FEMA's records.
In storm surge, almost every paid claim here was inside FEMA's high-risk zone. In rain and river floods, far more were outside it.

### What Florence did
During Hurricane Florence in 2018, the Waccamaw River at Conway rose to a record crest , more than three feet above the old record from Hurricane Matthew in 2016 . Nearly 1,000 homes and businesses near the river flooded, many of them badly.

### Does a clean claim history mean the house never flooded?
No. A house with no flood insurance leaves no flood claim. Horry County has about one federal flood policy for every seven residential buildings, so most houses here have no federal flood policy to claim on.

## Should you buy a house that flooded?
Buy a house that flooded only when three things are true. Our agents check each one.

- It was repaired with permits Each flood repair has its permit on file, as in check 4.
We match each repair to its permit record.

- It is raised, or its risk is known If repairs after a flood cost 50 percent or more of the house's value before it, the house must be raised above the flood height on FEMA's map .
We pull the survey of how high its floor sits.

- You know the flood insurance cost A house's federal flood claims stay with the address , not the owner, and its claim history can raise the cost of its flood insurance.
We help you get a flood insurance quote on the house.

A house outside the high-risk zone can still be a repeat-flood house: nearly 1 in 5 Horry County properties on FEMA's list of repeat flood claims are outside it. The worst, which FEMA calls severe repetitive loss , pay at least 15 percent more for federal flood insurance.
A seller who took federal flood aid that required flood insurance must tell you in writing, in the sale papers, that you must keep flood insurance on the house. Federal law requires it.

### Why does a street have empty lots between houses?
Sometimes because of a flood buyout. The state's voluntary buyout program has bought dozens of homes in the Socastee area that flooded again and again. It tears the houses down, and the land stays open green space.
When a house you like sits beside empty lots, we ask the county's floodplain staff about the street's flood history.

## What if the seller did not disclose flooding?
A seller who knowingly gives false, incomplete or misleading answers on the form is liable for the buyer's actual damages from them, and court costs. The court may also award reasonable attorney fees to whichever side wins.
Your own buyer's agent , under a written agreement, must tell you every serious problem the agent knows of. A fact that significantly lowers the value or the soundness of the house counts.
Where a complaint about a flood no one told you about goes The problem Who handles it
A seller who knew and did not tell you A South Carolina real estate attorney
An agent who knew and did not tell you Real Estate Commission and an attorney
A dispute over the sales contract An attorney, not the Commission

The Real Estate Commission takes complaints against licensed agents, not private sellers, and it does not handle contract disputes. Claims like these have deadlines in South Carolina law . Many are three years, and for fraud the time starts when the fraud is discovered.
If you already bought a house that flooded and the seller hid it, talk to a South Carolina real estate attorney. We work with several attorneys here and can introduce you. Chapter3 Realty does not give legal advice.

### How a flood check can change an offer
Example: A buyer likes a house near the Waccamaw River. The seller bought after Florence and answers No to every flood question on the form.
A Chapter3 agent puts the lot on the county's Florence flood map. Florence's water covered the yard. The agent asks for the house's FEMA claim records, and the seller will not send them.
The buyer walks away and offers on a house a mile off, on land the water did not cover.

The form never asked about that flood. The county's map showed it.

Common questions

## Flood history questions

### Can I get a CLUE report on a house I want to buy?
No. Only the owner, an insurer or a lender can order the CLUE report on a house, and it covers only recent years. We ask the seller to order it.

### Can I see FEMA flood claims by address?
Not until you own the house. Once you do, you can ask FEMA for its claims, including those from before you owned it.

### What is a severe repetitive loss property?
Severe repetitive loss is FEMA's label for a house that has flooded again and again. FEMA uses it for four or more paid flood claims over $5,000 each, or for building payments that add up to more than the house is worth, with two of them within 10 years of each other. The label stays with the address when the house sells.

### Will the lender tell me if the house is in a flood zone?
Yes, if the house is in FEMA's high-risk zone and the loan is from a bank or other federally regulated lender. The lender must make sure you are told in writing a reasonable time before you sign. The notice is about the zone, not about past floods.

## Myrtle Beach DST 1031 Exchange: Fees, Limits, Exits | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/strategies/dst/
Summary: A DST (Delaware statutory trust) lets you sell a rental, put off the tax and stop managing. What it costs, who can buy one and what you give up.

Home / Invest / DST
Strategy

# DST: the hands-off 1031 for a Grand Strand rental Swap a Grand Strand rental for a share of a large property: no tenants, tax put off, about 6% to sales commissions.

- What you get No tenants, tax later

- Who can buy $1M+ net worth or $200K+ income

- Usual minimum $100,000

- Sales commission About 6% of your money

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
A Delaware statutory trust (DST) owns real estate and sells shares in it. A share can replace your rental in a 1031 exchange, a trade that puts off the tax.

The short answer
In a DST, a sponsor, the real estate company that forms the trust, buys the property and runs it. You get a share of the cash it has left over. In return, you usually get your money back only when the trust sells, the payout can fall, and sales commissions come out of your money first.
It fits only if you are done managing, pass the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) wealth test, and will not need the money for years.

We time the sale of your Grand Strand rental to your exchange deadlines.
Plan my rental sale

- How a DST works

- What you give up

- Who can buy

- Cost and minimum

- Getting out

- As a 1031 backup

- DSTs here

- What we do

- DST questions

## Should you sell your Grand Strand rental into a DST, another rental, or pay the tax?
On a $400,000 rental sale on the Grand Strand, the Myrtle Beach area, you choose between paying the tax now, keeping the work of a rental, or giving up control of the money. The numbers are our example, worked through below.
Three choices for our $400,000 example sale What changes Sell and pay the tax 1031 into another rental 1031 into a DST
Tax this year about $39,000, or more at higher incomes None yet None yet
Income None from this rental The rent, less your costs A share of leftover cash, not fixed
Work each month None Yours, or a manager's None
When you get the money At closing When you sell that rental When the trust sells

### Which one fits

- A DST, if you would rather own a share of a large property someone else runs than a rental of your own.

- Another rental here, if you want to pick the property, set the rent and decide when to sell. Our 1031 exchange guide covers the deadlines and how we find a replacement on the Grand Strand.

- Paying the tax, if you want the cash now, or the tax is small next to what a DST would cost you to enter.

- Keeping the rental, if the work is the only problem. A property manager takes the calls, and our page on how long to hold a rental shows what waiting has meant here.

What would your rental sell for?
Send us the address, and we price it, so you weigh the three choices with your own sale price.
Have us price my rental

## Why does the IRS allow a DST in a 1031 exchange, and who sells one?
The IRS, in Revenue Ruling 2004-86 , has ruled that you may trade a rental for a share of a Delaware statutory trust with no tax on the gain yet. The trust must follow the ruling's limits, and the other 1031 rules must be met.
You buy the share through a securities firm or broker, called the DST broker on this page. Anyone who sells you a DST share must be registered with the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), the SEC or the state before they can sell you anything. FINRA's BrokerCheck lists each securities firm and broker, with their licenses and record.

## What do you give up in a DST, and can you lose money?
The ruling requires these limits on the trust:

- The trust cannot take in new money from anyone. A large repair has to be paid from the trust's own cash. That cash is not paid out to you.

- It cannot refinance its loan or sign a new lease. In the ruling, the trust may sign a new lease only if its tenant goes bankrupt or insolvent. A DST with many tenants, such as an apartment community, can lease the whole property to one master tenant. In one large sponsor's program , the master tenant is a company the sponsor owns. It signs the tenants, pays the costs of running the property and pays the trust its rent. Either way, the trust depends on one tenant's rent.

- You have no say in when the property sells. The trust's manager decides.

### What does a DST pay you?
The trust pays out the cash the property has left, less reserves, on a set schedule. In the IRS ruling, that is every quarter. The amount moves with the rent and with the cash held back for repairs.
The SEC filings we checked have no payout figure. If the sponsor projects a payout, the projection is in its offering document, often called a private placement memorandum (PPM).
To compare a DST with your rental, set the PPM's projected payout for a year on your share next to what your rental leaves you in a year: the rent, less every cost you pay, the mortgage included. Ask the DST broker for the PPM before you name a DST in your exchange, and look for four things in it:

- Every fee, with its amount.

- The projected payout, and what it rests on.

- How long the sponsor plans to hold the property.

- Who the tenants are, and how long their leases run.

### Can you get back less than you put in?
Yes. You get back your share of what is left of the sale price after the trust's loan is paid off. The sales commissions and the sponsor's fees were paid out of the money first, so the property has to gain value before your share is worth what you paid. If it sells for less than the trust paid, you get back less still.
Want to pick your own property instead?
We find and show you Grand Strand rentals you could buy in your exchange instead of a DST share.
Have us find a rental to buy

## Who can buy a DST?
Most DSTs are sold only to buyers who pass the SEC's wealth test, called accredited investors . For a person, you pass with either of these:

### Net worth
Over $1 million Alone or with a spouse or partner, not counting your home.

### Income
Over $200,000 Or $300,000 with a spouse or partner, in each of the last two years, with the same expected this year.

Holders of certain securities licenses also pass. Plan on needing to pass. Of the 160 DST real estate offerings we checked in the last year's SEC Form D filings, 159 had sold only to buyers who pass, as of the filing.
Most of them were filed under SEC Rule 506(c) , part of the SEC's Regulation D. Under it, the sponsor must check that you pass. The rule lists ways to check:

- Income: your IRS forms for the last two years, such as W-2s, 1099s, K-1s or your Form 1040.

- Net worth: bank and brokerage statements from the last three months, and a credit report.

- A letter from your CPA, your lawyer, a registered broker-dealer or an SEC-registered investment adviser that says they checked.

## What does a DST cost, and what is the minimum investment?
The usual minimum is $100,000. Sales commissions are about 6 percent of the money, and the sponsor's other fees come on top. The Form D filings show only the sales commissions. The other fees are in the PPM.
The minimum investment in 156 DST offerings Minimum, note Offerings

$1,000 · 20 from one sponsor; must pass the wealth test 21 offerings
$25,000 to $99,999 42 offerings
$100,000 · the most common minimum 57 offerings
$100,001 to $499,999 19 offerings
$500,000 or more 17 offerings

Of the 160 DST offerings we checked, 156 named a minimum.

### What the commission means on a $400,000 sale
Our example is the same as on our capital gains page : a Grand Strand rental bought for $250,000 and sold for $400,000, with $60,000 of depreciation taken, a gain of $186,000. A 1031 exchange into a rental or a DST puts off all of the tax. A higher-income seller owes up to about $7,100 more than the chart shows, the 3.8 percent net investment income tax .
Our $400,000 example sale: the tax put off, and the DST's sales commissions What, detail Dollars

Tax the exchange puts off · federal and South Carolina, before the 3.8% tax $39,000
DST sales commissions on the money you put in · about 6% of $376,000 $23,000

After selling costs, $376,000 is left, and it goes into the DST. The DST's commissions come on top of those selling costs.
The sales commissions alone come to about half the tax the exchange puts off, or more, before the sponsor's other fees. You do not get the commissions back. The tax is still owed later, unless you exchange again or still own the share at your death.

## How do you get your money out of a DST?
Mostly when the trust sells its property. The sponsor's planned hold is in the PPM. The SEC filings we checked do not show it. The trust in Revenue Ruling 2004-86 was set up to end after 10 years or when its building sold, whichever came first. A DST can end for you in four ways:

### You want out early
Plan to stay in until the trust sells. DST shares cannot be resold on a public market unless the conditions of SEC Rule 144 are met. A private buyer, if you find one, decides what to pay.

### The trust sells the property
You get your share of the money. Put it into a new 1031 exchange, with new deadlines, or pay the tax.

### A REIT buys back your shares
Some DSTs are sold by large real estate companies called REITs (real estate investment trusts). After two years, the REIT may take back your shares, for cash or for units that cannot go into a later 1031 exchange, at the REIT's choice. If you get the units, your exchanges stop there. At least 13 REITs described this kind of buy-back in their latest annual reports.

### You still own it at your death
Your heirs generally take it at its value on the date of death, so the gain you put off is not taxed to them. A rental you keep until death gets the same rule, 26 U.S.C. 1014 .

## Can a DST rescue a 1031 exchange that is going wrong?
Only if the DST is on the list you name by day 45. A 1031 exchange trades real property only for other real property. Every replacement, a DST share included, must be named in writing within 45 days of the sale. A DST named as a backup can still be bought if the rental you wanted falls through.
The exchange covers less of the tax if you keep cash or the sale pays off a mortgage:

- Cash you keep. You can put part of the money into the exchange and keep the rest. The cash you keep is taxed, up to the amount of your gain.

- A mortgage the sale paid off. It counts as cash you received and is taxed the same way, unless the replacement carries as much debt or you add cash. A DST can help: your share of its loan can count toward that debt. If your rental has a mortgage, raise it with your intermediary and tax adviser before you choose a DST. We give them the closing figures.

Common questions

## DST questions

### Is a DST the same as a 1031 exchange?
No. A 1031 exchange is the tax rule. A DST share is one kind of property you can buy with it.

### Is a DST a REIT?
No. A REIT is a company, and its owners hold shares in it. A DST share counts, for federal income tax, as owning part of the trust's real estate itself. Because of that, it can go into a 1031 exchange.

### How is income from a DST taxed?
For federal income tax, you are treated as owning part of the trust's real estate. Your share of the rent goes on your own return, and you deduct your share of the depreciation.

### Are you personally liable for a DST's loan?
Not in the trust the IRS ruling describes. The trust took over the property's loan, and neither the trust nor any owner is personally liable on it.

## How much does it cost to own a Myrtle Beach condo each year?
About $18,000 a year before insurance and the loan, for the middle two-bedroom for sale in an oceanfront building with a Myrtle Beach address. The HOA fee is most of it. Our page on whether HOA fees are tax deductible covers the fee on a condo you rent out.
One typical oceanfront condo, a year
HOA fee $1,075 a month $12,900
Property tax City of Myrtle Beach, at the rental rate $5,200
Total before insurance and the loan $18,100
The middle two-bedroom for sale in an oceanfront building with a Myrtle Beach address asks about $340,000. Not in the total: insurance on the unit, the loan, and the running costs of renting it.

### What are HOA fees on a Myrtle Beach condo?
The middle condo for sale charges a homeowners association (HOA) fee of about $650 a month. In oceanfront buildings the middle fee is about $925. About 1 in 5 condos for sale charge more than $1,000 a month.
About 8 in 10 condos for sale say the fee includes the building's insurance, which a house owner pays alone.

### What does insurance add?
You still need a policy on your own unit, and flood cover if the building sits in a flood zone. The price depends on the unit and the cover. If you buy with us, we can get you an insurance quote for the unit before you make an offer.
A unit you rent out costs more to insure. In our files, a landlord policy on a house costs 15 to 20 percent more than a homeowner policy on the same house. Nationally, the Insurance Information Institute puts it at about 25 percent more.

### What property tax does a rental condo pay?
A condo you rent out or keep as a second home is taxed at the 6 percent rate. The home you live in is taxed at 4 percent.
Property tax on a South Carolina condo, by how it is used How the condo is used The tax rate applies to
The home you live in 4 percent of its value
A unit rented out 6 percent of its value
A second home 6 percent of its value

The rate is the share of the value that is taxed, not the tax. On the $340,000 example, 6 percent is about $20,000. The 2026 tax rates in the City of Myrtle Beach turn that into about $5,200 a year, before the exemption below. Outside city limits it would be about $4,100; some fire districts add more.
If you buy a condo already taxed at 6 percent and keep it at 6 percent, a quarter of its new value is exempt. The taxed value cannot fall below the county's current market value for it, so the tax inside the city could fall to about $3,900 at the lowest. You or your agent must tell the county assessor before January 31 of the first year you claim it.

### Who pays the lodging tax?
The guest, on top of the price: about 13 percent in lodging taxes on a stay under 90 days inside the City of Myrtle Beach.

## Can you rent out a Myrtle Beach condo by the night?
In most oceanfront buildings, yes. About 94 in 100 condos for sale in oceanfront buildings say they allow short-term rentals. Across all condos for sale in the county it is about 7 in 10.
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, nightly rentals are legal only in the zones the city shades on its rental map , apart from 24 grandfathered houses. They are most of the oceanfront hotel and condo strip, the Broadway at the Beach area, stretches of the US 17 Bypass and US 501, and The Market Common's town center. About 3 in 4 condos in the city sit in those zones.

### Who are your neighbors in a condo building?
Mostly investors and second-home owners. About 1 in 5 condo units here is taxed at the 4 percent rate for a home its owner lives in. Of the county's other homes, about 6 in 10 are.
Homes in Horry County taxed at the 4 percent rate for a home its owner lives in Kind of home share

## Can you get a mortgage on a Myrtle Beach oceanfront condo?
Often not a normal one. Fannie Mae, one of the two big companies that buy normal home loans from lenders, will not buy a loan on a unit in a building run like a hotel , even if each unit is owned separately. The signs it lists:

- registration services that check guests in, as a hotel does

- the HOA or its manager renting units by the night or for short stays

- daily cleaning

- one key system for every unit, run by the building

- owners required to put their units in a shared rental pool

- rent shared with the HOA or a rental company

It also will not buy one where one person or company owns too many of the units, or in a building facing large repairs that no one has paid for.

### What is a non-warrantable condo?
A condo in a building that fails these tests. Lenders call it non-warrantable . Buildings with a rental program usually are, because so many owners are investors. That also shows the building is run for renting.
For you it means a larger down payment, so more of your cash stays in that unit and cannot fund the next purchase. A loan officer at our preferred lender can tell you which loans work, including a DSCR loan , which is approved on what the unit rents for.

### Can you use an FHA or VA loan on a Myrtle Beach condo?
Rarely. About 1 in 9 condos for sale say they accept an FHA loan, and about 1 in 12 a VA loan. That is what the seller's agent wrote. The FHA's own list holds only 9 approved condo buildings in Horry County, so we confirm the building with the lender before you offer.

## Where are the bargains on Myrtle Beach condos?
With an owner in trouble, in a sound building. In our own files, condos bought from a distressed owner in a stable building sold for about 22 percent less on average. The building still qualifies for normal loans; only that one unit was mismanaged.
Want a condo like that?
