## What should you look for in a Myrtle Beach condo building?
The building matters more than the unit. Two units with the same view can cost and earn different amounts because their buildings differ. Five parts of a building matter most:

- The budget and the fee. What the fee pays for, how much it has risen, and whether the HOA collects enough to pay its bills.

- The savings for repairs. How much the HOA has saved for roofs, elevators and balconies, and any special assessment voted or planned. An older building may charge one for a large repair.

- The rental rules. Whether the rules allow short-term rentals, and whether the building runs its own rental program.

- The loan. Whether a normal loan, an FHA loan or a VA loan works in the building.

- The flood zone. About 1 in 6 condos sold last year sat in a high-risk flood zone, against about 1 in 10 other homes.

### Can you owe the seller's HOA dues?
Yes, up to a limit. Under South Carolina's condo law, a buyer owes the seller's unpaid HOA dues together with the seller, unless the buyer bought at a foreclosure sale. Your share is capped at the amount on a statement the HOA must give you when you ask for it, so the amount is known before closing.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach condo investing FAQ

### Can you live in a Myrtle Beach condo and rent it out part of the year?
Yes, but the home you live in loses the 4 percent tax rate if it is rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year, unless its owner is on active military duty under orders. Then it is taxed at 6 percent, like any rental.

### What do you pay the HOA when you buy a Myrtle Beach condo?
Usually a transfer fee, and often a few months of dues paid ahead into escrow. Both are common in condo buildings here, with or without a rental program.

### Is it harder to sell a Myrtle Beach condo than a house?
Usually. At last year's pace of sales, the condos for sale now would take about a year to sell, and the houses and townhouses about 4 months. A condo owner should plan on more time to sell.

### Are most Myrtle Beach condos in big buildings?
Almost half of the county's condo units are in complexes of 100 units or more. Many others are in small buildings: the middle complex has 8 units.

## Horry County Property Tax Rate: 4% vs 6%, With a Calculator
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/property-taxes/
Summary: Horry County taxes the home you live in at 4% of its value and every other home at 6%, so a rental pays three to four times more. Estimate your bill.

Home / Buyers / Property Taxes
Property taxes

# Horry County property tax rates: 4% if you live there, 6% if you don't.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Horry County property taxes: live in the house and pay one of the lowest bills on the East Coast. Rent it and pay three to four times more. Calculator included.
Estimate a tax bill

The direct answer

## How South Carolina's 4% and 6% property tax rates work
Every home in Horry County falls into one of two classes. Your legal residence , the home you own and live in, is assessed at 4 percent of its value. Everything else , second homes, vacation condos, rentals, investment property, is assessed at 6 percent. Those are the official names in state law, and there is no separate "second home rate": 6 percent is simply what you pay when the home is not your legal residence. The federal count for a unit you both rent and use is a different test, on our 14-day rule page .
The ratio is only half the story. Legal residences are also fully exempt from the school operating tax, the single biggest line on a Horry County bill at 109.1 mills for 2026. Six percent properties pay all of it. Stack the two rules and the real gap is not 1.5 times. It is about 3.3 times in unincorporated Horry County and about 3.8 times inside the city of Myrtle Beach. In Conway it is about 2.5 times.
Real numbers for a $400,000 house, tax year 2026:
Location 4% legal residence 6% second home / rental
City of Myrtle Beach about $1,615 about $6,110
Unincorporated Horry County about $1,470 about $4,820

Myrtle Beach's 4 percent figure includes the city's Tourism Development Fee credit, 53.4 percent of the city tax for 2026. All figures are estimates from certified 2026 millage, before the 65-plus Homestead Exemption.

Getting the 4%

## Applying for the 4% legal residence rate in Horry County
Move into a home you own and do nothing, and Horry County bills you at 6 percent. The 4 percent legal residence rate takes an application with the county Assessor, and approval turns on proving the home is your primary residence. Planning to rent it short-term instead? Start with the short-term rental rules by city . To claim the 4 percent rate you will need:

- &#10003; SC driver's license or ID for every owner-occupant, and their spouse.

- &#10003; SC vehicle registration showing the property address.

- &#10003; Redacted tax returns , the first pages of your most recent federal 1040 and SC return.

- &#10003; One per household, nationwide. You and your spouse get one 4 percent residence between you, and you certify under penalty of perjury that you claim no other.

- &#10003; The 72-day rental rule. Rent the home more than 72 days in a calendar year and the 4 percent is gone. Fourteen days or fewer and the rental income is federal income tax free on top.

The legal window runs through January 15 of the year after the tax year, but the county asks for applications by May 31 so your October bill prints at 4 percent from the start. File once and it stays until something changes; you have six months to report a change like moving out or renting it. Relocating here? Getting the license, registration, and this application done in the right order is part of our relocation checklist .

The reset

## Why property taxes go up the year after you buy
This sequence surprises almost every new owner. Your first October bill is still calculated from the seller's assessment class and the seller's taxable value. Then, the following year, up to three resets land at once. The taxable value resets to roughly what you paid, because a sale is an "assessable transfer of interest." The ratio flips to 6 percent if the home is not your legal residence. With the 6 percent comes the full school operating tax. A bill that read $1,500 at closing becomes $5,000 or more twelve months later, and if your mortgage escrow was set from the old bill, the shortage gets collected from you on top. Inherited homes get the same reset when they leave the 4 percent class; details in our guide to selling an inherited house .
Investors get one partial break: the 25 percent ATI exemption. If the property was already taxed at 6 percent before you bought it, you can knock 25 percent off the new taxable value, with limits, by filing with the Assessor before January 31 of the first year you claim it. It is not automatic either. We flag it on every eligible purchase.
Our clients do not get the year-two surprise, because we never price a deal from the seller's old bill. Every analysis we run prices the tax at your future reality: your purchase price, the correct district millage, 6 percent if it is a rental. What still surprises people is what the honest number does to a deal. Taxes at the 6 percent rate can be the roughly $150 a month that turns a marginal rental's cash flow negative, and we would rather show you that before you offer than let the county show you after. Run any address through the Grand Investor Tool and the correct tax is already in the projection.

65 and older

## The South Carolina Homestead Exemption at age 65
Homeowners 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind get the first $50,000 of their legal residence's market value exempted entirely. Requirements: the home already has the 4 percent rate, one year of South Carolina residency, and you reached 65 by December 31 of the year before. In Horry County you apply in person at the Auditor's office, once; it renews on its own afterward.
On a typical bill that is another $180 to $290 a year saved, on top of a 4 percent bill that is already among the lowest of any East Coast beach market. Low carrying costs are a large part of why this area works so well on a fixed income; the full picture is on our retiring to Myrtle Beach page.

The calendar

## Horry County property tax due dates and penalties

- &#10003; Around October 1: bills mail to the owner of record.

- &#10003; January 15: last day to pay without penalty.

- &#10003; January 16 / February 2 / March 17: penalties step up 3 percent, then 10, then 15, and on March 17 the account goes delinquent and starts down the tax sale track.

- &#10003; Also separate: vehicles, boats, and RVs get their own 6 percent bills in Horry County, paid before you can register with the DMV, plus a $50 per-vehicle road fee. New residents meet these first.

Tell us the address and how you will use it. We price the bill at your purchase price and the correct district millage, not the seller's old number. Ratios and exemptions in this guide come from the South Carolina Department of Revenue and the Horry County Assessor ; millage is the county's 2026 certified schedule. Common questions

## Horry County property tax FAQ

### How much are property taxes in Myrtle Beach?
For tax year 2026, a $400,000 home in the city of Myrtle Beach pays about $1,615 a year if it is the owner's legal residence at the 4 percent rate. The same home pays about $6,100 a year at the 6 percent rate that applies to second homes and rentals. In unincorporated Horry County the same house is taxed about $1,470 at 4 percent and about $4,800 at 6 percent. The rate class matters more than the house.

### Why is the gap between the 4% and 6% rate so large?
Two reasons stack. The assessment ratio, the share of your home's value that gets taxed, is 1.5 times higher. Properties at 6 percent also pay the school operating tax, 109.1 mills in Horry County for 2026, which 4 percent legal residences are fully exempt from under Act 388. Together the real bill is about 2.5 to 3.8 times higher, depending on the town.

### How do I get the 4% legal residence rate in Horry County?
Apply with the Horry County Assessor after you move in. It is never automatic; without an approved application you are billed at 6 percent. You will need your SC driver's license or ID, SC vehicle registration at the property address, and redacted federal and state tax returns, for both spouses. The county asks for applications by May 31 so your October bill prints at the right rate. One legal residence per household, and renting the home more than 72 days a year forfeits the rate.

### Why did my property tax bill jump the year after I bought?
Your first October bill still reflects the seller's status and the seller's taxable value. The following year, three resets can hit at once. The value resets to roughly your purchase price because a sale is an assessable transfer of interest. The ratio changes to 6 percent if the home is not your legal residence, and you lose the school operating exemption with it. That is how a $1,500 bill becomes $5,000 or more. We calculate the real post-sale number for every buyer before they offer.

### Do retirees get a property tax break in South Carolina?
Yes. On top of the 4 percent rate, homeowners 65 and older, or totally disabled or legally blind, get the Homestead Exemption: the first $50,000 of the home's market value is exempt. You need one year of South Carolina residency, and in Horry County you apply in person at the Auditor's office. It renews automatically after the first application.

### Can I rent my home out and keep the 4% rate?
Only up to 72 days per calendar year. Rent it more than that and the property moves to 6 percent. Rent it 14 days or fewer and the rental income is also federal income tax free on top. Between 15 and 72 days you keep the 4 percent but owe accommodations taxes and need a business license.

## Myrtle Beach Homeowners Insurance Cost: Home, Wind and Flood
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/coastal-insurance/
Summary: Horry County house policies averaged about $1,600 to $2,900 a year by ZIP in 2022, before wind and flood. What the three policies cost, and six ways to pay less.

Home / Buyers / Coastal Insurance
Insurance on the coast

# What home and flood insurance cost in Myrtle Beach, and six ways to pay less.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
In 2022 the average homeowners policy on a house in Horry County cost about $1,600 to $2,900 a year, depending on the ZIP code, before any separate wind or flood policy.
Three separate insurance policies, percentage deductibles, and flood risk the map does not show. What each one costs on the Grand Strand, and how to pay less.
Get a property's insurance costs Call 854.333.2135

The direct answer

## Average home insurance cost in Myrtle Beach
In 2022 the average homeowners policy on a house in Horry County cost about $1,600 to $2,900 a year, depending on the ZIP code. That average leaves out wind pool and surplus-lines policies, and flood. The figures are from the U.S. Treasury's homeowners insurance data, 2018 to 2022 .
On the coast, quotes on the same house vary by thousands of dollars, so the person who shops wins. Check any address's flood zone free at the FEMA Map Service Center .
South Carolina home insurance rose about 10 percent in 2025, roughly double the national pace. The state insurance department attributes the pressure to repair-cost inflation, reinsurance costs, and rising home values. Reinsurance is the coverage insurers buy to protect themselves. No carrier exodus has happened here, but several national companies slowed new coastal business in 2024 and 2025, which makes shopping across many carriers matter even more.
The bigger surprise for buyers from inland states is not the price. It is that "insurance" on the coast can mean three separate policies. That is the next section.

The structure

## Homeowners, wind, and flood: the three coastal policies

- 1. Homeowners. Fire, theft, liability, the standard package. On the coast, check what it excludes before you check the price.

- 2. Wind and hail, sometimes separate. Inside the state wind pool's territory, South Carolina lets insurers exclude wind from the homeowners policy. About 1 in 6 coastal policies are written that way. Around Myrtle Beach the territory reaches inland to Carolina Bays Parkway and River Oaks Drive. The wind coverage then comes from another carrier or from the state's wind pool, the insurer of last resort. Two premiums instead of one.

- 3. Flood, always separate. No homeowners policy covers flood, anywhere, at any price. Flood coverage is its own federal or private policy. Statewide, federal flood policies average roughly $740 to $930 a year; high-risk beach and inlet properties pay well more.

Then the deductible math. Coastal policies use percentage deductibles for named storms, usually 1 to 5 percent of the dwelling coverage. On a $400,000 house, 2 percent means the first $8,000 of hurricane damage is yours. At 5 percent, $20,000. Two policies can carry the same premium and be thousands of dollars apart in a storm. We read the deductible page as well as the quote. What named storms have done here since 1989 is on our storm history page .

The flood map myth

## Myrtle Beach flood zones: Zone X does not mean no flood risk
Buyers read "Zone X" on the flood map and hear "does not flood." The map does not say that. It says the lender will not force you to buy flood insurance. FEMA's own numbers: more than 1 in 4 flood claims come from outside the high-risk zones. In Horry County, thousands more properties face real flood risk than sit inside the mapped zones that require coverage.
Two pieces of good news. Horry County's participation in the federal Community Rating System takes 25 percent off flood premiums countywide. For lower-risk homes, a flood policy is often a few hundred dollars a year, cheap insurance against the claim category most likely to surprise you.
The map also says nothing about the past. A house can sit in Zone X and still have flooded before, and sellers do not always volunteer that. We pull the flood zone on every property we show, and when the history matters, we dig for it: how to find out if a house flooded .

Rentals pay more

## Landlord and short-term rental insurance: renting changes every policy
Investment property costs more to insure , and the penalty for not telling your insurer is worse than the premium. A long-term rental needs a landlord policy, typically 15 to 25 percent above an owner-occupant policy. Short-term rental use needs coverage written for short-term rentals.
Federal flood insurance charges non-primary homes a $250 annual surcharge instead of $25, with premiums allowed to rise 25 percent a year instead of 18 as rates are brought up to full risk.
An owner on the Grand Strand went through exactly this. He was moving out, buying his next home, and turning his current house into an Airbnb. When his insurance company learned the home was being rented on Airbnb, they called him and raised his flood premium by more than 25 percent.
The policy was re-shopped across a network of local insurance agents, the same way it had been when he bought the house, and an agent who had not been the cheapest option the first time won the business now. His increase landed at about 10 percent instead of 25.
Two lessons. Rental use gets discovered, so declare it and price it from the start, our investment analyzer budgets the landlord premium into the cash flow. The carrier that was right for you as an owner-occupant is often not the right one for you as a landlord. Shop the change the same way you shopped the purchase.

Condos

## What condo owners pay, and why dues went up with it
A condo owner pays twice for insurance. You buy your own unit policy, commonly $40 to $60 a month here.
You also pay a share of the building's master policy through your dues, and that is where the increases happened. Master policy premiums on oceanfront buildings roughly doubled or tripled between 2022 and 2025, and dues rose with them.
The market has been stabilising since, with many associations finding cheaper wind coverage again, but the dues increases already happened.
Which policy pays for what is decided by the recorded master deed, not by state law, and it varies building to building. That split decides how much your own policy has to cover, whether a storm deductible can reach you, and what a lender will require. We cover the mechanism in full on condo master insurance versus your HO-6 .
Paying less

## How to lower coastal home insurance costs: six ways

- &#10003; A fortified roof, partly paid by the state. South Carolina's SC Safe Home program grants up to $7,500 toward a storm-rated roof retrofit on owner-occupied homes. Horry County owners won 294 of those grants in 2025, more than any county in the state, and grantees report premium cuts up to 24 percent. Applications open in windows, so get on the list early.

- &#10003; Wind mitigation credits. Shutters, roof straps, impact glass. State law requires insurers to tell you at every renewal which discounts exist. A wind mitigation inspection costs a couple hundred dollars and can trim the wind portion of the bill for years.

- &#10003; Deductibles you choose on purpose. Raising the named-storm percentage lowers the premium. Pair it with South Carolina's Catastrophe Savings Account, which lets you bank the deductible free of state income tax.

- &#10003; Shop through independent agents. One coastal quote is not a market. Our re-shop of that flood policy cut a 25 percent increase to 10. The state insurance department even runs a free locator service for owners who get stuck.

- &#10003; Document your elevation. For flood pricing, first-floor height matters. An elevation certificate can reprice a policy, and private flood quotes are worth comparing against the federal program.

- &#10003; Buy the right house. Roof age, construction year, elevation, and distance from the water all affect the price. We give you the insurance costs before you offer, not at closing.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach home insurance FAQ

### How much is homeowners insurance in Myrtle Beach?
In 2022 the average homeowners policy on a house in Horry County cost about $1,600 to $2,900 a year, depending on the ZIP code, before any separate wind or flood policy. The honest answer is a range: age of roof, distance to the ocean, deductibles, and rental use swing the number by thousands. The spread between quotes on the same house is exactly why we shop every policy across multiple agents.

### Do I need flood insurance in Myrtle Beach?
Your lender requires it only if the home sits in a FEMA high-risk zone (AE or VE). But no homeowners policy covers flood, and FEMA reports that more than 1 in 4 flood claims come from outside high-risk zones. Horry County properties get a 25 percent discount on federal flood insurance through the county's rating, and lower-risk homes often cost a few hundred dollars a year to cover. We pull the flood zone on every property before you offer.

### What is the South Carolina wind pool, and will my policy exclude wind?
Inside the state wind pool's territory, insurers are allowed to exclude wind and hail from a homeowners policy. Around Myrtle Beach that territory reaches inland to Carolina Bays Parkway and River Oaks Drive. Farther south it reaches the Intracoastal Waterway. When that happens, you buy a separate wind policy, sometimes from the state's insurer of last resort, the South Carolina Wind and Hail Underwriting Association. About 1 in 6 coastal policies are written without wind. It is not a dealbreaker, it is a second premium to budget for, and we flag it before you offer.

### What is a hurricane deductible?
Coastal policies carry a percentage deductible for named storms instead of a flat dollar amount, usually 1 to 5 percent of the dwelling coverage. On a $400,000 house, a 2 percent hurricane deductible means the first $8,000 of storm damage is yours; at 5 percent it is $20,000. Know the percentage before you buy, and consider South Carolina's Catastrophe Savings Account, which lets you set aside that deductible free of state income tax.

### Does renting my house out raise my insurance?
Yes, and hiding it is worse. A long-term rental needs a landlord policy, typically 15 to 25 percent more than a homeowner policy. Short-term rental use needs coverage written for it. Federal flood insurance also charges non-primary homes more: a $250 annual surcharge instead of $25, and premiums allowed to rise 25 percent a year instead of 18. If your insurer discovers rental use on its own, expect a repriced policy or a denied claim. Tell them, then shop the new premium hard.

### How can I lower my coastal insurance premium?
The biggest levers are a fortified roof, wind mitigation credits insurers must disclose by law, and raising deductibles you can cover. Also compare the on-site quote against multiple carriers through an independent agent, and for flood, document your elevation. South Carolina's SC Safe Home program grants up to $7,500 toward a fortified roof, and Horry County received more of those grants in 2025 than any other county. Grantees of the roof program report premium cuts up to 24 percent.

# Condotel financing in Myrtle Beach: which loans work, and which units qualify A bank says no because of the building, not your credit. The size of the unit decides what works instead.

Which loans close on a Myrtle Beach condotel unit, which units qualify, and which oceanfront buildings run like hotels.

The short answer
Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA loans do not work in a Myrtle Beach building run like a hotel. About 8 in 10 oceanfront condos for sale here say the unit is in a rental program.
Condotel loans do work when the unit itself is big enough. One published condotel program asks for 500 square feet, a separate bedroom and a full kitchen. More than 3 in 4 rental-program condos for sale have the size and the bedroom.

## Can you get a mortgage on a condotel in Myrtle Beach?
Yes, but not with the loans most buyers know. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the two companies Congress created to buy mortgages from lenders , will not buy a loan in a condo hotel. FHA will not insure one. The rule is about the building, so a strong credit score does not change it.
Which loans work on a unit in a Myrtle Beach building run like a hotel Loan Works? Why
Conventional loans (Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac) Works? No Why Fannie Mae will not take a building run as a hotel, or one with a rental pool. A resort company that manages the building and rents units for owners rules it out too. Freddie Mac will not take a condo hotel.
FHA Works? No Why FHA will not insure a loan on a condotel , or approve a building with a required rental pool. None of the 47 oceanfront buildings in our directory is on HUD's approved condo list .
VA Works? Only a home you live in Why A VA buyer certifies that they will live in the home. At least 6 of the 47 buildings in our directory have an accepted record on the VA's condo list .
Condotel loans Works? Yes, if the unit qualifies Why These loans are made outside the Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA rules. Each lender makes its own rules for the unit and the building.

One kind of condotel loan, a DSCR loan , qualifies on the unit's rent instead of your income. A cash buyer needs no lender to approve the building.

## What makes a Myrtle Beach condo a condotel?
A condotel is a condo building run like a hotel. Each unit has its own owner, but the building is managed and operated as a hotel. These are the signs Fannie Mae lists , put as what you see on a visit:

- Guest registration and short stays Guests register with the building, and the HOA or its manager rents units by the day or for short stays.

- Hotel services Daily cleaning, a central phone line and a central key system.

- A rental pool Owners pool their units with the HOA or the manager and share the rent, whether the papers require it or not.

- A resort company in charge A hotel or resort company manages the building and also rents units for owners.

- Limits on owners Rules on when owners may stay or how they decorate, or an HOA licensed as a hotel or resort.

- A resort name Fannie Mae will not take a building whose name contains hotel, motel or resort, unless the word only refers to the building's past use. Hotel marketing and a hotel rating on booking sites count too.

23 of the 47 oceanfront buildings in our directory go by a name with Resort or a hotel brand in it. Freddie Mac has its own tests, and it reads the building's papers and services to decide what is a condo hotel.
Every condotel is non-warrantable. Not every non-warrantable building is a condotel. Our non-warrantable condo guide covers the other reasons a building fails the lender rules.

A condotel is worth the harder loan for a buyer who wants the resort to do the renting. What you gain, and what it costs you:
What you gain

- Units that sell About 780 units sold in a year in 43 of the directory's oceanfront buildings, about 1 in 15 of their units. In a resort of 300 units, that is about 20 sales a year.

### What is a condotel in Myrtle Beach?

## Why are HOA fees so high in Myrtle Beach?
Myrtle Beach's highest HOA fees are in the oceanfront towers. Most of a $940 tower fee goes to the building's insurance, its utilities and its upkeep.
The building's federal flood policy is a small part of the fee. For condo buildings in Horry County with one, the middle cost was about $405 a unit a year, or about $34 a month.

## Are HOA complaints common in Horry County?
Yes. Of the HOA complaints in South Carolina's latest yearly report, 31 percent were about associations in Horry County, more than any other county. Horry also had the most complaints per person, and Georgetown County was second.

## Myrtle Beach HOA fees FAQ

### What is a regime fee?
A regime fee is the condo fee. South Carolina's condo law calls a condo a regime, so its association fee is also called a regime fee.

### Can I refuse to join an HOA?
No, not when the home is in one. Under South Carolina law, the recorded declaration requires each owner to pay the association's assessments.

### Can HOA fees go up?
Yes. South Carolina's HOA law and condo law set no cap on dues, on a special assessment or on a fine. The limits are in the association's own recorded rules.

## Myrtle Beach Condo Special Assessments: Who Pays | Chapter3

# The buyer of a Myrtle Beach condo can owe the seller's special assessment What one costs, who pays it, and how we find it in the board's minutes.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
An agent reads a Myrtle Beach condo board's meeting minutes for you, so you know about a coming special assessment before you make an offer.

The short answer
A special assessment is a one-time bill from a condo association, which all the owners belong to, on top of the regular dues. It pays for a cost the yearly budget and the reserve fund, the money saved for big repairs, do not cover. South Carolina law puts no limit on the amount. Your share is your unit's percentage, set in the condo's founding papers, recorded when the condo was created.
If a seller leaves an assessment unpaid, the association can collect it from the buyer too. The buyer's limit is the amount on the association's written statement of what the seller owes. We get that statement before closing, the day the sale is final.

Know about an assessment before you sign.
Have us check a building

On this page

- What it is

- How much

- Building age

- Votes and limits

- How to spot one

- Who pays at sale

- Loans

- Not paying

- Special assessment questions

## What is a special assessment on a condo?
A special assessment is a bill the association sends every owner, once, for a cost its budget and its reserve fund cannot pay. Dues pay the yearly budget. The reserve fund is money the association saves for big repairs, such as a roof. A special assessment pays the rest.
When a part of a condo building the association must insure is damaged, the repair is paid in this order.

- 1 The building's insurance The association must insure the building.

- 2 The reserve fund The money the association has saved for big repairs.

- 3 The owners The rest, divided among the owners. This can be a special assessment.

Who pays to repair damage to an insured part of a South Carolina condo building, in order. A building's bylaws can split the owners' part another way. The board can bill that part as a special assessment, or add it to the yearly budget.
In a neighborhood of houses, the recorded rules of the homeowners association (HOA) say whether it can charge one. Our page on South Carolina's HOA laws covers both kinds.

## How much is a condo special assessment?
The size depends on the repair, what the reserve fund holds, and your unit's percentage. At one Pawleys Island condo, the board proposed about $65,000 to $88,000 a unit. In our example below, it is $5,850 to $10,350.

### What did one Pawleys Island condo's board ask each owner to pay?
At Shipyard Village, a condo in Pawleys Island, south of Myrtle Beach, the board said two of its buildings needed extensive repairs. It said every unit's windows and sliding doors had to be replaced, at $12 million to $13 million. A consultant found corroded reinforcing steel and an outer shell that was not weather tight.
Shipyard Village, Pawleys Island
About $88,000
The special assessment its board proposed in 2009 for each unit in two of its buildings.
The owners voted it down. The board then put the repair cost into the next two yearly budgets instead.

Owners sued the association, and the South Carolina Supreme Court ruled on the case, Fisher v. Shipyard Village. For a buyer, this means a no vote can still lead to a bigger yearly budget, so the budget is on our list too.

### How is each owner's share of a special assessment worked out?
Example, with our numbers: a 120-unit building needs a $1.2 million roof and has $300,000 saved for it. The $900,000 still needed is split by each unit's percentage.
Unit Bill
One‑bedroom
60 units at 0.65% $5,850
Two‑bedroom
40 units at 0.95% $8,550
Three‑bedroom
20 units at 1.15% $10,350
All 120 units
100% together $900,000

The average is $7,500 a unit. Each unit's percentage is based on its value against the whole property when the condo was created. A unit with a higher percentage pays more of every assessment.

### How long do a condo building's roof, elevator and windows last?
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) publishes how long building parts last when it plans repairs.
How many years HUD plans for each building part to last Building part years

Flat roof 15 years
Shingle roof 20 years
Elevator machinery 20 years
Aluminum windows 35 years
Concrete or steel balconies 40 years

HUD's estimated useful life table for family housing.
A building built before 1990 is older than HUD expects a flat or shingle roof, elevator machinery or aluminum windows to last. That does not mean those parts were never replaced. We find out which ones were from the minutes and the reserve study, if there is one. A reserve study is a list of the building's big parts, with when each needs replacing and what it will cost.

## Can a condo HOA charge a special assessment without a vote in South Carolina?
Yes, if the building's bylaws allow it. Under South Carolina's condo law, each building's recorded bylaws say how owners are billed. Any limit on the amount is in those bylaws and the founding papers.

### Does South Carolina require a reserve study or regular structural inspections?
No. The state's condo and HOA laws require neither.

- &#10005; No reserve study required

- &#10005; No periodic structural inspection required

In the Shipyard Village case, the South Carolina Supreme Court said a court will not overrule a board that acts within its powers and in good faith. A court can rule against a board that breaks its own founding papers or bylaws.

### Do owners in Horry County dispute special assessments?
Yes. More of South Carolina's HOA complaints are about associations in Horry County than in any other county. Associations there are also the subject of about 2 in 5 of the complaints over fees or special assessments. For a buyer, that is a reason to see how a building's last assessment was voted. That vote is in the minutes we read.
Can this board bill you without a vote?
Tell us the building. We read its bylaws and tell you whether the board can charge an assessment without a vote, and any limit on the amount.
Have us read the bylaws

## How can I tell if a condo has a special assessment coming?
We read the building's papers, the same ones Fannie Mae, which buys home loans from lenders, tells a lender to read. The right to see them belongs to owners, so we ask the seller for them before you make an offer.

- Board minutes. An association that is a nonprofit corporation must keep minutes of every board meeting, so a repair being priced shows up there.

- The association's list of special assessments and needed repairs. It shows what is billed now and what repairs are planned.

- Any engineer's or inspection report. A lender must read a structural or mechanical inspection done in the last 3 years, and so do we.

- The reserve study, if there is one, against the building's age. We compare what the fund holds with the parts HUD expects to be worn out. If a building has none, the minutes and the budget carry more weight. Our reserves page shows how much a building should have saved.

- The budget and the record of every expense. A condo board must keep a detailed record of every receipt and expense, open to all owners.

- The seller's disclosure. It asks: "Has the owners association levied any special assessments or similar charges?" It also asks about "any known common area problems".

In most resales the seller fills in that disclosure form before a contract. The answer can be yes, no or No Representation, which means the seller does not know.
Words in the minutes we look for

- special assessment

- engineer's report

- structural inspection

- water intrusion

- balconies

- waterproofing

- necessary repairs

- added to the operating budget

### What if the papers come after I sign?
Then we read them inside the contract's due diligence period. The standard South Carolina sales contract has one, for a length you and the seller agree on. Inside it, you can end the contract for any reason, with written notice and the fee the contract names. After it ends, that right ends.
Our page on HOA documents explains each paper a buyer gets.

## Who pays a special assessment when a condo sells?
The seller pays what was billed before closing. It comes out of the sale price.
If the seller does not pay, the association can collect from the buyer too, for everything owed up to closing. The buyer owes no more of the seller's bill than the association's written statement shows. If it shows nothing owed, the buyer owes none of it. We get that statement and find out what the seller owes before closing, so you do not get stuck with it. Our page on that statement and its fee says what it costs.
Where the assessment stands at closing, and who pays Where it stands at closing Who pays What we do
Billed before closing, not yet paid The seller, from the sale price We get the association's statement
Voted before closing, billed after You, unless the offer says otherwise We write who pays into the offer
Talked about, not yet voted Usually you, the owner when it is billed We look for it in the minutes

When owners vote for one before closing and the bill comes after, the association bills you, as the owner then, unless the offer says the seller pays it. The offer can say the same for installments due after closing.
If the minutes show one coming, we tell you. Before you offer, you can offer less, ask the seller for a credit at closing, or not make an offer. The seller's disclosure form asks only about assessments already levied, so the minutes are where a coming one shows up.
Selling a condo with an assessment pending? See selling a condo in Myrtle Beach .
Leave the seller's bill with the seller
We get the association's statement of what the seller owes, and we write who pays a voted assessment into your offer.
Have us write it into your offer

## Can a special assessment stop a condo loan?
Yes. If a building's special assessment pays for a critical repair that has not been fixed, Fannie Mae will not buy a loan on any unit in that building. For a buyer, that rules out a regular loan your lender plans to sell to Fannie Mae, until the repair is done. Cash still works. FHA, VA and other loans have their own rules, and our page on condos most lenders will not lend on explains them.

### Which repairs does Fannie Mae count as critical?

- Repairs to items such as sea walls, elevators, waterproofing, stairwells, balconies, foundations, electrical systems and parking structures.

- Mold, water intrusion and damaging leaks in the buildings.

- A repair over $10,000 per unit, due within 12 months, with no money set aside for it.

- A full or partial evacuation order for an unsafe condition. The building is ineligible until it is safe.

Damage to only one or a few units does not count.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Stacked balconies with railings on oceanfront buildings in North Myrtle Beach, seen from a plane. Balconies and waterproofing are on Fannie Mae's list.

Buying with a loan? Know the repair list first.
Tell us the building and your loan. Before you offer, we check its papers for a repair on Fannie Mae's critical list.
Have us check it for your loan

## Can I refuse to pay a special assessment, or pay it over time?
No owner can refuse a lawful share. Not using the shared areas, or giving up the unit, does not end it.
No South Carolina statute gives an owner a right to a payment plan. Whether one is offered is the board's choice.

### What happens if a special assessment goes unpaid in South Carolina?
An unpaid condo assessment is a lien on the unit. If the unit is sold to pay its debts, property taxes and the mortgage are paid first, then the association. The association can foreclose its lien in court like a mortgage, or sue for the money without foreclosing. Our page on HOA liens and foreclosure has each step.
A neighbor's unpaid share can become every owner's cost. When a lender forecloses on a unit, some of that unit's unpaid assessments are split among all the owners.
Association assessments are not deductible as real estate tax, because an association, not a government, charges them. Our page on whether HOA fees are tax deductible has the detail.

Common questions

## Special assessment questions

### Can the board change my unit's percentage to raise my share?
No. Your unit's percentage is set in the condo's founding papers. It cannot be changed without every owner's agreement, except as a phased condo's founding papers provide or when owners vote not to rebuild a unit.

### How much say does one owner have in a vote on a special assessment?
As much as the unit's percentage. Where owners vote, a majority means owners holding at least 51 percent of the building's value, not 51 percent of the units.

### Can a condo board borrow money instead of charging a special assessment?
Yes, if the association is a nonprofit corporation and its articles do not forbid it. Under South Carolina law, it may borrow money and pledge its income to repay the loan.

### Does a special assessment matter if I pay cash?
Yes. You owe your share like every other owner. Fannie Mae's loan rules do not stop a cash purchase, but they apply to a later buyer of your unit who needs a loan.

# Can a Myrtle Beach condo association pay for its own roof? Its reserve fund tells you. South Carolina law does not require one.

- 56% of condos for sale are in buildings 30+ years old

- 20 years the federal planning life of elevator machinery

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
A Myrtle Beach condo's roof and elevators wear out on a schedule. If its reserves cover the worn part, it can pay. If not, the owners do.

The short answer
Only if it has saved enough. Its reserve fund is its savings for big repairs. Compare the cash in that fund with what its reserve study, a report on the building's big shared parts, says the fund should hold by now. That share is called percent funded. The higher it is, the lower the chance the owners get a special assessment, a one-time bill to each owner for a cost the fund cannot cover.

Send us the building. We read its reserve study, budget and balance sheet.

- An example

- Other states

- No study, or an old one

- What we read

- Reserve questions

## What is an HOA reserve fund?
A reserve fund is money a homeowners association (HOA) or condo association saves each year for big repairs it knows are coming. The roof, the elevators and the paving are the usual ones.

- Account 1 The operating budget Pays this year's bills, from this year's dues.

- Account 2 The reserve fund Saves for the big repairs ahead: the roof, the elevators, the paving.

- When the reserve is short The owners Pay the rest, often as a special assessment .

Saving ahead spreads the cost of a roof across every owner who uses it. Without savings, the whole bill falls on whoever owns a unit the year the roof fails.
A reserve study is a report on the building's big shared parts: what each one costs, how long it lasts, and how much the fund should hold by now.

## Does South Carolina require HOA reserves or a reserve study?
No. South Carolina law does not require a condo or an HOA to keep a reserve fund, to put any amount into one, or to have a reserve study. How much a building saves is up to its board and its own documents.
In a South Carolina condo, every owner shares the cost of keeping up and repairing the shared parts. Each unit's share is the percentage set for it in the condo's founding papers, the recorded documents that created it. After damage, the bill is paid in this order:

- Insurance Pays first, for what the master policy covers.

- The reserve fund Pays next, from what the board has saved.

- The owners Share the rest, by each unit's percentage in the founding papers.

A condo board must keep a book of every receipt and expense, with repair costs shown, open to every owner. A buyer is not yet an owner, so we get the papers through the seller.
Not an owner yet? We ask the seller for the papers
A buyer cannot see the board's books, so we ask the seller for them before you sign.
Have us ask for the papers

## How much should a Myrtle Beach condo association have in reserves?
Enough to cover the part of each big repair that has already worn out. A roof halfway through its life should have about half its cost saved.
Percent funded: the cash in the fund, as a share of what it should hold by now
Association Reserves, a national reserve-study firm, set these bands from its clients' studies. The two marks show the example building below: as it is, and with more saved.
In the weak band, repairs are often put off. In the strong band, the risk of a special assessment is low, and a fund does not need to be full to get there.
Among the firm's own clients, about a third were weak and a quarter strong. Those are associations that pay for a study, and the firm says they may be more careful with money than most.
Percent funded is a snapshot of today. It does not grade the plan, so we read the plan as well.

## What does an underfunded condo building look like?
Here is one building with round numbers. It has 80 units, is 30 years old and has $400,000 saved.
The example building's six big parts, and how much of each one's life is used

- 1 Flat roof 15 of 20 years used

- 2 Elevator machinery, two elevators 17 of 20 years used

- 3 Exterior paint 6 of 8 years used

- 4 Concrete balconies 30 of 40 years used

- 5 Parking lot paving 12 of 25 years used

- 6 Pool equipment 4 of 10 years used

Red: due within the next 5 years. Each part's life is the planning life used by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
Together, these parts should have about $1.5 million saved by now. The fund is 26 percent funded: weak.
The example building, the next 5 years
$380,000 short
The flat roof, the elevator machinery and the exterior paint come due. By then the fund will hold about two thirds of what they cost.
Split evenly: about $4,750 for each of the 80 owners.

The same building at 75 percent funded has no gap. The concrete balconies come next, 10 years out.
The example leaves out inflation and interest. A real condo splits a gap by each unit's percentage in its founding papers, not evenly.

### Saving ahead costs owners less
Saved money earns interest. A special assessment pays the full price, and a bank loan adds its interest.
What a $250,000 roof costs the owners, three ways How it is paid, why cost to owners

Paid from savings · less than the price, as savings earn interest $230,000
A special assessment · the full price, all at once $250,000
A bank loan · plus the interest on the loan $320,000

The same reserve-study firm's example, rounded to the nearest $10,000.

Have us check its savings

## What do lenders require for condo reserves?
For most conventional condo loans, the lender tests the building's budget. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy these loans from lenders, and the test is theirs.

- How a building passes At least 10 percent of its dues goes into reserves. Or it saves what a current reserve study says it should.

- When it fails A buyer there cannot get a conventional loan that follows these rules, though some other loans still work. When you sell a condo there, your buyer's lender runs the same test.

### 10 percent or 15 percent?
Freddie Mac raises its line to 15 percent for loan applications received on or after January 4, 2027. It says it made the change with its regulator and in alignment with Fannie Mae. Fannie Mae's own guide still says 10 percent.
From that date, a building that puts 12 percent into reserves fails Freddie Mac's test and passes Fannie Mae's guide as it reads now. Which one applies depends on which company buys your loan. Your loan officer can tell you before you apply.
Freddie Mac made the change after buildings with underfunded reserves turned out to be the same ones needing critical repairs. It says owners in those buildings can face special assessments or higher dues .

### A building can pass and still be weak
The test reads one line of this year's budget, not the cash in the bank. Our example building puts 10.4 percent of its dues into reserves, so it passes while 26 percent funded. Try your own building's numbers:
Does this budget pass the lender's test?

## What do other states require for condo reserves?
Florida , New Jersey , Maryland and Virginia make condo boards study their reserves on a schedule. A buyer from one of them should not expect the same here.
What the law requires of condo associations, by state
State Reserve study required How often
South Carolina No Never required
Florida Yes, for condo buildings 3 stories or taller At least every 10 years
New Jersey Yes At least every 5 years for concrete, masonry or steel condo buildings
Maryland Yes At least every 5 years
Virginia Yes, unless the condo's own papers say otherwise At least every 5 years

## What if a building has no reserve study, or an old one?
No law here requires a reserve study, so a building can have none, or one that is years old. A missing study is a reason to look harder, not proof of a problem.
Without one, we judge the building from its budget, its balance sheet, its board minutes and the age of its big parts.
When there is a study, a lender accepts it, or an update, only if it is no more than three years old. Among the same reserve-study firm's clients, associations that update at least every three years were told to charge a new special assessment about half as often as those that update every five.

## What should a buyer check in a condo's reserves?
Our agents read the HOA documents for a buyer. For reserves, these five tell us whether the building can pay for its own roof:

- The reserve study. Its date, the percent funded and its plan. A plan that only keeps the fund above zero is a warning.

- The budget's reserve line. The share of the dues it puts into reserves.

- The balance sheet. The cash in reserves, against what the study says should be there.

- The age of the big parts. The roof, the elevators, the paint and the balconies, against HUD's lives and the year the building was built.

- The board's minutes. Repairs put off, or a special assessment under discussion. The HOA documents a buyer receives are only part of what we ask for.

What you get when we read a building
Its percent funded, its cash against the study, whether its budget passes a lender's test, and the big parts coming due.
Send us the building's name

### When you see the papers, and when you can still back out

- Before you sign In most resales, the seller fills in a disclosure form. It asks whether the association has levied any special assessments.

- After you sign The standard South Carolina sales contract has a due diligence period. In it, you can end the contract with a written notice to the seller.

- Inside that period Read the reserve study, the budget, the balance sheet and the minutes.

If they are weak, you can ask for a lower price or a credit at closing, or walk away.

Common questions

## Reserve questions

### Does South Carolina require a reserve study?
No, and it requires no reserve fund either. A board can still choose to get one, and a lender can accept a current study in place of its budget test.

### Who pays a special assessment voted before closing?
The purchase contract decides, so it belongs in the offer. A bill the seller already owes is paid at closing, and a buyer can be held to it only up to the association's written statement of it.

### Can I see an HOA's reserve records before I buy?
Members can. An HOA member can inspect and copy the budget and the accounting records after giving written notice five business days ahead. A buyer is not yet a member, so we ask the seller for them.

### Does a newer condo building need strong reserves?
A newer building needs less saved by now. A building finished in 2015 is 11 years old, short of HUD's planning life for its elevator machinery and its flat roof, so less of each has worn out. Percent funded still applies: what the fund holds against that smaller amount.

## What to Check in HOA Documents Before Buying in South Carolina
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/documents/
Summary: What to look for in HOA documents before buying on the Grand Strand: the red flags, the papers that show them, and how SC compares with VA and FL.

# What should you look for in HOA documents before you buy in South Carolina? The red flags, the papers that show them, and when they arrive.

- 5 of 6 listings in our search show an HOA fee

- 60 fine policies filed by Horry associations in a year

- 2 in 3 Horry owners who complained got the papers after buying

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Five red flags in HOA documents in South Carolina, the papers that show them, and when they arrive.

The short answer
Read the papers of a homeowners association (HOA) for five red flags. They are a rule that blocks your plan, a special assessment on the way, thin savings, strict fine and collection rules, and dues the seller still owes. In a condo, the lender also tests the whole building before it lends.
South Carolina law does not make an HOA hand a buyer these papers. They come only if someone asks, so we ask for them and read them inside your contract's review time.

## What are the red flags in HOA documents?
Five things in the papers should stop you, in a house, a townhouse or a condo. A rule that blocks your plan comes first, because a lower price does not fix it. The other four cost you money after you buy.

- In the declaration and the rules A rule that blocks your plan A limit on renting, pets, parking, boats or golf carts that rules out how you will use the home. A condo's founding papers must state any limit on renting a unit. More on rental rules

- In the board's minutes A special assessment on the way A special assessment is a one-time bill on top of the dues, for a cost the budget and the savings do not cover. South Carolina's condo and HOA laws set no cap on one. We read the minutes for one being planned. What a special assessment can cost

- In the budget and the reserve study Thin savings for big repairs South Carolina does not require an HOA or a condo to save for big repairs. A reserve study shows what the savings should hold today. One national study firm calls under 30 percent of that weak, with a high chance of special assessments, and 70 percent or more strong. How we read HOA reserves

- In the rules and the declaration Strict fine and collection rules In the past 12 months, Horry County associations filed 60 fine policies and 43 collection policies for unpaid dues. In one South Carolina case , the court judgment came to more than 11 times the unpaid dues, after interest, court costs and lawyer's fees. How an HOA lien works

- In the association's statement Dues the seller still owes Unpaid dues are usually a lien paid from the seller's money at closing. If the sale leaves nothing to pay them, the association may go after the new owner, or waive them. In a condo, the buyer owes no more than the association's statement says. What the closing statement shows

### In a condo: the lender's building review
If the home is a condo, the lender also reviews the whole building. The tests come from Fannie Mae, a company that buys home loans from lenders. A house in an HOA skips this review , apart from some basic rules.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Houses and oceanfront towers on the same beach in Myrtle Beach. For a condo in a tower, the lender reviews the whole building. A house in an HOA skips that review.

- Savings In Fannie Mae's full review of a condo building, the budget must put at least 10 percent of dues income into savings. Freddie Mac, which also buys home loans, raises its test to 15 percent for loan applications from January 4, 2027.

- Owners behind on dues No more than 15 percent of units can be 60 days or more behind. In a 100-unit building, that is 15 units.

- Repairs put off A building that needs critical repairs, or has major upkeep put off, does not pass.

- Lawsuits A suit naming the association can block a normal loan. A suit against the builder about safety, structure, use or whether units can be lived in can too.

- Who owns the space Shops and offices can fill no more than 35 percent of the building. In a building of 21 or more units, one owner can hold no more than 20 percent of them.

When a building fails, a loan on a unit there cannot be sold to Fannie Mae. Buyers then need a different loan, often at a higher cost. Buildings with a rental program here usually fail, because so many owners are investors.
If you pay cash, no lender reviews the building for you. When you sell, a buyer who needs a loan may face the same review.

### How our agents read the rules
Our agents read the rules against how you plan to live: a boat, a golf cart, a rental, a pool. For a buyer who plans to rent, we leave out communities that ban renting before the search starts. Then we read the HOA papers for any rule that would undo the plan.

## Which HOA documents should you get before buying?
Ten papers, from four places: the county, the association, the seller and your lender. Most buyers here need them. In our listing search, nearly every condo, 9 of 10 townhouses and about 7 of 10 houses for sale list an association fee.
The HOA documents to get, and what each one tells you

## Does an HOA have to give a buyer its documents in South Carolina?
No. No South Carolina law makes an association give a buyer a resale packet, gives it a deadline, or caps its fee. The state's HOA law , condo law and nonprofit law have no such rule.
The seller's duty is a form. Unless the sale is exempt, the seller fills in the state's disclosure form before the contract is signed. If the home is in an association, that includes a one-page HOA addendum.
The seller's form asks 11 yes-or-no questions

- Dues and other charges

- Limits on reselling or renting

- Special assessments

- Limits on guests

- Limits on pets

- Assigned parking, lockers or garages

- Keys, fobs or codes for shared areas

- Other memberships that come with the home

- Known problems in shared areas

- Whether the home is under the state's coastal zone law

- A transfer fee

Only the papers show

- The exact words of each rule

- How much the association has saved

- What the board plans next

- What the seller still owes

- Whether a lender will approve a condo building

The seller may answer any question "No Representation", which means no answer at all. The form itself tells buyers to read the documents before signing a contract. If the seller never gives the form, the law says the contract still stands and the closing goes ahead.
Some sales skip the form. Examples are the first sale of a home no one has lived in, a foreclosure sale and an auction. A sale is also exempt when both sides agree in writing.

### What other states give a buyer
Buyers who move here from Virginia, Maryland or Florida often expect the papers to arrive by law, with days to cancel. Maryland and Florida are among the states that send the most movers to Horry County.

- Virginia What the buyer gets by law The association's resale certificate. Unless the sale is exempt, the seller must get it for the buyer. The way out If the contract names no period, 3 days after the buyer gets it. Any time before settlement if it never comes.

- Maryland What the buyer gets by law The HOA disclosures, within 20 calendar days of the contract. The law caps the association's fee for them. The way out 5 calendar days to cancel if they come late.

- Florida, in an HOA What the buyer gets by law A disclosure summary before the buyer signs. The way out If it came late: void the contract within 3 days of getting it or before closing, whichever comes first.

- North Carolina, in a condo What the buyer gets by law In most condo resales, a statement of the monthly dues and other fees, before closing. The way out None. This law has no days to cancel.

A bill now in a House committee, H. 5204 , would require an HOA seller packet on a website at no charge. It would also require the seller certification and governing documents within 15 days of the seller's request. It has not moved out of committee and is not law.

## Are HOA documents public record in Horry County?
Yes, the recorded ones. An association's declaration, its bylaws, their amendments and its rules must be filed with the county's Register of Deeds to be enforced. The county's index is online, but the pages are not, so we pull them at the county and send you the copies. To look up a property's records yourself, use our Horry County property records lookup .

### The papers the county does not keep
The budget, the minutes, the reserve study and the insurance certificate come from the association or its manager. The seller, who still owns the home, can ask for them, and we ask the seller and the manager as soon as you are under contract.
Need the budget and the minutes?
We get them from the seller and the manager, then mark what the savings, the dues and the board's plans mean for you.
Ask us to get the budget and minutes

## How often do HOA rules change in Horry County?
Often. In the 12 months to October 2026, about 700 association papers were recorded in Horry County. More than 300 associations filed them, and about 400 were rules and policies.
Before 2018, almost no rules were on file. Associations that already existed had until January 10, 2019, to record theirs under a 2018 law, and 554 papers were filed that January alone.
The rules you read under contract can change after you buy. A new rule takes effect when the board adopts it. It must reach the county by January 10 of the next year, so until then only the association's copy shows it.

## When do you get HOA documents, and what if you find a problem?
The seller's form comes before the contract. Everything else arrives during your review time, and only if someone asks for it. We ask the day you sign.

- 1 Before you offer The seller's form, and the recorded papers The seller's HOA answers come with the disclosure statement. We pull the recorded declaration from the county.

- 2 When you sign Your review time starts South Carolina law has no set number of days for the HOA papers. The review time in your contract, often called the due diligence period, is your clock.

- 3 During the review The papers the association keeps We ask for the rules, budget, minutes, reserve study and insurance certificate at once. Your lender sends the condo questionnaire.

- 4 Before closing What the seller still owes The association's statement shows any unpaid dues. We check for them before closing.

- 5 After you buy The rules can change The board can adopt new rules. The minutes you read under contract show what it plans next.

### If the papers show a problem

- A line you cannot read The association explains it We ask the manager in writing what the line in the budget or minutes means, and how much any coming bill will be.

- A debt or a coming bill The seller pays or fixes it We ask the seller to pay what is owed, or to take a coming bill off the price.

- A rule that blocks your plan You walk away No price cut fixes it. We tell you while you can still leave on your contract's terms.

Common questions

## HOA documents FAQ

### Are HOA documents public record in South Carolina?
The recorded ones are: the declaration, the bylaws, their amendments and the rules. In Horry County the index is online; we pull the pages at the county for you. The rest come from the association.

### Can I back out of buying a house because of the HOA documents?
Not under a South Carolina law. Your contract's review time is when to act. In Virginia, Maryland and Florida, a buyer has a set number of days by law.

### How long does it take to get HOA documents?
South Carolina law has no deadline for them, so it depends on the association. That is why we ask the manager for the papers and a date as soon as you are under contract.

### Who pays for HOA documents in South Carolina?
No South Carolina law caps the association's fee for them or names an amount. We find out what the manager charges before the papers are ordered, so the cost is known up front.

### Does the seller have to tell me there is an HOA?
Yes, unless the sale is exempt, such as the first sale of a new home. The seller's disclosure form asks, and a yes brings the one-page HOA addendum. A missing form does not undo the contract.

## Can an HOA Ban Rentals in Myrtle Beach? 15 Real Rules
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/rental-restrictions/
Summary: Can an HOA ban rentals in South Carolina? Yes, if the rule is recorded. The rental rules of 15 Grand Strand communities, and how owners can change them.

HOA rental rules

# Can an HOA stop you from renting your home in Myrtle Beach? Yes, if its papers say so. We read the rental rules of 15 Grand Strand communities.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
An HOA or condo can limit renting in Horry County when its recorded papers say so, and the real rules differ by community.

The short answer
Yes. A South Carolina HOA or condo association can ban or limit renting when the rule is in its recorded papers. South Carolina law has no exemption for owners who bought before a new rule.
On the Grand Strand, North Beach Plantation's papers allow "any form of rental". At Del Webb at Grande Dunes and Robber's Roost, no lease may be shorter than a year.

Tell us your rental plan. We read the rules for the home before you offer.

## Can an HOA ban rentals in South Carolina?
Yes, when the rule is in the association's papers and its words are clear. State law and the courts say four things about it:

- The papers must be recorded An HOA's governing documents must be recorded at the county to be enforced. Board rules take effect when adopted, and stay enforceable only if recorded by January 10 of the next year ( 27-30-130 ).

- A condo's master deed states it The master deed is the paper that creates a condo building and its association. South Carolina requires it to state any limits on leasing a unit, including the term. Each owner must follow it strictly ( 27-31-100 and 27-31-170 ).

- No cap and no grandfather rule Neither South Carolina's HOA Act nor its condo law caps an association's rental rules, or exempts owners who bought before a new one.

- A clear rule holds; an unclear one is read for the owner In a 2015 case , a Richland County condo barred renting to college students not related to the owner. Owners who paid $470,000 in 2007 rented to students anyway, and lost. In a 2017 Hilton Head case , the court read unclear rules the way that "least restricts the use of the property", and the owners won.

In the 2015 case, the court also said the association had not given up its rule, even if it had not watched rentals before. It acted once it got a complaint.
The city's rule comes on top. The city or county decides whether a home may be rented by the night at that address. The association's papers say whether that one home may be. Both must say yes.
You can rent by the night only when both say yes City or county HOA or condo papers Rent by the night?
Yes HOA or condo papers Yes Rent by the night? Yes
Yes HOA or condo papers No Rent by the night? No
No HOA or condo papers Yes Rent by the night? No

The rules for each town are on our Myrtle Beach short-term rental rules page .

## What do HOA rental rules say in real Grand Strand communities?
Some allow any rental at all. Others require a lease of a year or more. These 15 come from each community's own posted or recorded papers. The first seven are ordered from the most open to the most limited.

### 1 North Beach Plantation, North Myrtle Beach: rent it any way you like
Its resort towers stand on a 7.5-acre island between the Atlantic Ocean and Whitepoint Swash. Around them are 2.5 acres of pools , spas, a lazy river and a swim-up pool bar.
The master declaration says its residential-use rule "shall not prohibit or restrict any form of rental". The Exchange lets an owner rent by the day, week, month or year.
Rental guests must register. In the Exchange, the single-family homes and the Villas, a guest not staying with the owner registers with the on-site access company. The unit's front door must have that company's lock and fob system.

Send me homes in North Beach Plantation

### 2 Sand Dunes Oceanfront Tower, Myrtle Beach: papers that allow short stays
Sand Dunes Resort has a water park with slides and a large lazy river on the oceanfront. Our oceanfront condo building guide has its fees and prices.
The tower's master deed allows "permanent or transient residential use". It also says nothing in it limits an owner's right to rent or lease a unit.
Transient means short stays. The city's zoning says whether a stay by the night is legal in a unit, so we check it for that unit before you offer.
Another oceanfront building, the Palace Resort, has its own guide , covering how its owners rent by the night.

Get the Sand Dunes condos for sale

### 3 The Farm at Carolina Forest: renting is allowed, and no board rule can ban it
The state land along The Farm's north side holds habitat for the wild Venus flytrap. South Carolina's largest wild population of the plant is centered in the Lewis Ocean Bay Heritage Preserve.
The declaration says no board rule may prohibit leasing, though the board may require a minimum lease of up to six months. Its rules require every lease in writing. The owner sends the manager a copy and the tenants' names and phone numbers within 10 days.
The board's minutes say the builder's documents include no limit on the share of homes that may be rented. More on the neighborhood is in our guide to The Farm .

Have us read The Farm's rules for one home

### 4 Coquina Harbour, Little River: a condo on a boat basin, with 12-month leases
Coquina Harbour's condos line a marina basin off the Intracoastal Waterway in Little River. The county lists 78 boat-slip parcels in the harbor's marina, each its own parcel, about 100 to 500 feet from the condo buildings.

U.S. government aerial photo Coquina Harbour and Lightkeepers Village share one marina basin between US 17 and the Intracoastal Waterway in Little River.
The association's rules require a lease of at least 12 months. A copy of each lease goes to the management company.
It fits a buyer who wants a harbor home and a tenant by the year. It does not fit a plan to rent it by the week.

Have us find a condo in Coquina Harbour

### 5 Del Webb at Grande Dunes, Myrtle Beach: a year's lease, once a year
At Del Webb at Grande Dunes, every owner pays a required fee for the Grande Dunes Ocean Club, the beach club, and the association bills it with its own dues. Pulte said in 2017 it was the only Del Webb in the country to include beach club access in its base HOA dues.
The recorded declaration requires a lease of at least 12 months, one time a year, unless the association's rules say otherwise. The posted rules add that the whole home is leased, in writing, with notice to the manager within 10 days.
This is a 55+ community. An owner may not lease to anyone under 55 who will live in the home without the board's written approval. Life there is in our Del Webb at Grande Dunes guide .

Ask us about homes in Del Webb at Grande Dunes

### 6 Seasons at Prince Creek West, Murrells Inlet area: a one-year lease
The Murrells Inlet MarshWalk is about 10 minutes away by car, and so is the beach in Garden City. At home, the management company lists indoor and outdoor pools, tennis and bocce.
The association's posted copy of its charter says no lease may be shorter than one year. Every lease is in writing and says the homes are for people 55 or older.

Send me Seasons at Prince Creek West homes

### 7 Myrtle Trace, Conway: a tenant 55 or older who lives there full time
Myrtle Trace has fifteen ponds. They sit on 42 acres of common land the HOA owns, with the clubhouse and the pool .
Its owner and tenant agreement says at least one person on the lease must be 55 or older and live in the home full time. If no one on the lease meets that rule, the lease ends and the tenants leave within 30 days.
The rule fits a tenant who lives there, not a vacation guest. Our Myrtle Trace guide covers the rest.

## Can the HOA change the rental rules after you buy?
Yes, by the vote its papers require.

### The Atrium, a condo building on North Ocean Boulevard
In 1997 the owners of The Atrium, at 7600 North Ocean Boulevard in Myrtle Beach, met with 93.75 percent of owners present. Not less than two-thirds of all owners voted to amend the master deed .
The amendment, filed in 1998, says no unit may be leased for 30 days or less. It says it was meant to end "short term or vacation rentals". The posted papers show no later change.
Its master deed asks for two approvals: owners of at least 66 percent of the units, and the lenders holding first mortgages on 66 percent of them.

A vote that misses the papers' number fails. In a 2015 case , affirmed in 2017, a South Carolina court threw out a subdivision's amendment that lacked the vote its restrictions required.

### How often the papers change
More often than buyers expect. From 2012 through October 2026, the county's index lists 10 amendments to The Farm at Carolina Forest's declaration, its sixth to fifteenth, and 7 to Berkshire Forest's.

## Can an HOA ban Airbnb but allow yearly leases?
Yes. Eleven of the 15 communities above do: their papers bar stays of a month or less and allow a longer lease. Waterfall's rules name Airbnb and VRBO.
For the state's lodging tax, a short-term rental is a stay of fewer than 90 days in a row by the same guest ( 12-36-920 ). Papers may use their own definition: Surf Estates calls any use under a year short-term.

## Does a building full of renters change the loan?
It can. FHA and Fannie Mae both look at how many owners live in a condo building and how it is rented.

- FHA approval of the building At least half of a condo project's units must be owner-occupied. Under extra conditions, an existing project more than a year old can be approved with 35 percent, and a new one with 30 percent ( HUD Handbook 4000.1 ).

- What counts as owner-occupied A unit counts only if the owner lives there part of the year and does not rent it out for most of the year.

- One unit in an unapproved building FHA may insure it only if, among other things, at least half the units are owner-occupied. In a building of 20 or more units, FHA may stop new loans once it insures more than 10 percent of them. In a smaller one, the limit is two.

- Fannie Mae It will not buy a loan in a building whose papers require a rental pool or limit when owners may stay. The same goes for papers that make owners share rental profits with the association or a rental company. A building with hotel services, such as daily rentals and daily cleaning, is out too ( B4-2.1-03 ).

Loans on these buildings are on our page on condos most lenders will not lend on and our condotel financing page .

## What other HOA rules apply only to renters?
Some papers keep a few rules for renters alone. The ones we read cover pets and parking:

- Pets At Teal Lake Village, North Myrtle Beach condos, renters on a lease shorter than half a year may not keep pets. A lease of 6 months or longer on file allows them. At Cypress Bay II and North Beach Towers , renters and guests may not bring pets.

- The golf cart space At Carolina Keyes , an owner who rents the unit to long-term renters loses the unit's golf cart parking space.

## How do you find out before you buy?
We find out for the one home, before you make an offer, in three steps:

- We check the address. Whether the city or county allows the rental you plan there. Each town's rule is on our short-term rental rules page .

- We pull the papers. The recorded papers, their amendments and the latest rules. The county's index is online, but its pages are not, so the copies come from the Register of Deeds or the association. One North Myrtle Beach manager posts 210 files for the 62 associations it runs.

- We read the seller's answer. South Carolina's HOA disclosure addendum asks the seller about any owners association "resale or rental restrictions". The seller may answer "No Representation", so we read the papers either way.

## HOA rental restrictions FAQ

### Am I grandfathered if my HOA bans rentals after I buy?
Not by South Carolina law. Neither its HOA law nor its condo law exempts owners who bought before a new rule. Florida has such a law, and South Carolina does not. At The Atrium in Myrtle Beach, a 1998 amendment ended leases of 30 days or less for every unit.

### Does residential use only ban Airbnb?
Not by those words alone in the papers we read. North Beach Plantation's residential-use rule says it does not restrict any form of rental, and Sand Dunes Oceanfront Tower allows transient residential use. A South Carolina court reads unclear words the way that least restricts the owner.

### Can an HOA make my renters register?
Yes, if its papers say so. In parts of North Beach Plantation, rental guests not staying with the owner register with the on-site access company. Del Webb at Grande Dunes wants notice of each lease within 10 days, and The Farm at Carolina Forest wants the tenants' names.

### What counts as a short-term rental in South Carolina?
For the state's lodging tax, a stay of fewer than 90 days in a row by the same guest. A community's papers can define it differently. Surf Estates treats any use under a year as short-term.

### Can I rent out a home in a 55+ community near Myrtle Beach?
Yes, with the age rule. Del Webb at Grande Dunes asks for a 12-month lease and board approval for a tenant under 55. Seasons at Prince Creek West asks for a one-year lease. At Myrtle Trace, a tenant 55 or older must live there full time.
