## Can an HOA Foreclose in South Carolina? Liens and Unpaid Dues
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/liens-and-foreclosure/
Summary: Yes, through the court. How a South Carolina HOA lien and foreclosure work, how often it happens in Horry County, and what stops it before the sale.

Home / HOA Guide / Liens and Foreclosure
HOA Guide

# Can an HOA take your house in South Carolina over unpaid dues? Yes, through the court, and the bill that starts it can be small.

- 4 of 19 of one month's Horry County foreclosures were for HOA or condo debts

- 89% of one South Carolina HOA's court bill was lawyers' fees and court costs

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
How an association forecloses, how often it happens in Horry County, and the steps that stop it before the sale.

The short answer
Yes. For a house or a condo, a South Carolina homeowners association (HOA) or condo association can put a lien on your home for unpaid dues and ask a court to sell it. A lien is a legal claim for money owed. The lien is on the home itself, so it applies whether or not you have a mortgage.
The bill that starts it can be small. Lawyers' fees and court costs are added to it.
If you are sued, you usually have 30 days to answer; the summons, the paper served on you, gives the time. Answer, and get the case itself dismissed, because paying the bill does not by itself end the lawsuit. Or sell before the auction.

## Can an HOA foreclose on your house in South Carolina?
Yes, for a house or a condo, through the court. An association cannot sell your home on its own. It files a lawsuit, and a judge orders the sale, the same way a bank forecloses, or forces a sale, when a mortgage is not paid. It can also sue you for the money alone, without asking to sell the home.
The power comes from one of two places:

- Condo association South Carolina's condo law Unpaid dues are a lien on the unit by law, and the association can foreclose it in court.

- HOA that is not a condo The community's recorded rules These are the rules filed with the county. Courts enforce them like a contract. A lien under them is enforced through the court too.

In a 2019 case , the community's rules allowed foreclosure, and the South Carolina Supreme Court said the HOA had the legal right to foreclose. It still set that sale aside.
For an HOA that is not a condo, the state's HOA law says nothing about late fees, interest, liens or foreclosure. Those rules are in your community's own papers, so they differ from one community to the next. Our guide to South Carolina HOA law has what the state does say, and our guide to HOA violations and fines covers fines.

## What happens if you stop paying HOA dues?
The bill grows, a lien goes on the home, and the association can sue to have it sold. The months below are from one South Carolina case, Winrose, in Richland County. The time to answer, usually 30 days, is in the court's rules, and the summons states it.

- 1 The start Dues go unpaid Your community's rules say what is added. In the Winrose case, dues unpaid for 30 days began to earn interest, and a court judgment would add a reasonable attorney's fee and the court costs.

- 2 Winrose: 3 months in A lien goes on the home The lien is the association's claim against the home itself. In Winrose, the HOA filed it three months after the owners fell behind.

- 3 Winrose: about 3 years in The lawsuit The association sues to foreclose. A notice of the lawsuit, called a lis pendens, may be filed with the county clerk, so it shows on the home's title.

- 4 Usually 30 days Your answer is due You usually have 30 days from the day you are served to answer the lawsuit in writing. The time is in the court's rules , and the summons states it.

- 5 No answer: no notice of the rest An owner who does not answer usually gets no notice of the hearings that follow. In the Winrose case, one owner put the lawsuit papers in a drawer and forgot them. The owners did not answer and got no further notice of the judgment or the sale. A sale notice still runs in the newspaper. In Horry County it runs three times over three weeks.

- 6 Winrose: 5 months after the suit The judgment The judge enters a judgment and orders the home sold. It adds the interest, the fees and the court costs to the dues.

- 7 Winrose: 2 weeks later The auction In Horry County, the Master in Equity holds the sale at 11 a.m. on the first Monday of each month, or on the Tuesday when that Monday is a holiday. The sale is on the third floor of the Government and Justice Center in Conway. The winning bidder pays 5 percent of the bid by noon the next day.

- 8 The buyer's deed The highest bidder gets a deed to the home. What happens to a mortgage on it is below .

Photo: Pollinator at English Wikipedia
Horry County's Government and Justice Center in Conway, where the county's foreclosure cases are heard and its foreclosure sales are held.

In all 4 association cases on the county's list, the bidding closes at the auction . It does not stay open 30 days for higher bids. Plan to settle or sell before that day.

## How does a small HOA bill turn into thousands?
Mostly through lawyers' fees and court costs. In the Winrose case , the court's judgment was almost $2,900 on $250 of unpaid dues, about 12 times the dues.

One South Carolina case, Winrose, in Richland County. The cents are the court's.
Then the house was sold.
The Winrose house, after the judgment

- $128,000 What the house was worth, with about $66,000 left on its mortgage.

- $3,036 What a company paid for it at the auction, with the mortgage still on it.

- $35,000 What the company then asked the owners to pay to keep their home.

Five years later, the South Carolina Supreme Court set the sale aside. The winning bid was about 5 cents for each dollar of the owners' equity in the house, and the court called the price grossly inadequate. It wrote:
"A foreclosure proceeding is a last resort, not a business model to be swiftly invoked for the purpose of exploiting property owners."
South Carolina Supreme Court, Winrose Homeowners' Association v. Hale
The steps that stop a bill like this are in what to do if you are behind .

## Does an HOA lien come before your mortgage?
No, not before a mortgage that was recorded first. South Carolina has no law that puts an association's lien ahead of a first mortgage, the rule called a super lien.
Who is paid first, in a South Carolina condo

- Property taxes

- Recorded mortgages and other recorded liens

- The condo association's unpaid dues Then ahead of any other lien on the unit

From South Carolina's condo law, for the lien and for the money from a sale.
For an HOA that is not a condo, no law ranks the HOA's lien. In a 1994 case , a mortgage recorded before the dues fell due came first. That HOA's papers did not say the HOA came first.
The order works both ways:

- The association forecloses The mortgage stays The buyer at the sale takes the home with the first mortgage still on it, when that mortgage ranks ahead. If you are bidding, read our guide to buying at the courthouse sale .

- The bank forecloses a condo Your neighbors pay the gap When a bank forecloses on a condo, the new owner does not pay the dues the last owner left unpaid after the mortgage was recorded. Every owner in the building pays that share instead.

- While a condo case goes on The owner owes rent Once the association sues to foreclose a condo, the owner must pay a reasonable rent for the unit while the case goes on.

## Behind on HOA dues? What to do before the sale
Start with the lawsuit papers.

- Answer the lawsuit within the time on the summons, usually 30 days. An answer is your written reply to the association's complaint. Serve it on the association's lawyer, whose name and address are on the summons, and file it with the clerk of court. A lawyer can write it with you; the $50 line below is a start.

- Have the case dismissed when you pay. In Winrose, the owners paid $250 and got a letter that the lien was satisfied. The HOA did not withdraw its suit. Ask the association's lawyer to dismiss the lawsuit and to file a cancellation of the lawsuit notice with the clerk. Under state law , whoever filed that notice can cancel it once the case is settled or dismissed.

- A fight over the amount can go to small claims. A money dispute with your HOA of $7,500 or less can go to magistrate court, the county's small claims court. A foreclosure cannot. It goes to the circuit court.

- A lawyer for $50. The SC Bar's Lawyer Referral Service , (803) 799-7100, connects you with a local lawyer. The first 30 minutes cost no more than $50.

- Sell before the auction. The lawsuit notice on your title does not stop a sale. It warns any buyer, and a buyer who closes while the case is open is bound by it. Plan for the sale to pay the association and end the case. Unpaid dues usually come out of the seller's money at closing, before you are paid.

Selling to pay the association

## Buying a condo or HOA home: will the seller's unpaid dues follow you?
In a condo, only up to what the association puts in writing. A condo buyer is liable with the seller for unpaid dues, but only up to the amount in the statement the association must issue on request. The unpaid dues are paid from the sale price at closing, after taxes and recorded mortgages. That limit does not cover a buyer at a foreclosure sale.
When a sale leaves no profit to pay them, the association could go after the new buyer for the fees, or waive them. Our agents check for unpaid fees before closing. A title search shows a lien the association has recorded and any notice of a lawsuit. You can also search Horry County land records by name for a recorded lien. Dues owed but not recorded show only in the association's statement , a letter that says what the seller still owes.

### Owners behind on dues can affect your loan

- Can block the loan More than 15 in 100 units behind Fannie Mae buys home loans from lenders. When it reviews a whole building, it will not buy a loan on a unit there if that many units are 60 days or more behind on dues.

- Does not by itself The association suing an owner An association that sues an owner for past-due dues, or forecloses on one, does not by itself make the building ineligible.

A building's savings matter for the same reason. Our guide to condo reserves shows how we read them.

## Is South Carolina changing its HOA foreclosure law?
Not yet. Three bills before the legislature would limit HOA foreclosure. None has become law.

- S. 366 No HOA foreclosure clauses Any clause in an HOA's papers that allows foreclosure could not be enforced. A primary home would be protected from a court sale brought only by an HOA. The HOA could still place a lien. In the Senate Judiciary Committee

- H. 3447 A hearing first An HOA would need a court hearing before it could advertise a foreclosure sale against an owner who did not answer. Passed the House 110 to 2; now in the Senate Judiciary Committee

- H. 5204 A minimum debt No foreclosure for less than $10,000 in dues, or $1,000 per home in the association if that is less. Also 90 days' notice, mediation and a cap on attorney's fees. In a House committee

Common questions

## HOA liens and foreclosure FAQ

### Does an HOA have to agree to a payment plan?
No. South Carolina's HOA and condo laws do not make an association offer one. If it agrees to a plan, get the plan in writing, including what happens to the lawsuit.

### Can you get your house back after an HOA foreclosure sale?
Not by paying the association afterward. In a Murrells Inlet case, the owner offered the full fees as soon as he learned of the sale, and the association's lawyers turned it down because someone had already bid. The Supreme Court set the Winrose sale aside because the price was far too low, but that took five years.

### Can I stop paying HOA dues if the HOA is not doing its job?
No. A condo owner cannot avoid the dues by not using the shared areas or by leaving the unit. In an HOA, paying the dues is a duty in the community's recorded rules. Holding them back starts the late charges, the lien and the lawsuit.

### Can an HOA put a lien on your house for fines?
Only if your community's papers make fines part of the dues the lien covers. South Carolina's HOA law does not say.

### Does bankruptcy wipe out HOA dues?
Not the dues that fall due after you file. Those stay owed for as long as you still own the home.

## South Carolina HOA Laws: What They Say and Who Enforces Them
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/south-carolina-hoa-laws/
Summary: South Carolina HOA laws in one table: what the HOA Act, condo law and nonprofit law require, what they leave out, and how 416 Horry County complaints ended.

Home / HOA Guide / South Carolina HOA Law
The HOA guide

# South Carolina HOA laws: what the state requires, and what your HOA's papers say.

- No cap on fines in the HOA Act or the condo law

- About 700 association papers recorded in Horry County in the past 12 months

- 10 of 416 Horry County complaints ended with the owner satisfied

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
The three state laws, the rules they leave to each community's recorded papers, and how Horry County's 416 HOA complaints to the state ended.

The short answer
South Carolina has no one complete law on how an HOA must run. Under the 2018 HOA Act, an HOA's papers must be recorded at the county to be enforced, and money disputes up to $7,500 can go to magistrate court.
Fines, dues limits, rental rules and developer turnover are not in South Carolina HOA laws. Your community's recorded papers have those rules. Consumer Affairs records complaints, but the law bars it from acting as a referee.

## What are South Carolina's HOA laws?
South Carolina's HOA laws are three state laws, plus the papers each community records at the county. Consumer Affairs lists the three: the HOA Act, the Nonprofit Corporation Act and the condo law.
Each common question has its answer in one of them, or in your HOA's own papers:
South Carolina HOA law, question by question Question What South Carolina law says Read more
Do the HOA's papers have to be recorded? Yes. The papers count only once they are recorded at the county. A new rule must be recorded by January 10 of the next year. SC Code 27-30-130 Read more Unenforceable rules HOA documents
Does the HOA have to give notice before raising the budget? 48 hours' notice of the vote, unless the HOA is a nonprofit. A nonprofit HOA follows its bylaws. SC Code 27-30-140 Read more Dues increases
Can owners see the HOA's records? Yes. The budget and owner list, and more if the HOA is a nonprofit. In a condo, the account book too. SC Code 27-30-150 Read more Records and meetings
Must board meetings be open to owners? No state law requires it. A nonprofit HOA must hold an owners' meeting once a year. SC Code 33-31-701 Read more Records and meetings
Is there a cap on HOA fines? No. Neither the HOA Act nor the condo law caps fines or says a hearing must come before one. Whether a fine can become a lien depends on the papers. Read more Violations and fines
Can the HOA foreclose? Yes, through the court. A condo's lien is in the condo law. A neighborhood's is in its recorded papers. SC Code 27-31-210 Read more Liens and foreclosure
Is there a cap on dues or special assessments? No. State law also requires no reserve fund. Read more Special assessments Reserves
Can the HOA ban rentals? Yes, if its recorded papers say so. State law has no limit on rental rules, and no rule that exempts earlier buyers. SC Code 27-31-100 Read more Rental restrictions
When must the developer hand the HOA to the owners? There is no deadline in state law. Read more Developer turnover
Can the HOA ban the U.S. flag? Not one portable, removable U.S. flag, shown in a respectful manner. SC Code 27-1-60 Read more Unenforceable rules
Who takes complaints about an HOA? Consumer Affairs records them and sends each one to the HOA. The law bars it from acting as a referee. SC Code 27-30-340 Read more Complaints
Where can a money dispute go? Magistrate court, for $7,500 or less. SC Code 27-30-160 Read more Who enforces

## Which South Carolina law applies to my HOA or condo?
The HOA Act applies to every HOA and condo whose owners must pay assessments. A nonprofit HOA also follows the Nonprofit Corporation Act, and a condo also follows the condo law.

- The HOA Act Every neighborhood or condo where recorded papers make owners pay assessments, except a timeshare. The HOA Act dates from 2018. It has been changed once, in 2019, when its definition of an HOA was edited where it leaves out timeshares.

- The Nonprofit Corporation Act An HOA that filed nonprofit papers with the Secretary of State also follows this law on meetings, notice, the board and records. Whether an HOA did shows in the Secretary of State's business name search .

- The condo law The Horizontal Property Act, from 1962, applies to condos. It says what a condo's founding papers and bylaws must include, how records are kept and how shared costs are split.

The HOA Act itself is short. It deals with five things: recording the papers, notice before a budget increase, the budget and owner list, magistrate court for money disputes, and complaints to Consumer Affairs.
The HOA Act has no rule on late fees, fines, liens or foreclosure.
A property owners association is an HOA under the Act if it meets the same test; our page on HOA vs POA explains the names. An owner cannot opt out, because the recorded papers require each owner to pay. Our HOA guide shows what the fees pay for.

## How do South Carolina's HOA laws compare with North Carolina and Florida?
Households moving to Horry County come most often from other South Carolina counties, then North Carolina, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Florida and Maryland. North Carolina and Florida both limit HOA fines in law:
HOA fines in three states State Cap on a fine Hearing before a fine
South Carolina Cap on a fine None in the HOA Act or the condo law Hearing before a fine Not required by either law
North Carolina Cap on a fine Up to $100 for the violation, and up to $100 for each day it goes on more than five days after the decision Hearing before a fine Yes, unless the declaration has its own process. If a panel made the decision, the owner may appeal to the full board within 15 days.
Florida Cap on a fine $100 a violation, and $1,000 in all for one that goes on, unless the papers say otherwise. A fine under $1,000 cannot become a lien. Hearing before a fine Yes, with 14 days' written notice. The hearing is before a committee of at least three members who are not officers, directors or employees of the association, or their close relatives.

Florida's limits cover HOAs, not condos. North Carolina's cover planned communities.
Moving here from another state? Have us read the papers against how you live
The biggest mistake New York buyers make is not checking that the community's rules fit how they live: HOA rules on boats, golf carts, rentals and pools. We read them against your plans before you offer.

## What HOA rules are unenforceable in South Carolina?
An HOA rule is unenforceable in South Carolina if it was not recorded at the county by January 10 of the year after it was adopted or changed.

- A rule not recorded in time A rule takes effect when it is adopted. It stays enforceable only if it is recorded by January 10 of the next year. The HOA must give you a copy on request, unless it is posted in a common area or on its website.

- Papers never recorded An HOA's governing papers must be recorded in the county where the property is to be enforceable.

- An amendment without the vote A South Carolina appeals court threw out an amendment to a subdivision's restrictions because it did not have the vote the restrictions required.

- A ban on the U.S. flag Whatever the papers say, an owner or tenant may display one portable, removable U.S. flag in a respectful manner, on the property they are entitled to use.

- An unclear rule It can be read against the HOA. In a Hilton Head rental case , the court took the reading that "least restricts the use of the property", and both sides agreed short-term renting was allowed. Our page on HOA rental restrictions tells the story.

Horry County's index of recorded papers is online, and copies come from the Register of Deeds in Conway. Our page on HOA documents before you buy shows which papers to get.
Have us pull a community's recorded rules before you offer
Send us the community's name. We ask the seller for the papers and check the county's index for each rule's recording, so you know which rules count.
Have us pull the recorded rules

## Can I see my HOA's records and go to its meetings?
Yes to the records. A nonprofit HOA must also hold an owners' meeting each year, but owners have no right under state law to attend board meetings.

### The records you can see

- An HOA that is not a nonprofit Its yearly budget and owner list.

- A nonprofit HOA Its articles, bylaws, minutes of owners' meetings and three years of financial statements. You can inspect and copy them with written notice five business days ahead, paying only for copies.

- A condo The board must keep a dated book of every receipt and expense. It is open to all owners at set hours on working days.

### The meetings you can go to

- A yearly owners' meeting A nonprofit HOA must hold one each year. Notice 10 to 60 days ahead is fair under the law, or 30 to 60 days if it is not sent first class or registered.

- A special meeting Owners with at least 5 percent of the votes can demand one.

- Board meetings The Nonprofit Corporation Act's notice rules for board meetings are about notice to directors. Owners have no right under it to notice of a board meeting, and no right under any of the three laws to attend one. Bylaws can give both.

- A condo owners' vote Decisions need a majority of at least 51 percent, counted by the units' value percentages. Changing the system of running the building takes owners with two-thirds of the value.

When you buy, the seller must tell you about the HOA. Unless the sale is exempt, the seller fills in the state's disclosure form before the contract is signed. If the home is in an association, that includes a one-page HOA addendum.
Our page on what to check in HOA documents lists the papers we get from the seller.

## Who enforces South Carolina HOA law?
No state agency enforces South Carolina's HOA Act. In its own words, Consumer Affairs "does not administer or enforce" the Act. It records each complaint and sends it to the HOA.
The law bars Consumer Affairs from issuing rules on how an HOA is run, and from acting as a referee in a dispute. Its complaint process is voluntary mediation. It cannot make an HOA or an owner take part, require an outcome or arbitrate.

### Where an owner can take a dispute

- Magistrate court A money dispute under the HOA Act of $7,500 or less can go to magistrate court.

- The condo law In a condo, the board, or an owner who is harmed, can sue an owner who breaks the bylaws or the recorded restrictions, for damages or a court order.

- A lawyer The SC Bar runs a lawyer referral service, at 800-868-2284.

## How do I file an HOA complaint in South Carolina?
File an HOA complaint with the SC Department of Consumer Affairs, online or by mail, and send the HOA Supplemental Questionnaire with it.

- Raise it with the board first Talk with the board, and check your HOA's papers for a dispute process. That is Consumer Affairs' first advice. 98 percent of those who filed in 2025 said they had raised the issue with the HOA or its management company first.

- File online or by mail Use Consumer Affairs' online complaint portal , or mail the paper form to PO Box 5757, Columbia, SC 29250. The online form times out after 30 minutes.

- Send the HOA Supplemental Questionnaire Consumer Affairs requires it. In the same year, 78 complaints were closed and left out of its report because the owner did not send it. Questions go to hoahelp@scconsumer.gov or (800) 922-1594, toll free in South Carolina.

- Consumer Affairs sends it to the HOA The HOA may answer. The agency cannot make it take part.

- The complaint is closed Consumer Affairs closes it and counts it in its yearly report. It says the data helps lawmakers decide if the law needs to change.

Horry County leads the state. In 2025, 140 of the 452 HOA complaints in the state's yearly report, 31 percent, were about associations in Horry County. That is the most of any county.

It means the HOA answered every point and named a policy that backs it, whether or not the owner was satisfied. The middle complaint took 33 days to close.

## Is South Carolina changing its HOA laws?
Not yet. None of the five HOA bills below, from the 2025-2026 session, has become law.
Photo: Farragutful
The South Carolina State House in Columbia, where the General Assembly meets.

### Five HOA bills from the 2025-2026 session

- H. 3447 A court hearing before an HOA foreclosure sale. Passed the House 110 to 2; now in the Senate Judiciary Committee.

- S. 903 Would count rules as governing documents, hold them all to the January 10 recording rule, and from 2027 require them to be witnessed and acknowledged to be recorded. Passed the Senate 39 to 0; now in a House committee.

- S. 366 Would void foreclosure clauses in HOA papers. In the Senate Judiciary Committee.

- H. 3350 Would require a dispute process inside every HOA, and let magistrate court hear all matters between an owner and an HOA. In the House.

- H. 5204 Would require a seller packet, and a minimum debt, notice and mediation before foreclosure. In a House committee.

## South Carolina HOA law FAQ

### What is the South Carolina Homeowners Association Act?
The HOA Act is a 2018 state law, SC Code Title 27, Chapter 30. It requires an HOA's papers to be recorded at the county to be enforced, and gives owners the budget and owner list. It lets magistrate court hear money disputes under the Act, and requires Consumer Affairs to record complaints. It has been changed once, in 2019.

### Who regulates HOAs in South Carolina?
No state agency enforces South Carolina's HOA Act. Consumer Affairs records complaints and sends each one to the HOA, and the law bars it from acting as a referee. An HOA that is a nonprofit files its papers with the Secretary of State. The rest is in each community's recorded papers.

### Can I complain about my HOA to the state?
Yes. File with SC Consumer Affairs online or by mail, with the HOA Supplemental Questionnaire. The agency sends the complaint to the HOA, but its process is voluntary mediation. Of 416 Horry County complaints from 2022 to 2025, 10 ended with the owner satisfied.

### Do HOA documents have to be recorded in South Carolina?
Yes. Under the HOA Act, an HOA's governing papers must be recorded at the county's register of deeds to be enforceable. A new rule stays enforceable only if it is recorded by January 10 of the year after it was adopted.

### Does a seller have to disclose an HOA in South Carolina?
Yes, unless the sale is exempt. The seller fills in the state's disclosure form before the contract is signed. If the home is in an association, the form includes a one-page HOA addendum.

### Can I sue my HOA in South Carolina?
A money dispute under the HOA Act of $7,500 or less can go to magistrate court. For anything larger, or any other dispute, talk to a South Carolina attorney. The SC Bar's lawyer referral service is at 800-868-2284.

### Is condo law different from HOA law in South Carolina?
Yes. A condo follows the HOA Act and also the Horizontal Property Act, the state's condo law. The condo law puts a lien on a unit for unpaid assessments and opens the condo's account book to owners. It also requires a condo's founding papers to state any limits on leasing.

## HOA vs POA in South Carolina: Same Thing in Law | Chapter3

# Is a POA the same as an HOA in South Carolina? Fees by kind of home, and why some homes pay two associations.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Yes. In South Carolina law they are the same. Also what you own in a Grand Strand condo, who fixes the roof, and how a condo can change the loan.

The short answer
Yes. In South Carolina, a property owners association (POA) and a homeowners association (HOA) are the same thing in law. Under the South Carolina Homeowners Association Act, a group is an HOA when papers filed with the county make the owners pay it dues.
The kind of home changes the fee. On the Grand Strand, the typical fee on a condo for sale is about $650 a month, and on a house about $95. Condo owners share the building, and the association insures it.

## What is the difference between an HOA and a POA?
You may read that a POA covers more kinds of property than an HOA, such as empty lots or shops. Under either name, the group's papers on file with the county list what it runs and what its owners pay.
If you fall behind on dues, a POA can put a lien on your home when its papers allow one. A lien is a claim on the home for the money you owe. An HOA can do the same. Of the more than 500 associations that recorded a lien for unpaid charges in Horry County in 2025, about half have "homeowners" or "HOA" in the name, and one in five "property owners" or "POA".
What Horry County associations call themselves Word in the name, for example share of associations

Homeowners or HOA 52%
Property owners or POA 20%
Another name · community or master association 18%
A condo word · condominium or regime 9%

Our count of the more than 500 associations that recorded a lien for unpaid charges in Horry County in 2025, from the county's deed index.
In a condo, an unpaid fee is a lien on the unit under state law. The association can foreclose in court, asking the court to sell the unit to pay the debt, as a lender can with a mortgage. For a house, the association's papers list what it can do. Can an HOA foreclose in South Carolina? covers the steps, and HOA violations and fines covers fines.
A name does not always tell you the kind of home. A few names mix a condo word with "property owners" or "homeowners". Some carry no label word at all, only a place name such as a Tower or Villas.
On this page, POA means a property owners association, not a power of attorney.

## How is a condo association different from an HOA?
A condo association is an HOA too, but it runs a building, not a neighborhood. In a condo, the owners share the building. In a neighborhood of houses, you own your lot and the house on it. That one difference changes the fee, what it covers and how a lender looks at the home.
House, townhouse or condo: what changes Kind of home What you own Roof and outside walls Lender reviews the whole building
House in an HOA or POA The lot and the house The HOA's rules say who No
Townhouse A lot or a unit, as its deed says Like a house or a condo, by the deed Like a house or a condo, by the deed
Condo Your unit and a share of the building Every owner shares the cost Yes, except detached or small buildings

Oceanfront towers in Myrtle Beach.

## What do you own, and who fixes the roof?
In a condo you own your unit alone, plus a share of the shared parts, given as a percentage in the condo's founding papers.
A house in an HOA or POA

A condo

Our drawing of what you own in each.
Unless the founding papers say otherwise, the shared parts include the land under the building, the foundations, main walls, roofs, halls, lobbies, stairways, elevators and the central power and water systems. Every owner pays a share of their upkeep by that percentage, and the association insures the building. It may also enter your unit at reasonable hours to repair the shared parts, and for emergency repairs.
Who pays after a leak or a fire is on our who pays for condo damage page.

### And in a neighborhood of houses?
South Carolina's HOA Act has no rule on who maintains or insures a house in a planned community. It is in the HOA's rules, in papers filed with the county. In most house listings, the fee does not include insurance.

## Why do some homes pay two HOA fees?
Because some master-planned communities have two layers. A master association has rules over the whole community. Inside it, a neighborhood association or a condo association can have its own rules and its own fee. For you, that can mean two bills and two sets of rules. The name will not warn you: only 4 of the more than 500 associations in the lien count above have "master" in the name.
Master association Rules over the whole community, and its own fee Neighborhood association Its own rules and fee for one neighborhood
Condo association Its own rules and fee for one building

Our diagram of two layers. A home can belong to the master association and to one association inside it.

### What do the two fees come to together?
The master's fee plus the fee of the association inside it. A listing's fee may leave out the second one, so we have no count of that total for homes here. For a home you send us, adding the two up is the second of our checks .

## What surprises buyers in an HOA or a condo?

- 1 Counting on the building's flood policy In a condo, the association insures the building, and a policy on your own unit is a separate one. Flood insurance has a limit: the building's National Flood Insurance Program policy and your own flood policy together pay at most $250,000 for your unit. Master insurance and your condo policy shows which policy covers what.

- 2 Finding a second association after closing The seller's disclosure form has room for one association's charges and one contact. The Horry County Register of Deeds index is free to search online, but the county does not show the papers themselves to the public online. They are viewed and printed in Conway, or ordered by mail.

## Does a condo association change your loan?
Yes, for many condos. A lender that follows Fannie Mae's rules reviews the whole condo project before a loan on an attached unit. That applies to a project of more than ten units, and to one of five to ten units inside a larger community or under a master association.
Three kinds of home skip the full review: a detached condo, a small condo project, and a house or townhouse in a neighborhood where every owner must belong to the HOA. A detached condo is a stand-alone home sold as a condo. Condos most lenders will not lend on covers buildings that fail it.

## Does it matter if it is called a POA?
The real choice is between a condo and a house, not between an HOA and a POA:

### A condo

- + The association keeps up and insures the building, roof included.

- + Your property tax bill is for your unit alone.

- &minus; The biggest monthly fee, because it pays for the building.

- &minus; Every owner shares the cost of big repairs to the building.

### A house in an HOA or POA

- + The smallest monthly fee.

- + The lot and the house are yours alone.

- &minus; The policy on the house is a bill of its own.

- &minus; In some master-planned communities, a second association with its own rules and fee.

Whether dues are tax deductible has its own page: are HOA fees tax deductible . How owners split the bill for a big condo repair is on condo special assessments . Our page are HOA fees worth it weighs what the fees buy against what you give up.

## HOA vs POA questions

### Is an HOA the same as a POA in South Carolina?
Yes. Under the South Carolina Homeowners Association Act, the name does not matter. A group is an HOA when papers filed with the county make the owners pay it dues, except a timeshare plan.

### Can a POA put a lien on my house?
Yes, if its papers filed with the county give it a lien for unpaid dues, as an HOA's papers can. That is a claim on your house for the unpaid dues. About one in five of the more than 500 associations that recorded a lien for unpaid charges in Horry County in 2025 had "property owners" or "POA" in the name.

### Is a POA voluntary in South Carolina?
Only when no papers filed with the county make the owners pay it. A group with no such papers, such as a voluntary civic club, is not an HOA under South Carolina's HOA Act. If the papers on your home make you pay, the dues are not voluntary, whatever the group calls itself.

### What is a regime fee in South Carolina?
The condo fee. South Carolina's condo law calls a condo a horizontal property regime, so the fee its owners pay is called a regime fee.

### What do I own in a condo?
Your unit alone, plus a share of the shared parts, given as a percentage in the condo's founding papers. No owner can force the shared parts to be split up, and selling a unit sells its share with it.

### Can a home have two HOAs?
Yes. A home in a master-planned community can belong to a master association and to a neighborhood or condo association inside it, each with its own papers and fee. Grande Dunes, Barefoot Resort and Prince Creek each have more than one association.

## Warrantable vs Non-Warrantable Condos: 43 Myrtle Beach Towers
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/non-warrantable-condos/
Summary: Warrantable vs non-warrantable condos in Myrtle Beach: Fannie Mae's rules, why 42 of 43 oceanfront buildings raise its investor flag, and loans that still work.

Home / Invest / Non-Warrantable Condos
Condo loans

# Warrantable vs non-warrantable condos in Myrtle Beach Why so many oceanfront buildings carry the word, which loans still work, and how we check a building before you offer.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Fannie Mae's condo rules, checked against county records for 43 Myrtle Beach oceanfront buildings, and the loans that still close.

The short answer
A non-warrantable condo is in a building that fails one of Fannie Mae's project rules, so the usual conventional loan will not work there. You can still buy it, with cash or with a loan made outside those rules.
On the Myrtle Beach oceanfront, the common sign is a building run for renting. In 42 of the 43 oceanfront buildings we checked, at least 3 in 4 units are not taxed as the owner's home. Fannie Mae tells lenders to look harder at that.

Send us the building. We read its papers before you make an offer.
Ask about a building

On this page

- What it means

- What makes one

- Why so many here

- Which buildings

- The loans that work

- Should you buy one

- How we check

- Non-warrantable condo FAQ

## What is a non-warrantable condo?
A warrantable condo is in a building that meets Fannie Mae's project rules. A non-warrantable condo is in a building that fails one of them. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the two companies Congress created to buy mortgages from lenders , will not buy a loan in a building that fails their project rules.
The rule is about the building, so a strong credit score does not change it.

- You can still buy it Pay cash, or use a loan the lender keeps or sells outside Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Each of those lenders makes its own building rules.

- There is no list to look up Fannie Mae publishes no list for buyers to search. A lender checks each building in Fannie Mae's own system, from the papers the HOA (homeowners association) gives it.

- The answer can change A building that fixes its problem can be reviewed again. A building's approval, or the lender's own certification of it, must be current on the day each loan closes.

Every condotel, a condo building run like a hotel, is non-warrantable. Many non-warrantable buildings are not condotels. Our condotel financing guide covers the hotel-run buildings.

## What makes a condo non-warrantable?
One failed rule is enough. These are among the reasons Fannie Mae lists , grouped by what you would see in the building. The first group is the one most oceanfront buildings here meet. It is about who owns the units and how they use them.
The building is run for renting

- Mostly investors and second homes When 75 percent or more of the units are owned as investments or second homes, the lender must look harder at whether the building runs as a hotel. That alone does not turn the building down.

- Run like a hotel Any one of these counts: an HOA licensed as a hotel or resort, or papers that limit when owners may stay. Papers that require a rental pool or that owners share rental profits count too.

- Hotel signs Hotel-type services, resort marketing and a hotel rating count too. A name with hotel, motel or resort in it counts, unless the word only refers to the building's past use.

- One owner with too many units In a building of 21 or more units, no one owner may hold more than 20 percent. Rented units count. A developer's vacant units that are for sale do not.

- Timeshare weeks Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will not take a timeshare building, where owners buy weeks.

The building's money

- Dues not paid In Fannie Mae's full review of a condo building, no more than 15 percent of units may be 60 days or more behind on dues.

- Thin savings for repairs The budget must put at least 10 percent of dues income into reserves. Freddie Mac raises the test to 15 percent for applications from January 4, 2027. It says it made the change with its regulator and in alignment with Fannie Mae. Our guide to HOA reserves has the details.

- Short master insurance The building's master policy must insure the full cost to rebuild. Its deductible can be at most 5 percent of that amount, a wind or storm deductible included, and at most $50,000 a unit.

- Too much business More than 35 percent of the space is commercial. Or the HOA earns more than 10 percent of its income from a business that serves the public, such as a restaurant or a spa.

Hard stops

- Critical repairs Problems that could cause a failure within a year count. Unfunded repairs over $10,000 a unit due within 12 months count too, unless an owner makes them or a special assessment pays for them. Sea walls, elevators, waterproofing and balconies are among the examples.

- A lawsuit A pending suit that names the HOA stops the loan. A suit that names the developer over safety or structure stops it too. Some minor suits are allowed when the lender finds no effect on the building's safety, structure, use or livability. Our guide to buying a condo in litigation covers suits.

For most condo loans, the building's budget and reserves are now checked in a full review.
Heard "non-warrantable" from a lender?
Tell us which building. We find which rule it fails and what that means for the loans you can use.

## Why are so many Myrtle Beach oceanfront condos non-warrantable?
Most of them are run for renting. Our directory has 43 oceanfront buildings with a county count, in Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach. By the county's tax records, at least three of four units in 42 of them are not the owner's home. That is one of the signs Fannie Mae tells a lender to look harder at.
Photo: USGS
Oceanfront condo towers in Myrtle Beach, with their pools behind the dunes, seen from a plane over the ocean.
An inland condo community on FHA's approved list makes the difference plain. At Seagate Village, about half the units are taxed as the owner's home.
At the beach, few condos are the owner's home. Inland, about half are. Condo building Units taxed as the owner's home

Share of condo units taxed at South Carolina's 4 percent rate for an owner's main home, from Horry County's parcel records. An owner who lives in the unit but never applied is counted as not.
A lender asks whether a building full of rentals is run like a hotel. To a buyer who wants a rental, it is a good sign: the building is run for exactly that, even when the loan costs more.
The listings say the same. About 8 in 10 condos for sale in these buildings say the unit is in a rental program.

### Timeshare weeks and big owners
Timeshare weeks are sold by recorded deed in Anderson Ocean Club, Towers on the Grove and SeaWatch's towers. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac both list timeshare buildings among the ones they will not take.
In three other buildings, one company holds more than 1 in 5 of the units in at least one part of the building. That is over Fannie Mae's 20 percent limit, unless they are a developer's vacant units for sale.

### The master insurance rule
Take a building that would cost $20 million to rebuild. Its master policy's deductible can be at most $1 million, which is 5 percent. A larger wind deductible fails the rule, and the lender checks the policy.
What your own condo owner's policy pays when the building's deductible comes due is in our guide to the master policy and your own condo policy .

Fannie Mae publishes no list for buyers to search. A lender decides for each building from its papers. What we can show you is the public signs a lender's review looks for, building by building.

## Can you get a loan on a non-warrantable condo?
Yes. Cash works, and so do loans a lender keeps or sells outside Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Each of those lenders writes its own building rules. One published program shows how far apart the rules can be.
Where one non-warrantable loan program says yes The test Fannie Mae One published program
One owner's share of the units, in a building of 21 or more Fannie Mae Up to 20 percent One published program Up to 49 percent, with conditions
Units 60 days or more behind on dues Fannie Mae Up to 15 percent One published program Up to 25 percent
Space used for business Fannie Mae Up to 35 percent One published program Up to 50 percent
A lawsuit Fannie Mae A suit naming the HOA, unless it is minor One published program Case by case, never one about the structure
Rules the building can miss Fannie Mae None One published program Up to 2

- A loan made outside Fannie Mae's rules The lender keeps the loan or sells it to other investors. These loans often cost more than a conventional loan.

- A DSCR loan It qualifies on the unit's rent instead of your income. Our DSCR loan guide covers it.

- Cash No lender reviews the building.

- FHA FHA works only in a building on HUD's approved list . Of its 117 Horry County records, 9 are approved. In our directory of oceanfront buildings, the only approved one is Sea Mark Tower, one of the Caravelle's nine buildings. FHA will not insure a loan on a condotel, and it will not approve a condo building that is a condo hotel or has a required rental pool.

- VA A VA loan is for a home you will live in. At least 6 of the 47 buildings in our full oceanfront directory have an accepted record on the VA's condo list . Our VA loan guide and buyer programs guide have more.

### How much do you need down?
For a rental you will not stay in more than 14 days a year, plan on about 25 percent down in a non-warrantable building. In a warrantable one, plan on about 20 percent. Figures from BrickWood Mortgage.
For a home or a second home you will use yourself, plan on a larger down payment than a conventional loan asks.

### Who makes these loans

## Should you buy a non-warrantable condo?
Yes, when the building's reason is one you can live with and the loan fits your plan. What you gain, and what it costs you:
What you gain

- A building run for renting A building full of investors is run for what a rental owner wants.

- Units that sell About 780 units sold one at a time by recorded deed in a year, in the 43 directory buildings with a county count.

- A reason that can be fixed A new master policy, a lawsuit that ends or dues collected can bring a building back. A lender then reviews it again.

What it costs you

- More cash at closing Plan on a larger down payment than a conventional loan, and often a higher cost.

- Fewer lenders, now and when you sell Fewer lenders make these loans, and each has its own limits. Your next buyer needs one too, unless they pay cash.

- Some reasons stop every loan A critical repair or a suit over the structure stops Fannie Mae loans. One published non-warrantable program will not take a suit over the structure either.

Whether a beach condo makes a good rental at all is in our guide to Myrtle Beach condos as investments .

## How do you find out if a condo is warrantable before you make an offer?
We find out for you, before you make an offer. Our agents read the same papers a lender's review reads:

- The lender questionnaire The HOA's answers to the questions a lender asks about the building.

- The budget and reserves What goes into savings for repairs, against the 10 percent test.

- The master policy What it insures and how big its deductible is, wind included.

- The minutes and any special assessment Repairs the board has talked about, and what owners have been asked to pay.

- Any lawsuit Who is suing whom, and over what.

- The county's records Whether one owner holds a block of units, and whether timeshare weeks are sold in the building.

A loan officer at our preferred lender then tells us how a lender will read it. You know before you pay for an appraisal or an inspection. The papers themselves are in our guide to HOA documents .

Common questions

## Non-warrantable condo FAQ

### What is the difference between a warrantable and a non-warrantable condo?
A warrantable condo is in a building that meets Fannie Mae's project rules, so a conventional loan there can be sold to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. A non-warrantable condo is in a building that fails one of those rules.

### Is there a list of non-warrantable condos in Myrtle Beach?
Fannie Mae publishes no list for buyers to search. A lender reviews each building from its papers. Our table shows the public signs for 43 oceanfront buildings.

### Can I use an FHA or VA loan on a non-warrantable condo?
Only in a building on that agency's own list. Of the oceanfront buildings in our directory, only Sea Mark Tower at the Caravelle is FHA-approved, and at least 6 have an accepted VA record.

### How much do you need down for a non-warrantable condo?
For a rental you will not stay in more than 14 days a year, about 25 percent down, against about 20 percent in a warrantable building. Figures from BrickWood Mortgage. For a home you will use, plan on a larger down payment.

### Can a non-warrantable condo become warrantable?
Yes. When the building fixes the reason, such as a new master policy or a lawsuit that ends, a lender can review it again.

### Can I buy a non-warrantable condo as a second home?
Yes, with cash or a loan made outside Fannie Mae's rules. Plan on a larger down payment than for a conventional loan.

## Are home prices dropping in Myrtle Beach?
No. House prices in Horry County have been about flat for a year, after rising about half in the four years before.

## How accurate are online home estimates in Myrtle Beach?
Redfin publishes how close its own estimate comes in Horry County. For homes that were not for sale, the middle miss was 6.6 percent: about $23,000 on a $350,000 house. Half of the homes were further off, and about 1 in 7 was off by more than 20 percent.
No online estimate, Zillow's Zestimate included, tells you whether your home is one of the close ones or one of the far ones.
Once a home is listed for sale, Redfin's middle miss here falls to 1.65 percent. It is closer then because there is more data about a home for sale. A listing adds what the county's records do not show: the rooms, the updates, the photos and an asking price. Our agent looks at those things with you before you list, and sends the number with the sales behind it. Before you list, read what to fix before you sell and the best month to list .

## Is the county's value or the nearest sales a good guess at my price?
Two quick numbers are often used as a price: the middle price of the six nearest sales, and the county's value, which is the market value on the home's county property record. We checked both against the prices of houses sold this year.
How far off two quick numbers were on a typical house Quick number how far off

Middle price of the six nearest sales 16% off
The county's value 9% off

The county's value was closer, but it is a mass estimate, made for every home at once, for tax. It is above the price on most condos and below it on most houses: about 7 in 10 condos sold for less than it, and 6 in 10 houses sold for more.
Your tax bill is a worse guide. About 2 in 3 Horry County homes are taxed on less than the county's value. A sale resets the value as of December 31 of the year the home sold, so your buyer's tax bill can be higher than yours.

## How is a home's value worked out in Myrtle Beach?
We start from the sales most like your home. The nearest sales, or the sales on your street, can be far off. Here is one Carolina Forest house from the county's records.
One Carolina Forest house, from county records. Gray dots are sales. The black line is the middle of the six nearest. The dashed line is what the house sold for.

- The six nearest sales had a middle price of about $556,000, about $74,000 more than the house sold for. Only one of the six was in its neighborhood.

- The other 4 house sales in its own neighborhood in the year went for $356,000 to $425,000.

- The house sold for about $482,000, more than any of them.

The county's records do not say why this house sold for more than its neighbors. A comparative market analysis, or CMA, finds out. It does five things the quick numbers cannot:

- It keeps only sales like the home in size, age, lot and condition, from the same neighborhood or the next one over. For a condo, that means sales in the same building. For a home on the water or a golf course, sales on the same water or course.

- It adjusts each of those sales for what differs from the home.

- It looks at the home's condition, updates and view, with the owner.

- It compares the home with the homes for sale near it now.

- It ends in a price range and a list price.

A condo's price also depends on whether lenders will lend in its building. Where many will not, fewer buyers can get a loan. Our guide to condos most lenders will not lend on explains which buildings and why.
Our agents do a CMA for your home, free.
Have an agent price your home
Usually in a day or two.
Ask us to price it

### Is a CMA the same as an appraisal?
No. An appraisal is a licensed appraiser's opinion of value. In South Carolina, appraisal work and the title of appraiser need an appraiser's license, and an agent's valuation may not be called an appraisal.
Our agents see low appraisals only rarely here. When a buyer's appraisal comes in low, our agents ask the appraiser to look again, and send recent sales of homes like yours. Once, the value went up, and the buyer brought less cash to closing.

## What changes a home's price in Myrtle Beach?

### How close it is to the ocean
Condos within 0.1 mile of the ocean ask about twice as much per square foot as condos more than 2 miles away.

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Crescent Beach in North Myrtle Beach from over the ocean in 2011: buildings on the beach, then streets of houses. Houses for sale within 0.1 mile of the ocean ask about 2.5 times as much a square foot as houses more than 2 miles away.

### New houses for sale near you
Your house competes with new ones . Builders sold new houses in the same 12 months for a middle price close to the resale one. More than 2 miles from the ocean, new houses for sale ask about $194 a square foot, and older ones about $200. A buyer at your price may also be touring new houses.

### The time of year
More houses sell in the warm months. From May to October the county recorded about 1.5 times as many house resales a month as in January and February. The price moved less: the middle stayed within about 5 percent of $350,000 in every month. Our Myrtle Beach market reports track prices, days on market and inventory.

### The flood line
About 13 percent of the county's resales were inside FEMA's high-risk flood zone , most of them condos. Being inside it did not lower the price. In neighborhoods with house sales on both sides of the line, the houses inside it did not sell for less than the others.

## How much will I keep when I sell in Myrtle Beach?
On a $350,000 sale, these come off the price:

- The deed fee, $1,295. It is a state fee, and the seller pays it.

- The commission you agree with your broker.

- What you still owe on your loan.

- Tax on your gain, often none. If you owned the home and lived in it for 2 of the last 5 years, up to $250,000 of gain can be left out of your income, or $500,000 for a married couple filing jointly who both lived there. It does not apply if you used it on another home in the 2 years before. Bought for $200,000 and sold for $350,000, your gain is less than $150,000, inside the limit.

- A hold-back if you live in another state. The buyer must hold back part of the price at closing for South Carolina income tax, unless the sale is exempt, for example a main home whose gain is inside that limit. With your signed statement of the gain, it is figured on the gain, not the whole price.

Our net proceeds calculator works out what you keep at your own price. Thinking of selling it yourself ? We will price your home either way.

## Home value FAQ

### What is my home worth in Myrtle Beach?
Across Horry County, houses and other homes resold for a middle price of about $350,000 in the latest 12 months of county deeds, and condos for about $215,000. In the city of Conway the middle house sold for about $265,000, and inside North Myrtle Beach for about $535,000.

### How accurate are online home estimates in Myrtle Beach?
Close on some homes and far off on others. Redfin's figures for Horry County put its middle miss at 6.6 percent on homes not for sale, and 1.65 percent once a home is listed.

### What is the difference between a CMA and an appraisal?
A CMA, a comparative market analysis, is an agent's pricing of your home from the sales most like it. An appraisal is a licensed appraiser's opinion of value. In South Carolina an agent's valuation must not be called an appraisal.

### Why is my county assessed value different from my market value?
The county values every home at once, for tax, so it cannot see what one home has. The taxable value is often lower still: under state law it can rise only so far between sales. A sale resets it.

### Are Myrtle Beach home prices dropping?
No. By the Federal Housing Finance Agency's house price index, house prices in Horry County were about flat in the year to mid-2026, after rising about half from mid-2021 to mid-2025.

### Does a home valuation cost anything?
No. Our valuation is free, and you do not have to list your home with us.

Live in another state? About 6 in 10 Horry County condo units have their tax bill mailed outside South Carolina. When your permanent home is outside the state, the buyer must hold back part of the price for state income tax.
For a 2026 sale it is 5.21 percent of your gain if you sign the state's gain affidavit. Without the affidavit, it is 5.21 percent of the price less your selling costs. A main home whose gain is inside the federal exclusion has no hold-back. Our capital gains page works it out.

## Who pays what when you sell a house in South Carolina?
On the state REALTORS' standard contract , you pay the deed stamps, your mortgage payoff, the fee you agreed with your agent and your own attorney. The buyer pays both title insurance policies.
You pay

- The deed preparation

- The deed stamps and the deed recording

- Your mortgage payoff, and recording its release

- Property tax for the months you owned the home

- The fee you agreed with your own agent

- Your own attorney

The buyer pays

- Both title insurance policies, the owner's and the lender's

- The title exam

- Inspections, the appraisal and any survey

- The buyer's attorney

The side the contract ticks pays You pay if no box is ticked

- The association's fees for its papers

- The association's letter of what is owed

- Transfer fees

- A capital or working-capital payment to the association

Each side pays its own costs unless both agree otherwise in writing. The form also tells both sides they are responsible for getting legal advice before they sign.
Buying another home here as well? Our closing costs page lists the buyer's side.

## What does the closing attorney charge the seller for?
A South Carolina attorney must supervise every home closing in the state. If the buyer has a loan for a home they will live in, the buyer chooses the closing attorney .
An attorney who represents only the buyer does not advise you. You may refuse to sign a settlement statement you do not agree with. The attorney charges on your side of the closing statement can include three things:

- The deed preparation Preparing a deed for someone else is the practice of law, so a lawyer prepares your deed. On the standard contract, that cost is yours.

- A payoff handling fee In a standard South Carolina closing, the buyer's attorney typically prepares the settlement statement. Under a South Carolina Bar ethics opinion , when that attorney also sends your mortgage payoff, they may add a reasonable payoff handling fee to your side.

- Your own attorney, if you hire one On the standard contract, your own attorney's fee is your cost.

These charges differ from one attorney's office to the next, so this page prints no figure for them.

## How much are SC deed stamps at your price?
Deed stamps, the state's fee on a deed that many people call the transfer tax, are $1.85 for each $500 of the price , or part of $500. The seller owes them.
The county also charges $15 to record the deed and $10 to record the release of a paid-off mortgage.

## What HOA fees does a seller pay at closing?
The association's charges for the sale go to the side the contract ticks, and to you if no box is ticked. Your regular dues are split as of the closing day instead, like the property tax.

- No cap in state law South Carolina has no cap on what an association charges for its resale papers or its letter of what is owed. A transfer fee covenant that makes an owner pay a third party on each sale is not binding if it was recorded after February 1, 2012. A fee paid to the association itself is still allowed.

- Unpaid dues come out of your money Unpaid HOA fees are usually a lien on the home, and they come out of the seller's money at closing. We look for them before closing. On a condo sale, state law requires your unpaid association charges to be paid out of the price, after past-due taxes and recorded mortgages.

- Special assessments For a special assessment approved before closing, the contract has two boxes: you pay all of it, or only the part due in the year of closing. One approved after closing is the buyer's. Our special assessments page goes further.

More than 1 in 4 houses for sale here list no HOA fee. Almost every condo for sale lists one. Our guide to HOA fees when a home sells covers the letter the association sends for the sale.

## Why is my mortgage payoff more than my balance?
Your payoff includes the interest due through the day the loan is paid off, and any fees charged and not yet paid. Some loans also charge a prepayment penalty, a fee for paying the loan off early.
On a home loan made for personal use, the servicer must send an accurate payoff statement within seven business days of a written request. A loan made to buy a rental the owner does not use counts as a business loan, and that rule does not apply to it. A beach place the owner planned to use more than 14 days a year still counts as personal.

### Closing day: guard the wire
Never follow wiring instructions that arrive in an email. Confirm them by phone with the attorney's office, at a number you agreed on in advance.

## Who pays the property taxes when you sell in Horry County?
You pay for the part of the year you owned the home, and the buyer pays for the rest. South Carolina property taxes for a year are due between September 30 and January 15 after they are assessed. To look up the bill for your home, use our guide to Horry County tax payments .
For most of the year, the tax for the months you have owned the home has not been billed yet. At closing you credit the buyer your share. The credit is your own tax for those months, not an extra cost.
The later you close, the bigger the tax credit to the buyer
On a $350,000 home outside city limits, at Horry County's 2026 tax rates.

### Why a second home pays about three times as much
A home its owner lives in is assessed at 4 percent of its value and pays no school operating tax. A second home or rental is assessed at 6 percent and pays the full county levy .
Inside a city or town, such as Myrtle Beach or Conway, the tax and the credit differ from these figures.

### If the bill turns out different
The closing attorney figures the tax split from the tax information they judge reliable. If the bill later turns out different, you and the buyer settle the difference between yourselves.
When a home's last deed is old, its tax bill, and the tax credit at closing, is often smaller than one figured on today's price. Our property tax page explains why.

## Is the money you keep from the sale taxed?
Often not, if it was your main home. You can exclude up to $250,000 of gain from your income, or $500,000 for a married couple filing jointly.

- Who can use the exclusion You owned and lived in the home at least 2 of the last 5 years. You also did not use the exclusion on another home in the 2 years before.

- Your selling costs lower the gain The commission, legal fees, and the deed stamps and other fees you pay as the seller count as selling expenses .

- The sale is reported on Form 1099-S The closing attorney's office reports most sales to the IRS . A main home that sells for $250,000 or less may be left off if you certify the whole gain is excluded. For a married seller the limit is $500,000.

A rental or a second home is taxed differently. Our capital gains guide works through it.

## How do sellers here keep more of the price?
Price it once. On a $350,000 home, each 1 percent off the asking price is $3,500, the same as 1 percent of commission.
We checked every resale house and townhouse for sale in Horry County for a price cut. More than half have cut their asking price at every price: about 63 percent under $300,000, and about 56 percent in each higher band.
Resale homes for sale in Horry County, our count

- 1,260 of 2,188 houses and townhouses have cut their asking price

- 1,372 of 2,652 condos have cut their asking price

The homes for sale near the top of this page are the kind a seller near the middle competes with. Our home value page shows how we price a home from the recorded sales most like it.

- The commission is yours to agree Agents' fees are fully negotiable , and no law fixes them. Offers to pay the buyer's agent are no longer made on the MLS, the agents' shared listing service. Offering to pay the buyer's agent is a choice, not a requirement.

- A credit to the buyer is your money The contract caps it at a dollar amount. If the buyer's costs come in lower, or the lender allows less, the rest stays with you. On an FHA loan , the seller and others may pay up to 6 percent of the price toward the buyer's closing costs. On a VA loan , other concessions are capped at 4 percent of the home's reasonable value.

- A home warranty is rare on a resale here Only 62 of 2,188 resale houses and townhouses for sale advertise one. Nearly all the home warranties offered here come with new homes. The standard contract has no home warranty clause; buyer and seller can add one with a separate addendum.

## Seller costs FAQ

### What is a seller net sheet?
A list of every line on the seller's side of the closing: the price, less the commission, the fees, the tax credit and the payoff. The $350,000 example near the top of this page is one.

### Who pays title insurance in South Carolina?
The buyer pays both policies, the owner's and the lender's, on the state REALTORS' standard contract. Buyer and seller can agree to something else in writing.

### Does the seller need an attorney in South Carolina?
Every South Carolina home closing must be supervised by a South Carolina attorney, and a lawyer prepares the seller's deed. When the buyer has a loan for a home they will live in, the buyer picks that attorney, who does not advise you. Your own attorney is your cost.

### Can I sell my house before the mortgage is paid off?
Yes. The closing pays off the loan out of the sale money, and you get what is left.

The short answer
Yes. You can sell your house by owner in Myrtle Beach, or anywhere in South Carolina, without a real estate agent or a license. A South Carolina attorney must supervise the closing, and you give the buyer the state's disclosure form before you both sign the contract.
In Horry County, the middle-priced home resold in the year to September 2026, not counting condos, sold for about $350,000. On that home, each 1 percent of fees you do not pay is $3,500.

## Can you sell your own house in South Carolina without a real estate agent?
Yes. South Carolina's license law does not apply to an owner selling their own home, so you need no real estate license. This is called selling "for sale by owner", or FSBO.
Three duties apply to most owners who sell, with or without an agent:

- A South Carolina attorney supervises the closing Who picks the attorney

- The buyer gets the state's disclosure form before the contract What the form asks

- Most homes built before 1978 need lead papers Which homes

## Do you need a lawyer to sell a house by owner in South Carolina?
Yes, for the closing, the meeting where the buyer pays and you sign the house over. Every home closing in South Carolina must be supervised by a South Carolina attorney.
Preparing a deed for someone else is the practice of law. Anyone who prepares your deed for you, the paper that transfers the house, must be a lawyer.

### Who picks the closing attorney?

- The buyer has a home loan The buyer chooses If the loan is for a home the buyer will live in, the buyer picks the closing attorney, and the lender must follow that choice.

- Every sale The contract can name one The contract can name the closing attorney and say who pays the attorney's fees. You and the buyer agree on it.

- You want advice Hire your own An attorney who represents only the buyer does not advise the seller. Advice on your side of the deal comes from your own attorney.

### Who writes the purchase contract?
A 2007 opinion of the state Attorney General's office looked at agents who fill in the blanks of a printed sale contract an attorney wrote. If the buyer has an agent, the offer may come to you on that kind of form.
The office said that does not appear to be the practice of law, if no legal advice is given or asked for. The state Supreme Court has the final word. Preparing a legal paper for someone else is the practice of law when it involves legal advice. Advice on the contract's terms comes from a lawyer. A South Carolina attorney can write the contract for you, or read the buyer's before you sign.

### How you get paid safely
Closing money often moves by wire transfer, and scammers send fake wiring instructions by email. Never follow wiring instructions in an email. Confirm them by phone with the attorney's office, at a number you agreed on in advance.

## What paperwork do you need to sell by owner in South Carolina?
The main paper is the state's Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement , a form where you tell the buyer what you know about the home. State law requires it for a home with one to four units, unless the sale is one of the kinds listed below that need no form. The form is free. Our guide to the South Carolina seller disclosure form goes through all 28 questions.
The form has nine parts. It asks 28 numbered questions, each answered Yes, No or No Representation, plus lines where you describe things such as the roof's age, pests and leases.
What South Carolina's disclosure form asks, part by part

- I Water and sewer Questions 1 to 4

- II Roof, gutters, foundation and floors Questions 5 to 7

- III Plumbing, electrical, appliances, heating and cooling Questions 8 to 14

- IV Termites, wood rot and other pests Describe

- V Zoning, rights of others to use your land, legal claims, water damage, flood and the beach Questions 15 to 28 Questions 22 to 28, on the coast and flooding
- 22 Erosion and erosion control

- 23 Flood hazards, wetlands, flood zones, flood risk

- 24 Flood insurance on the property now

- 25 Flood insurance claims during your ownership

- 26 Flood repairs not claimed on insurance during your ownership

- 27 Federal flood disaster aid during your ownership

- 28 A charge for beach nourishment, sand added to the beach, while you owned it

Question 20 also asks whether the house flooded while you owned it.

- VI Lead paint, asbestos, radon, buried tanks and mold Describe

- VII Leases and vacation rentals in place at closing Describe

- VIII Utility charges and equipment the utility financed Describe

- IX Whether the home is in an association Yes or No, then the addendum

Our drawing of the state's form. Each numbered question is answered Yes, No or No Representation. Parts marked "Describe" have lines to write on.
A home in a homeowners association (HOA), a property owners association or a condo also needs the form's addendum. It asks 11 more questions and lists the dues and the association's contact. Our HOA documents page lists the association papers a buyer will ask for.

### Why the flood questions matter here
USGS photo, 2011
Beach houses beside the Surfside Beach pier in 2011. Questions 22 to 28 on the state form ask every seller about erosion, flooding and beach nourishment.

FEMA has paid 8,815 flood insurance claims in Horry County since 1978. Nearly 1 in 4 were on buildings rated outside the high-risk flood zone. That is why questions 23 to 27 matter here, even away from the water. Our flood history page shows what a buyer can find out about a home's flood past.

### Four rules about the form

- "No Representation" Not a way to skip a question It means you do not know enough to answer Yes or No. It does not protect you if you know of the problem.

- After you hand it over Correct it if anything changes If the roof starts to leak before closing, you must correct the form or repair the roof.

- If you leave something out You can owe the buyer A seller who knowingly leaves a problem off the form, or answers falsely, can owe the buyer their actual losses and court costs. A court may add the winner's attorney fees.

- Selling as is The form still applies You can sell "as is", which means without repairs. An as-is sale still needs the form, unless it is one of the sales listed below.

Not giving the form does not cancel the contract or stop the closing.

### What you do not have to tell a buyer
You do not have to disclose that someone died in the home. You also do not have to disclose an illness of someone who lived there if it is highly unlikely to spread by living in the home. The same goes for the sex offender registry. If a buyer asks you directly, you may not lie.

### Sales that need no form
South Carolina lists 15 kinds of sale that need no form. Among them:

- A sale only to your spouse, or only to your children, grandchildren, parents or grandparents. If your child's spouse is also a buyer, the sale needs the form.

- A sale only between co-owners.

- A sale by an executor or trustee settling an estate or a trust.

- The first sale of a home no one has lived in.

- A sale at public auction.

- Any sale where buyer and seller both agree in writing to skip the form.

Homes built before 1978 A seller of most homes built before 1978 must also give the buyer the federal lead pamphlet . You also say what you know about lead paint and hand over any lead reports. The contract must include a lead warning statement. The buyer gets 10 days to test for lead, unless both agree in writing to a different period or the buyer waives it. Keep the signed form for three years. Four cases are not covered. One is a unit with no bedroom. Another is housing for older people or people with disabilities where no child under six lives. The others are a home a certified inspector found free of lead paint, and a foreclosure sale.

## Do houses sold by owner sell for less?
Nationally, yes, but many of those sales were to someone the seller knew. NAR, the National Association of Realtors, surveys people who bought a home to live in and also sold one. In its 2025 survey , 5 percent sold by owner, the lowest share in NAR's records.
More than half of by-owner sellers already knew the buyer. In resort and recreation areas, 9 percent sold by owner.
Middle sale price in NAR's 2025 survey, by how the home sold How it sold middle price

By owner, seller knew the buyer $360,000
By owner, seller did not know the buyer $372,200
Sold with an agent $425,000

The groups sell different homes in different places, so the gap is not all price lost. The survey covers people who bought a home to live in and also sold one.
County deeds point the same way for sales between people who share a last name. We read the county's deed index for a year and compared those sales with other sales between two people. To search that index yourself, see our guide to searching Horry County deeds by name .
Horry County home sales recorded under $100,000 Who sold to whom, how many share under $100,000

Seller and buyer share a last name · 22 of 73 sales 3 in 10
Other sales between people · 294 of 7,449 sales 1 in 25

Our count of the county's deeds, October 2025 to September 2026: resales between two people, with no company, trust, estate or builder on either side. The middle price was $200,000 when the two shared a last name and $310,000 for the rest.
A shared last name is not proof of family, and relatives with different last names are missed. Even so, those 73 sales recorded far lower prices.

### Selling to a stranger
Selling to a stranger is a different job. The price has to come from the sales most like your home, and enough buyers have to see the house.
Asked the hardest part, 17 percent of by-owner sellers named getting the price right, more than any other task.
Two quick numbers are a poor guide to a price. We checked both against 4,919 house resales recorded this year. On a typical house, each was this far off the sale price:
How far off, on a typical house

- 16 percent the middle price of the six nearest sales
