NAR's 2025 survey. Sellers could name more than one way, so the shares add to more than 100 percent.
The MLS is the database real estate brokers share to list homes for sale, so an owner gets on it through a broker. In NAR's survey, 7 percent of sellers who used an agent said the agent put the home on the MLS and did little else.
On the MLS, your house competes with every other home for sale:
Houses for sale in Horry County now

- About 3,700 houses listed for sale on the MLS, the database brokers share

- 56 percent of them have already cut their asking price. Buyers compare yours with all of them.

Broad marketing generally exposes a home to the greatest number of qualified buyers. Keeping a home off the open market may reduce buyer competition and may hurt the price, terms or time to sell.

### Do you have to pay the buyer's agent?
No rule requires it. Since August 2024, an agent who uses the MLS signs a written agreement with a buyer before touring a home. Offers to pay the buyer's agent are no longer made on the MLS.
You can still offer to pay the buyer's agent off the MLS, or offer the buyer a credit toward their costs. Agents' fees are negotiable, and no law names an amount.

## Is selling by owner a good idea for you?
The answer changes with who the buyer is and where the house is. Find your situation:

- You are selling to a stranger You want the most money See whether homes sold by owners sell for less , and what changes the price.

- Your house is near the water Or in a flood zone Gather your flood papers before you list: insurance, past claims and repair bills. Questions 20 and 22 to 28 of the form ask about each.

## What are the steps to sell a house by owner in South Carolina?
Eight steps, from the price to the money in your account. Steps marked "Required by law" come from state or federal rules.

- 1 Before you list Set the price Price it from the recorded sales most like your home. Our home value page shows how.

- 2 Before you list Required by law Fill in the papers The state's disclosure form, the HOA addendum if you have an association, and the lead papers for most homes built before 1978.

- 3 Showings Reach buyers and show the house Use the ways in the chart above . Keep valuables and medicines out of sight during showings.

- 4 Before you sign Check that the buyer can pay Ask for a loan approval letter from a lender, or proof of the cash, before you sign anything.

- 5 Signing Required by law Hand over the form, then sign the contract The form comes first, unless the contract names another time. Agree in writing on the deposit and who holds it, the inspection period, the loan deadline and the closing date. Who writes the contract

- 6 After signing Required by law The buyer's lead test For most homes built before 1978, the buyer's lead test period starts now.

- 7 Before closing Required by law Keep the form up to date The form rules apply until closing day.

- 8 Closing day Sign, and get paid by wire Check the wiring instructions by phone . The deed fee comes out of the sale.

### Do you pay tax on the sale?
Often not. Under federal tax law , you can leave part or all of your gain out of your income.

- How much Up to $250,000 of gain Or $500,000 of gain for a married couple filing jointly.

- Who qualifies You lived there 2 of 5 years You owned and lived in the home at least 2 of the last 5 years. You did not use this exclusion on another home in the 2 years before.

- You live in another state The buyer holds back state tax For a 2026 sale it is 5.21 percent. It is figured on your gain if you sign the state's gain affidavit , Form I-295, or on the whole price if you do not. A main home whose gain fits inside the federal exclusion has none.

- Getting it back Your South Carolina return File a South Carolina return for the year of the sale. The amount held back counts toward the tax you owe there. You can ask for a refund of any amount held back beyond the tax.

Our capital gains page works through the tax when the gain is larger.

Common questions

## Selling by owner FAQ

### Who pays the deed stamps when you sell by owner in South Carolina?
The seller pays them, whether or not an agent is involved: $1,295 on a $350,000 sale.

### Can I sell my house to my son or daughter without the disclosure form?
Yes, if the sale is only to your children, grandchildren, parents or grandparents. If your child's spouse is also a buyer, the sale needs the form.

### Do I have to tell a buyer that someone died in the house?
No. South Carolina does not require it. If a buyer asks you directly, you may not lie about it.

### Can I sell my house as is in South Carolina?
Yes. An as-is sale still needs the state's disclosure form, unless it is one of the sales that need no form, such as some family sales.

### Can a buyer use their own agent to buy a for-sale-by-owner home?
Yes. The buyer's written agreement with their agent says how that agent is paid. You can offer to pay that agent, or offer the buyer a credit toward their costs.

# New construction in Myrtle Beach: what the price on the sign leaves out.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
New construction in Horry County costs about what a nearly new house does. The sign leaves out lot premiums, options, HOA charges, closing costs and the full tax bill.

The short answer
A new house here lists for about the same price per square foot as a house built 2016 to 2023 of similar size nearby. A typical new house for sale is listed at about $370,000. Most are built inland, in large communities near Highway 90, Highway 22 and the Carolina Bays Parkway.
The sign leaves out the full tax bill, closing costs, HOA charges, options you pick and lot premiums, extra charges for a particular lot. For about 4 in 5 of the 2026 builder sales, the county still taxes only the lot. On a typical home you live in outside city limits, the yearly county bill goes from about $290 to about $1,210 once the county values the house.

## Is new construction worth it, or should you buy a nearly new house?
The price per square foot, the price divided by the floor space, will not decide it for you. Next to a house built 2016 to 2023 of similar size within a mile, about half of new houses list for less per square foot and half for more. Town by town, the typical prices are close too.

The lot is about the same size too. In Conway, Longs and Myrtle Beach addresses, a new house has about the same size lot as a house built 2016 to 2023 in the same town.

### What does a new house give you?

- No one has lived in it. If the builder has not started it, you also pick the plan and the finishes.

- A written warranty from the builder. The warranty section below lists what it covers.

- Built to today's codes. State law has the county or city enforce the building codes : building, electrical, plumbing, gas, energy and fire. East of U.S. 17, state law also has insurers count the building code , the construction and roof tie-downs when they price wind coverage. Roof tie-downs are straps that hold the roof to the walls.

- Less flood risk, on average. About 1 in 20 new houses for sale is in a high-risk flood zone on the map of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Of all houses for sale, about 8 in 100 are. Our coastal insurance guide covers wind and flood coverage.

Pick by your plans:

- You want to move in within a month Look at nearly new resales, houses built 2016 to 2023 and sold by their owners, and at new houses that are finished and never lived in.

- You want to pick the plan and the finishes Choose a house the builder has not started. Plan on about 6 months of building, more on your own lot.

- You are buying it to rent The county taxes a rental or second home on 6 percent of its value, not 4. It also adds the school tax a home you live in does not pay. Its yearly bill is more than three times as high. Our guide to new construction as a rental has the rest.

- You want to be near the beach New houses are a small share of what is for sale near the ocean. Three of the ten busiest new communities are about 1 to 2 miles from it.

A typical new house for sale in Horry County is listed at about $370,000, with about 1,900 square feet on just under a quarter acre. Half are listed for more, half for less. That is an asking price; the tax example below uses what buyers paid.

Our guide to homes with no HOA lists the areas where most homes have none, and our guide to the most affordable places to live covers the lowest prices.

## What does the price of a new house leave out?
Five things: the full property tax, lot premiums, options and upgrades, HOA charges and closing costs. First the tax. A South Carolina tax year looks back to December 31 of the year before. A house finished after that date, or still unsold in the builder's hands, is usually not in that year's bill. Your first bill is often for the lot alone.
Homes builders sold each month, and how many the county still taxes as a lot Still taxed as a lot House value on the tax roll

O N D J F M A M J J A S
2025 2026
For about 4 in 5 of the 2026 sales in the chart, the county record still shows the lot only, so the 2026 bill is on the lot. Every 2025 sale in the chart has its house value.
When the county does value the house, it values it at about what you paid.
Take a typical 2026 builder sale that the county still taxes as a lot. It sold for $329,000, and the county values the lot at $80,000. A home you live in is taxed on 4 percent of its value once you apply; a second home or rental on 6 percent. Outside city limits, the yearly county tax looks like this:
Kind of home Lot only Once valued
Home you live in, 4 percent About $290 About $1,210
Second home or rental, 6 percent About $960 About $3,970

Inside a city, the city's own tax is added, so the bill is higher. Of the ten communities above, Grande Dunes North Village, Waterside and Del Webb North Myrtle Beach are inside North Myrtle Beach and Kingston Oaks is inside Conway. Our property tax guide has each city's rate.

### Will the county bill you for the months before?
Not for the months before the house stood on a December 31. The tax year looks back to that date, so the house tax starts with the next year's bill. If a house that was standing is left off the tax roll, the county may bill the missed years . It can go back no more than three years, and never to a year before the house was built.

- Apply for the 4 percent assessment. Without it, the county taxes your home like a second home, at 6 percent. Apply to the Horry County Assessor by January 15 of the year after you move in, before the first penalty date . It covers the whole year if the house is the home you live in for any part of it. Overpaid tax can be refunded.

- Plan for a higher monthly payment later. If your lender collects the taxes with your loan, the tax part of the payment may go up once the house is valued. The lender's yearly escrow review finds the difference.

### Lot premiums, options and upgrades
The price on the sign is for the base house. Pulte's pages for its communities here say the price may not include lot premiums, upgrades and options. A lot premium is an extra charge for a particular lot. Pulte's annual report names flooring, countertops, fixtures and appliances among its options.
Toll Brothers, which recorded 97 of the builder sales here, gives a national figure in its annual report . Its buyers' options and lot premiums came to about a quarter of the base price in its 2025 fiscal year. Its spec homes have less to add, it says.

### Deposits
D.R. Horton, the builder with the most sales here, says in its annual report that its contracts take an earnest money deposit, and more deposits if you pick options or upgrades. If a contract is cancelled, the deposit is kept or refunded under the contract's terms. Our page on the new home builders in Myrtle Beach ranks them by homes sold.
The deposit terms matter before you sign.

### HOA charges and closing costs
Closing costs come on top of the price. The federal Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) says the buyer generally pays them .

- What they include. The appraisal, title insurance, government taxes, and property taxes and homeowners insurance paid ahead.

- Help from the builder. Meritage, which recorded 334 sales here, says in its annual report that it may pay part of the closing costs for buyers who use its preferred lenders. A seller will usually want a higher price to cover a credit, the CFPB says.

- HOA charges. A new community's HOA can also charge at closing. Pulte's pages here list community association fees as a possible extra. If you take out a mortgage, any HOA charge paid at closing is listed on your Closing Disclosure . Ask the builder for the HOA's fees before you sign.

## Do you need a realtor for new construction?
You can buy without one, but the salesperson in the model home works for the builder. Your own agent works for you. Nationwide, most of D.R. Horton's closings involve an independent real estate broker, its annual report says.
Since 2024, an agent asks you to sign a written agreement before you tour a home together. It states what the agent is paid, and that amount is fully negotiable. A builder, like any seller, can still offer to pay your agent. We confirm in writing what, if anything, you would pay before you tour.

### Why does the first visit matter?
Each builder writes its own terms for paying a buyer's agent. Under D.R. Horton's terms on its Florida listings , for example, the builder pays a buyer's agent only if the agent registers you on or before your first visit. You must also not have signed up on its website or talked with its sales agent first.

## Can you negotiate with a builder, and should you use the builder's lender?
Yes, you can negotiate. We see most builders here offer incentives to buyers with an FHA, VA or conventional loan. Incentives for investors, whose loans are based on the rent the home brings in, are rare.
Some promotions come with the builder's own lender. Lennar's Kingston Oaks page offers promotions when you finance through Lennar Mortgage, and nationwide, D.R. Horton's mortgage subsidiary financed 81 percent of the homes it closed in its 2025 fiscal year. You never have to use the builder's lender .

## Spec home or to-be-built: how long does a new house take?
A spec home, one the builder starts before it has a buyer, is often finished and ready now. Of the new houses for sale in the MLS feed, almost half are finished and never lived in. The rest are still being built.
A house the builder has not started takes months. In the South , a builder's house took about 5 and a half months from start to finish in the 2025 figures. A house a contractor builds on your own lot took about 9 months. To find a lot, see our guide to land for sale .

## What inspections does a new house need?
Three of your own: before the drywall, before closing and before the first year of the warranty ends. Each comes at the last point a problem is easy to see, or still the builder's to fix. The county or city also inspects, for the building code. Your own inspector works for you.
Before the drywall goes up, the framing, the wiring and the pipes are open to see. Drawing: Chapter3 Realty.

- Before the drywall goes up. The inspector sees the framing, the wiring and the pipes while the walls are open. Once the drywall is up, a problem inside a wall is hidden.

- Before closing. What is still wrong goes on a written list for the builder, while you can still ask for fixes before you close.

- In month 11. Book it before the one-year part of the warranty ends. It finds what to report while the builder still pays for the fix. We see many builders here also send a maintenance person once in the first year to fix defects and touch up paint.

We set up all three, ask the builder for the warranty booklet, and keep a list of what each one finds, so the builder has it in writing.
Your three inspections, booked for you
When you buy with us, we book all three inspections and keep each list until the builder answers every item.
Have us book inspections

## What can you do when something is wrong with a new house?
Report it to the builder in writing, under the warranty. D.R. Horton gives 1 year on most of the house, 2 years on major mechanical systems and 10 years on major structure. Other builders differ, and the written warranty states the terms.
After closing: the largest builder's warranty, and the state's outer limit Most of the house 1 year

Major mechanical systems 2 years

Major structure 10 years

Outer limit for most defect claims 8 years

Closing 5 years 10 years
Warranty: D.R. Horton's, from its annual report. Law: the 8 years run from when the house is substantially complete.
The warranty says what the builder will fix. The state law says how long you have to sue. Most lawsuits over defects must be filed within 8 years of the house being finished. Inside that, most claims must be filed within three years .
If the builder will not fix it, under South Carolina's defect law you send the builder written notice, and the builder may inspect and offer a repair before you can sue. We keep track of your warranty deadlines after closing.

Common questions

## New construction questions

### Can I find a new house in Myrtle Beach under $300,000?
Yes. About 1 in 5 new houses for sale in Horry County is listed at $300,000 or less. Of the ten communities where builders sold the most, The Overlook (Indigo Grove), Kingston Oaks and Cypress Ridge had typical sale prices under $300,000.

### Are there new townhomes in Myrtle Beach?
Yes. 108 new townhouses are for sale in Horry County, at a typical list price of about $275,000 for about 1,580 square feet.

### How does the county know a new house is being built?
From the building permit. South Carolina law has every county require a permit for new construction. The county must send the assessor a copy of each building permit within 10 days, so the assessor knows a house is being built.

### Does a home builder in South Carolina need a license?
Yes. A residential builder needs a state license for any job over $5,000, issued by the Residential Builders Commission. A complaint against a builder goes to the Commission in writing and sworn.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
A typical $350,000 house in Horry County costs about $650 a month to own besides the loan, $7,850 a year. Each part is below, town by town.

The short answer
A typical house in Horry County, about $350,000, costs about $650 a month to own if you live in it, about $7,850 a year. That does not count the loan payment: paying back the loan and its interest.
In Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach, a typical condo costs more to own each year than a typical house. The condo fee is the reason: condo owners pay it for the building they share. A second home pays about three times the property tax, about $2,900 more a year.

## How much does it cost to own a home in Myrtle Beach each year?
Upkeep and insurance are the biggest parts. Your lender usually collects the tax and insurance with each loan payment, but they are counted here, not in the loan. The HOA fee goes to your homeowners association. It and upkeep are usually paid separately. The fee in each community is in our HOA fee list by neighborhood .
A typical Horry County house, about $350,000, outside city limits: what it costs a year besides the loan What you pay Your home Second home
Property tax the rate is charged on 4 percent of the value (6 percent for a second home) $1,290 $4,220
County stormwater fee on most tax bills outside city limits $89 $89
Home insurance what owners of a house here pay for all their policies $2,000 $2,000
HOA fee a typical house for sale, $100 a month $1,200 $1,200
Upkeep routine repairs plus the big replacements $3,270 $3,270
Total a year $7,850 $10,780
A month $650 $900

Not in the total: electricity and water, about $2,280 a year. A home with a loan in the high-risk flood zone also needs a flood policy (see insurance below). The second-home column changes only the tax. Insurance on a second home can cost more.

Prices differ from town to town far more than these costs do. Our affordable places page shows where a typical home costs least.

## Is a condo cheaper to own than a house in Myrtle Beach?
In Carolina Forest, yes. Its condo fees are the lowest in the table below, and a typical condo there costs about $1,000 a year less to own than a typical house. In Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach, no: their condo fees are the highest.
How much more a year the condo or the house costs to own, as your home The condo costs more The house costs more
City of Myrtle Beach condo costs more The condo costs about $3,280 more a year. $3,280 more

North Myrtle Beach condo costs more The condo costs about $3,570 more a year. $3,570 more

Carolina Forest house costs more The house costs about $1,000 more a year. $1,000 more

A typical condo against a typical house in the same place: tax, the county fee where it applies, insurance, the HOA or condo fee and upkeep. The totals are in the town tables.
The condo is cheaper to buy, so its loan is smaller. In Myrtle Beach a typical condo costs less than half as much as a typical house; in North Myrtle Beach, a little more than half.

### Why are condo fees so high in Myrtle Beach?
They are highest near the ocean in Myrtle Beach. On the city's north end, a typical condo for sale lists about $875 a month. In Carolina Forest, inland, condos list about half that.
Owners pay the fee for everything they share: running the building, upkeep, and improvements to the grounds, halls, lobby, parking and pool. It may also include the tax and insurance on the shared property. Your own unit's insurance is separate: condo owners pay about $800 a year for it.
Photo: USGS
Condo buildings on the ocean in Myrtle Beach, seen from a plane. Condo owners share the cost of grounds, pools and parking lots like these through the condo fee.

In each place below, the condo fee is about three quarters of what a condo owner pays a year to own the unit.

### How many homes here pay an HOA fee?
More than half. About 6 in 10 homeowners across most of Horry County pay an HOA or condo fee; in the rest of South Carolina, about 1 in 3. Still, more than 1 in 4 houses for sale here list no HOA fee. Our page on homes with no HOA shows where they are.

## How much more does a second home pay in property tax?
About 2.5 to 3.8 times as much as the same house as your home. On a $350,000 house, that is about $2,900 to $3,900 more a year, depending on the town.

Outside city limits, the tax is in the table at the top. Horry County's current tax rates, with the City of Myrtle Beach credit for a home taxed at 4 percent. Tax only: the county's stormwater fee and small special districts are left out.
On a home you live in, the tax rate is charged on 4 percent of its value, not the whole value: on a $350,000 house, on $14,000. It also pays only part of the school tax. A second home or a rental is charged on 6 percent and pays all of the school tax. Our second home guide covers the rest of owning one.
The 4 percent rate is not automatic: you apply for it. Our property tax guide has the steps, and our buyer mistakes page shows what paying 6 percent by mistake costs.
At 65 you can have part of your home's value exempted from property tax. Our retiree guide covers who qualifies and how much.

## What does homeowners insurance cost in Myrtle Beach?
A typical house owner in Horry County pays about $2,000 a year, about 40 percent more than in the rest of South Carolina. That is all their home insurance together, with a wind or flood policy included where they have one. Half pay between about $1,300 and $3,000.
Near the ocean, wind can be a separate policy. On the ocean side of U.S. 17, the highway along the coast, an insurer may leave wind and hail out of a homeowners policy. In Myrtle Beach the line is the U.S. 17 Bypass. The owner then buys that cover separately, for example from the state's backup insurer for wind.

- On the ocean side
Most of the City of Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach and Garden City.

- West of the law's line
Carolina Forest, Socastee and Conway are west of it. The state has at times let its wind insurer write policies there too, so we check the address.

- On both sides
North Myrtle Beach and Little River. It depends on the street. Murrells Inlet straddles the Horry and Georgetown county line. On the Georgetown side, the law draws its own line near U.S. 17.

The $2,000 includes those wind policies. About 1 in 10 house owners here pay $4,000 or more a year for all their home insurance, and about 1 in 40 pay $6,000 or more. The Census figures do not split by side of the highway. Our coastal insurance guide explains each policy.
If you buy with us, we get you an insurance quote for the address before you make an offer, so wind and flood are in your budget before you commit.

### Do I need flood insurance in Myrtle Beach?
You must have it if the home is in the high-risk flood zone and your loan is from a bank or other lender the federal government regulates. Anywhere else it is your choice, but since 2015, 3 in 10 paid flood claims in Horry County were on buildings outside that zone. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps the zone.
About 1 in 15 houses resold in Horry County were in the zone, and about 1 in 4 condos.
A FEMA flood policy on a house, the typical cost a year:
$550 your home, outside the high-risk zone
$1,070 your home, inside the zone
$1,370 a second home, inside the zone

A FEMA flood policy on a condo unit its owner lives in, outside the high-risk zone, costs about $375 a year. Flood is not in the yearly total above; you can add it in the calculator below. Our page on homes that have flooded shows how we learn a house's flood history.

## How much should I budget for upkeep?
About $3,270 a year for a house: about $1,470 of routine repairs and about $1,800 put toward the big replacements. A condo owner spends about $690 a year on upkeep; the building's upkeep is paid from the condo fee.
Most years cost far less than the average, and some years cost much more. Half of house owners spend about $520 or less on routine repairs in a year, and about 1 in 6 spend nothing. The average is high because of the big jobs:

- A new roof $10,400
About 1 in 9 owners replaced one in two years.

- Central air conditioning $7,000
About 1 in 11 owners replaced it in two years.

- Heating equipment $5,000
The furnace or heat pump.

- A water heater $1,000

Budgeting 1 percent of the value a year is a little high: on the typical house it gives $3,500.

## What are electric and water bills like in Myrtle Beach?
Electricity costs less here than in the rest of South Carolina, and water is a small bill. These are typical bills for owners:
$150 a month for electricity on a house here
$190 a month in the rest of South Carolina
$480 a year for water and sewer on a house
$90 a month for electricity in a condo

One household's bills: on one of our team's own houses, about 1,400 square feet on two floors, summer electricity is about $130 a month and water about $50.

## Cost to own FAQ

### What is PITI, and what is not in it?
PITI stands for principal, interest, taxes and insurance. It is the loan payment plus the property tax and home insurance, which the lender usually collects with it, and mortgage insurance if the loan needs it. An HOA or condo fee is usually paid separately. Upkeep and utilities are not in it.

### Will my property tax be the same as the seller's?
Not always. After a sale, the county values the home again, and the new value is first taxed the year after the sale. Do not budget from the seller's tax bill.

### Does the cost change if I rent the home out?
Yes. A rental is taxed like a second home, on 6 percent of its value. The second-home section above shows the tax by town.

### Is Myrtle Beach expensive to own a home in?
A little more than the rest of South Carolina. Owners of a paid-off house here pay about $50 a month more for tax, insurance, utilities and any HOA fee together.

# Waterfront homes in Myrtle Beach: from the ocean to the lake, what each one costs.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
From the sun coming up out of the ocean to a boat at your own dock, seven kinds of water, each with its own price.

The short answer
In the past year, a house on the beach sold for about $2.2 million at the middle, and one on the Intracoastal Waterway for about $1.3 million.
A condo in an oceanfront building sold for about $200,000, and every waterfront house for sale under $300,000 is on a lake or pond.

## What does a waterfront home cost in Myrtle Beach?
The kind of water makes the biggest difference to the price. A house on the beach sold for about six times the middle house in Horry County. A house on the Waccamaw River sold for less than half of what one on the waterway did.
On the beach, a house sold for the most and a condo for the least Kind of home and water Middle sale price

A house on the beach $2.2 million

A house on the salt marsh, Garden City $1.24 million
A house on the Cherry Grove channels $715,000
A house on the Waccamaw River $537,000
Any house in Horry County $375,000
A condo in an oceanfront building $200,000

The middle sale price in the past year, from Horry County deed records. The gray bar is every house in the county, for comparison.
Lake houses have no bar, because the deeds do not show reliably which houses sit on a lake. On the day we counted, the 429 lake and pond houses for sale asked about $450,000 at the middle.

## Which kind of waterfront home fits you?
Waterfront here means seven different purchases. Pick what you want from the water, and go to its entry.

- The sun coming up out of the ocean, from your own porch: Oceanfront houses

- The same sunrise from a balcony, for far less: A condo in an oceanfront building

- A boat at your own dock that can travel north or south behind the coast: The Intracoastal Waterway

- Crabbing off your own dock on the tide: The salt marsh and tidal creeks

- A boat out back, with a city boat ramp and an inlet to the ocean: The Cherry Grove channels

- Cypress, dark river water and a wildlife refuge: The Waccamaw River

- A pontoon boat on a lake, for less: A lake or pond

### Oceanfront houses: the sun comes up out of the ocean
From central Myrtle Beach south to Garden City, the beach faces the southeast. The sun rises over open sea there on every morning of the year.
Farther north the shore curves. From Windy Hill to Cherry Grove, the sun comes up over the North Myrtle Beach shore on about 100 to 125 mornings around June.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Houses on wide lawns behind the dunes, facing the beach in Myrtle Beach, with wooden walkways down to the sand.
An oceanfront house has no other house between its lot and the beach. More than 400 houses in Horry County stand in the first row like this.
In the past year, at least 20 of them resold, and the middle price was about $2.2 million. Other houses within about two-thirds of a mile, off the water, resold for about $615,000. Want the sand a walk away instead? Our guide to houses near the beach counts them by distance, and our guide to homes with a pool shows where the pools are.
On the day we counted, the houses for sale listed as on the ocean asked about $3.4 million at the middle. About 6 in 10 first-row lots reach FEMA's VE zone, where waves are expected. To check one address, use our guide to checking a flood zone .

Book a showing on the oceanfront

### A condo in an oceanfront building: the same sunrise for less
A condo in a building on the beach gives you the same sunrise from a balcony, with the sand right below. It costs far less than a house on the beach.
Photo: DiscoA340
Oceanfront condo towers along the beach in Myrtle Beach.
More than 600 condos in oceanfront buildings resold in the past year, for about $200,000 at the middle.
On the day we counted, about 1,100 condos were for sale in oceanfront buildings, and about 2 in 3 asked under $300,000.
Not every unit in an oceanfront building faces the ocean. Of those condos for sale, about 700 list a unit that faces it.
Each building has its own monthly fee and its own rules on renting. We compare the HOA fees of the oceanfront buildings for you, and if you plan to rent, the numbers on an oceanfront condo .

Get the condos that face the ocean

### Intracoastal Waterway homes: your boat at your own dock
From a dock on the Intracoastal Waterway here, your boat can head north to Norfolk, Virginia, or south to Florida without going out on the ocean. Our guide to Plantation Point covers one Myrtle Beach neighborhood by the waterway.
The waterway runs behind the Atlantic coast. When you want the ocean, the way out is Little River Inlet, at the North Carolina line.
Our clients from New York bought beachfront in North Myrtle Beach near the waterway, so they could use their boat.
U.S. government aerial photo
The Intracoastal Waterway at Little River from above, with boats at the docks at the end of Mineola Avenue and in the slip basin at Mariner's Pointe.
Flooding is lighter here than on the beach, the channels or the river. About 3 in 10 waterway house lots are wholly outside FEMA's high-risk flood zone.
About 985 houses in Horry County have a lot that touches the waterway. In the past year, 55 houses on it sold for about $1.3 million at the middle, about twice the houses nearby, in every stretch.

Book a showing on the waterway

### Marsh front homes: crabs off your own dock
On salt water in South Carolina, you need no fishing license to go crabbing with three or fewer drop nets, fold-up traps or hand lines with bait. People call it chicken necking, and a dock on the marsh is a place to do it.
The marsh fills and drains with the tide twice a day. In Murrells Inlet's creeks, the water at a dock drops about 4 feet from high tide to low.
At low tide, a dock on a small creek may sit on mud. The width of the creek also limits the size of the dock the state allows. We check the depth at the dock at low tide, not at the showing.
U.S. government aerial photo
The salt marsh behind Garden City Beach from above, with private docks running out from the houses on both edges.
In Garden City , about 260 houses are on the salt marsh or a tidal creek. The 13 that sold in the past year went for about $1.24 million at the middle, about twice the other houses on that side of the beach road.
In Murrells Inlet , about 220 houses are on the salt marsh, almost all on the creek side of US 17 Business. Over three years, 21 of them sold for about $930,000 at the middle.

Have us check the depth at a marsh dock

### Cherry Grove channel homes: a boat out the back door
In Cherry Grove, in North Myrtle Beach , rows of houses line channels dug through the marsh behind the beach. Many have a dock behind the house.
Cherry Grove has the city's boat ramp on the marsh, with boat access to the marsh and the ocean through Hog Inlet. Inside Cherry Grove, the water moves about 4.5 feet between high and low tide.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
Houses on the Cherry Grove channels from above, many with a dock behind them, and the marsh and the city's boat ramp beyond.
The trade-off is flooding. Of about 680 houses on the channels and the marsh edge, all but 3 are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone.
A house on the channels resold for about $715,000 at the middle in the past year. A Cherry Grove house off the channels sold for about $665,000, a group that includes oceanfront houses.

Get the Cherry Grove channel homes for sale

### Waccamaw River homes: dark water, cypress and a wildlife refuge
The Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge, set up in 1997, protects tidal freshwater wetlands and old rice fields along the Waccamaw and Great Pee Dee rivers.
The Fish and Wildlife Service calls them some of the most diverse freshwater wetlands in North America. Visitors paddle a blackwater swamp, walk among cypress trees and look for swallow-tailed kites and more than 200 other bird species.
U.S. government aerial photo
The dark water of the Waccamaw River at Wacca Wache Landing, with a marina basin beside it, on the Georgetown County side.
Even at Conway , the tide still raises and lowers the river about a foot. Nearly every river lot reaches the high-risk flood zone: all but 4 of about 460.
In the past year, 14 houses on the river sold for about $537,000 at the middle, against about $330,000 for houses nearby that are not on the water.

Get the homes on the Waccamaw River

### Lakefront homes: a pontoon boat out back
In Plantation Lakes in Carolina Forest, owners take pontoon boats out on a lake with about 15 miles of shoreline. Many homes back onto the lake.
The owners' amenity area has day and overnight docks and a boat ramp. Boats on the lake are limited to 19 feet, with small motors.
U.S. government aerial photo
Plantation Lakes from above: houses along the lake, and the boat docks at the owners’ amenity area.
On the day we counted, 9 houses on the lake there were for sale, asking about $780,000 to $1.3 million.
Most lake and pond houses for sale ask far less. Every waterfront house for sale under $300,000 was on a lake or pond.
The state's coastal dock permit covers salt water and the marsh, not a lake. On a lake, we read the community's rules on docks and boats before you offer.

Get the lakefront homes under $500,000

## Can you build a dock on your waterfront lot?
On salt water, you can if the lot and the creek are wide enough and the state issues a permit. Only 52 of the 506 waterfront houses for sale list a dock. On canals, creeks, the marsh, rivers and the waterway, more than half do.
A dock over the tidal marsh or a saltwater creek needs a permit from the state's coastal permit office, SCDES, before it is built. That office used to be part of DHEC.
The permit covers tidal salt water, the marsh and other land the average high tide covers, and the beach. Docks on lakes and fresh water fall under other rules.

### Is the lot wide enough?
On a lot created after May 23, 1993, a private dock needs at least 75 feet of frontage at the marsh edge. On such a lot, under 50 feet means no dock of its own. Two neighbors with at least 50 feet each can share one.
A waterfront subdivision may have a dock master plan, recorded with its map of lots, that shows which lots may get a dock and where. A plan is a guide, not a promise of a permit. To see a lot's width and lines, use our Horry County GIS map guide .

### How big can the dock be?
Under the state rule in force now, a dock on a tidal creek is sized by the creek's width, from marsh grass to marsh grass.
Creek width Dock the state usually allows
Under 10 feet No dock
10 to 19 feet No dock, except 50 square feet with no boat lift on a lot with over 500 feet of frontage, or where no dock is possible from the other side
20 to 50 feet 120 square feet
51 to 150 feet 160 square feet
Over 150 feet 600 square feet

Walkways, ramps and mooring piles do not count, and neither does a lift 8 by 20 feet or smaller. The table is not for docks on the waterway itself. The state has proposed new widths and sizes, and they need the legislature's approval.

### What about the fee, the wait, repairs and selling?

- The fee. The state charges $150 to apply for a private dock with a walkway 100 feet or shorter, and $250 for a longer one.

- The wait. Once the file is complete, the state posts a 15-day public notice. By law, the state has 30 days from the complete file to decide.

- Repairs. Normal repair of a standing dock, kept to its old size, needs only a request and a letter back from the state.

- Storms. A dock a storm destroys can be rebuilt to its old layout if the work is done within five years.

- Selling. An active permit can be transferred to the buyer for $25. Both owners sign.

- Other approvals. The owner may also need the Army Corps of Engineers, the city or county, and the HOA to approve.

If you would rather not ask an HOA about a dock or a boat, 86 waterfront houses for sale listed no HOA fee on the day we counted.
Buying a house for its dock?
We find the dock's permit, make sure it is active and can transfer to you, and read the subdivision's dock master plan before you offer.

## Do you need flood insurance on a waterfront home?
A federally regulated lender requires flood insurance on a waterfront home in FEMA's high-risk zone. How many lots are in that zone depends on the water.
Water Lots that reach the high-risk flood zone
Cherry Grove channels Over 99%
Waccamaw River About 99%
Oceanfront houses About 98%
Oceanfront houses, in the zone where waves are expected (VE) About 60%
Intracoastal Waterway About 70%

For one-family houses with a FEMA policy in Horry County, the middle yearly cost was:
Where the house is Middle cost a year
Outside the high-risk zone, a home you live in About $550
Zone A or AE, a home you live in About $1,070
Zone A or AE, a home you do not live in About $1,370
Zone V, where waves are expected About $3,200

The zone of the lot is not always the zone of the house. FEMA and the lender go by where the house stands and by a survey of how high its floor is. We get both for the house you like.
We also look for past flooding at the house, in the records listed in how to find out if a house flooded . Wind and homeowners insurance are in coastal home insurance .

## Can you get from your dock to the ocean by boat?
Yes, from the waterway, the channels and the ocean-side creeks. From the waterway between Little River and Socastee, a marked channel about 2 miles long leads to the jetties of Little River Inlet.
The sandbar at the inlet's mouth shifts, and its buoys are moved often. Murrells Inlet opens straight to the ocean between its own jetties, and boaters new to it are advised to enter with local knowledge.

### Which bridges does your boat pass under?
Thirteen crossings span the waterway in about 30 waterway miles from the state line to Socastee. Every fixed bridge has a reported clearance of 65 feet, so a boat under 65 feet tall passes each one.
A boat taller than a swing bridge or the railroad bridge when it is closed waits for it to open.
Crossing, north to south Room under it
US 17 bridge, Little River 65 feet, as reported
Little River swing bridge 7 feet closed; it opens
Robert Edge Parkway bridge 65 feet, as reported
Barefoot Landing swing bridge 31 feet closed; it opens
SC 22 bridge 65 feet, as reported
Cable car, about a mile south of SC 22 67 feet
Grande Dunes Boulevard bridge 65 feet, as reported
Grissom Parkway bridge 65 feet, as reported
Railroad bridge, next to US 501 16 feet closed; it opens
US 501 bridge 65 feet, as reported
Fantasy Harbour bridge 65 feet, as reported
Socastee swing bridge 11 feet closed; it opens
Highway bridge at Socastee 65 feet, as reported

Under the federal rule, the Little River swing bridge opens on signal, except from 7 to 9 a.m. and 4 to 6 p.m. on weekdays that are not federal holidays. Then it opens only on the hour and the half hour.
The Barefoot Landing and Socastee swing bridges have no special schedule in the federal rules, so they open when a boat signals.
U.S. government aerial photo, 2023
The old Socastee swing bridge, the blue steel span, on the Intracoastal Waterway, with the newer high bridge at the lower left.
The federal channel is designed for at least 12 feet of depth. The federal chart guide still warns of rock ledges along its edges from about Little River to US 501.

On the ocean side, a lot that floats a boat at high tide may sit on mud at low tide.

### Can you keep a boat without a dock?
Yes. A deeded boat slip is another way to keep a boat on the water. Horry County has 322 slips sold as real estate, 223 of them in Little River .
In the past year, slips at Mariner's Pointe there sold for about $16,500 at the middle.

## Oceanfront or ocean view: what does waterfront mean in a listing?
Oceanfront means the first row, with no house between the lot and the beach. A house with an ocean view can be across the street or a few rows back.
A listing that names a water is often near it, not on it. Of 117 houses for sale whose listing names the Intracoastal Waterway, only 22 are marked as waterfront.
Every house that names a lake or a canal is marked as waterfront. Before you pay for water, we check the lot line, the deed and the flood map.

Common questions

## Waterfront home FAQ

### Does the sun rise over the ocean in Myrtle Beach?
Yes. From central Myrtle Beach south to Garden City, the sun rises over open sea every morning of the year. Farther north, from Windy Hill to Cherry Grove, it comes up over the shore on many mornings around June.

### What is the cheapest waterfront in Myrtle Beach?
A condo in an oceanfront building, which sold for about $200,000 at the middle. For a house, it is a lake or pond: every waterfront house for sale under $300,000 was on one.

### How much more does a waterfront home cost?
On the beach, a house resold for about $2.2 million at the middle, against about $615,000 for houses nearby off the water. On the Intracoastal Waterway, a house sold for about twice the houses nearby. On Garden City's salt marsh, a house sold for about twice the other houses on that side of the beach road.

### Can I build a dock on my waterfront lot?
On salt water, yes, if the lot and the creek are wide enough and the state issues a permit. Lots created since 1993 need 75 feet of frontage at the marsh edge.

### Can I keep a boat without a dock?
Yes. A deeded boat slip is another way, and most of the slips sold as real estate in Horry County are in Little River.

### Do I need flood insurance on a waterfront home?
A federally regulated lender requires it in FEMA's high-risk zone. Nearly every lot on the beach, the Cherry Grove channels and the Waccamaw River reaches that zone. On the Intracoastal Waterway, about 3 in 10 lots are wholly outside it.

## Myrtle Beach Short-Term Rental Rules: Where Airbnb Is Legal
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-rules/
Summary: Myrtle Beach bans short-term rentals in nearly all residential areas; North Myrtle Beach allows them with a license. Every town's rules and the 11-13% tax.

Home / Invest / STR Rules
Short-term rental regulations

# Myrtle Beach short-term rental rules: where Airbnb is legal, city by city.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
The City of Myrtle Beach bans short-term rentals in nearly all residential districts. North Myrtle Beach allows them citywide with a license. Unincorporated Horry County has no short-term rental ordinance.
Have us check an address's STR status

The direct answer

## Where short-term rentals are legal on the Grand Strand
The Grand Strand looks like one beach town. Legally it is seven jurisdictions: two cities, two towns, and two counties' unincorporated areas, each with its own short-term rental rules. Move the same house half a mile into the next jurisdiction and it can go from allowed to prohibited.
The one-paragraph map: the City of Myrtle Beach is the strictest, banning STRs in nearly all residential districts. North Myrtle Beach allows them citywide with a license, and is the market watching new rules most closely. Surfside Beach confines them to two districts. Unincorporated Horry County , which includes much of what people call Myrtle Beach, has no STR ordinance at all. Conway has no dedicated STR ordinance either. Pawleys Island allows vacation rentals everywhere and does not even require a business license. In every one of them, an HOA can still say no.
South Carolina taxes stays under 90 days; rent to one person for 90 or more continuous days and the stay is not taxed as lodging. A state bill to stop cities from banning them, H. 3861 , was introduced in January 2025. It never left the House committee. Details per jurisdiction below, then the tax table.

Jurisdiction by jurisdiction

## Short-term rental rules by city

### Myrtle Beach short-term rental rules: legal in resort zones, banned in residential neighborhoods
The city defines short-term as under 90 days and prohibits STRs in every residential "R" district except RMV, with fewer than 30 grandfathered houses citywide. They operate legally in the commercial and resort districts along the oceanside corridor east of Kings Highway, which is where the city's condo and condotel inventory lives. Violations are misdemeanors at up to $500 a day. Every rental needs a city business license. In December 2024 the city went further and created a conversion overlay east of Kings Highway from 29th Avenue South to 82nd Avenue North. Units that have operated commercially as short-term rentals there generally cannot convert to long-term leases. The city wants that stock to stay short-term, citing $7.6 million in lost revenue per 1,000 converted rooms. Area prices and rental data: our Myrtle Beach investing guide .

### North Myrtle Beach short-term rental rules: allowed citywide, new ordinance pending
STRs are allowed in any district that permits residential use, roughly 5,400 of them licensed, each needing an annual city business license. No special permit beyond that today. Watch this one: since 2024 the city has been workshopping a "responsible local agent" ordinance, an annual permit with inspection, a public registry, and a 24/7 local contact able to reach the property within an hour. City Council has not adopted it. The city did pass a nuisance party ordinance in February 2026 aimed squarely at out-of-control rentals, and a June 2026 incident renewed the pressure. If you are buying an STR in North Myrtle Beach, buy assuming a local-agent requirement is coming. Area prices and rental data: our North Myrtle Beach investing guide . The city code is on Municode .

### Surfside Beach short-term rental rules: two zoning districts only
Rentals under 30 days are permitted only in the R3 and C3 zoning districts and prohibited in the R1 and R2 single-family districts. Every rental is a business in the town's eyes: the STR license runs $90 minimum plus $2.27 per $1,000 of gross income, and the minimums double for non-resident owners. Unpaid license tax becomes a lien on the property. The regime has been stable for years; the common mistake is assuming a Surfside address allows what the neighboring unincorporated Garden City street allows. Area prices and rental data: our Surfside Beach investing guide .

### Unincorporated Horry County short-term rentals: no county ordinance, the HOA decides
Carolina Forest, Socastee, Little River, the north sides of Garden City and Murrells Inlet, Longs: no county STR permit, no STR zoning restrictions, no occupancy caps. What the county does expect: a county business license, a state retail license for the taxes, a county hospitality account, and a personal property return on your furnishings every April. The binding restriction out here is the HOA covenant, which can prohibit or restrict short-term rentals even though the county does not. That document gets read before you offer, not after. The biggest unincorporated rental pockets are Garden City and Little River .

### Conway short-term rental rules: no dedicated ordinance
Conway has never adopted a short-term rental ordinance and has actively encouraged STR projects downtown. You need a city business license, and the district's zoning has to permit transient lodging, which we confirm with city planning parcel by parcel. Conway is a long-term rental market. Our Conway guide covers why the investment case here is tenants, not tourists.

### Pawleys Island and Georgetown County short-term rentals: no regulation
Vacation rentals are the Town of Pawleys Island's main economy, and it is the only coastal town here with no business license at all, and unincorporated Georgetown County requires none either. Its 3 percent accommodations tax pays for beach renourishment. Unincorporated Georgetown County, which includes Litchfield and the south side of Murrells Inlet, treats short-term and long-term rentals as the same residential use and has chosen not to regulate them. The one exception: accessory dwelling units cannot be rented for less than 90 days. Neither is on Airbnb's automatic tax collection list, so owners remit the local 3 percent themselves. Area prices and rental data: our Pawleys Island investing guide .

The taxes

## Short-term rental taxes by jurisdiction, mid-2026
Every short-term stay carries South Carolina's 5 percent sales tax and 2 percent accommodations tax, plus county and city add-ons that differ by line on the map. What guests pay in total: State accommodations tax rules: SC Department of Revenue .
Jurisdiction Total lodging tax
City of Myrtle Beach (includes its 1% tourism fee) 13%
North Myrtle Beach 12%
Surfside Beach 12%
Unincorporated Horry County 12%
Conway 12%
Town of Pawleys Island 11%
Unincorporated Georgetown County 11%

Airbnb automatically collects the state-administered taxes and several local ones, including Horry County's hospitality fee and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, and Surfside city taxes. It collects nothing for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County. Most owners still owe at least one direct monthly filing, due the 20th. Guests do not pay these taxes on stays of 90 days or more. The full rate and license picture is on our accommodations tax page . Renting your own legal residence more than 72 days a year also costs you the 4 percent property tax rate; the full property tax math is on our Horry County property taxes page.

Before you buy

## Our pre-offer short-term rental checklist

- 1. Confirm the jurisdiction and the zoning district , parcel by parcel, not by mailing address. "Myrtle Beach" on the envelope often means unincorporated Horry County on the map, and the rules above flip accordingly.

- 2. Read the HOA covenants and master deed for rental minimums, rental caps, or required rental programs. The HOA's rules override the city's permission everywhere.

- 3. Price the licenses and tax filings : local business license, state retail license, county hospitality account, and the furnishings return in Horry County.

- 4. Insure it as a short-term rental , not a home. Coverage and flood pricing both change with rental use; the details are on our coastal insurance page.

- 5. Run the revenue honestly. Whether the numbers work as a short-term rental at all, versus a long-term lease, is its own analysis: STR vs LTR , our STR data tools , and the Grand Investor Tool do that math.

Common questions

## Grand Strand short-term rental FAQ

### Are Airbnbs legal in Myrtle Beach?
Depends which Myrtle Beach. Inside the city, short-term rentals are prohibited in every residential zoning district except one (RMV), with fewer than 30 grandfathered houses; they operate legally in the commercial and resort districts along the oceanside corridor. Most of what people call Myrtle Beach is unincorporated Horry County, where there is no county STR ordinance at all and the HOA is usually the only restriction. The parcel's jurisdiction is the first thing we check.

### Do I need a license to run a short-term rental on the Grand Strand?
In every jurisdiction except the Town of Pawleys Island, yes: a local business license (city or county), plus a South Carolina retail license from the Department of Revenue to remit accommodations taxes. Surfside Beach doubles its license rates for non-resident owners. Horry County also expects a personal property return on your furnishings each April.

### What taxes does a short-term rental collect in Myrtle Beach?
Total lodging tax runs 11 to 13 percent depending on jurisdiction. City of Myrtle Beach is highest at 13 percent, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Conway, and unincorporated Horry County are 12, and Pawleys Island and unincorporated Georgetown County are 11. The tax applies to stays under 90 days; rentals of 90 or more continuous days to the same person are exempt.

### Does Airbnb collect the taxes for me?
Only some of them. Airbnb automatically collects the state-administered taxes and several local ones, including Horry County's hospitality fee and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, and Surfside city taxes. It does not collect for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County, and platform coverage differs by tax line, so most owners still owe at least one direct filing. We map the exact filings for the specific address before you buy.

### Can an HOA ban short-term rentals even where the city allows them?
Yes. Covenants and master deeds override what zoning permits, and in unincorporated Horry County, where the county imposes no STR rules, the HOA document is usually the only thing that decides the question. Reading it is part of the building and neighborhood review we run before any offer.

## Myrtle Beach Accommodations Tax & Business License | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/accommodations-tax/
Summary: Which Grand Strand rentals owe accommodations tax, what the state and your county charge, what Airbnb pays for you, and the business license every rental needs.

Home / Invest / Accommodations tax
What a rental owes, by county

# Accommodations tax and business licenses, county by county.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Short-term rentals in Horry and Georgetown County owe accommodations tax that long-term rentals do not. This page lists what counts as short-term, what you owe, and who collects it.
Have us check my address

The short answer
Accommodations tax is a tax on rent from short stays. A short stay is under 90 days in Horry County and under 30 days in Georgetown County. A lease of 90 days or more owes none of it. The guest pays the tax. Whoever takes the payment collects it and sends it in. Every rental also needs a business license, short-term or long-term, priced on gross rent.
South Carolina charges 7 percent. With local sales taxes the state collects, it is 9 percent in most of Horry County and 10 percent in Myrtle Beach. With county and city fees, a stay pays 13 percent in Myrtle Beach and 12 percent in North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach and unincorporated Horry County.

## Which rentals owe accommodations tax?
Only rentals with short stays. The tax is charged on the rent for each stay that is shorter than the county limit. The limit is 90 days in Horry County and 30 days in Georgetown County.
Where A stay owes the tax if it is
South Carolina, state tax Under 90 days
Horry County hospitality fee Under 90 days
Conway Under 90 days
Georgetown County Under 30 days

A long-term lease owes none of these taxes. A vacation rental owes all of them. A furnished rental with monthly tenants owes them in Georgetown County only if the stay is under 30 days.
The guest pays the tax. It is added to the bill. You, or the platform that takes the payment, collect it and send it to the state, the county, or the city. Each has its own office.

## What does South Carolina charge?
The state charges 7 percent on the rent from every short stay. That is 5 percent sales tax plus 2 percent accommodations tax. The sales tax rate on rent is 5 percent, not the 6 percent charged in stores.
The state revenue department also collects the county's local sales taxes on rent. In Horry County those are 1 percent for school construction and 1 percent for transportation projects, so the department collects 9 percent. Myrtle Beach adds a 1 percent tourism development tax, for 10 percent. In Georgetown County the extra is 1 percent, for 8 percent.
What Rate
Sales tax on accommodations 5%
State accommodations tax 2%
State total 7%
Horry County local sales taxes, collected by the state 2%
Myrtle Beach tourism development tax, collected by the state 1% more
Highest local add-on allowed 3%

There is one exemption, set by the state revenue department . It applies if you live in the property, it has six bedrooms or fewer, and you do not use Airbnb, VRBO or a rental agency. Almost every investor uses a platform, so almost no investor qualifies.

## What does your county or city add?
What taxes you owe and how much they add up to depends on your county. Below is a chart of the taxes for each area for short-term rentals.
Where the property is Local tax on rent How often you pay
Unincorporated Horry County 3% hospitality fee Monthly, by the 20th
City of Myrtle Beach 1.5% county hospitality fee, plus the city's 1% hospitality fee and 0.5% local accommodations tax County fee monthly, by the 20th. The city's two go to the city, by the 20th after each filing period.
North Myrtle Beach 1.5% county hospitality fee, plus the city's 1.5% hospitality fee County fee monthly, by the 20th. The city's goes to the city, by the 20th after each filing period.
Surfside Beach 1.5% county hospitality fee, plus the town's 1% hospitality fee and 0.5% local accommodations tax County fee monthly, by the 20th. The town's two go to the town, by the 20th after each filing period.
Inside another Horry County city 1.5% hospitality fee Monthly, by the 20th
Conway 1% hospitality fee Monthly if over $50 a month
Georgetown County 3% accommodations tax Monthly, quarterly or yearly, by size

On a $1,000 booking, the guest pays $130 in state and local tax in Myrtle Beach. In North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach and unincorporated Horry County, the guest pays $120.
Horry County publishes its rates on its treasurer page . Myrtle Beach , North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach publish theirs on their own pages. Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and the county fee stop at 90 days, the same as the state.
Georgetown County publishes its rate on its finance page . Georgetown County also has a 2 percent hospitality tax. That one is on food and drink, not on rent. Do not add it to your rent estimate.
Georgetown County lets small owners file less often. If you collect under $25 a month in tax, you file once a year.

## When does a stay stop being taxable?
At 90 days in Horry County and at 30 days in Georgetown County. That single difference is the most common mistake we see people make when they are investing from out of state because they mix up the counties.
An example. A guest books 45 nights in a Murrells Inlet condo in Georgetown County. The stay is over 30 days, so the county tax stops. The stay is under 90 days, so the 7 percent state tax still applies. The same booking in Surfside Beach is under both limits and owes everything.
This page is about the tax on rent. A different rule decides how your rental income is taxed. That rule also uses the length of stays, but it uses a seven-day average. If you rent by the night, read our short-term rental tax treatment page next. It tells you whether your rental losses can reduce the tax on your other income.
Your own stays in the unit are a third count. That one is on our 14-day rule page . Our seasonal worker page covers long leases that owe none of the tax on this page.
Want to talk out your strategy with a local investment expert?
Our specialized investment agents can help you buy in the correct county so that you avoid extra taxes.
Talk to a local investor specialist

## What taxes does Airbnb pay for you?
A booking platform collects some of this but not all of it. The rest is your obligation.
If Airbnb or VRBO take the payment, they are responsible for the taxes on that booking. If you take the payment, you are responsible for the taxes. That is the rule set by the state revenue department .
Airbnb sends in the state taxes, the Horry County hospitality fee, and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside city taxes. It sends in nothing for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County. Direct bookings, repeat guests who pay you outside the platform, and second listing sites are yours to file.
If a property manager takes your bookings, get it in writing that they send in the tax. Ask which offices they send it to. The property owes the tax even when someone else collected the money.

## Do you need a business license?
Yes. Every rental needs one, short-term or long-term. The fee is based on gross rent, not on profit. An owner who lost money for the year still owes it. Myrtle Beach requires one of all owners of rental property. Surfside treats every real estate rental as a business.
Where Rental needs a license Year ends Late penalty
City of Myrtle Beach Yes April 30 5% per month or part month
North Myrtle Beach Yes April 30 5%, rising 5% each month
Surfside Beach Yes April 30 5% per month from June 1
Unincorporated Horry County Yes, county license Differs, ask the county Differs, ask the county
Town of Pawleys Island No town or county license n/a n/a
Unincorporated Georgetown County No license. A yearly furniture tax return instead n/a n/a

Georgetown County does not require a business license in its unincorporated areas or in Pawleys Island. Rentals there file a different form each year, below.
Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach publish their renewal dates and penalties. Horry County publishes the county requirement for anyone outside city limits. North Myrtle Beach mails renewals in mid-March.
Georgetown County has a yearly furniture tax instead. If you rent a furnished home there, you file a personal property return with the state each year and pay a small tax on the furniture. It is a tax on the contents, not on the building. Georgetown County says so on its own page. The form goes to the state, so ask your CPA whether a Horry County unit owes it too.

Four things. All four can be checked before you write an offer. We check them for you.
Check this Why
Which county and city the parcel is in The city boundary does not follow the mailing address. It sets which office you file with.
Whether the building allows short stays Some buildings and HOAs ban them. See our short-term rental rules page .
What the license will cost It is priced on gross rent. Put it in your numbers before you offer.
Whether your stays are above or below the county limit 90 days in Horry County. 30 days in Georgetown County.

Two other taxes are separate from this page. Renting your own legal residence more than a set number of days a year costs you the 4 percent property tax rate. The count is on our Horry County property taxes page . Depreciation is on our cost segregation page .

Common questions

## Grand Strand accommodations tax FAQ

### Does a long-term rental owe accommodations tax?
No. A lease of 90 days or more owes no accommodations tax and no hospitality fee. In Georgetown County the county tax stops at 30 days. A long-term rental still needs a business license.

### Does Airbnb pay the accommodations tax for me?
Partly. Airbnb sends in the state taxes, the Horry County hospitality fee, and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside city taxes. It sends in nothing for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County. Bookings you take directly are yours to file.

### How long does a guest have to stay before the tax stops?
90 continuous days for the state tax, the Horry County hospitality fee and Conway. 30 continuous days in Georgetown County.

### What happens if I miss the business license renewal?
Myrtle Beach charges 5 percent of the license fee for each month or part of a month. North Myrtle Beach starts at 5 percent and adds 5 percent every month after.

### Is the license fee based on my profit?
No. It is based on gross rent. An owner who lost money for the year still owes it.

## Can Airbnb Losses Offset W-2 Income? Myrtle Beach | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-tax-treatment/
Summary: Rental losses normally cannot reduce the tax on a W-2 salary. A short-term rental you run yourself is the exception. The two tests, and why rental pools fail one.

Home / Invest / Rental losses and W-2 income
Passive and active income

# Can rental losses reduce the tax on your W-2 income?
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
For most rentals, no. For a short-term rental you run yourself, the losses can offset your salary. Two tests apply. A Myrtle Beach rental pool usually fails the second.
Book a consultation call

The short answer
Your job pays active income. A rental pays passive income. That is the default label for tax. A loss on a passive activity can only reduce passive income. It cannot reduce the tax on a W-2 salary. There is one exception for short-term rentals. If the average guest stays seven days or less, and you do the work yourself, the rental is treated as a business. Then its losses can reduce the tax on your salary. This page explains both tests and the records to keep.

## What is the difference between active and passive income?
Active income is money you work for. Wages, a salary, and a business you run yourself are active. Passive income is money from something you own but do not work in. Rent is passive by default, even if you own the property outright.
The label matters when there is a loss. A rental often shows a tax loss after depreciation, even when it makes money. A passive loss can only reduce passive income. If you have no other passive income, the loss waits. It carries forward each year and offsets passive income in later years. Any rest is released at a taxable sale.
Long-term rentals have one allowance. If you take part in the management decisions, up to $25,000 of loss can reduce your other income. That allowance starts to shrink once your income passes $100,000, and it is gone at $150,000. The details are in the passive activity rules . Short-term rentals do not use that allowance. They use the two tests below.

## Who does this matter for?
You have a W-2 job. You own a rental, or you are buying one. The rental shows a tax loss after depreciation. You want that loss to lower the tax on your salary. This page is for you.
If that is not your goal, none of the tests below matter. You can hire out everything, put the unit in a rental pool, and never count an hour. The loss stays passive and carries forward. Many owners here do exactly that.

## What is the seven-day rule?
The seven-day rule is one of two tests. If the average guest stay across the year is seven days or less, the property is not a rental activity for tax purposes. It is treated as a business, the same way a hotel is. A second route exists at 30 days or less if you provide daily services to guests, such as cleaning during the stay or meals.
The rule is written in the passive activity regulation . It is explained in the passive activity rules .
Passing this test removes the automatic passive label. It does not make the loss active on its own. The second test does that.
The average is across the whole year, not the shortest stay. A property with weekend guests and one two-month winter booking can average more than seven days.

## What is material participation?
Material participation is the other test. It asks whether you did enough of the work yourself. There are seven ways to pass. You need only one.
Test What it requires
1 More than 500 hours of work on the property in the year.
2 Your work was almost all the work done on the property, counting owners and non-owners.
3 More than 100 hours, and more than any other single person.
4 More than 100 hours here, and more than 500 hours across all such activities combined.
5 You passed one of these tests in 5 of the last 10 years.
6 A personal service business you passed in any 3 earlier years.
7 Regular, continuous and substantial work, judged on the facts. Fails at 100 hours or less.

All seven are quoted from the passive activity rules . Test 3 is the one most owners use. You need more than 100 hours in the year. You also need more hours than any other single person. If your cleaner worked 150 hours and you worked 120, you fail test 3.

## What counts as work, and what records do you need?
Any work you do on a property you own. Answering guests, meeting trades, buying furniture, managing the listing, setting prices, cleaning and repairs all count.
The record is simple. A calendar, an appointment book, or a written summary of your hours is enough. Daily logs are not required. Start the calendar on the day you close.

## What is a rental pool, and why does it matter here?
A rental pool is how a condotel works. The building has a front desk and rents the units like hotel rooms. Owners put their unit in the pool. The building takes the bookings, cleans the unit, and pays each owner a share of the rent. The owner does no work.
A building's own documents can require the pool. In that building you cannot opt out. Other buildings let you manage the unit yourself or hire your own manager.
For the tests above, the pool is the problem. Your hours are near zero. The building's staff hours are high. Test 3 fails, and so do tests 1 and 2. A unit in a mandatory pool cannot pass material participation.
If you do not need the loss against your salary, the pool is fine. The loss stays passive and carries forward to a sale.
Talk through a building before you offer.
We will tell you whether the rental pool is mandatory, and what that does to these two tests.
Book a consultation call

## What does Chapter3 know that a national site does not?
Does the building require the rental pool? Can you self-manage? Will a management company here let an owner do the turnovers? A national tax site cannot answer that for one building, and it is the main question for a Myrtle Beach condo.
We check it before you offer. The financing side of these buildings is on our condotel financing page . What management costs against doing it yourself is on our Myrtle Beach Airbnb income page . Whether a cost segregation study does anything in year one comes back to the same two tests. Your own nights in the unit are not guest stays. They have their own test on our 14-day rule page .

Common questions

## Rental losses and W-2 income FAQ

### Can I deduct Airbnb losses from my W-2 income?
For a long-term rental, up to $25,000 of loss can reduce your salary income if you take part in the management decisions. The full amount applies while your income is $100,000 or less. Above that it shrinks by 50 cents per dollar, and it is gone at $150,000. It does not apply to a short-term rental with average stays of seven days or less. There, the loss can reduce your salary only if you pass a material participation test.

### What is the seven-day rule?
If the average guest stay across the year is seven days or less, the property is not a rental activity for tax purposes. It is treated as a business. That removes the automatic passive label. You still need to pass a material participation test.

### Do I need to be a real estate professional?
No. That is a different rule with its own hour requirements. The seven-day route does not use it.

### Does a property manager rule me out?
It makes the tests harder. Several tests compare your hours with everyone else who worked on the property. If the manager worked more hours than you, test 3 fails. If you do not need the loss against your salary, a manager is fine.

### What records do I need?
A calendar, an appointment book, or a written summary of your hours. Daily logs are not required. Start on the day you close.
Sources: Publication 925, passive activity and at-risk rules , 26 CFR 1.469-1T . Read September 5, 2026. Educational only, not tax advice. Whether you pass these tests is a question for your CPA.
