## Myrtle Beach Condo Cost Segregation & Recapture | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/cost-segregation/
Summary: What a study reclassifies in a furnished beach condo, the 100 percent allowance, whether the passive rules let you use the loss, and what comes back at sale.

Home / Invest / Cost segregation
Cost segregation, explained

# How do you write off a Myrtle Beach condo faster than 27.5 years?
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
A cost segregation study moves carpet, appliances and furniture from 27.5-year depreciation to 5 years. Almost every condo for sale in a Horry County oceanfront building is listed furnished.
Talk to a specialized agent

The short answer
A cost segregation study is an engineering report on your rental. It lists every part of the purchase that is not the building: carpet, appliances, furniture, cabinets, light fixtures. It gives each part a value and a recovery period. The tax rules depreciate the building over 27.5 years, but carpet and appliances over 5 years. Without a study, the whole price is depreciated over 27.5 years. With one, the short-life parts are written off in 5 years, or in full in year one for property acquired after January 19, 2025. An engineer visits the unit, values each part, and writes the report your CPA files. Whether it helps depends on two things: can you use the loss this year, and what recapture costs at sale.

## What does a cost segregation study do?
It splits one purchase price into parts with different recovery periods. The building stays on the 27.5-year residential schedule. Everything the study can support as personal property or a land improvement moves to a shorter one.
Years to write off each part.
5 years
Carpet, appliances, furniture, window treatments

7 years
Office furniture and fixtures

15 years
Land improvements: paving, fencing, landscaping

27.5 years
The building itself

Land is never depreciated. Bar length is the recovery period in years.

Part Recovery period
The building 27.5 years
Carpet, appliances, furniture 5 years
Office furniture and fixtures 7 years
Land improvements such as paving and fencing 15 years
Land Never depreciated

The periods come from the depreciation rules . Land is never depreciated. A study changes when you take deductions. It does not create new ones. The total over the life of the property is the same either way.
The moved share qualifies for the special depreciation allowance. For property acquired after the date above, that allowance is 100 percent. A furnished unit bought this year can deduct its whole moved share in year one.
How the 27.5-year schedule is set up from the closing statement is on our rental depreciation page .

### What does an example look like?
The middle furnished condo for sale in an oceanfront building in Horry County asks about $210,000. Use that as the price. The county record shows no land value for almost every condo unit , so your CPA sets the land share. Say it is $21,000. That leaves $189,000 to depreciate. Without a study, all of it is written off over 27.5 years: about $6,900 a year.
Say the study finds $31,500 of furniture, appliances, carpet and fixtures. That $31,500 moves to the 5-year class. If the unit was acquired after January 19, 2025, the whole $31,500 can be deducted in year one. The remaining $157,500 stays on 27.5 years: about $5,700 a year.
Year one: about $37,200 with the study, $6,900 without. Every later year: $5,700 with, $6,900 without. Over the life of the property the total is the same. At sale, the $31,500 comes back as ordinary income, up to the gain. These are full-year figures. The first year is prorated by month. The land share and the study's finding here are examples, not local figures. The share a study finds varies by unit.

### How is a study done?

- Confirm what came with the unit. The purchase contract and the inventory list are the starting point.

- Hire a firm that does engineering-based studies. Ask for a site visit, photographs and an itemized valuation.

- Give the firm the closing statement, the inventory and any invoices for furniture or appliances.

- The engineer visits, lists every short-life part, values each one and assigns its class. The report goes to your CPA.

- Your CPA files it with the return. If you bought in an earlier year, the CPA files a change of method, and the missed depreciation is taken in one year.

## What gets reclassified in a furnished beach condo?
More than in an unfurnished house. A condotel or rental-pool unit is sold furnished. The furniture, appliances, carpet, window treatments and light fixtures are inside the purchase price. All of them are short-life property. The study documents what they are worth.
Two things are different in a condo. You own no site improvements directly, only a share of the common elements, so the 15-year class is mostly out of reach. That share also includes the land under the building. How the land part of a condo purchase is split is a question for your CPA. Ask it before the study is ordered.
What comes with the unit is a contract question first. Our Myrtle Beach condo investing page covers what furnished sales here include. The purchase contract should list it.

## Can you use the deduction?
A study produces a large first-year loss. Rental losses are passive by default. A passive loss can only reduce passive income, unless you pass the material participation tests. An owner with a full-time job and a managed unit can order a perfect study and get a loss that cannot be used this year.
The test is separate from the study and comes first. Our short-term rental tax treatment page explains the seven-day average stay rule, the seven participation tests, and the records to keep. Read it before you pay an engineer.
A loss you cannot use this year is not lost. It carries forward to next year. There it offsets passive income, which includes the rent from this unit and from any other rental you own. You do not have to wait for a sale. Whatever is still unused when you sell the whole property in a taxable sale is released in that year.
Want help finding your next investment?
Our investor agents find furnished units that fit your plan and settle what comes with them before you offer.
Have us help find your next investment

## What comes back when you sell?
When you sell the reclassified items, gain up to the depreciation you took is taxed as ordinary income. That is the recapture rule for personal property . It is not taxed as capital gain. The faster you wrote it off, the more comes back at ordinary rates.
The building is treated differently. Depreciation on the structure comes back as gain taxed at up to 25 percent under the capital gains rules . Most other long-term gain is taxed at 15 percent or less. A sale after a study therefore has two recapture layers. Ordinary rates on the short-life items. Up to 25 percent on the building.
A 1031 exchange defers all of it. Owners who plan to keep trading up treat the study and the exchange as one decision. The steps are on our 1031 exchange page . An owner who plans to sell and cash out in three or four years should run the recapture numbers before ordering a study.
Planning to trade up with a 1031 exchange?
We help you find the next property and time the sale to meet the exchange deadlines.
Have us help with your next exchange

## When should you order a study?
Four things settle it. Can the passive rules let you use the loss this year? How much of the price is furniture, appliances and finishes? How long will you hold, since a quick sale returns the benefit as recapture? What does the study cost against all three? The cost varies by provider and property. Get a quote before you decide.
Quality matters. The audit guide that examiners use to review these studies states that the classification of building parts is factually intensive and must be supported. It lists what a good study contains. Someone with expertise and experience. A detailed description of the method. Supporting documents. Interviews with the right people. A site visit.
An estimate made from a purchase price and a percentage is not a study. It has no site visit and no support. That is the kind that fails a review.

## What should you settle before you buy?
The facts a study uses are knowable before closing. We check what comes with the unit, whether the building requires a rental pool, and how the management is set up. Those are property questions and we answer them before you offer.
The tax answer is whether a study is worth the cost and what the recapture looks like on your timeline. For that we can put you with a CPA who works on beach condos locally. That conversation goes faster with the building facts already settled.

Common questions

## Cost segregation FAQ for Grand Strand investors

### Does cost segregation create new deductions?
No. It changes when you take them. The total depreciation over the life of the property is the same with or without a study. More of it lands in year one.

### Can I use the loss against my salary?
Only if the property is outside the passive rules and you materially participate. A managed unit owned by someone with a full-time job usually cannot. The loss carries forward and offsets rent and other passive income in later years. Whatever is left is released at a taxable sale.

### Does my purchase qualify for the 100 percent allowance?
The allowance is 100 percent for qualified property acquired after the January 2025 date named at the top of this page. Whether your purchase qualifies depends on the acquisition date and the contract. Your CPA confirms it.

### What comes back when I sell?
Depreciation on the reclassified items comes back as ordinary income, up to the amount taken. Depreciation on the building comes back as gain taxed at up to 25 percent. A 1031 exchange defers both.

### Is a study useful on an unfurnished long-term rental?
Less often. Most of the value a study finds in a condo is the furniture, appliances and finishes that come with a furnished unit. An unfurnished unit has less to move.

## Rental Depreciation in Myrtle Beach: Basis & Land | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/rental-depreciation/
Summary: What goes into a Myrtle Beach rental's basis on closing day, how to split the price between land and building, and what the depreciation does at sale.

Home / Invest / Rental depreciation
Basis, land split, first year

# Depreciating a Myrtle Beach rental, from closing day.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Only the building depreciates, over 27.5 years. The Horry County record sets the land share, and a condo has its own rule. The steps are below.
Walk a closing statement with us

The short answer
Depreciation on a rental starts with two numbers. The basis is the price plus the closing costs that count. The land share is the part you cannot depreciate. To find it, open the unit's record on the county assessor's site, read the land and building values, and apply that ratio to your price. A condo record may show a land value for your share of the common elements. If it does not, your CPA sets it from the master deed. The building share is deducted in equal parts over 27.5 years, starting the month the unit is ready to rent. The steps and an example are below.

## What goes into the basis?
The basis is the purchase price plus the settlement costs that belong to the property. Costs of the loan do not belong in it. The closing statement lists both kinds on the same page, and that is where first-year mistakes happen.
Goes into basis Stays out of basis
Abstract and title fees Discount points and loan origination fees
Recording fees Loan assumption fees
Transfer taxes The credit report
Title insurance An appraisal the lender required
Legal fees and surveys Prorated property tax and insurance

Both lists come from the rental property rules . A cost of buying the property goes in. A cost of borrowing the money stays out. On a Grand Strand closing, the transfer tax, the title policy and the attorney fee are usually the largest costs that go in.

## How do you split the price between land and building?
Land cannot be depreciated, so the price has to be divided first. The rule is a ratio. Each part gets the share of the price that matches its share of the market value on the day you bought. If you do not know the two values, the rules let you use the assessed values on the county tax record instead.
Most owners here use the second method. The Horry County assessor values land and building separately. The record for any parcel shows both numbers. Use the record for the year you bought, not a later year.
There is no typical ratio. An oceanfront lot with a small house and an inland lot with a large house are at opposite ends. The county record settles it for a specific address.

### How do you find the land value on the county record?

- Open the Horry County assessor property record search. Enter the address or the parcel number.

- Open the record for the year you bought. It lists a land value and a building value on separate lines.

- Divide the land value by the two values added together. That is the land share.

- Multiply your purchase price by the land share. That part is land and is never depreciated.

- Add the closing costs that count to the rest. That is your depreciable basis.

- Divide it by 27.5. That is the yearly deduction. The first year is prorated by the month the unit was ready.

### What if it is a condo?
A condo record may carry a land value for the unit's share of the common elements. Most do not. Of about 40,700 condo units in the county record, all but 8 show no land value. A unit in an oceanfront tower in Myrtle Beach that sold for $215,000 shows land $0 and building $212,000.
If the record has a land value, use the same six steps. If the land line is blank, your CPA sets the land share from the master deed. It is the unit's percentage of the common elements times the land value of the whole parcel. Moving the furniture and appliances to shorter schedules is a separate decision, on our cost segregation page .

### How do you calculate the yearly deduction?
Two real Horry County homes that each sold for $326,000 show how far the share moves. The county record for a house in Socastee puts about 27 percent of its value in land, so about $89,000 of the price is land. The rest, plus the closing costs that count, is depreciated: about $8,600 a year before those costs.
A townhouse in Surfside Beach puts about 62 percent in land. At the same price, only about $123,000 is depreciated: about $4,500 a year. The table has the two records.
Sold for $326,000 Land on the record Building on the record Land share Land of the price Depreciated A year
A house in Socastee $86,250 $230,498 About 27% $88,769 $237,231 About $8,600
A townhouse in Surfside Beach $190,000 $115,000 About 62% $203,082 $122,918 About $4,500

## When does depreciation start?
It starts when the unit is placed in service. The rules define that as ready and available for use. A listed, vacant unit is in service. It does not wait for the first tenant.
Residential rental property uses a mid-month convention. The month the unit is placed in service counts as half a month, whatever the day. A unit ready on June 3 and one ready on June 28 get the same first-year deduction, six and a half months. The yearly amount is the building share of the basis divided by 27.5.
Keep three documents. The closing statement. The county record you used for the split. The date the unit was ready. Those are asked for at the sale, years later.
Not sure which closing lines count?
We read Grand Strand closing statements every week. We can mark the lines that go into basis to help make it make sense.
Send us a closing statement

## Is it a repair or an improvement?
A repair is deducted in the year you pay it. An improvement is added to the basis and depreciated. The rules require you to capitalize any cost that improves the property. Replacing one broken window is a repair. Replacing every window is an improvement.
Small items have a shortcut. If you elect the de minimis safe harbor for the year, you do not have to capitalize small purchases of tangible property, under the same rules . The dollar limit is in the regulations, not the publication. Confirm the current figure with your CPA. A furnished unit has many small purchases, so the election matters more on a beach condo.
Large furnished purchases go the other way. Furniture, appliances and carpet have shorter recovery periods. Moving them off the 27.5-year schedule is what a cost segregation study does. That is its own decision, on its own page .

## What does depreciation do to your sale?
Every dollar of depreciation lowers the basis. The sale price is measured against the lowered basis. Depreciation taken on the building comes back at sale as gain taxed at up to 25 percent. The details, and the South Carolina withholding for out-of-state owners, are on our capital gains page , with a calculator.
One rule matters here because the other pages do not state it. Your basis is reduced by the depreciation you were entitled to take, whether or not you took it, under the depreciation rules . An owner who skipped it for years to keep the return simple still pays recapture as if every year had been claimed. Skipping it loses the deduction and keeps the bill.
A 1031 exchange defers the whole gain, recapture included, into the next property. The steps are on our 1031 exchange page .

## What can Chapter3 settle before closing?
Two of the three inputs are property facts. We go through the closing statement with you line by line and mark what belongs to the property and what belongs to the loan. We also pull the county record for the land and building values in the year you bought. Your accountant gets a finished file.
The third input, the in-service date, is yours. Write it down. When the return needs doing, or a repair might be an improvement, we can put you with a CPA who works on Grand Strand rentals.

Common questions

## Rental depreciation FAQ for Myrtle Beach owners

### Do closing costs count toward the basis of a rental?
Some do. Title fees, recording fees, transfer taxes, title insurance, legal fees and surveys go in. Points, loan origination fees, loan assumption fees, the credit report and a lender-required appraisal stay out. Those are costs of the loan, not the property.

### How do I split the price between land and building?
By the ratio of their market values on the day you bought. If you do not know those values, you can use the assessed values on the county tax record. The Horry County record lists land and building separately. For a condo, use the land line on the unit's record if it has one. If not, your CPA sets the share from the master deed.

### When does depreciation start?
When the unit is ready and available to rent, not when the first tenant moves in. Residential rental property uses a mid-month convention. The month it is placed in service counts as half a month.

### What if I never claimed depreciation?
Your basis is still reduced by the amount you were entitled to claim. At sale the recapture is figured as if you had taken it every year. Skipping it loses the deduction and keeps the bill.

### Is a new roof a repair or an improvement?
An improvement. It is added to the basis and depreciated. Patching a leak is a repair, deducted in the year you pay it.
Sources: Publication 527, Residential Rental Property , Publication 946, How to Depreciate Property , Horry County Assessor, Guide to Assessment . Read September 4, 2026. Educational only, not tax advice. The split, the election and the return are for your CPA.

## The basis and the split are both set at closing.
Both are property facts we can settle with you before the first tax year.

## The 14-Day Rule for a Myrtle Beach Condo You Use | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/14-day-rule/
Summary: Personal use of more than 14 days or 10 percent of rented days makes a Grand Strand rental a home. What counts as a day, and what changes above the limit.

Home / Invest / The 14-day rule
Your own stays, counted

# How many nights can you use your own Myrtle Beach rental? The 14-day rule.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated September 7, 2026
Stay in your Myrtle Beach rental more than 14 nights, or 10 percent of its rented nights, and it counts as a home. Your deductions then cannot exceed the rent.
Speak to an expert

The short answer
A rental you also stay in is measured by days. Use it for personal purposes more than 14 days in the year, and it counts as a home. Use it more than 10 percent of the days it was rented, and it also counts as a home. The larger number applies. Then the expenses are split between rental days and personal days, and the rental share cannot exceed the rent. Below that, it is a rental with some personal use. Owners here exceed it often, because they were never told this.

## What is the 14-day rule?
It is the test in the rental property rules that decides whether a rental counts as a home. Personal use of more than 14 days makes it a home. Personal use of more than 10 percent of the days it was rented at a fair price also makes it a home. The larger number is the one that applies.
Days rented at a fair price 10 percent of that Personal days allowed before it counts as a home
100 10 14
140 14 14
200 20 20
250 25 25

A unit rented 200 nights allows 20 personal nights, not 14. A unit rented 100 nights allows 14, because 14 is more than 10. The rented-day count comes from your booking records. The limit is different for every unit and every year.

## What counts as a day of personal use?
More than your own nights. A day counts as personal use when the unit is used by you or a family member. It also counts when anyone uses it for less than a fair rent, or under a deal that lets you use their unit in return. A friend who stays for a token payment is a personal day. A week swapped with another owner is a personal day.
One exception helps the owner. A day spent mainly on repairs and maintenance is not a personal day, even if you sleep in the unit. An owner who comes down to repaint between seasons is working. Keep the receipts and the dates. That is how you prove it.

## What if you rent it fewer than 15 days?
Then the rental rules do not apply at all. If the unit counts as a home and is rented fewer than 15 days in the year, the rent is not reported as income. The expenses are not rental expenses. It is a second home that earned a little.
The count is exact. Fourteen rented days and the rent is yours with no reporting. Fifteen and the rules below apply, with the expense split and the income limit. If you rent a few peak weeks and use the unit the rest of the year, count the nights before you book the fifteenth.
Does the building let you use your own unit?
Some rental pools limit owner nights or charge for them. The building sets that. We read the rules before you offer.
Consult an expert real estate agent

## How are the expenses divided?
Once a unit counts as a home, every expense is split between rental use and personal use. The split is the ratio of rental days to total days used. Mortgage interest, taxes, insurance, utilities, management, repairs and depreciation all split the same way. A unit rented 150 days and used 30 days puts five sixths of each cost on the rental.
Example with round numbers. The year's costs are $12,000: mortgage interest, taxes, insurance, utilities, management, repairs and depreciation together. Five sixths is $10,000 for the rental side and $2,000 for the personal side. The rent for the year is $9,000. The rental deductions stop at $9,000. Interest and taxes are taken first, then the operating costs, then depreciation. The $1,000 left over carries forward to next year.
The rental share then has a limit. In a year the unit counts as a home, rental expenses cannot exceed rental income. The property cannot show a loss. Anything over the limit carries forward. The deductions are taken in a set order. Mortgage interest and taxes first. Operating costs next. Depreciation last, which is the part most often unused.
The personal share of the mortgage interest and property tax is still deductible elsewhere. It is treated the way it would be on a second home, with the limits that apply there.

## Why does this matter more on the Grand Strand?
Owners here buy to use the unit. Many of the condos we sell to investors are used by the owner for part of the year. The usual plan is to rent the summer and keep a few winter weeks. That plan goes over this limit more often than owners expect, because a busy summer raises the rented-day count and the 10 percent figure with it.
Three other day counts exist and they are all different. Renting your own legal residence more than a set number of days a year costs you the 4 percent property tax rate. That count is on our Horry County property taxes page . The 90 and 30-day limits on our accommodations tax page are about guests, not you. The seven-day average on our short-term rental tax page counts guests only. Your own nights affect none of those and all of this one.
The building has rules too. Some rental pools cap owner nights. Some charge for them. Some require the unit to be available in peak weeks. Those terms cap how much personal use is possible.

## What should you settle before you buy?
We read the building's rules on owner use and the rental-pool terms for any unit before you make an offer. How many nights the building allows, whether it charges for them, and whether peak weeks are reserved for guests are all written down. We find them.
The day count is yours to keep. A calendar with rented nights, personal nights and work days marked separately is the whole record. It shows which side of the limit you are on in April. When the return needs doing, we can put you with a CPA who works on beach condos locally.

Common questions

## 14-day rule FAQ for Grand Strand owners

### Is the rule 14 days, or 10 percent?
Both. The larger number applies. A unit rented 100 days allows 14 personal days. A unit rented 200 days allows 20, because 10 percent of 200 is more than 14.

### Do days I spend fixing the unit count as personal use?
No. A day spent mainly on repairs and maintenance is not a personal use day, even if you sleep there. Keep the dates and receipts.

### Does letting family stay count as personal use?
Yes. A day a family member uses the unit is personal use. A day anyone uses it for less than a fair rent is also personal use.

### What if I rent it for fewer than 15 days?
If the unit counts as a home and is rented fewer than 15 days in the year, the rent is not reported as income. The expenses are not rental expenses.

### Can the unit show a loss if it counts as a home?
No. In a year the unit counts as a home, rental expenses cannot exceed rental income. The excess carries forward. Depreciation is the last deduction taken.
Sources: Publication 527, personal use of a dwelling unit , Horry County Assessor, Guide to Assessment . Read September 4, 2026. Educational only, not tax advice. The count and the return are for your CPA.

## Owner-use limits are written into the rental-pool terms.
We read them before you offer. Owner-night caps, charges and reserved weeks are all in there.

Almost never for a house. The rule asks for a month's rent of at least 1 percent of the price. Of 2,975 houses with 3 or more bedrooms for sale in Horry County, 14 pass. Longs has 8 of them. We ran this count on November 1, 2026.

## Why is the tax on the listing not the tax you will pay?
Because the listing shows the seller's bill. After you buy, the county resets the value to about what you paid. A rental also pays a higher rate than a home its owner lives in.
A rental pays about $1,206 a year for each $100,000 of value outside city limits, and about $1,528 in the City of Myrtle Beach. Outside city limits, that is about 3 times what an owner who lives there pays.
A home its owner does not live in, such as a house rented out year-round or a second home, is taxed on 6 percent of its value . More on the 4 and 6 percent rates: Horry County property tax rates .
We read the county's deeds for this year's resales and the value each seller was taxed on. The middle home sold for about 1.2 times that value.
Your next tax bill outside city limits: about 3.9 times the seller's on an owner's home, 1.1 times on a rental Buying a home taxed at 4 percent, as an owner's home
The seller's bill: $1,000
Your next bill: about $3,900

Buying a home already taxed at 6 percent, such as a rental
The seller's bill: $1,000
Your next bill: about $1,100

The middle resale outside city limits, January to September 2026, by the rate on the seller's tax record. Your bill is figured on the sale price, before any exemption. A seller's Homestead exemption would make the jump larger.
Buy a home taxed at 4 percent and rent it out, outside city limits, and your next bill is about 3.9 times the seller's. Buy a home already taxed at 6 percent, such as a rental from another landlord, and it is about 1.1 times. In our experience, taxes stop more rental deals than insurance does.

### When the new bill starts
If you buy between January and September, your first October bill still uses the seller's value, and the next one uses the new value. Buy in October or later, and your first bill already uses the new value. Bills are mailed October 1 and are due by January 15.
A rental bought from another landlord can get a break. The 25 percent exemption applies only when the home was taxed at 6 percent before the sale and stays at 6 percent after it. Then a quarter of its new value is exempt, but the taxed value cannot fall below the county's current market value.
The owner or the owner's agent must notify the county assessor before January 31 of the first tax year it applies. We remind you before the deadline.
Every town's rate is in our property tax calculator .

## What can a calculator not see?
The community's rules, how rents keep up with prices, and the seller's own numbers. These are three things we check for you before you offer.

### A rental ban
Some communities here ban renting the house at all. We filter those out when we search for you, and we read the HOA papers for rules that would block your plan.

### Prices rose, the rent did not
An agent now on our team helped buyers purchase about eight nearly identical townhouses in a new Little River community. Each rented for a little over $2,000.
Prices rose from $230,000 to $292,000 over about 18 months. The rents stayed flat, and the cash flow went away for later buyers.

### The seller's cash flow is not yours
An agent at Chapter3 sold a rented house for an owner of 15 years. His cash flow was over $1,200 a month. The next investor would make about $600, because of higher taxes and a bigger loan.
The agent marketed it to investors who accept a modest cash flow in an area where prices are rising. A cash buyer closed 13 days after it was listed.

## Buying a Myrtle Beach Rental From Out of State | Chapter3

Summary: How to buy a Myrtle Beach rental without flying in: the video walk-through, the inspection, the attorney closing by mail, and management set up before you close.

Home / Invest / Buying from out of state
Remote buyers

# How do you buy a Myrtle Beach rental from out of state? Without flying in.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Many Grand Strand rental owners live in another state. The walk-through, the inspection and the closing can all be done without a flight to Myrtle Beach.

The short answer
You can buy a Grand Strand rental without visiting. A local agent walks the property on video. A licensed home inspector reports on it. A South Carolina attorney runs the closing, and you sign the papers in your own state before a notary with two witnesses. Flood insurance starts on the day the loan closes. Property tax is charged at the 6 percent rate because the property is not your legal residence. Two things go wrong for remote buyers: wire fraud, and a signing package that does not meet South Carolina form. Both are avoidable. Buying from Canada? Our Canadian buyers page covers the extra steps.

## What does buying from out of state involve?
Many owners here live somewhere else. About 1 in 4 homes in Horry County has its tax bill mailed outside South Carolina. More than half of condo buyers have a tax bill sent to another state. The county's counts are on our page on selling from another state .
Five steps have to happen in South Carolina while you are somewhere else. Each one has a person here who does it.
Step Who does it here What you do
Seeing the property A Chapter3 agent walks it on video and checks the things that do not show up in the photos. Watch, ask, and decide.
Inspection A licensed South Carolina home inspector writes the report. Read the report as issued and decide what to ask for.
Title, documents and closing A South Carolina attorney. State law requires it. Choose the attorney, or ask us which attorneys close for buyers who are not in the room.
Signing The attorney sends the package to you. Sign in your state before a notary, with two witnesses, or name an agent under a power of attorney.
Money The closing attorney receives the funds. Wire it after a phone call to a number you already had, never from an email.
Utilities and management The utility and the manager you chose. Set both up before closing so the first guest or tenant can arrive.

## Why does South Carolina require an attorney at closing?
South Carolina treats a real estate closing as the practice of law. The title search, the documents, the closing itself and the recording must be done or supervised by a South Carolina attorney. The state's highest court set that rule , and it applies to cash buyers as well as financed ones.
You do not pick a title company here. You pick an attorney. The attorney orders the title search, prepares the deed, collects the money, pays the seller and records the deed. If an LLC will own the rental , form it before the contract, so the deed is in its name. The fee is part of your closing costs. What closing costs in South Carolina include .

## How do you sign without being in South Carolina?
There are two ways. The attorney chooses which one the file can use, and your lender has a say if there is a loan.

### Sign by mail in your own state
The attorney sends the closing package to you. You sign before a notary in your state, and two witnesses sign with you. The notary writes the state of the commission and its expiry date. South Carolina accepts a deed acknowledged before an out-of-state notary when it carries those two witnesses. A package signed with one witness comes back, and the closing slips.

### Give someone a power of attorney
You sign a power of attorney naming a person who signs at the closing for you. It is signed with the same formality as a will, acknowledged like a deed, and recorded with the county for a fee. The attorney drafts it. Ask early, because a lender can refuse a power of attorney on some loan types.

### What about a notary on a video call?
Not with a South Carolina notary. South Carolina notary law requires the signer and the notary to be in the same room. Ask the closing attorney whether they accept a video notarization done under another state's law before you count on it.
Buying from another state?
Send the address and your timeline. We tell you which signing method fits and what to prepare.
Send the address

## How do you see a Myrtle Beach property without visiting?
On video, with a person who is in the unit and answers while you watch. Ask for these: the view from every window, the noise at the door, and the age plates on the HVAC and the water heater. In a condo, ask for the parking, the elevator and the hallways. In a house, ask for the lot drainage and the street.
Then the inspection. South Carolina licenses home inspectors . A licensed inspector reports on what a video cannot show: the roof, the electrical panel, the crawlspace, the plumbing under the sinks. You get the report as issued. What you ask the seller to fix or credit comes from that report, not from the photos.

## How do you keep the closing money safe?
The attack is an email that looks like it came from the attorney or the agent, with new wire instructions. It arrives the week of closing. Federal guidance is plain: never follow wire instructions in an email. Confirm the account name and number by phone, on a number you had before the email arrived.
Do this once, at the start. Get the attorney's phone number in person or from a document you trust. Wire only after a call to that number. A change in instructions is a stop, not a step.

## What is different for an owner who lives in another state?
Property tax. A rental you do not live in is assessed at the 6 percent rate . The 4 percent rate is for a legal residence, needs an application, and does not apply to a rental. How Horry County property tax is calculated .
Flood insurance. A new flood policy starts 30 days after you buy it , unless you buy it as part of a loan closing. A cash buyer gets no exception and should buy the policy a month before closing. Wind, flood and the coastal insurance bill .
Rental taxes and licenses. A short-term rental needs a business license and pays accommodations tax. If a platform takes the payment, the platform remits. Accommodations tax, explained .

## Who turns on the power and water?
Electricity comes from Santee Cooper or Horry Electric Cooperative, depending on the address. Inside the cities of Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach, the city bills water and sewer. Elsewhere it is Grand Strand Water and Sewer Authority. Natural gas, where it exists, is Dominion Energy.
Each utility wants an application, a copy of the settlement statement, and a deposit. The seller's last bills tell you which utilities serve the address. Ask for them with the disclosure.

## How is management set up before closing?
For a remote owner the manager is the local contact for guests, tenants and repairs. South Carolina requires a manager to be licensed and to keep deposits in a trust account. How to choose a property manager here . For an oceanfront condo, compare the building's own program with self-managing before you offer. Rental program or Airbnb .
If you keep the seller's tenant, the lease and the security deposit transfer to you at closing. The tenant must be told in writing who now owns the property and who manages it.
Want the whole thing set up before you close?
Tell us the address and the plan. We walk it, run the numbers, and line up the closing attorney, the inspector and the manager.

Common questions

## Out-of-state buyer FAQ

### Do I have to come to South Carolina to close?
No. You can sign the closing package in your own state before a notary, with two witnesses, or give someone a power of attorney. A South Carolina attorney still runs the closing.

### Can I sign the deed on a video call with a notary?
Not with a South Carolina notary. State law requires the signer and the notary to be in the same room. Ask the closing attorney whether they accept a video notarization done under another state's law.

### Who holds my earnest money?
Usually the closing attorney's trust account or the brokerage's escrow account. The contract says which. Confirm the wire instructions by phone before you send it.

### Why is my property tax higher than the seller's?
The seller may have paid the 4 percent legal-residence rate. A rental you do not live in is assessed at 6 percent. The bill is higher than the seller's for the same property.

### Do I need flood insurance if I pay cash?
A lender requires it in a high-risk zone. A cash buyer chooses. A new policy starts 30 days after purchase unless it is bought with a loan closing, so a cash buyer should buy it a month before closing.

## Myrtle Beach Property Management: What It Costs | Chapter3

# What does property management cost in Myrtle Beach? Five local fee schedules, and a year of fees worked out.

- 10% of the rent each month

- Half to one month's rent to place a tenant

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Five local fee schedules, a year of fees worked out, and when an owner needs a manager.

The short answer
Four of the five property managers serving Horry County that print their fees take 10 percent of each month's rent on a yearly lease. Most add half a month to a full month's rent each time they place a new tenant. On a 3-bedroom house renting for about $1,600 a month, that comes to about $2,200 to $2,400 a year.
A vacation rental manager costs more. In the rentals we have seen, a basic plan takes about 13 to 17 percent of the bookings. Full service takes about 40 to 60 percent of the profit after costs, not of the bookings. Chapter3 does not manage property. We work out what you keep after the manager's fee.

## How much do property managers charge in Myrtle Beach?
We read the fee pages of the five managers serving Horry County that print their long-term fees. A long-term rental is a home leased to one tenant for a year or more. Three of the five have an office in Horry County. Firm C serves Myrtle Beach from its Charleston office, in Summerville. Firm D is the Myrtle Beach rentals site of a national brokerage's local franchise, and it prints no office address.

The fee to find a tenant is called a leasing or placement fee. It runs from nothing to one full month's rent, and half a month is the middle. A renewal fee is charged when the tenant signs on for another year. The two firms that print one charge $100 or $150.
Compare dollars, not percents. A plan that prints "as low as 7 percent" with a $150 monthly minimum costs about 9 percent on a $1,600 rent. $150 is more than 7 percent of any rent under about $2,140.

## What does a property manager cost in a year?
The fee to find a tenant changes the total from one year to the next. We worked out a year of fees on a 3-bedroom house renting for $1,600 a month, on the terms in the table above.

Most years, with a new tenant about 1 year in 4 about $2,200 to $2,400
That is about 12 percent of the rent, not 10.

## What does a vacation rental manager charge in Myrtle Beach?
More than a long-term manager, because there is more work. A vacation rental, also called a short-term rental, is rented by the night or the week. Owners here pay for one of two kinds of plan:
What owners here pay a vacation rental manager, in the rentals we have seen Plan The manager takes What it covers
Basic plan About 13 to 17% of the bookings Marketing, guest messages, bookkeeping
Full service About 40 to 60% of profit after costs Basic, plus taxes and repairs

On a basic plan, you still arrange the cleaning, and repairs and tax help cost extra. Full service is a share of what is left after the costs of running the home. Its dollar cost depends on those costs.
Local firms that print a vacation rental fee show 10 to 25 percent of the booking. One Little River firm prints 15 percent and charges cleaning to the guests, not the owner. We plan with the ranges above, which come from rentals we have seen run.
The average Myrtle Beach vacation rental listing, of any type or size, takes in about $25,800 a year in bookings. That counts the cleaning fees guests pay. On all of it, 13 percent is about $3,400 and 17 percent is about $4,400.

## What do property managers charge besides the monthly fee?
For the monthly share, a long-term manager advertises the home, screens applicants and signs the lease. The manager also collects the rent and arranges repairs. Federal fair housing law applies to the advertising, the screening and the lease. The five fee pages also print charges on top of it, and a few things they leave out:

- A setup fee
Firm B charges $200 to start. Firm A prints no setup fee.

- A month with no rent
Firm D takes its fee only on rent it collects. The other four pages do not say what they charge in a month no rent comes in.

- Inspections
Firm B's standard plan includes the move-in and move-out inspections. It charges $100 for an extra inspection you ask for.

- Repairs
Firm B usually pays repair bills up front and takes them out of your next month's payment. You may use your own repair person. None of the five pages prints a markup on repair bills.

- Evictions
Many managers handle evictions, depending on the plan. Most charge their percentage of the rent whatever the work, but some bill an eviction by the hour. Firm E charges no eviction fee beyond the cost of serving the papers and the court's costs.

- A tenant who leaves early
If a tenant Firm D placed breaks the lease in the first 12 months, Firm D finds a new tenant for free.

- 1 The tenant pays The rent each month, and a security deposit at the start.

- 2 The manager's trust account A bank account for other people's money. The deposit stays in it until the lease ends.

- 3 You are paid The rent, after the bank clears it, less the manager's fee.

How the money moves on a long-term rental with a manager. Our own drawing.

## Who pays the taxes on a vacation rental in Myrtle Beach?
On stays under 90 days, whoever takes the guest's booking and payment collects the state's 7 percent accommodations tax on the full booking. That is the manager or the booking site, or you when you book the guest yourself.
On a stay under 90 days, what the guest pays The charge Taxed?
The nightly rent Yes
A cleaning fee every guest must pay Yes, like the rent
A cleaning fee the guest can choose to skip No

Three more rules for a vacation rental owner:

- A state retail license. An owner who rents only through a manager or a booking site needs none. An owner who books guests directly needs one. The exception is a home rented one week or less in each calendar quarter.

- The county's fee. Horry County adds a hospitality fee on short stays: 3 percent outside city limits and 1.5 percent inside. Cities may add their own. When a manager arranges the stay, the county's page says the manager should collect and pay it.

- A city business license. The City of Myrtle Beach requires one for every rental property, short-term or long-term.

Every tax on a stay is on our accommodations tax page , and the setup steps are on setting up a short-term rental .

## How do I fire a property manager in South Carolina?
Give the notice your agreement asks for. State law adds four rules an owner can use:

- A way out after the first term
An agreement that renews on its own must let either side cancel on 30 days' notice after the first term.

- Renewal pay on page one
The agreement must say how the manager is paid. Pay for a future lease renewal must be in underlined capital letters on page one.

- The deposit list, within 30 days
Any deduction must be listed in a written notice to the tenant, with any balance. The 30 days run from the latest of three things: the tenancy ends, the tenant hands back the home, and the tenant asks for the deposit.

- Three times what was wrongly kept
If the owner misses the 30 days, the tenant can recover three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus reasonable attorney's fees.

The agreement also may not bind you to list the home for sale with the same firm. The rest of the licensing law is about how a manager's office must run.
The deposit rules bind you as the owner, manager or not. More is on our South Carolina landlord rules page .

Common questions

## Property management FAQ

### Are property management fees tax deductible?
Yes. Management fees are a rental expense you deduct from rental income on your tax return.

### Does a property manager need a license in South Carolina?
Yes. Managing someone else's property for a fee needs a real estate license. Every licensed manager works under a broker-in-charge or a property manager-in-charge.

### Can a manager's unlicensed staff negotiate my lease?
No. Staff without a license may not negotiate a lease, approve an application, or explain the management agreement to you.

### Does my tenant have to be told who owns the home?
Yes. The tenant must be told in writing, at or before the lease starts, the name and address of the owner or the owner's agent. A manager who signs a lease without that notice takes on the landlord's duties for that lease and receives the tenant's notices and legal papers.

### Is an HOA management company the same thing?
No. A company that runs a homeowners association is a different job. This page is about a manager who rents out your home.

# Rental program or Airbnb for a Myrtle Beach condo? What you keep, both ways.

- 38.6% one resort's rental desk

- 15.5% Airbnb, most hosts

- 8 in 10 oceanfront condos for sale in a program

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
One Myrtle Beach resort's rental desk kept 38.6 percent of the rent. Airbnb takes 15.5 percent from most hosts.

The short answer
One oceanfront Myrtle Beach resort's rental desk kept 38.6 percent of the rent, before its other charges. Airbnb now takes 15.5 percent from most hosts, and Vrbo takes 12 percent.
Of each $1,000 guests paid, that desk left the owner $614. Airbnb leaves $845. Running it yourself keeps more while the cleaner, supplies and your time cost less than $231 of each $1,000.
A rental program is the building's own rental desk. It books the guests, cleans the unit and sends you the rest. We get the building's program agreement and owner statements and run it both ways before you offer.

## How much does a rental program take in Myrtle Beach?
One large oceanfront Myrtle Beach resort's rental desk took about 4 of every 10 rent dollars, then billed the owner for more. Its written rules set three fees on the gross rent, meaning all the rent guests paid:

- 35% management fee

- 2.6% marketing fee

- 1% to replace worn items

It also charged a health club fee of $53 a month plus tax. It billed repairs job by job, and added a handling fee when it paid an outside contractor's bill for the owner. It asked the owner's approval for any single repair over $500, unless the owner could not be reached or an emergency could not wait.
Its sample owner statement shows what was left. In one slow January, the unit rented 3 nights for $229.95. The owner's check was $66.84.
Owner statement, one January
Rent for 3 nights $229.95
Management fee, 35% &minus;$80.48
Marketing fee, 2.6% &minus;$5.98
After the program's fees $143.49
Health club &minus;$40.85
Replacing worn items, 1% &minus;$2.30
A repair &minus;$22.50
The owner's own charges &minus;$11.00
Check to the owner $66.84
The rental desk's sample owner statement, redrawn by Chapter3. The owner kept about 29 cents of each rent dollar that month.
The statement's only income line is the room rent for the nights booked. It has no line for the cleaning fees guests pay.

## Which keeps more: the program, Airbnb or Vrbo?
Running it yourself on Airbnb or Vrbo keeps more of each booking, before you pay for the work. Airbnb is moving every home host to one fee, and most hosts pay 15.5 percent. Its old 3 percent host fee is being phased out. Vrbo takes 12 percent of the rent and the cleaning fee.
What the owner keeps of each $1,000 of rent, before the cleaner and other costs Who rents it, fee owner keeps

Vrbo, run yourself · Vrbo takes 12% $880
Airbnb, run yourself · Airbnb takes 15.5% $845
The rental program · one resort's desk takes 38.6% $614

The program's figure is before its monthly club fee and its repair charges, so the real difference is larger. Airbnb's figure uses the fee most hosts pay. Vrbo's uses its pay-per-booking fee.
The difference, $231 of each $1,000, pays for the work the desk did: the cleaner, linens, supplies and answering guests. If those cost you less, running it yourself keeps more.

Airbnb or Vrbo, run yourself 15.5% on Airbnb, 12% on Vrbo You, a cleaner and a handyman The site pays it on its bookings
A local vacation rental manager A share of the profit, not of the rent The manager: guests, taxes, repairs The manager pays it when it books

A local manager is a third way. Full service here covers marketing, guest messages, the books, taxes and repairs. In what we see, managers price it as a share of gross profit, not of the rent. Its percentage cannot be set beside the shares above. What managers here charge is on our property management page .
The worst mistake we see when owners run it themselves is the cheapest cleaner. Owners who hired one have had theft and damage.

About 8 in 10 condos for sale in Horry County's oceanfront buildings say the unit is in a rental program. That is about 83 percent in Myrtle Beach and about 76 percent in North Myrtle Beach. Every one of the 43 oceanfront buildings with 8 or more condos for sale has units listed in a program.

## Can you leave the program or list on Airbnb too?
Not both at once at that resort. Its desk was the owner's only rental agent and collected all the rent. Booking your own guests and keeping the money broke the agreement.
An owner who booked a guest through the management office earned a referral commission instead, 20 percent of the nightly rate in most months.
Leaving took about three months:

- Written notice at least 90 days ahead.

- The desk took out its hotel items, such as the vacuum, linens and towels, and did a final cleaning.

- It turned off the keycard lock and had a locksmith rekey the door, so the unit had its own lock again.

- Any balance was due within 10 days of the final statement.

After the rekey, the door is yours again. You choose how your own guests get in.

## What does the program make you buy and keep up?
A unit furnished like a hotel room, to the desk's standard, down to the dishes:

- Locks and phone A keycard lock on the resort's key system, and a phone line with voicemail through the phone service the program named.

- Beds A queen sleeper sofa. A king bed in the main bedroom and two queens in each guest room, where they fit.

- Dishes Winter Frost White Corelle plates, Chivalry glasses by Libby and Allison flatware by Rogers.

- TV A flat screen of at least 42 inches in the living room.

- Updates Units were expected to be updated at least once every ten years. A unit came off the program if work rated below standard was not done in time.

- Insurance Liability cover of at least $500,000, carried by the owner.

A unit you run yourself has no such list. When we run the numbers on a program unit, we add what its furnishing rules will cost.

## Can you still use your own condo?
Yes, but in a program you book it like a guest. At that resort, owners booked their own stays through the management office, Monday to Friday, 8 to 5. They were asked to check in at the hotel front desk like any guest. The rules set no cap on owner nights.
Running it yourself, you block your own dates on the calendar.
Either way, the IRS limits your own days. The limit is the greater of 14 days or 10 percent of the days the condo is rented at a fair price. Days your family uses it count too.
Go over the limit, and the IRS counts the condo as a home, which limits a rental loss. More on our 14-day rule page .

## Does a rental program change the loan?
For many conventional loans, lenders look at the building, not at whether you join its program. Many conventional loans, the standard mortgages, are not made on any unit in a building run like a hotel. That includes a unit you run on Airbnb yourself.
Lenders list what makes a building ineligible. One is rules that make owners rent their units through the building's program, limit when owners may stay, or make owners share rental profit with the manager.
Hotel services count as well: registration at a front desk, daily cleaning, a central phone, central keys and limits on decorating. A name that says hotel, motel or resort counts too, unless the word only refers to the building's past use. Marketing as a hotel, resort or investment counts as well.
Four of those hotel services were written into that resort desk's rules:
Hotel services lenders list, and the rental desk's own rules What lenders list The rental desk's rules
Registration at a front desk Owners were asked to check in at the hotel front desk like any guest.
A central key system Every unit on the rental program had a keycard lock on the resort's key system.
A central phone service Phones ran through the phone service the program named.
Limits on decorating A full section of decorating rules, down to the dishes.

In what we see, buildings with a rental program usually do not qualify for standard loans, because so many owners are investors. Lenders call these buildings non-warrantable. That many investors also shows the building is run for renting.
The loans that work there are on our condotel financing and non-warrantable condos pages.

## Who pays the lodging taxes in each case?
Whoever books the stay and takes the payment collects and pays South Carolina's tax on it. That is the state's 5 percent sales tax and 2 percent accommodations tax, the tax on short stays.
Who pays South Carolina's tax on a short stay Who books it The state's tax on the stay Your state license
The program books the guest The program collects and pays it None needed
Airbnb or Vrbo books the guest The site pays it on the full booking None needed
You book the guest yourself You collect and pay it A state retail license, see below

The exception: an owner who books guests directly needs no retail license if the condo is rented no more than one week in each calendar quarter. That owner still files and pays the tax once a year.

- What else Airbnb collects The county's and the cities' taxes on the stay, and the local sales taxes the state collects for them. The host handles any other tax.

- The county's hospitality fee 3 percent of the rent outside city limits and 1.5 percent inside. When a manager books the stay, the county tells the owner to make sure the manager pays it.

- Long stays A stay of 90 days or more in a row by the same guest owes no hospitality fee.

- The city license Inside Myrtle Beach city limits, every rental property needs a city business license, short-term or long-term.

The totals by town are on our accommodations tax page .

## Who may run a Myrtle Beach rental for you?
You, or someone with a South Carolina real estate license. An owner renting his own condo needs no license.
Anyone paid to list it or rent it out for you must be licensed as a property manager or broker. That covers a paid Airbnb co-host, a helper who lists your condo or arranges its rentals. Chapter3 does not manage rentals.
Whether you or a manager runs the rental also changes your tax result. How is on our rental tax page .

## Program or Airbnb: which fits your condo?
The program fits an owner who wants no work, and running it yourself fits an owner who will do the work. About 58 percent of Horry County condo units mail their tax bill outside South Carolina. For an owner who lives out of state, the desk's share pays for someone on site. How to buy a Myrtle Beach rental from out of state , without flying in, is on its own page.

## Rental program FAQ

### How much do rental programs charge in Myrtle Beach?
One oceanfront resort's rental desk took 38.6 percent of the rent, plus a monthly health club fee and repairs. In its sample statement the owner kept about 29 cents of each rent dollar. Airbnb takes 15.5 percent from most hosts.

### Does Airbnb still charge hosts 3 percent?
Airbnb's 3 percent host fee is being phased out. Airbnb is moving every home host to one fee, and most hosts pay 15.5 percent. Vrbo charges 12 percent.

### Can I use Airbnb while I am in the program?
Not at the resort whose rules this page shows. Its desk was the only rental agent, and booking your own guests broke the agreement. Leaving took 90 days' notice.

### Who pays the accommodations tax when the program books the guest?
The program, because it takes the payment. If you book a guest yourself, you collect and pay that stay's tax.

### Does joining a rental program affect my loan?
For many standard loans, the lender looks at the building, not at whether you join. Many standard loans are not made on any unit in a building run like a hotel. Signs are a front desk, central keys or rules on when owners may stay.

### Do I need a license to rent out my own condo?
No real estate license. Anyone paid to list or rent it for you needs one. Inside Myrtle Beach city limits, every rental also needs a city business license.

# Where should you buy a rental near Myrtle Beach? Rent by the night at the beach, and by the year inland.
For a nightly rental, buy at the beach, where the zoning on this map allows it. For a yearly lease, buy inland.

Eleven Grand Strand areas compared for a rental investor.

The short answer
For a nightly rental, buy in one of the beach areas, where the rules for the address allow it. A rental-data company estimates that the average nightly rental there took in about $25,000 to $48,000 in a year, before costs. The license, the tax and every town's rules are on our short-term rental rules page .
For a yearly lease, buy inland. In Longs, Socastee and Conway, a year's rent is about 7 to 9 percent of a house's price. In North Myrtle Beach, Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Murrells Inlet and Pawleys Island, it is 3 to 4 percent. A higher share means more rent for each dollar of the price.

## 1. North Myrtle Beach: nightly rentals with a business license
North Myrtle Beach has no special zoning or permit for nightly rentals. It asks for a business license renewed each year and the lodging taxes. It also has rules on trash, parking, noise and how many guests may stay.
USGS photo, 2011
Condo towers and beach houses on the same oceanfront block in North Myrtle Beach.

Most homes here are condos, and four in five condos for sale are listed as open to nightly guests. In the rental data's North Myrtle Beach area, the average nightly rental took in about $34,000 a year, before costs.
The middle house within the city limits sold for about $565,000 and the middle condo for about $300,000.
Get rentals for sale in North Myrtle Beach

## 2. Surfside Beach: nightly rentals in two districts
Surfside Beach allows stays of less than 30 days in only two of its zoning districts. A lease of a year or more is allowed wherever homes are. The town's code does not define a lease of one month to a year. For a monthly rental, we get the town's reading before you make an offer.
USGS photo, 2011
The pier and rows of raised beach houses in Surfside Beach.

Houses cost more here than in any of the other ten areas, and almost no new ones are built. In the rental data's Surfside Beach area, the average nightly rental brought in about $43,000 a year, before costs.
The middle house within the town limits sold for about $705,000 and the middle condo for about $370,000.
Get rentals for sale in Surfside Beach

## 3. Garden City: the most houses for sale that say nightly is allowed
Garden City is outside the towns, in Horry County. A nightly rental here needs a county business license, a state sales tax number and a county hospitality and accommodations tax account.
More than half the houses for sale here say nightly stays are allowed, the highest share of the eleven areas. In the rental data's Garden City Beach area, the average nightly rental took in about $41,000 a year, before costs.
USGS photo, 2011
Condo buildings and houses on the strip between the ocean and the marsh at Garden City.

Houses here cost less than in the other five beach areas. FEMA puts 39 percent of homes here in its high-risk flood zone, the highest share of the eleven areas, so we price the flood insurance for each house.
The middle house in the Census area of Garden City sold for about $406,000 and the middle condo for about $221,000.

## 4. Murrells Inlet, Georgetown County side: no county business license, and a 30-day limit
Murrells Inlet sits on both sides of the county line. On this page, Murrells Inlet is the Census area of that name, which lies on the Georgetown County side. Georgetown County requires no business license. Its zoning allows a house to be rented for stays of up to 30 days in the county's resort zone. The lot may hold only that house, with a parking space for each bedroom. We look up the zoning of each address.

## Why do we run the rent against your price?
We price a rental against the rent it will get now, not against what earlier buyers paid. An agent now on our team learned why in Little River. He helped buyers purchase about eight nearly identical townhouses in a new community there. Each rented for a little over $2,000 a month.
The sale price rose from about $230,000 for the first to about $292,000 for the last, over about a year and a half. The rent stayed the same, so the later buyers lost the cash flow. Before you offer, we put today's rent against your price. The rest of the story, and the rules on renting a new house, are on our page on new construction as a rental .

## What does the tax on a rental cost in each area?
South Carolina taxes the home you live in on 4 percent of its value, and a rental or second home on 6 percent. Only the home you live in skips the school operating tax. Outside city limits, a rental's tax bill is about 3.3 times a resident's on the same house; in the towns it differs.

## Will the rules change?
Two bills in the state legislature would set a state rule. One would bar cities and counties from banning short-term rentals, and the other would expressly allow them to. Neither has left committee.
North Myrtle Beach's council has held workshops and public sessions on new rules. The city's page lists no new rule.
For a rental of one to three months, each area has its own rule:

- Myrtle Beach counts any stay under 90 days as short-term, so it needs a marked zone.

- In Conway, the same rule as for a nightly rental: one of three business districts.

- Surfside Beach's code leaves it open, so we ask the town first.

- In Georgetown County's resort zone, a stay may last up to 30 days.

- Outside the towns in Horry County, zoning puts no limit.

South Carolina's lodging tax applies to stays of less than 90 days in a row, unless the home is rented fewer than 15 days in a year. No state law bans nightly rentals.

## Where to buy a rental: questions

### Where are Airbnbs legal in Myrtle Beach?
In the City of Myrtle Beach, only in the zones the city marks for them. Most neighborhoods of houses are zoned against any stay of less than 90 days. About three in four condos in the city are in a marked zone. North Myrtle Beach has no special zoning step for them, and Surfside Beach allows them in two districts.

### Is Myrtle Beach a good place to buy a rental property?
For a yearly lease, the inland areas earn more rent for the price. A year's rent is about 9.1 percent of a house's price in Longs, against about 3.9 percent in Myrtle Beach. For a nightly rental, buy at the beach, where the rules for the address allow it.

### North Myrtle Beach or Myrtle Beach for a rental?
For a nightly rental, North Myrtle Beach asks only for a license, the lodging taxes and its everyday rules. Myrtle Beach allows it only in marked zones, where most of its condos are. Nightly rentals took in more a year on average in North Myrtle Beach. The middle condo sold for about $300,000 in North Myrtle Beach and about $175,000 in Myrtle Beach.

### Is Murrells Inlet in Horry or Georgetown County?
Both. The county line runs through Murrells Inlet. The Census area of that name, which this page counts, lies in Georgetown County. Georgetown County requires no business license, and its resort district allows a house to be rented for stays of up to 30 days.

### What is the property tax on a rental in Horry County?
Outside the towns, most homes pay about $1,206 a year on each $100,000 of price at the rental rate, before fees. Inside the towns it is higher, and highest in Conway.

### Where is the cheapest place to buy a rental near Myrtle Beach?
Conway for a house, at about $271,000 at the middle in the past year's recorded sales, and Little River for a condo, at about $155,000.

After closing

# What do you set up after closing on a Myrtle Beach short-term rental? In this order.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
Eight steps come after closing on a short-term rental and before the first guest: zoning, the license, taxes, the county fee, alarms, insurance, furnishing and the listing.

The short answer
After closing, a short-term rental needs the same set of accounts whichever town it is in. Confirm the zoning and the building's rules first, because a business license is refused without them. Then the state tax license if you take bookings yourself, the city or county business license, the county fee account, and the personal property return next spring. Alarms and a landlord policy before the first guest. Then the listing, with the taxes the platform collects and the ones it does not. The whole list fits on one page. Ask us for it at closing.
Ask for the closing-day checklist

- Short-term rental setup FAQ

## What has to be in place before the first guest?

- Zoning and the recorded building rules allow nightly rental at that address.

- The business license from the city or the county, which checks the zoning first.

- The state tax license, only if you take bookings and payments yourself.

- The county fee account, and the city account inside city limits.

- Working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms.

- A landlord policy, with wind and flood where required.

- Furnishing, and the utilities in your name.

- The listing, with the taxes set correctly.

Each step is explained below, with who issues what. The personal property return comes the following spring.

## Is the property zoned for nightly rentals?
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, the planning office says a property cannot be rented for less than 90 days unless it is zoned for short-term rentals. Most residential neighborhoods are not, and only 24 houses in traditional residential zones are grandfathered. A business license needs the zoning approval first. A violation is a misdemeanor.
North Myrtle Beach has no special zoning or permit process beyond the license. Surfside Beach allows stays under 30 days only in two districts. Unincorporated Horry County has no county short-term rental ordinance, so the recorded covenants decide. The rules by city, in full .
The building's recorded documents can bar nightly rental where the zoning allows it. Read the covenants and any rental amendment before closing, not after.

## Which licenses do you need?
Where the property is Business license Who issues it
City of Myrtle Beach Required for every rental property, short-term or long-term. The fee is set from gross receipts. Renewals are due April 30. Business License Division . The city
North Myrtle Beach Required for all short-term rentals. The city's short-term rental page . The city
Unincorporated Horry County Required for every business in the unincorporated area; the year runs May 1 to April 30 and zoning approval comes first. Application instructions . Rental real estate is rate class 6: $55 minimum on the first $50,000 of gross income , then $1.37 per $1,000, doubled for a business with no fixed place of business in the county. The county treasurer
Georgetown County No county business license . The county collects a 3 percent local accommodations tax instead. Check the Town of Pawleys Island separately. None at county level

The state license is separate. The state revenue department requires a retail license only if you take bookings and payments yourself. If every booking runs through a manager or a platform that takes the payment, they remit the tax and you need no state license. The license costs $50 , does not expire, and once you hold it you file a return every period, even with no rentals.

## Which tax accounts and fees?
The state charges 5 percent sales tax and 2 percent accommodations tax on stays under 90 consecutive days. Returns are due by the 20th of the following month. Whoever takes the payment remits it. Horry County's hospitality fee is 3 percent of rent outside the city limits and 1.5 percent inside, due the 20th. The county says to make sure a property manager who arranges the stay is remitting it.
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, a short-term rental also collects 0.5 percent local accommodations tax and a 1 percent hospitality fee for the city. North Myrtle Beach charges 1.5 percent on transient accommodations, due the 20th. Georgetown County charges 3 percent, remitted by the 20th, with a 5 percent penalty per month late.
Airbnb collects the 5 percent and 2 percent state taxes and the local taxes it lists for Horry County, Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach. It lists nothing for Georgetown County. You remit whatever the platform does not list, and everything on stays you book yourself. Accommodations tax, explained .

Send the address

## What is the personal property return?
A yearly form listing the furnishings in a rental. Horry County's auditor requires it from anyone who owned a property on December 31 that was not their legal residence. The county's inventory form lists beds, dressers, sofas, televisions, the refrigerator, the stove, the washer and the dryer. The county then bills a tax on those items in the fall.
Georgetown County requires the same return from every owner at the 6 percent rate, with furnishings and appliances included. If you do not file, the auditor assumes a fully furnished rental. File it either way.

## What do the alarms and the insurance require?
South Carolina adopts the national residential and fire codes statewide, and cities and counties enforce only those codes . The current editions are the 2021 codes, in force since January 2023. Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms are placed where those codes say; the city or county inspector can tell you the count for your floor plan.
Airbnb requires hosts to state whether smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are present and to keep them working. It provides a combination alarm to eligible hosts at no cost.
A homeowners policy is written for the home you live in. The state insurance department says renting a vacation home to others will likely raise the cost and may need added coverage. Airbnb's own cover is not a substitute for personal insurance. Get a landlord policy with the furnishings covered, and wind and flood where the zone requires. Coastal insurance, explained .

## How do you set up the listing?
Airbnb's ground rules require the photos and the description to represent the space as it is, and the home to be clean and free of hazards before check-in. Vrbo requires at least six published photos, at 1024 by 683 pixels or larger, and suspends a listing that drops under six for more than 30 days.
Set the house rules, the minimum nights, the cleaning fee and the tax settings before the listing goes live. Then choose a manager, or manage it yourself. What a manager costs . Rental program or Airbnb .
State law does not require you to register tenants with the association. The state HOA law has no such rule. The recorded governing documents set it, so read them for a guest registration or a parking rule.

## Who turns on the utilities?
Each utility wants identification, the settlement statement, and a deposit before the service goes into your name. Santee Cooper runs a credit check to set the deposit and connects after it is paid. Horry Electric Cooperative charges a $5 membership, a $10 application and a $20 connect fee, and asks for the settlement statement. The water systems work the same way. Which utility serves which area .

## What happens at tax time?
Rental income and expenses go on Schedule E , and depreciation starts when the unit is placed in service. A platform sends a Form 1099-K when your payouts pass $20,000 and 200 transactions in a year, and it can send one below that. Keep the owner statements either way. How short-term rental income is taxed .

Common questions

## Short-term rental setup FAQ

### Do I need a state retail license for my short-term rental?
Only if you take bookings and payments yourself. If every booking runs through a manager or a platform that takes the payment, they remit the tax and you need no state license.

### Does Airbnb pay all my taxes?
No. It collects the state taxes and the local taxes it lists for your area. You remit any local fee it does not list, and everything on stays you book yourself.

### Do I need a business license for a rental in the City of Myrtle Beach?
Yes. The city requires one for every rental property, short-term or long-term, and a zoning check comes first.

### What is the personal property return?
A yearly form to the county auditor listing the furnishings in a rental that is not your legal residence. The county then bills a tax on them in the fall.

### Can I rent nightly in a residential neighborhood in Myrtle Beach?
Almost never. Most residential zones in the city do not allow stays under 90 days. A 90-day lease is allowed there.
