## Condo, condotel or timeshare: what are you buying on the oceanfront?
Most units in these buildings are condos. Three kinds of ownership share the oceanfront:

- Condo You own the unit, and the owners together own the building through the HOA.

- Condotel A condo in a building run like a hotel, which rents units to guests by the night.

- Timeshare The use of a unit for some weeks a year, not the whole unit.

About 94 in 100 condos for sale in oceanfront buildings say short-term rentals are allowed, and we read each building's own rules on renting before you offer. The rules town by town are on our short-term rental rules page , and the choice of a building's rental program or Airbnb has its own page.
A condotel is harder to buy with a loan: Fannie Mae will not buy a loan on a unit in a building run like a hotel. Which loans close on these buildings is on our condotel financing page , and a lawsuit against the association is on our page on buying a condo in litigation .
Whether an oceanfront condo is a good investment is in our condo investing guide .

Common questions

## Oceanfront condo buildings FAQ

### Which Myrtle Beach oceanfront condos have the lowest HOA fees?
Sands Ocean Club, at a typical $425 a month, where most units for sale are studios. Then Towers on the Grove, about $500 from 3 listings, Anderson Ocean Club, about $570, and Beach Colony, about $595.

### Why are oceanfront condo HOA fees so high?
The fee pays the building's shared bills. Most listings in oceanfront buildings say it includes water and sewer, internet and insurance, and more than half say it pays the power bill.

### Can you have a dog in a Myrtle Beach oceanfront condo?
In some buildings. At Beach Colony, Margate Tower, Royale Palms and Ocean Creek, most units for sale allow pets. At Coral Beach, none of the 40 do. We read the building's pet rule before you offer.

### What is the tallest condo building in Myrtle Beach?
Margate Tower, in Kingston Plantation. It rises about 330 feet, and it also has the largest units and the highest fee of the oceanfront buildings on this page.

### Which Myrtle Beach oceanfront condo buildings have a lazy river?
Fifteen of the buildings on this page have one. You can float all year at Landmark, Bay View, the Caribbean, Monterey Bay, Grande Cayman, Ocean Reef and Avista, where it is indoors or under a roof. Prince Resort's is on its roof.

### What is the difference between a condotel and a timeshare?
A condotel unit is owned whole, like any condo. A timeshare sells the use of a unit for some weeks a year.

## Carolina Forest, SC: Home Prices, Schools, 11 Subdivisions

Home / Neighborhoods / Carolina Forest
Community guide

# Carolina Forest, SC real estate: home prices, eleven subdivisions, no city tax.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Published July 20, 2026
Carolina Forest is the Myrtle Beach area's biggest master-planned community: 26,000+ residents, eleven subdivisions, no city tax, and no wind-pool insurance surcharge.

The direct answer

## What Carolina Forest is, and why relocating buyers choose it
Carolina Forest is unincorporated Horry County between US 501 and International Drive, master-planned by International Paper in the late 1990s on part of its old 30,000-acre timber tract. It is not a city and pays no city taxes; the mailing address says Myrtle Beach, ZIP 29579, and the beach is a 10-to-15-minute drive. The 2020 Census counted 23,342 residents; the latest Census estimate puts it near 26,263, and 14.5 percent of residents moved in within the past year, roughly ten points above the state's migration rate.
The draw is a combination of four things: twenty years of continuous new construction , single-family prices well below beach product, no municipal millage, and simpler insurance. Insurance is standard homeowner coverage that still includes wind, because most of Carolina Forest is outside the state wind pool's territory. Most of our relocating clients tour it first, and many stop looking after.

The market

## Carolina Forest home prices
County deed records give the prices. In the year to September 2026, a house in Carolina Forest resold for about $440,000 at the middle, on 405 sales. Half sold between about $325,000 and $600,000. A condo resold for about $172,000 at the middle, on 91 sales, and a townhouse for about $230,000, on 34. These are resales in the Census-designated place of Carolina Forest; a builder's first sale is not counted.
Most homes sold here are houses: 405 of the 530 house, condo and townhouse resales. Prices for one community, or one street, are a different number: ask us, and see the July 2026 market report for the region.

The neighborhoods

See what it is like to live in The Farm at Carolina Forest , with its HOA fee, pools, zoned schools and rules.

Schools

## Carolina Forest schools and attendance zones
The attendance area belongs to Horry County Schools: Carolina Forest High School, Ten Oaks and Ocean Bay middle schools, and five elementary schools. Carolina Forest High enrolls about 3,181 students, the fifth-largest public high school in South Carolina, ranked 33rd in the state by U.S. News, with 80 percent math and 91 percent reading proficiency against state averages of 43 and 52.
The growth showed up in the classrooms first: by 2024, Carolina Forest Elementary ran at 136 percent of capacity, Ocean Bay at 144, and River Oaks at 166. The district's answer opened in August 2025: Ten Oaks Elementary ($62.3 million) and Pine Island Elementary ($65.7 million), 1,200 seats each, with 1,920 students reassigned to fill them. Which school serves which subdivision is set by the district's attendance maps, and lines just moved, so we check the current district maps on every showing rather than trusting what a home is advertised as.
Districtwide, Horry County Schools posted 38 of 57 schools rated Excellent or Good on the 2025 state report cards, with none Unsatisfactory, and an 89.6 percent graduation rate.

Costs and risk

## Carolina Forest property taxes, flood zones, and wind insurance
Taxes. Carolina Forest's 2026 levy totals about 201.0 mills: county base 52.1, schools 119.1, fire district 21.7, solid waste 8.1, plus an $89 stormwater fee and a $50 per-vehicle road fee. There is no city millage; Myrtle Beach city residents pay 83.4 additional mills for comparable houses. Owner-occupants at the 4 percent rate are also exempt from the 109.1 school-operating mills, which is most of the bill. Exact numbers for any price: our Horry County property tax calculator .
Flood. Much of the area maps outside FEMA high-risk zones, with Zone AE pockets near ponds and wetlands, so we pull the parcel-level map, in effect since December 16, 2021, on every home. A pond view and a flood requirement are sometimes the same lot; our flood history guide covers how we check what maps do not show.
Wind. Around Myrtle Beach, the state wind pool's territory reaches inland to Carolina Bays Parkway and River Oaks Drive. Most of Carolina Forest is inland of that line, outside the territory, so wind coverage stays inside a standard homeowner policy instead of a separate wind-pool policy. Homes between those roads and the Intracoastal Waterway are inside it. Against a beach address, that is a real annual saving; the full comparison is in our coastal insurance guide .

Renting
Rental data · Carolina Forest
Not a short-term rental market, and that is the point.
The vacation-rental data vendors publish a market report for every coastal Grand Strand town. They do not publish one for Carolina Forest, because there is no nightly-rental market here to measure. It is an inland, master-planned corridor where the HOAs require long leases and the tenants are families following the school zones. Judge it on yearly rent and school attendance, not on nightly rates. See how the coastal submarkets compare .

## Carolina Forest rental rules: long-term leases, not short-term
Horry County has no ordinance against short-term rentals in unincorporated areas, but in Carolina Forest the HOA decides, and the HOAs mostly say no. Avalon's recorded rules prohibit any rental under three months, and communities like Waterbridge are reported to require one-year minimum leases. Buy here for long-term tenants, not nightly guests; the county-by-county legal map is in our short-term rental rules guide .
As a long-term rental play, the corridor works: three-bedroom houses list roughly $1,650 to $2,500 a month against an area three-bedroom average near $1,941, tenant demand follows the school zones, and entry condos offer the highest yields. Run any address through the rental analyzer before you offer.

Growth

## Carolina Forest growth: roads, schools, and new development
The two long-running road complaints are resolved: the $54.7 million Carolina Forest Boulevard widening is complete, four lanes with a multi-use path, and the Postal Way extension is open. The RIDE 4 penny tax that took effect May 1, 2025 funds the next round, including an SC 31 interchange at Augusta Plantation Drive. County planners have also approved a 1,154-unit mixed-use village concept for the area, apartments over retail in the style of Market Common; its construction timing is not yet set.
The area's defining 2025 event was the Covington Drive Fire: 2,059 acres over 95 days, the longest-burning wildfire in South Carolina history, which forced evacuations in eight neighborhoods and destroyed zero homes. It reshaped how this market thinks about defensible space and insurance, and it is part of every honest conversation we have about buying along the preserve edges.

Common questions

## Carolina Forest FAQ

### Is Carolina Forest part of Myrtle Beach?
No. It is unincorporated Horry County with a Myrtle Beach mailing address and ZIP 29579, sitting between Myrtle Beach and Conway. That distinction is worth money: homeowners pay no city property tax, while City of Myrtle Beach residents pay an additional 83.4 municipal mills.

### What schools serve Carolina Forest?
Horry County Schools' Carolina Forest attendance area: Carolina Forest High School, Ten Oaks and Ocean Bay middle schools, and five elementary schools, including Ten Oaks Elementary and Pine Island Elementary, which both opened in August 2025 with 1,200 seats each. Carolina Forest High enrolls about 3,181 students, the fifth-largest high school in South Carolina, ranked 33rd in the state by U.S. News.

### How far is Carolina Forest from the beach?
About 10 to 15 minutes by car to Grand Strand beaches using US 501, SC 31, or International Drive, depending on the neighborhood and the season. It is the trade the area is built on: newer construction and bigger lots than the beach, a short drive from it.

### Is Carolina Forest in a flood zone?
Much of it maps outside FEMA's high-risk zones, but pockets of Zone AE exist near ponds and wetlands, so the parcel matters more than the neighborhood. Check any address against the county flood maps in effect since December 16, 2021. Most of Carolina Forest is inland of Carolina Bays Parkway, outside South Carolina's wind pool territory, so wind coverage stays inside a standard homeowner policy. Homes between Carolina Bays Parkway or River Oaks Drive and the Intracoastal Waterway are inside the territory, where a policy can leave wind out.

### Can you Airbnb a house in Carolina Forest?
Usually not. Horry County does not prohibit short-term rentals in unincorporated areas, but most Carolina Forest HOAs do: Avalon's recorded rules prohibit any rental under three months, and several communities require one-year minimum leases. Treat it as a long-term rental market and verify the covenants of the specific community before buying for rental income.

### What do homes cost in Carolina Forest?
In the year to September 2026, county deed records show houses in Carolina Forest resold for about $440,000 at the middle and condos for about $172,000.

The Farm is a finished neighborhood of houses, townhomes and condos in Carolina Forest, with a Myrtle Beach mailing address.

The short answer
Living in The Farm means a swim after work in pool season and spring walks among wildflowers in a state nature preserve. The county's trails and a rock wall are minutes away by car.
Houses with yards usually sold for about $350,000 in the past year.

## What makes The Farm at Carolina Forest different?
Conway Medical Center planned a $160 million healthcare facility on the 353 acres along The Farm's north edge. The state bought the land instead, for the Lewis Ocean Bay Heritage Preserve .
The preserve is home to South Carolina's largest wild population of Venus flytraps, and the new land holds habitat for them too.
State law says a heritage preserve may not be taken for any private use. Once the land is dedicated, that rules out private homes on it. The state has said it will dedicate it.
Back inside The Farm, the streets follow its farm theme, from Scarecrow Way to Pumpkin Patch Lane.

## What is a normal day like in The Farm at Carolina Forest?
From March through June, a Saturday here can start with a walk in the preserve, among pitcher plants and wildflowers in bloom.
The preserve is open in daylight all year, and the state asks visitors to park and walk its roads. Its main entrance is about 10 minutes by car.
Residents can start a weekday with a workout in the HOA's fitness room, which opens at 5:30 a.m.
A commute to Grand Strand Medical Center, a large hospital, takes about 12 minutes. In our experience, rush hour adds 5 to 10 minutes to the drive times on this page.
The pools stay open until 9 p.m. in season, so there is time for a swim after work. The large pool curves around two small islands of palms, and its wide deck is beside a pond. Owners can also reserve the activity center near it for a private party.
River Oaks Pizzeria is next to Publix, so dinner and groceries can be one stop.
On a free afternoon, the county library and the Carolina Forest Recreation Center share one campus, about 3 minutes away by car. The center has a rock climbing wall and a full gym.
For a longer outing, the county's Bike and Run Park has 7 miles of mountain bike and hiking trails, about 4 minutes by car. Its parking area is a trailhead on the East Coast Greenway, a walking and biking route from Maine to Florida.

Most houses here give you three or four bedrooms and a back yard of your own. A typical lot is about a fifth of an acre.

The Orchards has about 200 townhomes, and Planters Point has about 70 condos, most with two or three bedrooms.
Most houses here are about 20 years old. On any house you tour, we check how old the roof and the air conditioner are.
Over the past year, a typical townhome in The Orchards sold for about $230,000, and a condo in Planters Point about $240,000.

## What are the pros and cons of living in The Farm at Carolina Forest?

### Pros

- Woods along the north edge that belong to the state, not a builder.

- The same three public schools for every home, two of them at its edge.

- Groceries and dinner out without a long drive.

### Cons

- The large pool has sunk more than it should, and the HOA board has not decided whether to repair or replace it. The board can vote a one-time charge to owners, called a special assessment . We read the board's latest minutes on the pool for you.

- Townhomes and condos pay a second HOA fee. We show you both fees side by side for any townhome or condo.

- The preserve allows both hiking and hunting. Deer season runs from mid-September to January 1, and small game to March 1. On burn days, the road to its entrance can close because of the smoke. We show you how far any house is from the preserve's hunting land.

## What are the HOA rules in The Farm at Carolina Forest?
Under the HOA rules , owners can rent their homes with a written lease, and the HOA's governing documents have no cap on how many homes are rented.

- A fence or shed Needs the HOA's approval first, with a land surveyor's drawing of the lot.

- Cars and boats Cars go in the garage or driveway, not on the street or lawn. A boat, trailer or camper needs the HOA's written approval to stay outside.

- Pets Up to three dogs and cats in all. Dogs stay on a leash outside.

- The pools Open April 15 to October 15, with no lifeguard. Up to six guests per home, with the owner there.

Example: The house Rachel and Luis found in The Farm has a big back yard, and they picture a pool in it.

Rachel and Luis buy the house anyway. They swim at The Farm's large pool and plan a hot tub for the yard.

## Was The Farm at Carolina Forest part of an old bombing range?
Yes. From 1942 to 1948, the Army Air Force used the land as a bombing and gunnery range, along with other parts of Carolina Forest. The Army Corps of Engineers has finished the cleanup work on the land under every home in The Farm.
The Corps lists Range III, a section that borders The Farm, as under investigation. It touches some of The Farm's open land, but no home lot.
We check the Corps' map for every lot we show you. If you ever find something that looks like old ammunition, the Defense Department's advice is to leave it alone, move away and call 911.

Common questions

## The Farm at Carolina Forest FAQ

### How much is the HOA fee in The Farm at Carolina Forest?
The HOA fee is $107 a month, or about $1,300 a year. The HOA can raise it by up to 20 percent a year.

### Is The Farm at Carolina Forest a gated community?
No. The Farm is not gated, and its roads are county-owned. Entry to the HOA's pools is by key card.

### When was The Farm at Carolina Forest built?
The Farm was built in stages, on land D.R. Horton added over the years. Most houses were built from 2004 to 2009, and most of the rest about a decade later.

### Is The Farm at Carolina Forest in a high-risk flood zone?
No. Every home in The Farm is outside the high-risk flood zone on the government's flood map. That means federal law does not make your lender require flood insurance. If you want a policy for a house anyway, one in this ZIP code usually costs about $600 a year.

Listing sites get two facts wrong. Bella Vita in Carolina Forest is an all-ages community that attracts retirees, not an age-restricted one. The "Woodside Village" some directories list does not exist here; the community is Woodlake Village.

Restricted vs targeted

## Age-restricted vs age-targeted communities in Myrtle Beach
A true 55+ community has the age rule in its recorded covenants. An age-targeted community is built to appeal to the same buyers without the rule: single-level plans, low-maintenance yards, and an amenity list aimed at the 55+ market, but no age restriction in the deed. Both can be exactly what you want, and they resell differently, because a deed restriction defines the future buyer pool and an age-targeted community does not.
Clients of ours made exactly this move. They owned a single-family home in Blackmoor, the Gary Player golf community in Murrells Inlet, and sold it to buy in Seasons at Prince Creek West, the nearest true 55+ community, a few minutes up the road. Blackmoor carries no age restriction. Seasons is deed-restricted and built around single-level plans and a full amenity program. Their reasoning: a community designed for how you live now is worth moving for, even when the move is only a few miles.
Check the covenant, not the label. Several directories list golf communities like Blackmoor as 55+ when the recorded documents carry no age restriction at all. A listing site is not a covenant. We pull the recorded documents before you offer, for any community on this page.
Seasons at Prince Creek West has a gate at its main entrance, and Myrtle Trace has gates at its back entrance. For every gated neighborhood near Myrtle Beach, with the HOA fees and a map, see our guide to gated communities .

Care continuum

## CCRC and all-inclusive options: Brightwater, Covenant Towers, Lakes at Litchfield
Three properties here work on a different model than a neighborhood HOA. Brightwater in Myrtle Beach is a full continuing-care campus: independent cottages and villas with assisted living, memory care, and skilled nursing on the same grounds. Residents pay a one-time entrance fee, from the low $100,000s for villa apartments to the low $500,000s for cottages, plus a monthly service fee. The Lakes at Litchfield serves the south strand on a similar membership model. Covenant Towers, beside Pine Lakes Country Club, is a 169-unit senior condo high-rise where units list from around $40,000 because the monthly fee covers almost everything: daily dinner, housekeeping, utilities, security, and a shuttle.
The pattern to understand: the cheaper the entry price looks, the more of the real cost lives in the monthly fee or the entrance fee, and CCRC membership is not fee-simple real estate. We walk through the contract type before anyone falls for a number.

The tax case

## South Carolina retirement tax benefits, verified

- &#10003; Social Security: never taxed by South Carolina.

- &#10003; Military retirement pay: 100 percent exempt, at any age, since tax year 2022. Our VA loan guide covers the buying side for veterans.

- &#10003; Retirement income deduction: up to $3,000 a year before 65 and up to $10,000 at 65 and older, per qualifying taxpayer, against pensions, IRA, and 401(k) withdrawals.

- &#10003; Age-65 deduction: up to another $15,000 per person against any income, reduced by whatever retirement deduction you claimed, so the two overlap rather than fully stack.

- &#10003; The Homestead Exemption: at 65, after one full calendar year of South Carolina residency, the first $50,000 of your primary home's market value comes off the property tax rolls, stacked on the 4 percent owner-occupied rate. The full math, with a calculator, is on our Horry County property tax page .

Figures from the South Carolina Department of Revenue and SCDOR Homestead Exemption , current as of July 2026. Not tax advice; bring your CPA the specifics.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach 55+ communities FAQ

### What is the cheapest 55+ community in Myrtle Beach?
For houses, Lakeside Crossing in Conway starts near $190,000, but it is a land-lease community: you own the home and pay lot rent from about $650 a month. For fee-simple ownership, Woodlake Village in Murrells Inlet runs $260,000 to $379,000 with an HOA around $43 a month, and in Myrtle Trace in Conway, homes usually sell for about $300,000, with an HOA fee of $95 a month.

### Is there a Del Webb community in Myrtle Beach?
Two. In Del Webb at Grande Dunes in Myrtle Beach, a house usually sells for about $665,000 and a villa for about $430,000, and the HOA dues include the oceanfront Grande Dunes Ocean Club. Del Webb North Myrtle Beach is the only large 55+ community still building new homes. From October 2025 to September 2026, its new homes from the builder usually sold for about $635,000.

### What does land-lease mean at Lakeside Crossing?
You buy and own the house, but you rent the ground under it from Sun Communities, starting near $650 a month. The rent covers the amenity campus, lawn care, and trash, there is no HOA, and buyers must be approved for the lease before closing. The homes cost far less than fee-simple 55+ houses, and the trade is that lot rent continues forever and can rise.

### Which Myrtle Beach 55+ communities are gated?
In Myrtle Trace, the front entrance on Burning Ridge Road has no gate, and the back entrance on Myrtle Ridge Road has gates. Most of the area's 55+ communities, including Woodlake Village, are not gated. For any other community, ask the HOA how its entrance works today.

### Does South Carolina tax retirement income?
Lightly. Social Security is not taxed at all, and military retirement pay is 100 percent exempt. Other retirement income gets a deduction of up to $3,000 before 65 and up to $10,000 at 65 and older. A separate age-65 deduction of up to $15,000 per person overlaps with the retirement deduction rather than fully stacking.

### What happens to property taxes at 65 in South Carolina?
After one full calendar year as a South Carolina resident, the Homestead Exemption removes the first $50,000 of your primary home's market value from property tax at age 65, on top of the owner-occupied 4 percent assessment rate. On a typical Grand Strand home that combination produces some of the lowest tax bills on the East Coast.

## What is a month like in Myrtle Trace?
In a normal month in Myrtle Trace, you can play bingo, swim, fish and play in a league. The rest is on the neighborhood's calendar .

- Bingo and game nights Bingo two Friday nights a month, and a game night on Sundays

- The pool Open every day 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., until the start of October

- Bocce and shuffleboard A bocce league and a shuffleboard league you can join

- Fishing Ponds where you and your guests fish and let the fish go. You cannot swim or take a boat in the ponds.

## What are the homes like in Myrtle Trace?
Most homes in Myrtle Trace are one-story houses with their own yards, and a few are townhouses. Most were built in the 1980s and 1990s.

## Myrtle Trace FAQ

### Is Myrtle Trace a gated community?
Only in part. The front entrance is always open. The HOA put gates on the back entrance so drivers do not cut through the neighborhood.

### How much is the HOA fee in Myrtle Trace?
The HOA fee is $95 a month. The HOA uses it to keep up the pool, the clubhouse, the gates, the roads it owns, the ponds and the shared land.

### Is Myrtle Trace South part of Myrtle Trace?
No. Myrtle Trace South and Myrtle Trace Grande are separate neighborhoods, each with its own HOA. The fee and rules on this page are for Myrtle Trace.

### Who runs the Myrtle Trace HOA?
The owners run the Myrtle Trace HOA themselves, with volunteers. There is no management company.

### Is the golf course part of Myrtle Trace?
No. Burning Ridge Golf Club, next door, is privately owned and is not part of the HOA. Some Myrtle Trace homes back onto it.

### Can you fish in the Myrtle Trace ponds?
Yes. Residents and their house guests can fish from the shared land around the 15 ponds. You let every fish go.

### Do you need flood insurance in Myrtle Trace?
Probably not. No home here is in a high-risk flood zone. If you want a policy, it usually costs about $550 a year.

### Is Myrtle Trace inside Conway city limits?
No. Myrtle Trace has a Conway mailing address but is outside the city, so owners there pay no Conway city tax.

# Myrtle Beach golf communities, where membership is optional.

Fourteen Myrtle Beach golf communities compared: club membership is almost never required, fees start at $35 a month, entry from $150,000 condos, and the Intracoastal flood zones that surprise buyers.

The direct answer

## Myrtle Beach golf community membership is optional almost everywhere
The Grand Strand has more than 80 championship courses, and most golf-community homes here are on public courses. Arrowhead, Wild Wing, Blackmoor, Legends, International Club, Wachesaw East, and TPC Myrtle Beach all sell tee times to anyone, so living there requires no membership at all. Where clubs exist, membership is a choice: Barefoot, Prestwick, Pawleys Plantation, and Grande Dunes all separate homeownership from club dues.
The two real exceptions run in opposite directions. Wachesaw Plantation is private and member-owned, and while you can own without joining, every amenity belongs to the club, so a non-member owns a house behind a gate and nothing else. The Dunes Club is private, with limited package access, and its surrounding streets are some of the only prestige addresses here with no mandatory HOA. Details like those matter more than the name of the course designer when you are picking a community.

The fine print

## What Myrtle Beach golf community buyers miss

- &#10003; Transfer fees ride with the deed, not the listing. At Barefoot, a resale that carries a golf membership means a $2,750 transfer fee and a 60-day enrollment window after closing. Ask what obligations attach to the specific lot before you offer, not at the closing table.

- &#10003; The Intracoastal view can carry a flood premium. Waterway-adjacent pockets of Grande Dunes, Barefoot, and Arrowhead can sit in FEMA Zone AE, where lenders require flood insurance. The fairway lots a street inland often do not. Our coastal insurance guide covers what that costs; we pull the flood zone on every golf lot we show.

- &#10003; A public course means no membership obligation. Public-course communities like Blackmoor pair a Gary Player design with a $35 monthly HOA and no club dues at all. Clients of ours owned a home in Blackmoor, then sold it and bought in Seasons at Prince Creek West, a 55+ community a few minutes away. That side is covered on our 55+ communities page .

- &#10003; Second-home rules still apply on the fairway. A golf villa you use part-time is a second home or investment property to the county and the lender: the 6 percent tax rate, second-home loan occupancy rules, and rental restrictions all still run. The math is in our second home guide and property tax calculator .

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach golf communities FAQ

### Do you have to join the club to live in a Myrtle Beach golf community?
Almost never. Membership is optional at Barefoot, Prestwick, Pawleys Plantation, and even private Wachesaw Plantation, though non-members there get no amenities since everything belongs to the club. Where the course is public, like Arrowhead, Wild Wing, Blackmoor, Legends, International Club, and TPC Myrtle Beach, there is no membership to join at all.

### How many golf courses does Myrtle Beach have?
More than 80 championship courses, per Visit Myrtle Beach's current figure. The 100-course number still quoted around the internet is outdated. The oldest is Pine Lakes International, opened 1927; the most famous is the Dunes Golf and Beach Club, a 1948 Robert Trent Jones Sr. design that hosts the PGA Tour's Myrtle Beach Classic.

### What is the Barefoot Resort golf transfer fee?
Resale buyers of Barefoot homes that carry a golf membership pay a $2,750 transfer fee to Barefoot Resort Golf Club, with enrollment required within 60 days of closing. Dues run $205 a month for golf and social access or $85 for social only, covering the Dye, Love, Fazio, and Norman courses.

### Is TPC Myrtle Beach private?
No. It is the only TPC in South Carolina and it welcomes public play, which is rare for the brand. It anchors the Prince Creek master plan in Murrells Inlet, where villages range from the low $300,000s to the $600,000s and up, including the Seasons 55+ community.

### Which Myrtle Beach golf communities are gated with a guard?
Tidewater Plantation, Wachesaw Plantation, Willbrook Plantation and DeBordieu Colony have a guard gate or guard house. Grande Dunes and Barefoot Resort are gated only in some sections. Our guide to gated communities near Myrtle Beach has the map.

### What is the cheapest golf community in Myrtle Beach?
Legends' Turnberry Park condos at $150,000 to $215,000 and Arrowhead condos from about $175,000 are the verified low end for buying in. For houses, Blackmoor pairs a Gary Player course with roughly a $35 monthly HOA, the lowest fee we verified in any Grand Strand golf community.

# South Carolina closing costs calculator: buyers pay about 2 to 5 percent.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Published July 20, 2026
Buyers in South Carolina typically pay 2 to 5 percent of the price in closing costs and prepaids. Run both sides of the closing with real Horry County numbers.
Calculate my closing costs

The direct answer

## Who pays what at a South Carolina closing
Buyers pay the lender's fees, the closing attorney, both title insurance policies, recording, inspections, and the prepaid items: the first year of homeowners insurance plus escrow deposits for taxes and insurance. All-in, plan on roughly 2 to 5 percent of the purchase price on top of the down payment.
Horry County conventional purchase loans, 2025 At the middle
Loan costs paid by the buyer: the lender's charges, the lender's title policy, the attorney and the appraisal About $5,000
The lender's own origination charges About 0.9 percent of the loan
The owner's title policy, taxes, recording and the prepaid items On top of the loan costs

Sellers pay the commission they negotiated, the deed recording fee of $1.85 per $500 of price, deed preparation, their mortgage payoff, and any HOA document or transfer fees the contract assigns them. South Carolina has no separate state or local transfer tax beyond the deed stamps, which keeps seller costs lower than in most coastal states.

The seller's tax

## SC deed stamps: $1.85 per $500, and the seller pays
South Carolina's transfer tax is the deed recording fee: $1.85 per $500 of the price, split $1.30 to the state and $0.55 to the county, and state law makes the seller pay it. That is $1,110 on a $300,000 sale and $1,480 on a $400,000 sale, about 0.37 percent, modest by coastal-state standards. Horry County's own recording charges are flat under its predictable-fee schedule: $15 for a deed, $25 for a mortgage. The statute is S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 24 ; exemptions exist for transfers under $100, family court transfers, and foreclosure deeds.

The attorney and the title

## Why South Carolina closings include an attorney and what title insurance costs
South Carolina is an attorney-closing state. Since a 1987 state Supreme Court ruling, a licensed South Carolina attorney has to run the closing. The attorney checks the title, prepares the paperwork, closes the sale, records the deed, and pays everyone out. Residential closing fees typically run $600 to $1,200. The buyer customarily chooses and pays the closing attorney. This is a feature, not a tax. The attorney is the person who finds title problems before they become your problems.
Title insurance rates are set by each insurance company and filed with the state, so they vary a little from one to the next. The lender's policy is added for about $100 to $150 when issued simultaneously.
Ask about two discounts. The reissue rate applies when the seller can produce a prior owner's policy under ten years old. The enhanced-versus-standard choice changes both price and coverage. Your closing attorney's underwriter quote governs.

The Horry County wrinkle

## Horry County tax escrow: billed in arrears, set at your rate
Horry County bills property taxes after the fact, not up front: bills go out around October 1 and are due January 15, and penalties start after that. At closing the seller credits you for their share of the year, and your lender starts collecting escrow months ahead of the first bill it will pay. That is why the escrow deposit can be the biggest line on the statement.
The expensive mistake is letting anyone set that escrow from the seller's old bill. Your first full bill will be computed on your price and your rate class. It is 4 percent with the school-operating exemption if this is your legal residence and you file the application. It is 6 percent with the full school tax if it is not. On a $400,000 second home, that is the difference between roughly $1,500 and $4,800 or more a year, depending on the district. The calculator above escrows at your future rate on purpose; the complete math lives in our Horry County property tax calculator .

VA buyers

## VA loans: the funding fee and the fees veterans never pay
The VA funding fee for purchases is a one-time percentage of the loan. Two things set it: whether it is your first VA use, and how much you choose to put down. A first use with nothing down is high on the schedule. A second use with nothing down is the highest tier. A larger down payment lowers it. The fee is almost always financed rather than paid in cash. Your lender quotes the exact figure with your Loan Estimate. Veterans receiving service-connected disability compensation, Purple Heart recipients on active duty, and eligible surviving spouses are exempt.
VA rules also cap what lenders can charge. A lender may charge a flat origination fee of up to 1 percent of the loan. If it does, it cannot also charge separate processing, underwriting or document fees. A veteran can never be charged a tax service fee, lender attorney fees, or prepayment penalties. Where a normally buyer-paid charge is non-allowable, the seller or lender credit picks it up. That is a negotiation point your agent should be making. The full picture is in our VA loan guide .

Common questions

## South Carolina closing costs FAQ

### How much are closing costs in South Carolina?
Buyers typically pay roughly 2 to 5 percent of the price in closing costs and prepaids, covering lender fees, the attorney, title insurance, and escrow deposits. Federal loan records for Horry County put the loan costs paid by the buyer on the middle conventional purchase in 2025 at about $5,000, before the owner's title policy, taxes, recording and prepaids. Sellers pay the commission they negotiate plus about 0.37 percent in deed stamps and small document fees.

### Who pays the transfer tax in South Carolina?
The seller, by statute. South Carolina's deed recording fee is $1.85 per $500 of price, which is $1,480 on a $400,000 sale, and state law makes it the grantor's liability. It is often called deed stamps or transfer tax; the money splits $1.30 to the state and $0.55 to the county.

### Do I need an attorney to close on a house in South Carolina?
Yes. The South Carolina Supreme Court requires a licensed attorney to supervise real estate closings, including the title work, document preparation, recording, and disbursement. Residential closing fees typically run $600 to $1,200, and the buyer customarily selects and pays the closing attorney.

### What is a CL-100 letter?
South Carolina's official wood infestation report, covering termites and wood-destroying organisms. Most lenders require one, it typically costs about $75 to $150, and it is ordered near closing because it is valid for roughly 45 days. Homes with crawl spaces are the ones to watch.

### Why is my Horry County tax escrow so high?
Two reasons. Taxes here are billed in arrears, mailed October 1 and due January 15, so the lender collects months of them up front. If the home will not be your legal residence, it is assessed at the 6 percent ratio with the full school operating tax, several times the seller's 4 percent bill. A correct escrow is built on your future bill, not the seller's old one.

### What is the VA funding fee in 2026?
A one-time percentage of the loan that varies with first or subsequent VA use and with any down payment you choose to make; more down means a smaller fee. Veterans receiving service-connected disability compensation are exempt. The fee is almost always financed into the loan rather than paid in cash.

The strategy

## Pricing a Myrtle Beach condo to its real buyer pool
The type of building you own limits who can get a loan to buy your condo. A unit in a building that passes a lender's review can sell to any financed buyer. A unit in a hotel-style oceanfront tower usually cannot. FHA and VA buyers are almost never an option there, since only eight condo projects in all of Horry County were FHA-approved as of July 2026, and none were oceanfront. Regular conventional loans often fail the building review too. The real buyers for that tower are cash buyers, and DSCR or portfolio-loan buyers making large down payments. Unpaid assessments follow the unit, so request an estoppel statement: see liens and unpaid dues .
Across the country, about a third of recent home sales were all cash, mostly vacation-home buyers and investors. That is exactly who buys here. This is not bad news. It is useful information about which buyers to target. A condo priced and marketed to buyers who can close will not waste 30 to 45 days on a loan that was never going to fund, in a market where condos already averaged 137 days to an accepted offer.
This is where we are different. Our affiliated lender, BrickWood Mortgage, a separate company, arranges condotel and non-warrantable loans through wholesale lenders that accept these buildings. When a buyer's agent asks how someone could finance your unit, we have an answer instead of a dead end. That widens your buyer pool in exactly the buildings where other listings lose buyers. Start by finding your building in our oceanfront building directory .

The building review

## How an HOA master policy can stop a condo sale
A lender reviews the building as well as the buyer. An underinsured master policy is one of the things that can make a building fail that review partway through a loan, for reasons that have nothing to do with the unit, the buyer or the seller.
Those lessons apply to sellers too. Your building's insurance, reserves, and paperwork habits are part of your listing whether you like it or not. We check all of this before we list your home, because a problem like this can cost you money in negotiations if the buyer's agent finds it before we do.

The law

## What South Carolina law requires a condo seller to disclose

- &#10003; Give the buyer the disclosure before they sign. South Carolina makes you hand the buyer a Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement before the contract is signed. Since 2018 it includes an HOA section, where you list the fees, assessments, and rental rules. The law is S.C. Code Title 27, Chapter 50 .

- &#10003; List every future booking in writing before the contract is final. If the unit is a vacation rental, state law makes you disclose all upcoming bookings in writing before the contract is ratified. The buyer must honor any booking that starts within 90 days of closing, so those guests keep their reservations.

- &#10003; There is no resale certificate in South Carolina. Unlike Florida or Texas, the state has no required resale package. The buyer relies on the recorded master deed, the bylaws, the budget, and whatever the contract asks for. Who pays each HOA fee is just a checkbox in the standard state contract.

The paperwork

## Myrtle Beach condo HOA documents and third-party fees
Estoppel letters, transfer fees, and capital contributions differ by community. A transfer fee is only legal if the building's documents allow it, and slow document companies are a common reason closings run late.
Two things protect a condo seller. First, find out on day one whether your association uses an outside document company and what it charges. Second, order the document package the week you list, not the week you go under contract. If you are also buying, check the same thing on the building you are buying into, because these fees apply to purchases and refinances alike.

Bookings and furniture

## Selling a rental condo with future bookings
A full booking calendar usually helps you, it does not hurt. The rental history and upcoming bookings prove the unit's income to an investor buyer, which is what a DSCR loan is based on, and our Airbnb income report shows what buyers will compare your numbers to. As a rule, deposits for stays after closing pass to the buyer at closing , rental income is split at the closing date, and oceanfront units are sold furnished with an inventory list. Your contract controls all three, so put them in writing rather than assume them.
Showings work around guests. In peak season, a booked week is often shown with photos, video, and a floor plan instead of in person. That matters less than it sounds, because most buyers for these units live out of state and shop online anyway. That is why our out-of-state marketing matters more for condos than for any house.

### What do I legally have to disclose when selling a condo in South Carolina?
The South Carolina Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement, including its owners-association addendum covering fees, assessments, and rental restrictions, delivered before the purchase contract is signed. If the unit takes vacation rentals, state law also requires written disclosure of every future booked rental period before the contract is ratified.

### What happens to my rental bookings when I sell my condo?
Under South Carolina's Vacation Rental Act, the buyer takes title subject to bookings that begin within 90 days of the deed being recorded, so those guests keep their reservations. Bookings further out than 90 days do not bind the buyer unless the contract says so, and every future booked period must be disclosed in writing before ratification.

### Do I need a resale certificate to sell a condo in South Carolina?
No. South Carolina has no statutory resale certificate or estoppel package like some states. Buyers rely on the recorded master deed and bylaws plus whatever documents the contract requires, and fee allocation for HOA paperwork is negotiated by checkbox in the standard SC contract.

### Why did my condo buyer's loan fall through?
Usually the building, not the buyer. Conventional lenders review the project: hotel-style rental operations, an underinsured master policy, low reserves, or litigation can each make the building ineligible mid-transaction. Knowing how your building reviews before you list, and having a lender who can finance it anyway, prevents the 30 to 45 days a doomed contract wastes.

## SC Capital Gains Tax on a Home Sale: 2026 Rate and Withholding
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/sell/capital-gains/
Summary: SC taxes long-term gains at about 2.92% after its 44% deduction. Out-of-state sellers face 5.21% withholding at closing; Form I-295 cuts it to the gain.

Home / Sell / Capital Gains
Tax guide and calculator · 2026 law

# Capital gains tax when you sell in South Carolina.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Published July 20, 2026
South Carolina taxes long-term gains at an effective 2.92 percent for 2026 after its 44 percent deduction, and primary residences usually owe nothing. Out-of-state sellers meet a withholding at closing.
Estimate my taxes

The direct answer

## The three layers of tax on a South Carolina home sale
Federal: long-term gains are taxed at 0, 15, or 20 percent depending on income. For 2026, the 0 percent bracket runs to $49,450 of taxable income single and $98,900 married filing jointly, and the 15 percent bracket to $545,500 and $613,700. High earners add a 3.8 percent surtax. If you rented the home out and wrote off wear and tear over the years (called depreciation), the IRS taxes that part back at up to 25 percent when you sell. A primary residence excludes up to $250,000 single or $500,000 married under Section 121 if you owned and lived in it two of the last five years. How the basis and the depreciation were set at purchase is on our rental depreciation page .
South Carolina: the state deducts 44 percent of net long-term gains and taxes the rest at its new 2026 top rate of 5.21 percent, an effective rate of roughly 2.92 percent. Anything the federal exclusion wipes out, South Carolina never sees.
At the closing table, for out-of-state sellers only: South Carolina collects early. The withholding described below is the piece that surprises absentee owners, and it is manageable with one form.

The withholding

## The SC nonresident withholding: Form I-290, Form I-295, and why the affidavit is everything
When a nonresident sells South Carolina real estate, state law requires the buyer to withhold tax at closing. The closing attorney often does this for the buyer and sends it to the Department of Revenue on Form I-290 by the 15th of the following month. Since a 2024 law change, that rate simply matches South Carolina's top income tax rate: 5.21 percent for a 2026 sale, or 5 percent for a corporation. The old 7 percent figure still on many websites is wrong. A Canadian seller also has a federal withholding, covered on our page on what happens when a Canadian sells a rental here .
What the rate applies to is the part sellers can control. Sign the Form I-295 seller's affidavit stating your actual gain, and the withholding is 5.21 percent of the gain. Skip it, and the buyer has to withhold 5.21 percent of the whole sale price (minus your selling costs), capped only by the cash you would walk away with after paying off the mortgage. On a $400,000 sale with a $186,000 gain, that is the difference between roughly $9,700 withheld and roughly $19,600.
Either way it is a prepayment, not the tax. The withholding math ignores the 44 percent deduction, so it almost always takes too much. You file a South Carolina return, report the gain with the deduction, list the amount already withheld, and the state sends back the difference. The withheld amount works like a big W-2. The I-295 also covers the full exemptions: no withholding for a Section 121 primary residence, a 1031 exchange with full deferral, or a certified zero gain, which is exactly the situation of most heirs selling at stepped-up basis. Forms: I-290 and I-295 ; statute: S.C. Code 12-8-580 .

Worked example

## An illustrative example: the Ohio owner selling a $400,000 rental
This is a constructed example, not a client. An Ohio resident sells a Myrtle Beach rental for $400,000 that was bought for $250,000, with $60,000 of depreciation taken and 6 percent selling costs. Amount realized: $376,000. Adjusted basis: $190,000. Gain: $186,000, of which $60,000 is depreciation recapture taxed federally at 25 percent and $126,000 is long-term gain, typically at 15 percent, roughly $33,900 federal before any net investment income tax.
South Carolina taxes 56 percent of the $186,000, about $104,160, at 5.21 percent: roughly $5,400. At closing, with a signed I-295 gain affidavit, about $9,700 is withheld; without one, about $19,600. After filing the South Carolina nonresident return, the affidavit seller gets roughly $4,300 back. Ohio then generally credits the South Carolina tax against its own.
The pattern to remember: the withholding is always bigger than the final South Carolina tax on a long-term gain, the affidavit controls how much bigger, and the refund requires filing. Nobody at a closing table volunteers this; your closing attorney and CPA handle it well when someone puts it on their desk early. We put it there early.

Ways around and out

## Section 121, 1031, and stepped-up basis: the exclusions that cut the tax

- &#10003; Primary residence: up to $250,000 single and $500,000 married of gain simply is not taxed, federally or by South Carolina, if you owned and lived there two of the last five years. The window keeps working for up to three years after you move away, which matters to people who relocated and then decided to sell. Selling in a divorce? Our guide to selling a house during a divorce in South Carolina has the three choices and the tax.

- &#10003; Inherited property: basis steps up to date-of-death value, so selling soon after inheriting usually produces little or no gain. The problem is the withholding on nonresident heirs, solved by the I-295 affidavit; the rest of that process is in our inherited house guide .

- &#10003; 1031 exchange: a fully deferred exchange pays no tax now and no withholding at closing, certified on the same affidavit. Miss a deadline and the tax comes due; see the 1031 guide and the hands-off DST alternative .

- &#10003; Depreciation is the asterisk on everything: every dollar you claimed, or could have claimed, on a rental comes back at up to 25 percent federally and is never covered by the primary-residence exclusion, even if you moved back in. Converted properties need a CPA's eyes before you count your net.

## Plan the South Carolina tax before you list.
We put the I-295 on your CPA's desk early, price the sale with the real net in view, and reach the out-of-state buyers who dominate this market. Absentee sales are half of what we do.

Common questions

## SC capital gains and withholding FAQ

### Does South Carolina tax capital gains on a home sale?
Yes, but gently: South Carolina deducts 44 percent of a net long-term capital gain, so only 56 percent is taxed. At the new 5.21 percent top rate for 2026 that works out to an effective rate of about 2.92 percent on long-term gains, on top of whatever federal tax applies.

### What is South Carolina's income tax rate for 2026?
Two brackets under the law signed March 30, 2026: 1.99 percent on taxable income up to $30,000 and 5.21 percent above it. The 2025 top rate was 6.0 percent. Further automatic cuts can trigger from 2027 if state revenue targets are met.

### How much does South Carolina withhold when an out-of-state owner sells?
The buyer's side withholds at South Carolina's top individual rate for the year of the sale, 5.21 percent for 2026 closings, or 5 percent for corporations. With a signed Form I-295 gain affidavit, the rate applies only to your actual gain. Without one, it applies to the entire amount realized, capped at your net proceeds.

### Is the South Carolina withholding an extra tax?
No. It is a prepayment. The withholding ignores the 44 percent gain deduction, so it nearly always over-collects; you claim the withheld amount as a credit on a South Carolina nonresident return and receive the difference back. Most long-term sellers are owed a refund.

### Do I pay the withholding when selling my primary residence?
No, if the gain is excluded under the federal Section 121 primary-residence exclusion, up to $250,000 single or $500,000 married. You certify the exclusion on Form I-295 and no withholding applies, even if you have already moved out of state, as long as you are within the exclusion's two-of-five-year window.

### What if I inherit a house in South Carolina and sell it?
Your basis steps up to the date-of-death value, so the taxable gain is usually small or zero. But the withholding still applies by default for nonresident heirs: without a gain affidavit, 5.21 percent of the whole sale price gets withheld and you wait for a refund. The I-295 affidavit certifying the near-zero gain is what prevents that; our inherited house guide covers the rest.

## Condo Master Policy vs HO-6 in Myrtle Beach: What to Buy
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/master-insurance-ho6/
Summary: What a Myrtle Beach condo's master policy covers, how much HO-6 your lender wants, what a storm deductible could cost you, and when to add flood cover.

Home / HOA Guide / Master Policy and HO-6
The HOA guide

# Condo master policy vs HO-6 in Myrtle Beach: what each covers, and how much to buy.

- Your own HO-6 About $800 a year

- Your unit flood policy About $495 a year

- Example share, 5% storm deductible About $6,500

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 12, 2026
The building's policy, your own HO-6, the storm deductible and flood, with Fannie Mae's rules and FEMA's numbers for Horry County condos.

The short answer
The condo building's master policy, paid through your condo fee, insures the structure and the shared areas. Your HO-6 insures your belongings, your liability, and whatever the master policy leaves out inside your unit.
On this coast, ask first for the building's storm deductible. For a typical Horry condo building of 10 or more units, a 5 percent storm deductible split evenly would come to about $6,500 for each owner. A basic condo policy pays only a small set amount toward that bill, unless you buy a higher limit.

- Master policy and HO-6 FAQ

## What is the difference between a condo master policy and an HO-6?
A condo master policy is the insurance the condo association buys for the whole building. You pay your share of it through the condo fee. An HO-6 is the policy you buy for your own unit.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Roofs, balconies and a pool on oceanfront buildings in North Myrtle Beach, seen from a plane. A condo master policy insures parts like these.

South Carolina's condo law requires the association to insure the property. It also gives each owner the right to insure their own unit. An HO-6 insures your belongings, the improvements made to your unit, and your liability.
Who insures what in a condo: the building's master policy and your HO-6 What Building's master policy Your HO-6
The roof, the outside walls, the halls, the elevators and the pool Building's policy Yes Your HO-6 No
Cabinets, floors and fixtures inside your unit, as built Building's policy Depends on the building Your HO-6 When the building's policy leaves them out
Upgrades you or an earlier owner made Building's policy Only in an all-in policy Your HO-6 Yes
Your furniture, clothes and other belongings Building's policy No Your HO-6 Yes

About 8 in 10 oceanfront condos for sale list insurance among what the condo fee includes. Our page on what HOA fees cover breaks the fee down.
Owners who live in their condo here pay about $800 a year for their own policy.

## Does the condo master policy cover the inside of my unit?
There are three kinds of master policy. Two of them cover some of the inside of your unit. The building's recorded papers usually say which kind applies:

- Bare walls. The association insures the structure and the shared areas. You insure the building parts inside your unit, such as sinks, built-in cabinets, appliances, flooring and wall coverings, and any upgrades.

- Single entity. The association also insures the fixtures in each unit as built. You insure your belongings and your own upgrades.

- All in. The association also insures the upgrades owners made. You insure your belongings.

Some agents say "walls in" for single entity, and some use it for the owner's own policy. We go by the building's papers, not the label.

### How do I find out which kind my building has?
South Carolina's condo law does not say where the association's policy stops inside a unit. The building's own papers do: the insurance section of its recorded founding papers, and its policy's declarations page.
With bare walls, a new kitchen or a tiled floor is yours to insure.
Know what the building's policy leaves to you
Send us the building's name. We get its recorded papers and its policy's declarations page, and tell you what your HO-6 must insure.
Have us read the building's insurance section

## How much HO-6 coverage do I need for my mortgage?
For most conventional loans, your HO-6 must insure at least what the building's policy leaves out inside your unit, or the building's per-unit deductible, whichever is more. Fannie Mae's rules for the HO-6, in full:

- When you need one When the building's policy leaves out any part of the inside of your unit, or charges a deductible to each unit.

- How much it must insure At least the larger of two amounts: what it costs to restore what the building's policy leaves out, or the building's per-unit deductible.

- How it pays At replacement cost, the cost to restore your unit as it was.

- Its own deductible At most 5 percent of its coverage or $2,500, whichever is more.

- Wind If the building's per-unit deductible is for one peril, such as wind, your HO-6 must cover that peril.

Fannie Mae's rules are not a law. An FHA or VA loan, a loan the lender keeps, or a cash purchase can have other rules.
Fannie Mae has rules for the building's policy too. Its deductible can be at most 5 percent of what it insures.
A deductible charged to each unit can be at most $50,000. Our page on condos most lenders will not lend on explains what a building that misses these rules means for a loan.

### Does an HO-6 cover wind and hail?
Near the ocean, it may not. East of U.S. 17 or Bypass 17, whichever is farther west, an insurer may leave wind out of a policy. You can then buy wind cover on its own, for example from the state's wind and hail pool.
When we get you an insurance quote, we ask that it include wind. Our page on coastal insurance in Myrtle Beach explains the state's wind and hail pool.

## Does an HO-6 cover the master policy deductible?
Sometimes. The part of an HO-6 that can pay your share of the building's deductible is its loss assessment coverage. It pays your share, up to its limit, and nothing above it.
On this coast, the deductible to ask about is the one for storms. A building's policy can have a separate wind or named storm deductible. For a loan Fannie Mae buys, it must meet the same 5 percent limit.
A 5 percent storm deductible could bill each owner about $6,500 Storm deductible, note One owner's share

A 1 percent storm deductible About $1,300
A 2 percent storm deductible About $2,600
A 5 percent storm deductible · the most Fannie Mae allows About $6,500

Example: a building insured for about $131,000 a unit, the middle rebuild cost for Horry condo buildings of 10 or more units, with the bill split evenly.
A basic condo policy pays only a small set amount toward your share of an association's assessment, unless you buy a higher limit.
Before you close, we put the building's storm deductible, in dollars, next to the loss assessment limit on your HO-6 quote. If the limit is smaller, we ask for a quote with a higher one.
We also ask the insurance agent, in writing, whether the policy pays an assessment that comes from the association's storm deductible. The answer depends on the policy.
How a deductible is split among owners, and who pays after a leak or a fire, is on our page on who pays for condo damage . When the association bills every owner for it, that bill is a special assessment .

### How to spot a storm deductible on the policy
South Carolina requires any home or building policy with a separate hurricane, named storm or wind deductible to say so in capital letters, on its front and on its declarations page. The rule applies to the association's policy too.
The sentence starts:
THIS POLICY CONTAINS A SEPARATE DEDUCTIBLE FOR HURRICANE, NAMED STORM OR WIND/HAIL LOSSES, WHICH MAY RESULT IN HIGH OUT-OF-POCKET EXPENSES TO YOU.
A named storm is a hurricane, tropical storm or tropical depression named by the National Weather Service or the National Hurricane Center. If your HO-6 has a separate storm deductible, the insurer must show you, when you buy it and at each renewal, how it works on a $100,000 policy.
Know your share of a storm bill before you close
Send us the building. We get its storm deductible and tell you the loss assessment limit that pays your share.
Have us compare the deductible to your quote

## How does flood insurance work on a Myrtle Beach condo?
Your HO-6 most likely does not cover flood. Most homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage. Flood cover is its own policy.
The building's flood policy does not insure your furniture or belongings either. A flood policy on your own unit can, if you buy contents cover. It can also pay your share of a flood assessment from the association.
When to add your own flood policy: if a flood would leave you replacing what is in the unit. A unit flood policy here cost a middle of about $495 a year.

### The building's flood policy
The federal flood program sells two flood policies for a condo. One goes to the association for the building, called an RCBAP. The other goes to an owner for a unit.
The building's policies on Horry condos, in FEMA's latest full year:

- Insured close to full value Of the 702 that report a rebuild cost, 701 meet the program's 80 percent rule. A building insured for less than that gets a smaller payment after a flood.

- Often at the top limit 276 of 1,172 buy $250,000 a unit, the program's top limit.

- A small deductible 832 of 1,172 carry a $1,250 deductible. Another 105 carry $25,000.

- Your share of the cost A middle of about $405 a unit a year, paid through the condo fee. Our page on HOA fees shows the rest of the fee.

- Contents Only property the owners share or the association owns. 151 of 1,172 buy any.

### Your own flood policy on a unit
You can buy your own federal flood policy on your unit, even when the building has one. Half the unit policies here cost between about $370 and $640 a year.
About 3 in 4 of these unit policies were outside FEMA's high-risk flood zones. The two policies together pay at most $250,000 for one unit, and pay for the same damage only once.
A unit flood policy pays your share of a flood assessment from the association, up to its building limit. It does not pay an assessment that comes from the association's own flood deductible.
That deductible is usually small, as the list above shows.

## What should I ask for before I buy a condo, and when?
Get the building's papers first, then have your HO-6 written once, at the right size. Your lender checks that your policy is big enough. The right size comes from what the building's policy leaves out.
Buying a policy before you know means paying to redo it, and that can hold up your closing. We read these papers, in this order:

- The insurance section of the condo's founding papers It says which kind of master policy the building has.

- The declarations page of the building's policy It shows the amount insured and every deductible, with any separate one for wind.

- The per-unit deductible, if there is one Your lender sizes your HO-6 against it.

- The building's flood policy and its deductible Most are $1,250; some are $25,000.

- The loss assessment limit on your HO-6 quote It should be enough to pay your share of the storm deductible.

- The budget and the reserves Money the building has saved for repairs. Our page on condo reserves explains how much is enough.

- The statement of what the seller owes The association's letter on unpaid dues, explained on our page on what the seller still owes the HOA .

If you buy with us, we get you an insurance quote for the address before you make an offer. Insurance is a commodity: we recommend the cheapest policy that satisfies you and your lender.
If you will rent the unit out, our page on landlord insurance on a Myrtle Beach rental covers the policy for a rental.

Common questions

## Master policy and HO-6 FAQ

### Do I need an HO-6 if the HOA has a master policy?
For most conventional loans, yes, when the master policy leaves out any part of the inside of your unit or charges a deductible to each unit. Your belongings are yours to insure under every kind of master policy.

### Is HO-6 insurance required in South Carolina?
Not by state law. South Carolina's condo law requires the association to insure the building and lets each owner insure their own unit. A lender usually requires an HO-6.

### How much is HO-6 insurance in Myrtle Beach?
Owners in Horry County pay about $800 a year for their own condo policy. A flood policy on the unit, if you buy one, cost a middle of about $495 a year.

### How much loss assessment coverage should I have?
Enough to pay your share of the building's storm deductible. There is no legal minimum, so the number printed on your policy is the number you have. In a typical Horry building of 10 or more units, each owner's even share of a 5 percent storm deductible is about $6,500.

### Does my HO-6 cover flood?
Most likely not. Most homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage, and the building's flood policy does not insure your belongings. A flood policy on your unit can, and here it cost a middle of about $495 a year.

### What is an RCBAP?
The Residential Condominium Building Association Policy, the federal flood policy a condo association buys on its building. It does not insure owners' furniture or belongings.

## Who Pays for Water Damage in a Condo (SC) | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/who-pays-for-damage/
Summary: In a South Carolina condo the HOA insures and repairs the building. Costs above insurance are split among all owners. Here is who pays.

Home / HOA Guide / Who Pays for Damage
Damage and liability

# Who pays for water damage in a condo on the Grand Strand
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge, 30+ years on the Grand Strand · Updated November 12, 2026
In a South Carolina condo the HOA insures the building and repairs covered water damage. Insurance and reserves pay first, and anything left is split among all owners by percentage.
Have us check the documents Call 854.333.2135

THE BASIC RULE

## The HOA insures and repairs the building
South Carolina condo law puts two duties on the HOA. It has to insure the building. It has to repair the insured parts when they are damaged. Both duties sit with the board, not with you.
The money moves in an order. Insurance pays first. The reserve fund pays next. Whatever the repair still costs after that is a shared expense. Every owner pays a share of it, set by their percentage in the master deed.
That surprises most buyers. The bill does not follow the unit the water reached. It follows the ownership percentages. A leak in one unit can put a charge on all of them.

- &#10003; The law sets no dollar amount. It does not say how much cover the HOA has to buy, which events have to be covered, or how big the deductible can be. The master deed and the policy decide that.

- &#10003; The repair duty has two exits. The HOA can skip a repair only if rebuilding would break a law or a health rule, or if 80 percent of owners vote not to rebuild.

- &#10003; Roofs, foundations and main walls are shared parts. A pipe inside a wall may or may not be. The master deed draws that line.

- &#10003; A regular HOA is not a condo . If the community is not a condo, state law puts no insurance duty and no repair duty on the association at all.

WATER FROM UPSTAIRS

## Water from the unit above you
This is two questions, and they have different answers. One is who fixes your ceiling, your walls and your paint. If the damaged part is one the HOA had to insure, the HOA repairs it. Anything insurance and the reserve do not cover gets shared by all owners.
The other is whether the owner upstairs owes you money for what you lost inside your unit. State condo law does not answer that. Your own policy is usually the faster route. If you believe you are owed, talk to a South Carolina attorney. This page is general information, not legal advice.
You do not have to guess at any of this. Send us the master deed and the building policy summary before you write an offer, and we will show you where your unit ends and what a deductible could cost you.
Have us check the documents Call 854.333.2135

THE DEDUCTIBLE

## The deductible is what owners pay
A building policy pays a covered loss minus its deductible. Someone has to cover that gap. State law treats the deductible as a repair cost above the insurance money, so it is a shared expense, split by percentage.
Your lender expects that cost to reach you. Most lenders want your own condo policy to cover deductible charges the HOA passes down, and to cover loss assessments. Those are two different coverages. Have your insurance agent confirm both in writing.
Some building policies carry a per unit deductible, which is charged to the unit where the loss started. If the building policy has one, your own policy has to be big enough to absorb it. Ask the HOA in writing how it handled the deductible the last time the building had a claim.

- &#10003; Ask for the deductible in dollars. A policy can state it as a percentage. The dollar figure is the one that would get split among owners, so get that number.

- &#10003; Ask how the last one was paid. Some HOAs take it out of reserves. Some bill owners directly. The answer tells you what would probably happen next time.

- &#10003; Ask if the HOA insures its own deductible. Some buy cover for it. If the deductible is large, that changes how much could land on you.

- &#10003; Ask what is not covered at all. A deductible only matters on a covered loss. Flood and rising ground water are usually left out of a building policy, so ask about those separately.

WIND

## Wind deductibles cost the most here
On this coast, wind is the loss that turns a deductible into a real bill. Most building policies here carry a separate deductible for wind, and often another for named storms. A named storm is one that has been given a name or a number.
A wind deductible is usually far larger than the regular one. It is often written as a share of the building's insured value rather than a flat number, so it moves when the building is revalued. Ask for it in dollars, not in percent.
Wind cover on the Grand Strand has been repriced hard. Older wooden buildings close to the ocean have the hardest time getting it. Ask when the building policy last renewed, and what happened to the wind deductible when it did.
Have us check the documents Call 854.333.2135

BEFORE YOU OFFER

## Read these papers before you offer
Every question on this page can be answered before you are locked in. The papers already exist. The problem is timing. Most buyers never see them until after they close.
You do not have to wait on the HOA for all of it. A master deed is recorded at the county, so it is public. A buyer under contract has no legal right to the rest, so the seller has to request it. Have them start early. Expect an HOA to take a few days.
Send us the documents the day you get them. Ask us for the document list before you start touring, so you are not chasing paper while the clock runs on a contract.

- &#10003; The unit description in the master deed. It says where your unit ends. That line decides which policy covers your cabinets, floors and paint.

- &#10003; The building policy summary page. Look for the deductible for a single event, and for any separate wind or named storm deductible.

- &#10003; Your own condo policy. Check that it covers HOA deductible charges and loss assessments, and that the limit is high enough for a per unit deductible.

- &#10003; Any open claim or pending assessment. A loss that already happened but has not been paid for is the one that lands on you after closing.

- &#10003; The HOA costs due at closing. Most charge a few months of dues up front, plus a document fee and a fee to open your account. Ask early and it is not a surprise.

What an HO-6 and loss assessment coverage add is on our master policy vs HO-6 page .

Common questions

## Who Pays for Damage FAQ

### Who pays for water damage in a condo in South Carolina?
The HOA insures the building and repairs the insured parts. Insurance pays first, then the reserve fund. Whatever the repair still costs is shared by every owner, by percentage. The master deed decides where your unit ends and how far the building policy reaches inside it.

### Does the HOA pay for water damage from the unit above me?
If the damaged part is one the HOA had to insure, the HOA repairs it, and any cost above insurance and reserves is shared. Whether the owner above owes you money for your own things is a separate question. State condo law does not answer it. Ask a South Carolina attorney.

### Who pays the condo master policy deductible?
Owners do, together. State law treats repair costs above the insurance money and the reserve fund as a shared expense, split by percentage. A deductible on a covered loss is that kind of cost. A per unit deductible works differently and is charged to one unit.

### Does the HOA have to insure the building in South Carolina?
Yes, if the community is a condo. State law makes the group that runs it insure the building, and repair the insured parts when they are damaged. You may still insure your own unit. A community that is not a condo has no insurance duty under state law.

### Do I need my own condo policy if the building has a master policy?
Usually yes, and your lender will likely require it. You need one if the building policy leaves out any part of the inside of your unit, or the upgrades in it. You also need one if the building policy carries a per unit deductible.

# Are HOA fees worth it on the Grand Strand? Yes, when the fee buys what you would pay for anyway.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Whether HOA fees are worth it, from real Grand Strand budgets priced per home against what the same things cost alone.

The short answer
A homeowners association (HOA) fee is worth it when it buys things you would pay for anyway, for less than they cost alone. In The Farm at Carolina Forest, the HOA spends about $43 of each home's $107 monthly fee on cable TV.
The budget's pool line there comes to about $63 a home a year, less than one adult's year at a city pool. The trade-off is room: newer houses with a fee sit on smaller lots, and few houses with a fee list a place to park a boat.

## What does an HOA fee pay for?
The Farm at Carolina Forest is a neighborhood of 1,571 homes outside any city limit, with a Myrtle Beach mailing address. Its main HOA fee is $107 a month, and its newest budget keeps it at $107.
The HOA buys cable TV from Spectrum for its homes, the largest line in the budget at about 40 cents of each dollar. Trash pickup, which the HOA hires, is the next largest.
The Farm spends about $43 of each home's $107 fee on cable TV Budget line Each home's share a month

Trash pickup $13
Common-area landscaping and ponds $12
The management company $9
Power for shared areas $7
Savings for future projects $6
The two pools $5
Insurance $3
All other lines $10

Each home's share of the HOA's newest approved budget is about $108 a month: $107 from the fee, and the rest from transfer fees, rent and key cards.
Cable TV and trash pickup take about half of each home's share. If you would pay for cable TV anyway, about $43 of the fee is a bill you already have.
The rest keeps up the shared land and its ponds, two pools, an activity center and a clubhouse with a fitness room. It also pays the company that runs the HOA.
From April 15 to October 15, both pools stay open until 9 p.m., so a swim after work is part of what the fee buys.
The Farm's large pool and activity center from above. The HOA keeps up two pools. Photo: NOAA National Geodetic Survey, public domain. Labels by Chapter3 Realty.
Other communities put other services in the fee. In Del Webb North Myrtle Beach, the fee is $315 a month on most homes for sale or recently sold. The builder lists lawn care and a 175-channel TV package in it.

- On The Farm's north edge The state bought land there for a nature preserve. That land holds habitat for the Venus flytrap.

- The trade-off No private pool on a lot. A boat, trailer, camper or RV may be kept outside only with the HOA's written approval; pickups and SUVs are fine.
