Home / Condo Buildings / The Palace
Palace Resort, Myrtle Beach

# The Palace Resort, Myrtle Beach: condos for sale on the ocean. A 241-foot tower with a water park next door.

- On the beach 241-foot tower

- Condos 298

- Built Mid-1980s

- Nightly rentals Allowed

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Two pools on the ocean with a putting green beside them, and three 40-foot water slides at the resort next door, at 1605 S Ocean Blvd.

The short answer
The Palace Resort is a 241-foot tower on the beach at the south end of Myrtle Beach. It holds 298 condos you can own: studios, one-bedrooms and two-bedrooms. The middle sale price over the past year was about $142,000.
The monthly HOA fee goes by the unit's size: about $460 for a studio, $685 for a one-bedroom and $915 for a two-bedroom. Units may rent by the night, and guests who book through the resort's own rental program get the water park next door.
Booking a stay instead? The resort takes reservations on its own website .

The Palace is one of 47 buildings in our guide to Myrtle Beach oceanfront condo buildings .

## What is it like to own a condo at the Palace?
Book a stay through the Palace's own rental program, and the first two guests on the reservation get the H2Oasis water park free, every day of the stay. H2Oasis is next door at Landmark Resort. Its three slides are each 40 feet tall, and the longest runs 250 feet.
Other guests in the room can buy a pass for $5. The water park opens for the summer season. For an owner who rents through the resort, it is a reason a guest picks your unit over one down the beach.
Whether owners get passes is in the association's rules, and we ask before you offer.
The Palace has its own two pools on the ocean, three outdoor whirlpools, an indoor whirlpool and a sauna. A putting green sits next to the oceanfront pools, and two beach accesses lead to the sand. Most of the outdoor features are open in season.

### A 241-foot tower on the south end
The Palace stands 241 feet tall. No floor is numbered 13: unit numbers run on floors 1 to 12 and 14 to 23. The top two floors hold 10 condos each, against 14 on most floors below.
It stands next door to Landmark Resort, on the south end of the city's oceanfront. Family Kingdom's rides are under a mile north along the beach, and Springmaid Pier is about a mile and a half south.
U.S. government aerial photo
The Palace from above, on the beach, with Landmark Resort next door.
Every unit has a full kitchen, and the resort lists a private balcony among its room features. The resort calls a studio an efficiency. A studio or a one-bedroom sleeps 4, and a two-bedroom sleeps 6.
All 25 condos for sale on November 13, 2026 came furnished, with covered parking. 23 were listed with an ocean view, and 8 of those as oceanfront units.

## What are the HOA fees at the Palace Resort?
At the Palace Resort, the HOA fee pays water and sewer, trash, internet and the building's insurance, by nearly every listing. Most listings add pest control. Units of the same size list nearly the same fee.

## Can you Airbnb a condo at the Palace Resort?
Yes. The Palace is in a City of Myrtle Beach zoning district where nightly rentals are allowed, and the resort itself rents units by the night. About 8 in 10 of the condos for sale on November 13 were in a rental program.

- Through the resort's own program The Palace runs an on-site rental program, part of the Vacation Myrtle Beach group. It collects and pays the lodging taxes, sends monthly and year-end statements, and holds the rent in escrow, a separate account, until it pays the owner. Its guests get the water-park passes.

- On your own You can hire a licensed manager or list the unit on Airbnb yourself. The license and the taxes are on our short-term rental rules page .

The program does not publish its share of the rent, so we get its terms for any unit you consider. Our page on a rental program versus Airbnb shows the money both ways.
What studios, one-bedrooms and two-bedrooms earn across Myrtle Beach is on our Airbnb income page . No public source gives income for the Palace alone.

### The resort's rules for guests
Guests must be 21 to check in. Guests may not bring pets, and a $500 fine applies; registered service animals are not counted as pets. Guests register one car for a studio or one-bedroom, and up to two for a two-bedroom.
An owner's own rules on pets and cars are in the condo's founding documents and rules. We read them before you offer.

# Myrtle Beach or Charleston? More home for the money here. More jobs, flights and history in Charleston.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 14, 2026
Myrtle Beach and Charleston side by side: home prices, property tax, the beach, the summer, flood insurance, jobs and the drive to work.

The short answer
The typical home in the Myrtle Beach area is worth about $340,000, about $98,000 less than in the Charleston area. In Myrtle Beach, after the summer season, you can walk a leashed dog on the beach at any hour.
Charleston has more jobs, higher pay and a busier airport, and ferries leave downtown for Fort Sumter, where the Civil War began. The saving here goes furthest when your income or savings come with you.

## Is Myrtle Beach or Charleston better to live in?
Pick Myrtle Beach for more home, the beach and a lower tax bill. Pick Charleston for a bigger job market, more flights and its history.

## Is it cheaper to live in Myrtle Beach than Charleston?
Yes. The typical home in the Myrtle Beach area is worth about $340,000, and in the Charleston area about $437,000. That is about $98,000 less.
The Census Bureau's survey of homeowners shows about the same difference: about $105,000 between the two areas' middle home values. In the past year, values held about flat in both areas.
The difference in typical home value has almost doubled in ten years
- Charleston area

- Myrtle Beach area

Zillow's typical home value for all homes, each September. Both areas rose about 80% since 2016, so the difference in dollars almost doubled.
Everyday prices are lower too. On the federal government's price index, prices in the Myrtle Beach area are about 7% lower overall. To compare your own budget, use our cost of living calculator .

## Which has more beach, Myrtle Beach or Charleston?
Myrtle Beach is on the ocean. Downtown has a boardwalk about 1.3 miles long, beside the sand. After the summer season and until May 1, you can walk a leashed dog or ride a bike on the beach and the Boardwalk at any hour.
Horry County has more than 360 public beach accesses, and Charleston County has 136. North Myrtle Beach alone has 167, more than Charleston County's whole coast. Parking and tent rules differ by town; our beach rules by town lists them.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Houses and condo towers on the beach in Myrtle Beach, with wooden walkways over the dunes to the sand.
Charleston's beaches are on its islands. From Charleston City Hall, Sullivan's Island and Folly Beach are each about 20 minutes by car with no traffic. On Sullivan's Island is Fort Moultrie, where patriots in a fort of palmetto logs beat the Royal Navy in 1776.

## Is Myrtle Beach hotter than Charleston?
Near the ocean, no. Myrtle Beach and Charleston have about the same summer, with about three weeks a year at 90 degrees or more.
Days a year at 90 degrees or more: about the same near the ocean Weather station, where Days a year at 90 degrees or more

North Myrtle Beach airport · near the ocean 21 days
Downtown Charleston · harbor station 25 days
Charleston airport · inland, in North Charleston 64 days

NOAA's 1991 to 2020 averages at each weather station. Charleston's airport is inland, so it is hotter than either beach town.
Winter is colder here. The North Myrtle Beach airport has about 34 nights a year at or below freezing, and downtown Charleston about 6. Rain is about the same in both.
One of our team found the first summer here hot and humid, got used to it within a short time, and now likes being outside.
Month by month, see Myrtle Beach weather , with the ocean temperature.

## Are property taxes lower in Myrtle Beach than Charleston?
Yes. The middle property tax a homeowner pays is about $1,180 a year in the Myrtle Beach area and about $1,930 in the Charleston area.
The state's rule is the same in both: the home you live in is taxed on 4% of its fair market value, once you apply for it.
The bills differ because each county, city and school district has its own tax rate. In Charleston County alone, the middle bill is about $2,310.
Our Horry County property tax guide shows how to apply for the 4% rate, with a calculator.

## Is flood insurance more common in Charleston?
Yes. FEMA estimates about one in seven residential buildings in Horry County are covered by a federal flood policy. In Charleston County, it is about one in three.
FEMA also counts about three in ten residential buildings in Charleston County in its high-risk flood zone. Its file has no matching count for Horry County.
For a house here, our agents check its flood zone and flood history before you make an offer. Our guides to home, wind and flood insurance and finding out if a house has flooded cover both.

## More new homes are being built in Myrtle Beach
Half of all homes in the Myrtle Beach area, vacation homes included, were built in 2003 or later. In the Charleston area, the middle year is 1999.
In 2025, builders in the Myrtle Beach area took out permits for 6,418 new single-family houses. That is more than the Charleston area's 5,799, with less than half the people.
The construction cost on those permits, without the land, averaged about $218,000 here and at least $370,000 in the Charleston area. Our new construction guide covers buying a new home here.

## Charleston has more jobs and higher pay
The Charleston area has about 449,000 working residents, and the Myrtle Beach area about 185,000. The middle household income is about $93,000 there and about $71,000 here.
Pay is higher there, and homes cost more by about the same share. In both areas, the middle home value is about 4.6 times the middle household income.

### Where people work
Health care and education employ the most people in both. Here, about one in seven workers is in hotels, restaurants, entertainment and recreation. In the Charleston area, about one in ten works in manufacturing.

### The drive to work
The drive to work is shorter here: about 25 minutes on average, against about 30. About one in eight commuters here take 45 minutes or more, and about one in five in the Charleston area.
In our experience, rush hour here adds 5 to 10 minutes, and leaving for work between 5 and 8 in the morning has few stops.
Who hires here, and what the work pays, is in our jobs guide . Why so many people move here is in why everyone is moving to Myrtle Beach .

## What Charleston does better

### More flights
Charleston's airport is busier. About 3.1 million passengers boarded there in 2025, against about 1.7 million at Myrtle Beach International.

### The state's teaching hospital
The Medical University of South Carolina, MUSC, is in Charleston. It is the state's only comprehensive academic health system, and its cancer center is the only one in the state the National Cancer Institute has designated.
For veterans, the Myrtle Beach VA Clinic is an outpatient clinic in the VA Charleston system. That system's medical center, the Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center, is in Charleston. Our Myrtle Beach hospitals guide lists every hospital that serves the Grand Strand.

### History in the harbor
Two forts stand at the entrance to Charleston's harbor. Ferries leave downtown for Fort Sumter, where the Civil War began in April 1861.
For the full list of what is good and hard about living here, read living in Myrtle Beach year-round . Choosing a town on the Grand Strand next? Our 13 towns compared puts each one side by side.

## What Myrtle Beach does better
Charleston has real strengths, and Myrtle Beach has its own. These are the places Myrtle Beach comes out ahead.

### Housing costs less in every way we measured
The typical home is worth about $340,000, against about $437,000. Median rent is about $1,441 a month, against about $1,855. The middle property tax bill is about $1,180 a year, against about $1,930.

### Far more new houses
The 2025 permits work out to about 15 new single-family houses per 1,000 residents in the Myrtle Beach area. The Charleston area's figure is about 6.5.

### A beach that is the city itself
Myrtle Beach has 143 public beach accesses inside the city, and a boardwalk about 1.3 miles long. From Charleston City Hall, the nearest beach is about 20 minutes away by car.

### A shorter drive to work
The average one-way commute is about 25 minutes here, against about 30. About 1 in 8 commuters here drives 45 minutes or more, against about 1 in 5 in the Charleston area.
If these matter most to you, the houses above are where to start. A day of showings shows you the rest.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach vs Charleston FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach part of Charleston?
No. Myrtle Beach is in Horry County, and Charleston is in Charleston County. They are separate cities with separate local governments.

### How far is Myrtle Beach from Charleston?
About 98 miles by road, city hall to city hall. With no traffic, the drive takes about 2 hours 15 minutes each way.

### Which is bigger, Myrtle Beach or Charleston?
Charleston. The Charleston area has about 889,000 people, about twice the Myrtle Beach area's 428,000.

### Is Charleston's airport bigger than Myrtle Beach's?
Yes. The FAA ranks Charleston International a medium hub and Myrtle Beach International a small hub, by passengers boarded.
